novel_info.title: Reverend Insanity: The Goody Two-Shoes System
novel_info.author: Drechenaux
novel_info.summary: Man is the spirit of all things, and gu are the refined fragments of the Great Dao.The ambition which blooms with the spring's morning breeze withers at the call of autumn's night.The accumulation of five hundred years - triumphs and failures -  will be naught but ash with dawn's first light.The rising of the sun bathes the mountains in golden flame, but 'tis sunset upon the demon's time.The demonic overlord, Fang Yuan, is cornered by his enemies after word gets out that he refined the Spring Autumn Cicada - a gu worm rumored to be capable of having a chance at sending one back in time but demands a terrifying price in return - the user's entire existence!With no hope of escape, in desperation, Fang Yuan uses the Spring Autumn Cicada which miraculously lives up to its name and sends him back in time. And now, he's back in Gu Yue Village as a fifteen-year-old ready to use his knowledge of the future to conquer the world... but there's something wrong. Something is quite different this time around. What's with this new notification that keeps popping up in his view? It calls itself 'The Goody Two-Shoes System.' It also starts giving him quests to complete."Help Fang Zheng gain his confidence back!" - get a Green Copper Relic Gu!"Help your friends refine their gu worms!" - have your aptitude raised by 2%!All of these rewards and quests before him, why are they trying to convert this demonic overlord to the path of righteousness?And aren't some of these quests kind of... sus? Why does marrying Bai Ning Bing give him an immortal gu?Whatever, anything for benefits!This is a fanfiction based on Gu Zhen Re's work 'Reverend Insanity' known in Chinese as 蛊真人 or 'Gu Taoist Master'. I don't own the rights to the original work.'Gu' in the context of this story are mystical insects that have various powers and are the basis of the world's cultivation system.

chapters.title: Chapter 1 - 1: The Goody Two-Shoes System
chapters.content:
"Man is the spirit of all things, and gu are the refined fragments of the Great Dao.
The ambition which blooms with the spring's morning breeze withers at the call of autumn's night.
Night-black hair in summer's light turns snow-white at winter's sight,
The accumulation of five hundred years - triumphs and failures - will be naught but ash with dawn's first light.
The rising of the sun bathes the mountains in golden flame, but 'tis sunset upon the demon's time,
The road to eternal life - filled with thorns and tribulations, unyielding winds and solitude,
The journey of five hundred years ends in the blink of an eye, yet,
The heart of a demon has no regret even in death."
"Quick- hand over the Spring Autumn Cicada!"
"Oh demon, your wicked sins are too numerous to count. Relinquish the fruit of your ill-gotten efforts, and I will bestow the mercy of a quick death upon thee!"
"Watch out, he's finally moving!"
"Stay back, the demon's counterattacking!"
Fang Yuan laughed in their faces as he decided it was time to gamble it all. "If the Spring Autumn Cicada truly works, I will be an even greater demon in my next life!"
Blood alone greases the wheels of history- and the wheel of time is never-ending, churning ever forward, crushing those who stand in its path with reckless abandon.
And yet, here Fang Yuan's soul was, going not forward, but defying heaven itself as he soared through the stream of the River of Time backwards, back, until he found himself in a familiar room.
"This is..." he muttered. Gu Yue village?
The last thing he remembered was being surrounded by his enemies. He had slaughtered twenty million people in order to refine the Spring Autumn Cicada, alas, just as he was savoring his victory, he was cornered and had no choice but to use that gu worm.
It was rumored to be able to take one back, traveling upstream the river of time rather than the normal sequence of events. The price for this was massive- it demanded everything. One's body would detonate, their gu worms and cultivation destroyed as their will would be transported alongside the Spring Autumn Cicada back to the past.
Of course, that was what was rumored. No one could confirm this fact, and it was said that there was always a chance of failure while using the cicada. Given this, who would dare use it?
And yet, with no choice, enemies all around him, he had had no choice but to detonate it.
"Thankfully it worked or else-" Fang Yuan was about to say when something interrupted his vision.
It was not correct to say that he 'saw' it with his vision, more that he saw it in his mind's eye.
Congratulations on awakening the Goody Two-Shoes System!
Fang Yuan was calm as he analyzed this. Was this a side effect of using the Spring Autumn Cicada? It wasn't like he had any person he could ask regarding this.
You have been chosen to bring peace and balance to the world! The Goody Two-Shoes System will be your guide on bringing harmony and joy on your path to becoming a Venerable!
That last line caught his attention. To become a Venerable... though it would not grant him Eternal Life by itself, it was an essential step in his plans on the same.
As an introduction, here is a list of quests and what is in your inventory!
Inventory: Currently empty.
Daily Quest: Complete five push-ups. (Reward: 3 Primeval Stones)
[Daily Quests appear once a day, the more regularly you do them, the greater the rewards!]
Main Quests:
1. Complete the awakening ceremony! (Reward: ???)New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
[Main Quests are those which are important on your journey to becoming a Righteous Venerable, more of them will appear with time]
Secret Quests:
You have no secret quests as of yet.
[Secret quests can be unlocked or completed with certain triggers. Explore around to find out!]
Fang Yuan frowned. He had encountered many things during his five hundred year's of existence, though nothing of this exact sort. It almost seemed like the inheritance or the land spirit of a blessed land, though he had never encountered something like this within his head though.
Unless this was the will of someone who had entered his mind while he had traveled alongside the Spring Autumn Cicada- though he strangely enough could feel very little 'thought' from it, nor could his own mind grasp onto the will.
As it was right now he lacked the wisdom path methods necessary in order to detect something like that, let alone deal with it.
The first thing, the 'daily quest' caught his eye.
Do five pushups? That seemed simple enough.
As it was, the worst that could happen if he was wrong was that he'd look slightly silly.
"Brother..." as Fang Yuan was in the middle of this impromptu workout, a carbon copy of himself walked in. His younger brother- Fang Zheng.
Ah, Fang Yuan thought as memories poured back in. During this time, Fang Zheng was treated poorly by their adoptive parents- their aunt and uncle. In order to somewhat lessen the harshness of their treatment, Fang Yuan had revealed some of the poems he had learned back on Earth, gaining their admiration as a 'genius.'
Of course, this was all based on his prior knowledge. It was not genuine genius, and on the awakening ceremony, it was found out that Fang Yuan was a mere C-grade talent.
In this world, when it came to cultivation, talent was everything. It determined how far you could go as a Gu master- granted, one with a huge pile of resources could overcome even the worst lack of talent, but in their remote village one would not find anything that could greatly overcome the gap between talents.
Because he had been a C-grade talent, average at best, it meant that Fang Yuan had taken ten years to reach Rank Two in his prior life, and it was only thanks to a fortuitous encounter that he had managed to reach Rank Three a hundred years into life before he had regressed.
In contrast, his younger brother had turned out to be an A-grade talent, meaning that he was able to soar past boundaries that Fang Yuan was unable to. Suddenly, Fang Zheng was showered with praise and resources, and quickly forgot all about his elder brother.
Fang Zheng knew nothing of all of this, however, and still thought of Fang Yuan as the budding rising star of the clan.
He had been a bit nervous, and noted that his elder brother's door was ajar. He had gone to check up on Fang Yuan, only to see him doing push-ups on the floor.
"Is something wrong? Um... shouldn't you be sleeping?" Fang Zheng asked. It was a bit of an odd sight, someone working out like that so late at night. Was he also having trouble sleeping?
Once Fang Yuan was done, he got up, and simply said, "Nothing. I'm fine, you should go to sleep too."
The cold reply stung Fang Zheng's heart, but this was how his brother had always been. He simply nodded and retreated into the shadows.
Fang Yuan saw a notification pop up.
First daily quest complete! 3 primeval stones have been added to your inventory!

chapters.title: Chapter 2 - 2: The Awakening Ceremony Part One
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan became aware that something had been added to his 'inventory.'
What surprised him slightly was that it had not been given to him directly.
Come to think of it, did he even have the primeval stone in reality or was this just messing with him?
Withdraw from inventory?
The moment he thought about it, that message popped up.
What was this 'inventory?' He knew of storage-type gu worms, though this seemed to have an inventory all on its own.
Come to think of it, this 'system' seemed to be able to do far too much. Gu worms typically could only do one thing, be that attack or defense or something else.
As an example, the Spring Autumn Cicada had been the highest ranked gu worm that he had ever owned, and yet, it had been no help to him during his last battle before he used it to go back in time. That was because going back in time was its only ability, not attack or defense.
And yet this 'system' could generate primeval stones, store them, and even seemed to have some information-type methods. It was far too expansive to simply be a single gu worm.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs
He only withdrew a single primeval stone, and his pupils dilated as he felt one appear in his hand. The count of stones in his inventory had dropped down from three to two, but this was a real, for goodness sake primeval stone!
Primeval stones were used in cultivation to replete one's primeval essence, and since they were so useful to Gu Masters, they were used as this world's currency in the place of normal gold and silver coinage.
However, Fang Yuan had not awakened his aperture yet, and could not use this. He hastily wanted to put it back, only to find that he couldn't.
Note: Items once withdrawn from 'Inventory' cannot be placed back.
So that was it...
It looked like he would need a storage-type gu worm to store the primeval stone and could not use the system to do so.
He frowned. The primeval stone he was holding, although valuable, now felt like a mouse trap he had placed his hand into.
After all, if people asked, where would he say that it came from?
His aunt and uncle, though they doted upon him simply out of respect for his talent, would not give him something like this. A primeval stone could feed a family easily for a week, and while a single stone was less valuable for Gu Masters, it was still not something that could be taken lightly.
There had been times during his previous life where he did not have a single stone to his name, he had not been able to feed his gu worms, and had basically fallen into worse straights than a mortal. He had done odd jobs during those time periods to get by...
As he contemplated those things, with firm resolution he shattered the stone in his hand. The primeval essence scattered in the air before being carried away by the wind.
He had considered hiding it somewhere, but it was far too likely that he would be discovered.
After all, he would soon be exposed as a C-grade talent tomorrow, and then would lose favor with his aunt and uncle. They would soon seek a reason to get rid of him afterwards, and framing him for stealing a primeval stone would make this task much easier.
Birds die for food, humans die for wealth!
Even though Fang Yuan knew he needed many thousands if not tens of thousands of primeval stones in the future, it was courting trouble to keep that primeval stone with him.
A beggar holding a diamond necklace was asking to be robbed- it was much the same!
However, it had not been a total waste. He still had the two stones in his inventory, and would be able to use them later.
He wanted to look into the system further, but knew he had to sleep for tomorrow's ceremony.
The next day, the daily quest was much the same, to do five push-ups. The reward was also the same, three primeval stones.
With this, Fang Yuan had to say that the system's primeval stone rewards in and of themselves were of great help during his journey.
That of course, made him slightly worried. Not only about the origin of the system itself, but if it could be detected by others. Something that could generate primeval stones practically for free, even if small in amount, would be widely coveted.
He had no idea if others could see it, though as he thought so a notification popped up.
System is visible only to the user.
He frowned. He somehow doubted that it could say, protect itself from a Venerable's deduction, though at this point he could only take its word for it.
"Is Young Master satisfied with his appearance?" a girl asked him.
He had been so engrossed in thinking about the system that he had barely taken note of Shen Cui. She was one of the family servants, a mortal who had only slightly above average looks- but because she had been in close proximity to the two brothers had been able to charm both of them.
Fang Yuan had fell for her feminine wiles in his last life, though he knew her true nature. What concerned him currently was to reach Rank Three as soon as possible and bounce, as he knew the locations of some very valuable inheritances that could greatly speed up his journey. However, they were in remote and dangerous areas, meaning he could not go to them right now.
Secret Quest Unlocked!
If She Breathes, She's a Thot I
Description: ???
Reward: ???
Ah, it looked like there was a secret quest... though the fact that he couldn't figure out how to do it or what it would give him as a reward was annoying.
He was supposed to get something for finishing the Awakening ceremony, but what that was was also a mystery.
Shen Cui pouted as Fang Yuan was not doting upon her as he usually did.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 - 3: The Awakening Ceremony Part Two
chapters.content:
Even though Fang Yuan was not paying attention to her, which Shen Cui chalked up to simple stress for the upcoming ceremony, Fang Zheng couldn't help but enviously glance at the two of them.
Ever since they had been orphaned at a young age, the two brothers had been taken care of by their aunt and uncle. 'Taken care of' was used here more in the mafia sense of the word rather than the parental sense- Cinderella was likely treated better by her stepmother than the two were treated by their aunt and uncle.
In truth their 'adoption' was merely a way for the two to embezzle their parent's assets. Of course, while their treatment was subpar, it wasn't like they could do whatsoever they wanted. They couldn't kill the two of them, and the day would eventually come when the two brothers were old enough to strike out on their own, and more worrisome, able to inherit their parent's fortune.
They already had plans in motion to deal with this. Much like an invading force might use the tactic of 'divide and conquer' they too had applied something masterfully to the two brothers.
Their treatment couldn't have been more different- one could see it even in the clothes they were adorned in for the awakening ceremony.
Fang Yuan was dressed as one would expect the young master of an influential house to dress on such an occasion, while Fang Zheng was dressed like a commoner. Fang Yuan had Shen Cui to dote upon him, though this was more truly a way for this aunt and uncle to keep him under their thumb. Fang Zheng hadn't even had a servant initially until Fang Yuan explicitly asked one for him, and she was an old lady, Shen Cui's mother.
The purpose of this was to drive a wedge between the two brothers so that their aunt and uncle could more easily manipulate them by egging them against one another.
Fang Yuan, before he had mysteriously transmigrated to this world, had been a Chinese scholar. What that meant was that he already had the wisdom of an adult, though even he had been deceived somewhat by his aunt and uncle's schemes. Fang Zheng was even more susceptible, having none of this advantage.
Not that Fang Yuan cared the slightest for this. He could see beyond these petty schemes, and he had risen far above the confines of this village in his last life.
The world was vast, and stretched far beyond Gu Yue village. He only needed to become strong enough to explore, and that was where his true journey would start.
Someone like Fang Zheng, who could only still think of how he was ever eclipsed by his brother's shadow, and could only think so far as to how to impress Shen Cui, could not begin to imagine the vastness of his elder brother's ambition.
The two of them headed out, and even on the street, it was as if Fang Zheng was walking in Fang Yuan's shadow, the Luigi to his Mario.
"Hey- is that Fang Yuan?"
"The genius who makes poems?"
"Right, everyone says he's going to be hugely talented!"
"He has a bit of an arrogant expression doesn't he..."
"You'd have the same kind of expression if you could do what he could!"
"And who's that behind him?"
"Oh, that's Fang Yuan's younger brother."
Fang Zheng sighed.
'Will I only ever be acknowledged as his younger brother?'- he thought to himself.
Fang Yuan took no notice of these comments. No doubt they were all riled up for awakening ceremony, though these comments would soon change.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
The crowd's opinion was as fickle as the seasons, and would do a complete one-eighty once the results of the awakening ceremony were made public.
Fang Yuan would crash and burn like Icarus, while Fang Zhen would soar above the clouds like a hawk who had just learned to fly.
Fang Yuan had only one thing on his mind- that was how to obtain his parent's inheritance. He had been unable to during his past life, though now, with the benefit of hindsight, he would be able to do so.
Without the help of those resources, he basically stood very little chance of reaching Rank Three in anything resembling a timely manner.
There was a massive crowd near the main pavilion- everyone who had turned fifteen had come here for the awakening ceremony.
The clan head was even here, along with many elders. No doubt they were interested in scouting out the new talent among this batch.
"If only we had someone who could match up to Bai clan's Bai Ning Bing. To think he is already an elder at age eighteen..."
"We haven't had an A-grade talent in three years..."
"Oh, but haven't you heard of Fang Yuan?"
"The boy famous for his poems?"
Most of Fang Yuan's 'poems' were of course, actually famous poems from Earth that he had passed off as his own, but his 'creation' of them had already cemented itself firmly in the minds of everyone in Gu Yue village.
After all, those who had precocious talents such as with poetry, or who had bene born with immense strength, usually grew up to be talented Gu Masters.
Of course, these achievements were thanks to his memories from Earth, and not a sign of heaven favoring Fang Yuan.
The youngsters were led into the pavilion and down below, near the clan's spirit spring.
The area here was dark, though the spirit spring cast an eerie azure glow over everyone. The kids were all quiet as the observed this place- as one of the clan's main strongholds, not anyone could just waltz in here whensoever they pleased. Security had to be top-notch as well, as many of the clan's enemies would've loved to poison, pollute, or otherwise damage the spirit spring. It would mean the collapse of the entire Gu Yue clan!
As such, it was their first time for them seeing such a place.
Every clan or major force needed a spirit spring to maintain themselves. They were naturally occurring phenomenon, which generated large numbers of primeval stones. Clans were built around them and protected them as well as distributed the stones generated by the spirit spring to their members.
Within the waters, there were many glowing lights as if the spring was filled with underwater fireflies.
These lights were budding Hope gu.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 - 4: The Awakening Ceremony Part Three
chapters.content:
Hope Gu was one of the legendary three gu mentioned in the beginning of 'The Legends of Ren Zu.'
Ren Zu was the OG human, and as he found himself in an unfamiliar world, found that he was surrounded by monsters known as 'Predicaments.' These Predicaments hunted him down relentlessly, and in the harsh environment he constantly was hounded and harassed.
One day, three gu appeared before him. One was Strength Gu, which offered him strength in exchange for his youth.
Using strength, Ren Zu was able to overcome many of the Predicaments.
Yet, even brute strength was not enough. There were many Predicaments that could not be overcome with just Strength Gu's help, and so he had to rely on Wisdom Gu, the second of the three gu which had gathered before him.
"Oh human, give me your middle life, and I will help you," Wisdom Gu said.
Ren Zu gave up even his middle life, and with that gained the power of Wisdom Gu. He was able to outsmart and outfight nearly all of the Predicaments who were after him, but eventually, after trading so much of his lifespan away, he was left as nothing but the husk of an old man. His hair had turned grey, he could barely see, and all of his teeth had fallen out.
Both Wisdom Gu and Strength Gu left him, and he was abandoned, left to the whims of nature.
So there he was, breathing raggedly, as the Predicaments finally caught up with him.
"Looks like this... is the end..." he sighed to himself.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
"Human," the third gu that had approached him said. "I can still help you!"
"I no longer have anything to offer you," Ren Zu replied. "I gave up my youth first, and then my middle ages. I wish to enjoy whatever lifespan I have left, even if it is just for one breath longer."
"Human, out of the three gu, I have the least requirement when it comes to using me," the third gu said. "I only need your heart."
"But oh, even if that were true, what can I do?" Ren Zu asked. He was surrounded on all sides by Predicaments like a rock in a lake. "Even if both Strength and Wisdom came back to help me, it would not be enough to tip the scales. But... alright, I shall offer my heart to you."
The third gu was Hope Gu, and entered Ren Zu's heart.
Immediately, it let out a bright light, and wheresoever the light landed, the Predicaments screamed out in pain and agony.
"Oh no! It's Hope!"
"We're terrified of Hope Gu!"
Immediately, the Predicaments turned tail and fled the scene.
And in that way, Hope Gu had saved Ren Zu's life.
In the present day, Fang Yuan watched as the elder called out the youngsters names one by one.
The first person nearly tripped over his own feet as he began to walk into the spirit spring.
As he took a step, Hope Gu began to fly around him.
After three steps, this person felt like he could not walk any further, as if he had run into an invisible wall.
The elder frowned. "Three steps, no talent to become a Gu Master. Next!"
The boy in question burst into tears. Many looked at him sympathetically- only about half of humans had any talent to become a Gu Master. It was a bit higher among the Gu Yue villagers, about sixty percent or so, because the founder of their village, the Gu Yue ancestor, had been a powerful Rank Five Gu Master in his own right.
If one was not a Gu Master, they were at the bottom of the hierarchy of this world. In other words, that boy was destined for nothing higher than servitude. Upon seeing him, many of the youngsters began desperately praying for at least a D-grade talent if nothing else.
There were two people that Fang Yuan remembered were of note during this ceremony, aside from himself and Fang Zheng.
One was Gu Yue Mo Bei, a boy who had a long face like that of a horse, who was a B-grade talent. His grandfather Gu Yue Mo Chen, was an elder of the clan.
The other was Gu Yue Chi Chen, Gu Yue Chi Lian's grandson. He was also a B-grade talent... at least, it had seemed so at first. In reality Chi Chen only had C-grade talent much like Fang Yuan, but his grandfather had helped him cheat and appear as a B-grade talent. They were both punished later for this by the village head - after all, cheating during this time was greatly frowned upon.
Though, there was a reason why Chi Lian had done so. He and Mo Chen were both elders, and political rivals. But neither could live forever, and their future prospects depended on their inheritors. If word got out that Chi Lian's grandson and heir was only a C-grade talent, it would massively damage their family's future.
Fang Yuan tapped his chin, considering if there was a move he could make to take advantage of the situation. Unfortunately, right now he was too weak to get away with blackmailing Chi Lian.
The further that one walked, the greater one's talent when it came to cultivating. Anything less than ten steps meant that one had no talent whatsoever, but both Chi Chen and Mo Bei managed to walk thirty-six steps, just as Fang Yuan had remembered.
"B-grade talent!" the elder exclaimed. Until that point, there were many frowns among the elders. After all, it seemed that only about half rather than sixty percent of the youngsters had talent, and of these all were D-grade or C-grade talents. To finally have two B-grade talents gave them some relief.
"Gu Yue Fang Yuan!"
Finally, his own name was called out. Fang Yuan sighed, as everyone suddenly turned to look at him expectantly.
The greater one's expectations, the greater the disappointment when they were dashed. Fang Yuan knew the result already, so his heart was calm and tranquil. Though, there was one big change this time.
Fang Yuan smiled, he was a bit surprised that this 'system' had not been discovered yet. Here, there were countless eyes and investigative methods watching, so whoever set up the 'system' must've been a Rank Five expert at the least.
As Fang Yuan walked, Hope Gu began to enter a region above his umbilicus and below his sternum, coalescing until he could walk no further than twenty-seven steps.
Main Mission Complete!
Completed the Awakening Ceremony!
Cultivation Blessing Granted - Talent Obscuration!
Cultivation Blessings are single-use effects granted by the system. Using Talent Obscuration, you can deceive others and show yourself to be a B-grade talent!
New main mission unlocked!
I'm A B-Grade Genius!
Requirement: Deceive people into thinking you have B-grade talent using this Cultivation Blessing!
Reward: ???

chapters.title: Chapter 5 - 5: The Awakening Ceremony Part Four
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan frowned.
This was out of expectations. He had finished a mission only to be given another one?
Already, he could feel the Hope Gu coalescing, forming his aperture. Within the area that they entered his body, a space formed, which simultaneously extremely small yet infinitely big inside.
This space was filled to 44% of its capacity with a green liquid- primeval essence! The lifeblood of Gu Masters!
Talent was important for Gu Masters because the higher one's talent, the greater the amount of primeval essence in their aperture.
A C-grade talent would have between 40-59%. B-grade between 60-79%. A-grade 80-90%.
Fang Yuan was squarely at the bottom rungs of C-grade with only 44% primeval essence, or aptitude.
His brother, Fang Zheng, an A-grade talent, would soon be discovered to have 80% aptitude!
Did that mean that Fang Zheng was twice as talented compared to Fang Yuan when it came to cultivation?
Absolutely not!
The difference was much, much, greater than that!
The reason being was that the way that Gu Masters advanced was by sending their primeval essence against their aperture walls, hoping to break them.
The issue was that the aperture walls would recover on their own, so one could not chip away at them slowly over time.
What would happen eventually is that the rate of recovery of the aperture walls would surpass the amount of primeval essence that one could drive at them to damage them. These 'break points' would greatly limit how far one could go.
Gu Masters recovered their primeval essence after six hours without outside help, meaning someone with higher aptitude also gained proportionately greater primeval essence back.
So it was not just with cultivation, but battle strength that would also be affected by talent.
Advancing was like trying to kick a ball out of a ditch. Even if you could kick it ninety percent up the way out, it would just roll back down and you'd have to do so again. If you couldn't kick it out in one go, you were stuck.
In other words, once one reached that limit, chipping away at their aperture walls would accomplish nothing aside from frustrating them.
As an example, to get to Rank 2, a person needed 50% primeval essence, meaning that Fang Yuan would struggle greatly to get past that point, and would need to expend a large amount of resources to make up for the deficit.
In his past life, it had taken him ten years to reach Rank 2. On the other hand, Fang Zheng could reach Rank 2 with his A-grade aptitude in little under a year, meaning his potential was not double, but ten times Fang Yuan's at this level!
It got worse the higher one rose in rank. It had taken Fang Yuan nearly a century to reach Rank 3 in his previous life, though Fang Zheng would reach it in about three or four years. As for Rank 4, Fang Yuan had no hope of getting there unless he chanced upon a talent-raising gu worm like he had in his past life.
Actually, he knew the locations of several such places where one could find such rare gu, he just couldn't get to them right now.
As it was, once he reached Rank 3, which he could do far more easily with the knowledge gained from his previous life, he could go to those areas. But not now.
However, Fang Zheng could likely reach Rank 4 in a matter of a decade or so.
It was not without good reason that the clan invested so heavily in those with high-grade talents.
"Fang Yuan, can't you go any further?" the elder asked.
Right, they were expecting him to have at least B-grade if not A-grade talent.
And all of this thinking distracted from the fact that the system wanted him to cheat, and had given him the means to do so. Activating this Cultivation Blessing- although he had never heard of such a thing, was as easy as using a gu worm.
But was Fang Yuan going to follow through with it and complete this other mission the system had given him?
Hell no!
It wasn't because he was against cheating. After all, he had been a demonic overlord in his previous life, causing suffering to millions of innocents. If asked to, he would gladly slit his own twin brother's throat if it would increase his aptitude by even 1% if he could get away with it.
But still, there had to be a reason to cheat.
If he recalled correctly, during his first year, his aperture would be evaluated at regular intervals by the academy elder. It would be difficult to keep up this façade.
And while he might be able to squeeze out some extra benefits if he was B-grade, in the end, it would also come with increased scrutiny. Fang Yuan's methods tended to be chaotic and demonic, meaning that it was best for people to underestimate him and overlook him.
Not to mention he found it highly suspicious that this 'system' had essentially thrust this secondary mission upon him just now instead of earlier.
If caught, he did not have the backing of an elder like Chi Chen and would be more severely punished if found out.
Fang Yuan had little faith in this 'system' or what it wanted to accomplish,Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
"What!? Fang Yuan is only a C-grade talent?"
"Unbelievable, only a C-grade for a genius like him!?"
The exclamations came, though Fang Yuan was indifferent to all of them. He had already been through it all.
"Fang Yuan, can you really not move any more?" the elder asked.
Fang Yuan was about to shake his head when another notification popped up.
I'm A B-Grade Genius!
Requirement: Deceive people into thinking you have B-grade talent using this Cultivation Blessing!
Reward: 2% permanent increase to your aptitude.
Fang Yuan's eyes flashed.
The system seemed to detect his reluctance to follow through, and to entice him, it had revealed what the reward was.
A 2% increase in aptitude, that too permanent?
Now the risk-and-reward equation had been greatly altered!
A 2% permanent increase in aptitude was worth more to him than 200 primeval stones.
One could even argue that it was worth more than even 2,000 primeval stone in the long run, though given the fact that he wanted to rush to Rank 3 and bounce from Gu Yue village as quickly as possible, he would take the 2,000 stones right now.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 - 6: The Awakening Ceremony Part Five
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan made his decision right then.
He was balancing on a knife's edge, though he had been in far more uncertain situations than this.
"No, sorry, my foot just got caught somehow," Fang Yuan explained, giving a lame excuse. He then activated the Cultivation Blessing, and found that the pressure that was pressing against him had suddenly lifted, and he took a step forward.
The Hope Gu swarmed into his aperture, though his aptitude did not increase. No one could see this however, as the formation of his aperture was noticed only by Fang Yuan.
"Thirty-nine steps!" one person called out, as Fang Yuan could truly not move forward.
It marked him down as a B-grade talent, and he had even walked further than either Chi Chen and Mo Bei.
True to its word, the system granted him his reward.
Some of the Hope Gu dissolved, increasing his aptitude to 46%!
While a 2% difference was not much, in the long run, it would save him a large amount when it came to primeval stones. Well worth the risk of accepting this mission.
There was of course, another dimension to this.
A lie was no longer a lie if it were true.
In other words, if the 'system' could raise his aptitude by 2%, it could likely raise it even further.
If it went above 60%, he would be a true B-grade Gu Master! If that happened, he could become a Rank 3 Gu Master without having to resort to some unsavory means. Not to mention that his battle strength would surge greatly!
That was assuming he could get further increases, however.
"So, not A-grade, but B-grade instead..."
"Having three B-grades in one class isn't bad..."
They had expected Fang Yuan to be A-grade, but B-grade wasn't bad. It meant that Fang Yuan would be an elder in the future. It was like looking for gold and finding silver instead, though silver was still better than copper (C-grade talent).
Chi Chen and Chi Lian were calm on the surface but were likely very agitated inside, as it meant that a new player was on the field.
"So brother is only a B-grade..." Fang Zheng said, eyes downcast. While not A-grade, it still meant that Fang Yuan was a future elder of the clan. Already, Fang Zheng could feel his elder brother towering over him.
Worries began to besiege him. What if he was only D-grade? What if he had no talent at all?
He was so preoccupied with this that he didn't even hear his name until it was called out four times.
"Coming!" Fang Zheng said, before tripping and landing on his face. He felt himself turn as red as a tomato as laughter entered his ears. It took him quite a bit of willpower to not burst into tears.
The elders shook their heads.
"Get up," a voice said to Fang Zheng calmly. He looked up to see his brother, who had waded out back to reach him and had extended a hand to him. Fang Zheng took his brother's hand. "The road to the future will be interesting. So long as you can persevere and put one foot in front of the other, who knows what you can't accomplish?"
Fang Yuan helped Fang Zheng gain his footing, and Fang Zheng began to walk. The laughter was soon replaced by exclamations of astonishment.
No one was laughing now.
"Forty-six steps! An A-grade talent!"
"The Fang brothers- one of them B-grade, and the other A-grade!"
Simply put, Fang Yuan had the capability to become an elder in the future.
Fang Zheng had the capability to go even further, to potentially become clan head!
The two of them combined would make great waves in the future, that was what everyone felt.
Fang Yuan, however, was concentrated on something else.
Secret quest complete!
An Elder Brother's Guidance!
Reward: Green Copper Relic Gu (x1).
He had not expected a quest to appear like that, nor for a reward like that to appear.
Green Copper Relic Gu could raise his cultivation by a minor realm at Rank 1. Needless to say this was quite valuable, worth several thousand primeval stones, and could save him several months of effort.
However, it was precisely because of such that he couldn't use it!
For the first year of his cultivating life, his aperture would be regularly examined. How would he explain how he had suddenly soared in his cultivation level?
Not to mention there was the problem of feeding this Gu. Relic Gu required primeval essence of the corresponding Rank to feed, so this was put a strain on his primeval essence the longer he didn't use it.
It was like being handed a very fancy car but being so busy that you couldn't actually drive it. Instead, it would just eat away at your wallet with maintenance costs.
Fang Yuan could not even sell it.
Just as he was bemoaning this, a notification popped up.
Gu worms given as rewards do not need to be fed unless they are taken out of the inventory. Once removed from inventory, however, they cannot be put back.
He raised an eyebrow slightly.
That was extremely convenient but...Google seaʀᴄh
How did that work? Oftentimes, the greatest limiting factor to the number of gu worms that one could have was the costs involved with feeding them.
Every gu worm ate something different, and the higher the rank, the harder it was to obtain those materials.
The only way that this 'system' could accomplish this was if it had some kind of Food path method. Fang Yuan, despite his plentiful experience, knew next to nothing when it came to the Food path.
Or alternatively, it 'created' the gu worms once they were taken out of his 'inventory.'
But that was something even harder to wrap his head around than some kind of Food path method existing.
The mysteries of this 'system' deepened in his mind, as well as to what it really wished to accomplish.
He was a B-grade talent in the eyes of his clansmen, though that was as of yet, a falsehood.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 - 7: Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance Part One
chapters.content:
As Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng walked back home, Fang Yuan contemplated the mysteries of this system.
As he thought of it- only one name came to mind as to who could be responsible for such.
Paradise Earth Immortal Venerable!
He had been a peaceful righteous path Gu Master, who was notable for his various formations. He did not strike out or kill his enemies, instead making it so that they could neither attack nor retreat until they gave up.
By contrast, the Venerable that came before him, Spectral Soul Demonic Venerable killed as easily as one would breathe. His reign had been marked by a loss of life on a massive scale- and it was partially because of this that Paradise Earth Immortal Venerable's reign was so cherished.
Paradise Earth Immortal Venerable had reformed countless demonic cultivators, he even had a Rank Eight Immortal Gu called 'Regret' using which he could use a move called 'Regret and Repent.'
He was a remarkable Gu Master when it came to gu formations, accomplishing things that could not be replicated even today.
It was this habit of his of 'reforming demonic cultivators' that made Fang Yuan think that he might be responsible for this system. After all, Rank 9 Gu Masters were peak existences that could accomplish much that was otherwise impossible.
These rewards and the like could be his doing.
Two new 'main mission's had popped up now.
Main Missions:
Inheritor
Description: Obtain your family's inheritance.
Rewards: ???
Flower Wine Monk
Description: Find the Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance
Rewards: ???ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
Both of these were things he intended to do anyway, so any reward on top was just icing on the cake.
It was clear that the system was using him, but from his experience- being used was not always a bad thing. After all, if one was being used, it implied that one had value in some way. In certain ways, a pawn could be more free than the king.
Of course, Fang Yuan would ultimately rely on no one but himself. While he was happy to reap the rewards of the system, it was clear that it had it sown ulterior motives. Not to mention, he needed to investigate it further.
Fang Zheng meanwhile, was lost in his own complicated feelings. He was now the rising star of the Gu Yue clan, though his brother wasn't far behind him.
Other people were finally noticing him as they walked down the street. For someone like him, it was a surreal experience. Something he didn't know how to deal with.
The next day, Fang Yuan skipped doing the daily quest. The system was rather angry with him it seemed due to this, constantly buzzing him with notifications, though he paid it no mind.
Ultimately, his 'counter' was reset and the reward for next day was diminished.
However, this was good- as he now knew what skipping a daily mission would mean.
The morning after the next one, there was a mortal woman wandering the streets of Gu Yue village early in the morning.
She was struggling to carry a load of firewood. Her body was not as robust as it had once been before, and now even this weight which was otherwise easy to carry in her early days felt like a heavy burden.
Yet, she had no choice but to carry this load every single day, no matter how much her body ached. One who did not work, did not eat- it was doubly so for mortals who could barely eke out their lives within Gu Yue village.
To say that mortals did not have a high standing was an understatement. They were slaves in all but name, as there was no where else they could go. The surrounding areas were dangerous and could only be explored by Rank 3 Gu Masters, usually traveling in groups. Were it not so, Fang Yuan would've set out this very day and not waited to stay within the confines of the village.
As such they had no choice but to endure the suffering of the world. This woman's husband and children had all died in the wolf tide several years back, and with no one to rely on, she had to make sure that her job, which was carrying firewood, was done on time.
Her employer would care naught for her plight; she was completely expendable, after all.
Just as she felt like her legs would not carry her any further despite how much she knew that she had to persevere for her own life's sake, she felt the load lighten greatly.
"Granny, let this one help you out," a voice filled with warmth and kindness reached her ears.
She should've protested, but was so exhausted that she couldn't in the moment. She simply enjoyed the respite from the heavy weight, and it was only after she had traveled twenty paces that she looked at the face of her benefactor.
She nearly recoiled in horror as she saw the darkness hidden deep within the young man's eyes. Those eyes... they could watch a trillion souls being snuffed out in an instant and not feel a shred of sympathy.
But, the darkness disappeared in an instant.
And also, how was it that his voice carried such warmth? How could his smile be so endearing?
No, she must've imagined the coldness in his eyes.
This young man was a Gu Master, it was clear from how he was dressed, and for someone like that to take pity upon her- he had to have a heart of gold!
"Take care," he said as they reached her destination. It had seemed so vast before, though with the load off of her shoulders, they made it in time.
"Bless you my child," the lady said, nearly brought to tears. "I don't know how to thank you..."
The man waved a hand. "It was my pleasure, there is no need for gratitude." His easygoing attitude made her even more certain that she had been wrong about him when it came to the first impression she had gotten of him.
Yes, this man carried the aura of a true hero! It was clear that her eyesight was beginning to fail her if she hadn't been able to see that immediately.
As Fang Yuan walked away, the daily quest was completed, and he saw a number of primeval stones added to his inventory.
The daily quest primeval stone reward, though nice, could not compare to the main and secret quest rewards. His aptitude was still at 46%, and he was most interested in things that could increase it. The Green Copper Relic Gu could somewhat hide his C-grade talent once he got a chance to use it by letting him leapfrog over a small realm - preferably when there was a break in the year and it would be easy to muddle things. Either that, or he would need time to find a plausible excuse as to how he had been able to find or afford it.
Barring any further increase in aptitude, what would really hasten his progress, however, would be the Liquor Worm, if he could find it.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 - 8: Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance Part Two
chapters.content:
The budding Gu Masters were supposed to spend a year at the village academy before they could graduate and go out into the world, ultimately taking missions for the clan.
"Humans are clever in over ten thousand ways, and gu are fragments of the great Dao. Gu Masters raise, nurture, and refine gu. All of you have awakened your apertures during the awakening ceremony, and now are Rank 1 Gu Masters," the academy elder said.
Someone raised their hand. An eager youngster, who was clearly bursting at the seams to ask a question. "Elder, I've heard that Gu Masters come in ranks up till 9, is that true?"
"Yes," the academy elder said. "Rank 1 to Rank 5 are mortal Gu Masters, while those Rank 6 and above are immortals. Unfortunately, even in the thousand year history of our clan, we haven't had a single Rank 6 or higher Gu Master, and only had two who were Rank 5. Those were the Gu Yue ancestor, and the fourth generation clan head." He had no idea that there was a former Rank 6 Gu Master sitting before him, in Fang Yuan who had reached that level before he had used the Spring Autumn Cicada.
Everyone was paying attention to him eagerly- that is to say, everyone except for Fang Yuan, who was currently drooling against a window.
The elder noticed this, and so did everyone else.
"Look, still sleeping."ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
"Honestly, you'd think he'd try to work harder if he's only B-grade."
"Can you really make up the difference between B-grade and A-grade with hard work?"
"Don't know, but you can at least try."
The academy elder frowned. Fang Yuan's potential was not as strong as that of Fang Zheng's, but that didn't mean that he was hopeless. He could easily become an elder, a pillar of the clan, and depending on how good his B-grade aptitude was, he might even reach Rank 4. That was what the academy elder felt, though if he was going to doze off like this he would accomplish nothing.
"He has been acting weird lately, hasn't he though?"
"I saw him hand over a entire primeval stone to a beggar yesterday?"
"No way- you're joking. An entire primeval stone?"
"I couldn't believe it either."
"Is he really that loaded? Or does he just not care about money?"
"It's not just that, he's also been buying lots of wine lately."
"Man, his aunt and uncle are going full throttle with supporting him, aren't they."
"Nah, last I heard he's broke!"
The academy elder had actually heard of the incident with the beggar- it raised a few eyebrows, and he had intended to have a word with Fang Yuan later.
As it was, he had no desire to interrupt his flow for Fang Yuan.
"Is it true that the fourth generation clan head was killed by the Flower Wine Demon?" one of the students asked, putting the conversation back on track.
"Of course," the academy elder said. There was hardly a soul who didn't know the story in the village, though with time, the story had been warped somewhat and turned into an urban legend, so he figured he would give them the way things went down so there was no confusion in the future. "The Flower Wine Monk was a demonic path cultivator who had come to the village several hundred years ago. He was a Rank Five cultivator, and ended up fighting with the fourth generation clan head. The clan head won, though in a moment of mercy let his guard down as he was about to let the Flower Wine Monk escape with his life- though the Flower Wine Monk used this opportunity to land a lethal blow upon the fourth generation clan head. Though the clan head got his revenge, he too passed away from his wounds tragically."
Because of this, the fourth generation clan head wasn't able to spread his oats and was one reason as to why it looked like the clan's blood was thinning over the years, as well as potential candidates to be Gu Masters.
Several curses rang out from the class against the Flower Wine Monk.
Fang Yuan had heard this story countless times of course, but he was thinking of something else.
In his previous life, he had heard a story which was told over and over again almost as much as this tale of the Flower Wine Monk.
A Rank 2 Gu Master, dejected after a breakup, had gone drinking in the area around the village. He had managed to attract a Liquor Worm, which he followed and was able to capture- a Liquor Worm which had been left behind by the Flower Wine Monk!
Gu had no natural lifespans, and could persist so long as they were fed.
The Liquor Worm was quite useful for cultivation, though only at the Rank 1 level.
He was Rank 2, but he turned over the Liquor Worm to the village, was handsomely rewarded, and was able to advance to Rank 3, become an elder, and patch things up with his lover.
It was this inheritance that Fang Yuan was after right now, and also what the system wanted to egg him on to get. However, regardless, Fang Yuan was determined to find it- which is why he had spent a large amount of money on wine and gone drinking around the outskirts of the village at night, hoping to attract it, though he had no luck up till now.
Gu were like Pokemon for cultivating, and just like with Pokemon, the choice of your starter was an important one.
A Gu Master's vital gu was a gu that was attached to their own lifespan, and was important when it came to their future development.
The Liquor Worm, though not ideal as a vital gu candidate, was still much better than his other options.
Though, a new 'secret quest' had also popped up.
The Ideal Vital Gu
Description: ???
Reward: ???
It seemed to imply that there was a 'best option' for Fang Yuan when it came to his vital gu, though he couldn't see how it would be any different from the Liquor Worm. Unless the system wanted to reward him doubly for the same thing?
"Alright," the academy elder said. "We're going to take you all to get your first gu worm today, and later on I'll explain how to cultivate and advance when it comes to ranks."

chapters.title: Chapter 9 - 9: Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance Part Three
chapters.content:
They were led to a separate room where many gu worms were stored.
Gu came in all shapes and sizes, though most of them took the appearance of insects. The clan nourished all of the gu worms inside, the costs to feed which were paid for by primeval stones obtained from the spirit spring. This was a huge burden upon the clan's finances, which is why Fang Yuan had been very shocked to learn that gu in his inventory didn't need to be fed.
The only gu worm he had currently was the Green Copper Relic Gu, which was a gu that could only be used once. It was a terrible choice for a vital gu, despite its other uses, which is why
"Go ahead, each of you can take a single Rank 1 gu worm," the academy elder said.
Gu, just like Gu Masters, came in ranks from 1 to 9. For best effect, the rank of Gu Master and gu had to match, if one used a gu of weaker rank than oneself, it was akin to fighting with rubber gloves. If one used one of higher rank, it was like trying to use a Pokemon which you didn't have enough badges to control.
The vital gu would great affect his development, and if he couldn't get the Liquor Worm, he would have to settle for something from here.
"Moonlight Gu..."
It was the signature gu of their clan, and about eighty percent of the class would choose this gu worm. Seeing nothing better in sight, Fang Yuan resolved himself to take this.
A message popped up as he left.
New Main Quest!
Refining The Moonlight Gu
Description: Be the first to refine the Moonlight Gu and win the contest!
Reward: ???
The academy elder had already promised 20 primeval stones to whoever was the first to refine a gu worm, though Fang Yuan had little hope in succeeding. Others might think that he would be able to, but that was because he was disguised as a B-grade talent who was second only the Fang Zheng. They though that he might be able to get lucky, though Fang Yuan knew that he actually had no chance of succeeding.
'What's important right now is the Liquor Worm...' he thought to himself. That was worth more than whatever reward he would get like this.
As he was about to leave though, he was stopped by the academy elder. "Fang Yuan, I wanted to have a word with you."
"Ah, sorry about sleeping in class, I was so eager to start today that I couldn't sleep last night ehehe..." Fang Yuan said, sheepishly rubbing the back of his neck.
"It's not about that," the elder said. "It's about the beggar you ended up giving a primeval stone too a few days back."
"Right, there was that..."Follow current novels on novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"I wanted to tell you that it's a waste of your time and resources," the elder said. "That beggar was a mere mortal, and that stone would've been spent better in helping you cultivate."
"I understand," Fang Yuan said. There was something oddly... robotic about the way he replied. The academy elder had thought that Fang Yuan would protest, but he seemed to already recognize the futility of his actions.
Or did he? The academy elder decided to deal the killing blow. "Do you know what happened after you gave him the primeval stone, Fang Yuan? Your action was noticed by a few Gu Masters, one of whom snatched it away from the beggar after giving him a good beating."
The beggar, of course, was a mortal and had no status in the village hierarchy. Many Gu Masters struggled with finances, and a single stone was still valuable for someone at Rank 1 or Rank 2.
The Gu Master who took it might have even justified his actions saying that he was doing the beggar a favor, after all, all he did was beat the mortal up- if it was someone else, they might've opted to kill him to get that stone instead, after all.
Forget Gu Masters, if mortals had seen the beggar with a stone, they too would have conspired to rob him. Either way, the beggar would've ended up worse off thanks to Fang Yuan's 'gift.'
The academy elder was explaining this to Fang Yuan to get him to understand that while kindness had its place, it should be directed at the proper people.
He expected Fang Yuan to either protest and look horrified, but Fang Yuan's expression was unchanged. "I knew that was going to happen," was his reply.
The academy elder was lost for words.
What did he mean by that?
Why hand over the stone in the first place if he knew no good would come of it?
Was this some sort of strange sadistic joke that Fang Yuan had played?
"Oh... I see..." the academy elder finally got those words out, the lecture he had prepared beforehand now lost.
Fang Yuan left, leaving the elder mystified. Fang Yuan's actions now were incongruous with what he had done earlier.
Mortals were lower than even the dogs in many ways within the villages of Gu Masters. Perhaps someone like Paradise Earth Immortal Venerable could make a society where they were treated with respect, but that was a massive exception.
Still, humans were humans and empathy was part and parcel of such. It was not abnormal for a young boy like Fang Yuan to take pity upon someone suffering and offering them some money.
The academy elder had wanted to explain to Fang Yuan that while kindness and charity had its place, such aid was best directed at the clan members, not mortals.
Fang Yuan was a B-grade talent after all, a future elder of the village. It was important to impart the value of family ties within him.
But, Fang Yuan had been completely unfazed by learning of what had happened to the beggar. Shouldn't he feel some guilt at what happened to the mortal?
It seemed to be too elaborate for a simple prank as well, and as such, the academy elder could not wrap his head around it.
How could he know that Fang Yuan had earned a net profit of four primeval stones from that transaction through the system? Whatever happened afterwards was of no concern to Fang Yuan.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 - 10: Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance Part Four
chapters.content:
Back home, his aunt and uncle were already scheming.
"Both of you have taken the first steps on your journey to become Gu Masters," Uncle said. "Here is a gift from us, six primeval stones for each of you. Use them wisely in your cultivation journeys."
"Thank you!" Fang Zheng said, nearly starry-eyed at this complete one-eighty in treatment from them.
Fang Yuan took the stones, though he had a blank expression. He already had a small fortune accumulated, but it was good to have some explanation in case anyone asked him where he was getting the stones from.
Aunt was teary-eyed. "To think that the two of you grew up so quickly... it's almost as if... you were just like our children all along."
"We don't have our own children, so we always treated you like you were our own," Uncle said, lying flawlessly.
Fang Zheng actually seemed to fall for their crocodile tears- though Fang Yuan couldn't entirely blame him. He too, had almost fallen for them in his past life.
"Why pretend though?" Aunt asked suddenly. "We were thinking of adopting the two of you for real?"
"Yes!" Fang Zheng said excitedly. He had always wanted a family, and though he had Fang Yuan- his elder brother could not make up for a parent's love.
Fang Yuan saw through their scheme immediatley.
Right now, the two of them were basically treated as minors until they graduate from the academy. Their parent's 'inheritance' so to speak were being taken care of by their guardians- Aunt and Uncle. If however, they agreed to this adoption before they came of age, then their parent's inheritance would pass on to Aunt and Uncle.
"Allow me to pass," Fang Yuan said with a slight smile.
"Brother-" Fang Zheng said, shocked, though Uncle waved him down.
"I understand," Uncle said, seemingly unmoved by Fang Yuan's decision. "In such a case, it may be better to strike out on your own- take 200 primeval stones and be on your way then. Consider a gift when it comes to starting your own family."
Fang Zheng's eyes nearly popped out of his head when he saw the amount, though again, Fang Yuan was unfazed as he shook his head.
"I will take your leave then," Fang Yuan said, cupping his hands before departing to try to refine the Moonlight Gu.
"Right, I won't let you down either!" Fang Zheng said, cheering as he too went to his room.
Once the two were out of sight Aunt and Uncle's faces darkened.
"Fang Yuan is too smart for his own good..." Aunt muttered. "What if he turns against us and tries to snatch the inheritance?"
Uncle stroked his chin. It was indeed a problem, given that Fang Yuan was a B-grade talent. Once he got to Rank 2, he would be able to contest them for the inheritance after graduating. There was nothing they could really do regarding such, after all, being B-grade, he could eventually reach Rank Two with or without resources.
"Simple, we frame him and then kick him out!" Uncle said, plotting out things in his mind. If Fang Yuan wasn't going to play along, they would just find an excuse to get rid of him.
While it was risky to offend a B-grade talent, they had an A-grade one on their side.
While Fang Yuan could not be ignored, he would still be greatly suppressed without access to resources.
Of course, neither of them knew that Fang Yuan only had 46% aptitude right now- nor the fact that he was not lacking in resources.
After having no further luck with obtaining the Liquor Worm, he decided to attempt to refine the Moonlight Gu.
His mind reached into his aperture as he held it in his hand.
In order to refine it, he needed to inject it with his primeval essence, which began to move from his aperture and into the Moonlight Gu.
Naturally, being a living creature, it had a will of its own and began resisting. But this was only to be expected. As the primeval essence entered the Moonlight Gu, he could feel it resisting, though slowly but surely, part of it was subjugated under his will.
Sweat began to coat Fang Yuan's face as his primeval essence was nearly exhausted, though it looked like had only made about 8% in terms of progress.
He now had two choices: one was to use his primeval stones to recover the primeval essence, and the other was to wait for it to recover naturally.
The problem was that with time, the Moonlight Gu would write away some of his progress. In other words, just like with cultivating, one couldn't chip away at it over time. The rate that one could muster was also very important.
That was why he knew that he had no chance of actually winning the competition to be the first one to refine it. Those with talent had a clear advantage here, though if Mo Bei or Chi Lian were liberal with their primeval stone spending they could potentially break past him.
Fang Yuan wasn't even a real B-grade talent, and though he had a large amount of primeval stones, he would end up spending more than twenty to refine this worm.
That wasn't even what his ultimate goal was, which was to get the Liquor Worm. He would rather spend time and resources on that than this.
There was a third option- he could use the Green Copper Relic Gu and advance by a minor realm. That would not increase the amount of primeval essence he had, but with each minor realm, the quality of the primeval essence would double.
In other words, if Fang Yuan used the Green Copper Relic Gu, he would go from Rank 1 initial stage to Rank 1 middle stage. Ranks 1 through 5 were subdivided into four minor realms: initial, middle, upper and peak.
If he became a Rank 1 middle stage Gu Master, the quality of his primeval essence would double that of what it was at the initial stage. Meaning that his 46% primeval essence would functionally act equivalent to what 92% would be at initial stage, surpassing even Fang Zheng!

chapters.title: Chapter 11 - 11: Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance Part Five
chapters.content:
Using the Copper Green Relic Gu also did not have any major drawbacks, as it would hasten his progress in his cultivation which he wanted to do anyway. Granted, it was more efficient to wait until he was at the upper minor realm so that it would have the largest effect.
It was possible that the 'system' would give him another Copper Green Relic Gu at some point down the line, but there was no guarantee of that.
Still, it was not too much of a massive loss to use it now.
The issue was, once again, that he could not explain how he had done so if anyone were to ask how he had suddenly advanced by a massive leap overnight! Although they thought he had B-grade talent, he could not greatly overshadow Fang Zheng.
Copper Green Relic Gu were so rare that none were sold in Gu Yue village. How would he explain where he got it from? It would put him under intense scrutiny. He could also not hide his cultivation as his aperture would be regularly examined by the academy elder during this first year.
People would not assume he had a 'system' they would think that he had found an inheritance and would be extremely eager to find out where that inheritance was. They would not believe Fang Yuan about this 'system' even if he told them so.
For that matter, the Liquor Worm accomplished something similar to the Green Copper Relic Gu. It could raise the quality of one's primeval essence by a minor realm. The difference was that the Liquor Worm's effect did not change one's actual cultivation level, and it had to be fed and nourished while using so.
This would normally be two drawbacks, but they were actually beneficial to Fang Yuan in this situation. Once he went up a minor realm, the walls of his aperture would also change, which is something that he could not hide, though if he had the Liquor Worm, all he had to do was not use it before his aperture was examined. Not only that, its effect could be turned 'off' at crucial moments.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
As he pondered this issue, he was interrupted by a knock at the door.
Shen Cui's voice floated inside. "Young Master, I have brought something for you."
"Come in."
Shen Cui had changed in a flowing diaphanous pink nightgown and had put on dark scarlet lipstick. She was carrying a tray with wine and dinner on it, and a sweet fragrance accompanied her. She was dolled up like she was ready for her honeymoon night.
'So they've chosen to act much faster this time,' Fang Yuan thought. The fact that he was considered a B-grade talent in this timeline likely forced his Uncle to act swifter and with more fierceness this time.
Shen Cui put the tray on the table, but did not leave, instead sidling up to Fang Yuan. The smell of her perfume- crushed pine needles and jasmine tea, was even more prominent.
"Young Master Fang Yuan," Shen Cui whispered. "I know that your heart is dejected, being only B-grade talent compared to your brother's A-grade... I've seen you wandering out at night drinking your worries away. But as for me..." she said as she poured him a glass, "...I do not care for your talent, Young Master, this servant only wishes to accompany you. Allow me to give my body to you tonight..."
She froze for a second. There was something... extremely frosty about Fang Yuan's expression, but as he turned away, her confidence came back.
After all, he was still just a young hormonal teenage boy. How could he possibly resist-
Before she could finish that thought and stroke his face, a hand had emerged and gripped onto her throat.
Within an instant, she was asphyxiating.
"Young Master you..."
He turned to her, a dark expression on her face. "So Aunt and Uncle decided to make this kind of a play... not bad, if I say so myself." With one hand he continued to choke her, and with the other hand he reached down her gown and twisted her bosom.
"Please stop-" she barely managed to choke out. The cold aura he was emanating cut off any thought she had of fighting back- she didn't doubt for an instant that he would crush her throat if given the chance.
Since when had he become like this? She had watched Fang Yuan closely for many years,
"Did you think those two useless lumps of flesh could entice me?" he asked her. "I should kill you, but tell you what... in view of your years of service, I'll let you off so long as you get out of my sight immediately."
The moment he let go, Shen Cui left without making another sound.
Those eyes... those pools of darkness would haunt her dreams!
Secret mission complete!
If She Breathes, She's A Thot I

Reward: Cultivation Blessing: Gu Upgrade [Mortal]
Gu Upgrade [Mortal] can increase the rank of any mortal Gu by one rank without need of expending any primeval stones or refinement materials. The upgraded Gu is random.
'Interesting power,' Fang Yuan thought. His first thought was to use it on the Green Copper Relic Gu- it had only one path of advancement and would then become a Red Steel Relic Gu which could raise his cultivation by a minor realm at Rank Two. That was more valuable than the Green Copper Relic Gu, especially given the fact that he had other methods to get to Rank One peak stage right now if he got the Liquor Worm or was able to raise his aptitude high enough.
However, it was apparent that it was too dangerous to stay here for now. Shen Cui had left without making a fuss, and while the people waiting outside to frame him for assault were no doubt frustrated right now, it would not stop them from trying something else.
It would be best to stay in the village inn for now.
Although it was late, the innkeeper gave no trouble to Fang Yuan on account of him being a Gu Master as he walked in, purchased some more wine, and headed out to see if he could encounter the Liquor Worm.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 - 12: Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance: Part Six
chapters.content:
Although Fang Yuan had no reason to go looking for trouble and would've loved to keep a low profile, trouble came looking for him the next day in the form of his younger brother.
"Brother!" Fang Zheng exclaimed, spotting Fang Yuan nonchalantly eating lunch in the inn the next day. "I saw Shen Cui run out of your room in tears last night. What did you do to her?"
Fang Yuan did not respond and continued eating, like Fang Zheng was far below his notice.
Fang Zheng was frustrated, but continued. "You even left the house without explaining anything last night! Aunt and Uncle are worried about you! And here you are, eating lunch whithout a care for what they think!"ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
Fang Yuan kept chewing, still taking no notice of Fang Zheng whatsoever.
Fang Zheng was flustered now. Up till this moment, he had been living in his brother's shadow, but now, the roles were reversed- he was the main character, and his brother the NPC!
At least, that was how it felt. While walking along the road, people no longer referred to him as 'Fang Yuan's little brother.' He was Fang Zheng!
And yet, despite escaping into what seemed like the light, he was still standing here, stupefied, under his elder brother's shadow.
"Just because you turned out to be a B-grade talent instead of A-grade like me," Fang Zheng said, continuing, "doesn't mean you take your frustration out on Shen Cui. What did she ever do to you? Our talents are a result of fate, not because of-"
SLAP!
Fang Zheng did not get a single word in further as Fang Yuan got up and smacked him across the face.
Fang Zheng was stunned. He had been beaten by Aunt and Uncle many times before, even by the other children, but never by his elder brother. "Brother, you've never put a hand upon me and yet now-"
SLAP!
Fang Yuan struck him again. "Worthless idiot! Just a few days in the limelight and you've already forgotten who stood with you when you were at your lowest? When our parents passed away, who did his best to wipe away your tears? When you wanted new robes at New Year's, who gave you his set? When the bullies used to beat you, who took revenge for you? Whenever you wanted an extra serving of porridge, who was the one who gave up his own portion for your happiness? If I were to recount the other things, we'd be here until next week, but forget about all that. What I mean to say is that you would dare take the side of a lowly servant over that of your own brother, the only one who supported you back when you were considered worthless? Did I ever lord the fact that I was a so-called 'genius' over you? And yet when the shoe is on the other foot, I see that you could not be any faster to use my shoulder blades as a scabbard!"
Fang Zheng opened his mouth to respond, but could not. After all, whatever Fang Yuan had said was true.
"On top of that, you've not only betrayed me, but betrayed our parent's legacy as well!" Fang Yuan said, not relenting in his attack upon Fang Zheng whatsoever. "You changed sides and allowed Aunt and Uncle to adopt you- forgetting their years of abuse after some honeyed words? You know why Shen Cui is after you, no? Simply because of your talent, and yet you've deluded yourself into thinking that she gives so much as a damn about you!"
"Brother, how could you say that about our parents. I... I've always wanted a family and-"
"And yet you've turned against and abandoned me, the only real family you had left?!" Fang Yuan barked, not letting up for even a moment. He then sneered. "Let's not beat around the bush here, there's only one reason that you're here isn't it, to see if something happened between Shen Cui and I? Don't worry, she's still a virgin, tell you what- you can have her if you give me the six primeval stones that Aunt and Uncle gave you."
"Wha-I-" Fang Zheng began to say, but he could not make any kind of retort. After all, what Fang Yuan had just said was true.
"Let's not pretend that you have any semblance of self-respect left," Fang Yuan said coldly. "I'm willing to make a transaction, aren't I? Do you agree or not?"
"I uh- alright," Fang Zheng said, fumbling with his pockets as he took out five and a half stones. "I uh, used half of one up to refine my gu worm. This is all I have."
Fang Yuan glanced at the stones, realizing that Fang Zheng was telling the truth. If it were someone else, he might've suspected that they were hiding something, but at this point the only thing that Fang Zheng was thinking with was his cock, so this really was probably all that he had.
"Alright then, go!" Fang Yuan said after swiping the stones in a swift motion. "From now on, forget the fact that we were ever family!"
Fang Zheng left, cheeks burning, though he was feeling quite happy indeed, not only at the fact that Shen Cui was still untouched, but that she was now his.
This only lasted until he got home though and told Aunt and Uncle what happened.
"What!?" Uncle exclaimed. "He did that to you?"
"Why- what's wrong?"
"Fang Zheng, don't you know, Shen Cui was not his personal servant- she was assigned by us. He had no right to 'trade' her to you, if you wanted her, you should've just asked!"
Fang Zheng realized that Fang Yuan had just finessed him and felt extremely dumb about it.
"Ah, whatever, relax," Uncle said, sighing. "It can't be helped- here's another six stones to help with your refinement. As for Shen Cui, she's yours now. Make sure that you work hard."
"I-uh, yes! I will make you both proud, Mother, Father," Fang Zheng said as he ran to his room.
Both of them had dark expressions on their faces.
"Fang Yuan is too crafty," Uncle said. "He saw right through our scheme... tch!"
"What do we do now?"
"What can we do, woman? Give it time, we need to think of something," Uncle said, frowning. It was not easy to restrict Fang Yuan if he gave it his all to get the inheritance.
After all, both of them still thought of Fang Yuan as a B-grade talent.

chapters.title: Chapter 13 - 13: Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance: Part Seven
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan felt mixed emotions within his heart.
For one, he was happy to have gotten the five and a half stones, but there was a surprising bitterness within himself.
He had thought that he no longer cared for Fang Zheng, and after what Fang Zheng had originally done in his prior life, there was no reason to care in this one either.
And yet, why was he so angry?
That speech hadn't just been performative, he had felt genuine anger rising up within himself.
He sighed.
In the end, no matter how much he pretended otherwise, he could not completely repress his emotions. It had been another matter entirely when this had all been five hundred years in the rearview mirror and he had been a demonic overlord, but now, when he was back as young Fang Yuan, it looked like he was not as over his feelings as he'd once thought.
In his last life, he had been seen as only C-grade, his actual aptitude, and had been shunned by the clan as a result. It was not just that, Fang Zheng had completely turned on him at the time, until he had had no choice but to leave the village.
The betrayal stung his heart for a long time, though he had eventually forgotten about it- or so he'd thought. Traveling back in time had reopened some of the old wounds.
It did not change one thing that he had realized with experience- the world did not care for his feelings or for his emotions. So there was no point dwelling on them.

Desc-
"Oh shut your retarded mouth," Fang Yuan muttered, not even bothering to read the rest of the notification.
Behind him, the mortal waiter had no idea why he was suddenly being insulted by Fang Yuan, especially given the fact that he hadn't said anything.
Fang Yuan left to try to refine the Moonlight Gu, though once again, he was making frustratingly little progress unless he used his primeval stones.
That evening, he was eating and weighing his options. Should he give up on the Liquor Worm entirely?
He was fond of taking risks if they could pay off, but he was also not a compulsive gambler.
He knew when to cut his losses. Granted, there was an 'unknown' factor in the equation, namely, what the reward from the system would be, but he could not account for that.
'One more night... I think I should give it one more night...' he thought to himself.
At a nearby table, there was a loud bunch of customers. They were mortal hunters. Hunters were quite strong, though not as strong as Gu Masters, of course, but they could earn relatively well by hunting big prey such as boars. This was dangerous, but risk and reward nearly always walked together. That was why they were so loud as they were celebrating returning from a successful hunt.
"Excellent work, to think that you took down that black boar all by yourself," one of them said.
"Brother Feng, you're not drinking?"
"I'm sorry, I can't drink anymore."
"Ah, is the alcohol not up to your standards? Waiter, bring us some good wine, not this cheap stuff!"
"Ah, sirs, we do have good wine," the waiter said. "But it is a tad bit expensive..."
"What?! You think we can't pay up?" The hunters glared at the waiter, and a normal person might've wilted under their gazes, though this waiter was firm.
"A single jar costs 2 primeval stones," the waiter said.
The hunter's expressions immediately changed. 2 stones could feed a family for a few weeks. While they did earn more being hunters, it was not on par with the earnings of Gu Masters.
"You're not lying, are you? Is there really such expensive wine?"
"I wouldn't dare, our green bamboo wine is among the finest in the whole village," the waiter said.
Fang Yuan knew the waiter wasn't lying, as he had been buying high-quality wine in large amounts to try to entice the Liquor Worm to show up, though without success.
"Brothers, let's forget about it, I don't feel like drinking anymore as it is..."
Basically, the hunters, despite their early bravado, could only say 'eh, those grapes are probably sour anyway' after hearing the price.

Fang Yuan only had to read the quest description to realize what it wanted to say.
It was a bit of a risk, but he had no shortage of primeval stones recently, and if he could use this opportunity to probe the system.

Within moments, the waiter had brought Fang Yuan two jars, and then walked over to the hunter's table. "Sirs, here is three jars of green bamboo wine."
