"I was hanging outside with my crew,
When we decided to refine some Gu,
We worked when the sun was up,
And when it was night too."
Fang Yuan stared at the poem for two seconds before ripping it up right in front of Fang Zheng's face.
"You know, it's good that you never volunteered to recite anything back when we were younger," Fang Yuan said. "The crowd might've beaten you to death as punishment if they had to hear something like that. Tell you what, since you seem so hot-headed, I think you should take three laps around the academy to cool your head down."
Fang Zheng grit his teeth. For one, he was constantly being outshone by Fang Yuan, even now. And to have his work humiliated right in front of his face! And in front of the entire class!
But he could do nothing but curse as he went outside to start running.
The academy elder walked in. He had heard everything, though pretended not to notice.
He was perturbed by Fang Yuan's actions against an A-grade talent, but at the same time, couldn't tell Fang Yuan off. Fang Zheng, had, in badmouthing Fang Yuan, also badmouthed not only him but the clan head in a way as well! He would have to talk to Fang Zheng later. The punishment, having him run three laps, was more than adequate in his opinion though. It cemented Fang Yuan's authority, while also not causing any major problems for Fang Zheng.
Chatter was already echoing regarding what had happened.
"Wow, the relationship between those two brothers is really bad..."
"I thought twins were supposed to be close..."
"Yeah, I heard that twins could not only read each other's minds but also finish each other sentences!"
"I heard that if you hurt a twin, the other one feels pain too!"
"Yeah, but those too are nothing like that..."
The academy elder told Fang Zheng off later, in private, and the boy understood that he had crossed a line.
Over the next few days, the academy elder watched as the students began to slowly segregate themselves into groups.
There was Mo Bei's faction and Chi Chen's faction; these were students whose families were also aligned with them.
Then there was Fang Zheng's faction, mainly composed of students who backed the clan head.
These 'factions' were more of cliques at this point, and were rather amorphous and students went in and out of them, not being fixed- though these were the seeds of the future political groups in Gu Yue village.
As the year progressed, the factions would become more solidified as students realized who they wanted to support.
These usually emerged towards the latter half of the year, but there was a reason why they were forming sooner.
Normally, a class would have at most one or two B-grade talents. This time though, there were three B-grade talents and an A-grade, all of whom had the potential to be great leaders in the clan! The competition was fiercer this year, and it had precipitated in this hastened self-segregation into groups.
There was a problem though, which was greatly bothering the academy elder.
Why was there no Fang Yuan faction?
At first, he thought it was because Fang Yuan was the least illustrious of the four candidates. He was a B-grade talent unlike Fang Zheng's A-grade talent, and did not have the backing that Chi Chen and Mo Bei had.
But, he realized there was a different reason for the same.
It was that Fang Yuan was rejecting anyone who wanted to come under him to form a faction!
It was as if he were oil and the clan's social system was water. He refused to mix it at every opportunity. Even though he was class president, it was as if he had only dipped his toe in the water.
People would naturally not follow a leader like that!
That disturbed him more than anything else - it was odd. There had been students who had caused problems in the past, though Fang Yuan was not one of them.
And yet, he irritated the academy elder in a way no one else had done.
Who could live alone? Everyone needed the clan's help to survive in the future.
These actions of Fang Yuan also contrasted with his rumored generous nature that he had heard of from some of the villagers. Why was he so warm and helpful at some times, and so cold and distant at others?
The academy elder could not wrap his head around it.
Maybe, with enough time, Fang Yuan would slowly dissolve into the clan's social system. There was still much of the academic year left, after all.
And on that note, he had a flash of inspiration.

chapters.title: Chapter 49 - 49: Classroom Politics: Part Five
chapters.content:
Unbeknownst to the academy elder, and also to Fang Yuan for that matter, there was indeed a fourth pro-Fang Yuan faction among the student body, regardless of how small it was.
"Thanks for joining," Li Mei said to Yu Sai after he agreed to join her in her movement to support Fang Yuan. "With you joining us, our numbers have doubled!"
"Wait- are you telling me that before I joined, you were the only member?"The source of this content ɪs NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
"Yup, but now are numbers have doubled."
"You can't count that as doubling- we went from having one person to having two people."
"But that's literally what it means to double. One times two is two, just like eight times eight is eighty-eight."
"Eight times eight is not eighty-eight!"
"Sorry, I'm bad with Maths. But honestly I don't know why it isn't- it just makes sense for eight and eight to make eighty-eight, you know?"
Yu Sai sighed. "Okay, maybe this is a number you can wrap your head around. Both of us have only 20% aptitude, meaning that we both have about a zero percent chance of doing anything remotely worthy of noticing."
Li Mei's face fell. Inwardly, she knew that what Yu Sai was saying was the truth, she just wished that he wouldn't frame it so. "Maybe... but who knows? We're both Fang Yuan's first supporters, right? Maybe that will mean that we will get noticed?"
"Does he even know that we exist?"
"About that uh... I don't think so. But hey, you joined, so now we have two people! This is just the beginning!"
"Hey, I only joined because I felt sorry for you being on your own..." Yu Sai said.
"The other groups didn't want you, did they?"
"No! Well, maybe kinda..."
As the two of them were busy doing nothing of value, Fang Yuan spent his time cultivating.
Before leaving for class that day, as was his daily ritual, Fang Yuan examined the mysterious Rank 3 gu worm that he'd gotten. It still looked as healthy as ever, despite him not feeding it anything.
He continued to keep it mostly hidden for now. Even if no one knew what it would do, the mere fact that it was Rank 3 would be more than enough to entice many a thief, especially as he himself was not Rank 3.
"Alright everyone," the martial arts instructor said later that day during lessons. He had been trying to encourage everyone to start paying more attention to martial arts and the like, but his efforts had fallen on deaf ears. He now tried a new approach. "I'll be hosting a martial arts tournament! Winner gets forty primeval stones!"
That got some of the students talking.
Most of them had no chance at winning at the usual contests because of their aptitudes- but what did that matter when it came to fighting? They were all on a more even playing field when it came to hand-to-hand combat, and forty primeval stones was not a small amount.
It was not insignificant even to someone like Fang Yuan.
"Alright, who's up first?" the martial arts instructor asked two days later when the contest actually began.
Fang Yuan stepped forward without hesitation.
"Good! As expected of our class president, being a great inspiration to the others," the martial arts instructor nodded in approval.
The others were a bit more hesitant, but soon enough, Mo Bei stepped up, cracking his knuckles.
'Fang Yuan, I'm going to repay you for all the misery and humiliation you've caused me until now!' he thought to himself.
This was wonderful- perfect even. This was one of the ways that he could get back at Fang Yuan and not get in trouble for it. After all, the academy did not exist to nurture weaklings. It existed to make the students stronger, and fights to some extent were encouraged. This was not even a brawl, but an official fight, so it was even more in line with things. Mo Bei couldn't just throw hands with Fang Yuan normally given he had a reputation to uphold, but this was completely within societal norms.
That is to say, it would not be a problem at all if Mo Bei punched Fang Yuan right in the face! Who wouldn't want to do that- to be able to beat up your boss who often gave you unpaid overtime, whom you deeply hated without suffering any consequences?
Of course, lethal blows were forbidden, but Mo Bei wouldn't have been able to kill someone anyway. He had not tempered his heart enough, and was not like Fang Yuan in that aspect.
Everyone watching felt that Mo Bei absolutely had an advantage over Fang Yuan and was likely going to win. After all, Mo Bei stood a head taller than Fang Yuan and likely weighed at least ten kilograms more. His body was more toned and tempered, while Fang Yuan was standing there with what looked like noodle arms.
Neither of them had much time to practice, so things like weight class and build overall were of great importance.
No one had high hopes for Fang Yuan.
"Hehe... let's see Fang Yuan cough up blood and beg for mercy!"
"Heh, Mo Bei's gonna beat him so bad he's going to end up crying for his mother!"
"Oh wait- he doesn't have one!"
The supporters of the Mo faction began laughing loudly, though they quieted down at the glares they got from Fang Zheng's faction.
After all, although the Fang Zheng faction had beef with Fang Yuan more than anyone, insulting Fang Yuan for being an orphan was basically doing the same to Fang Zheng!
"Do you think that Fang Yuan's going to get hurt?" Li Mei asked Yu Sai worriedly.
"I'd estimate his chances of winning at being less than ten percent," Yu Sai said.
The martial arts instructor did nothing to stop the fight, as this is precisely what he and the academy wanted- competition!
'Fang Yuan, I'm going to plant my fist firmly in your face!' Mo Bei said. He still didn't say something like that out loud, he had to maintain some sense of decorum after all, but he was fuming inside as the martial arts instructor said that it was time for the round to start.
Mo Bei rushed forward without hesitation, intending to use his larger frame and momentum to earn a decisive victory against Fang Yuan.
Two moves later, he was lying down on the floor, unconscious.
....
"What the hell just happened!?" someone from the crowd finally yelled out, breaking the awkward silence.
To their eyes, it seemed as if Fang Yuan had just moved and in the next instant, Mo Bei was lying down on the floor. The only person who had clearly seen what had happened was the martial arts instructor - the students did not have enough experience to gauge what was going on, and were distracted by other things.
The martial arts instructor, though, saw things clearly. He saw as Fang Yuan used Mo Bei's momentum against him, sidestepping and tripping him before striking fluidly at a pressure point, knocking Mo Bei out. It was so fast to the students it looked like it was instantaneous.
"Oh no, Fang Yuan killed Mo Bei!" someone yelled out, who couldn't see that Mo Bei's chest was still rising.
"Relax, he's only unconscious," Fang Yuan said. "I wouldn't kill him- not when I need him to stand outside my room this evening to deal with things while I cultivate."

chapters.title: Chapter 50 - 50: Classroom Politics: Part Six
chapters.content:
The students couldn't fully wrap their heads around what had happened.
It was not so unbelievable to see that Fang Yuan had won- many of them would be disappointed by that kind of news, but it was digestible.
What was unbelievable was that Fang Yuan had won so swiftly and handily, to the point where many of them hadn't seen it happen. If Fang Yuan had won, they felt, it would've been after an intense period of fighting.
The guards came to drag Mo Bei away to a healer, after which he would presumably recover quickly, but an awkward silence now precipitated on the student body.
"What was that? I wanted a real fight, but Mo Bei only lasted a few seconds..." someone from the Chi faction said.
"Hey, he still lasted longer than I did with your mother last night," someone from the Mo faction retorted.
The two nearly got into a fistfight before the martial arts instructor barked, "If you want to fight so badly, do it in the ring!"
The awkwardness continued after that.
It lasted for nearly a minute before another challenger stepped up.
"Fang Yuan," Chi Chen said, as he walked into the ring. "Mo Bei might've been overconfident, and you took advantage of that and got a lucky hit in. But there's no way that your luck's going to sustain you for another round!"
As he said that, the students began to let out sighs of relief.
Of course- Fang Yuan was only able to beat Mo Bei because he had gotten a lucky strike in. Mo Bei might've even been too eager and tripped while fighting Fang Yuan or something along those lines. Fang Yuan then used that to his advantage and won.
That was far easier for them to process than the fact that Fang Yuan had won through an immense talent in martial arts. After all, they had all basically started training at the same time. Even if Fang Yuan had received better instruction or started earlier secretly somehow, how could he possibly dominate someone like Mo Bei so easily?
'They're wrong,' the martial arts instruct thought. 'That was no fluke. I saw it- that boy must be a naturally-gifted martial artist! To think that he's so good with hand-to-hand combat and a B-grade talent to boot! But it's not just raw talent, where did he learn to fight like that? And who trained him? Even if I had started training earlier, I wouldn't be able to equal his technique.'
Despite all of this, he said nothing aloud. The other students would just have to learn the hard way.
For that matter, Chi Chen wasn't entirely sure of what he was saying either. The truth was that he did have sour grapes from not getting the vice-presidential position. Sure, it meant that he might pull ahead of Mo Bei and maybe even Fang Zheng with the next contest, but it did not bode well for his future prospects. It meant that once they were out of the academy, he would be unable to keep up.
But that was the future, and there would be no future if there was no present. And for that matter, while Chi Chen losing the contest to be vice-president could be seen as being a sort of victory, it did not look that way to outsiders. It instead looked like the Chi clan was lagging behind, which is something that he could not tolerate.
Basically, he needed a W really bad, and given his C-grade talent, he felt that this was the best opportunity to do so. Him saying that Fang Yuan just got lucky with a fluke was more of his own internal hype, which just so happened to motivate the other students who agreed with him.
Was Fang Yuan really just lucky? He didn't know for sure, but he had to try to one-up Mo Bei in some way.
"Argh!" he said as he launched himself at Fang Yuan, being careful not to trip or make any kind of mistake like Mo Bei likely had. To this degree he played defensively, though it only took Fang Yuan a few breaths of time to circumvent his defenses and knock him out cold too.
The earlier bluster that the students had was now completely gone.
Fang Yuan had not won once, but twice. This was no fluke.
"I'll go next!" someone said. The rest of them were C-grade and D-grade talents with no hope of really competing with anyone, but there was a chance they could distinguish themselves using their physical abilities.
One by one, Fang Yuan knocked them all out cold.
The martial arts instructor watched him intently. 'Not only is he strong but he is careful not to strike at vital areas. He has not just power, but restraint. This is not just innate talent, but skills honed over a long period of time.' He would normally be a bit wary of the students potentially killing each other- that was rare but still happened from time to time. It would not be much of an issue if a C-grade or a D-grade died, as this was considered to just be an acceptable part of training, though it would have been a massive catastrophe if someone like Fang Zheng died. However, he had nothing to worry about on that front.
Instead, he had a new problem now. After twelve victories, no one wanted to fight against Fang Yuan, despite his goading.
This was not what he had wanted. He had wanted to raise their fighting spirits and interest in martial arts, but had failed to do so.
Yes, Fang Yuan was good- but he wasn't here just to teach Fang Yuan, now then was he? Not to mention Fang Yuan had clearly received outside instruction so he couldn't claim to be the cause of that either.
Now, it looked like the rest were even less interested in learning how to fight. They had been completely dominated by Fang Yuan in their hearts.
He couldn't say anything to Fang Yuan after having openly praised him initially.Follow current novels on
"Alright, I'm up next."
"Bro, you really want to throw hands with him? He beat twelve guys in a row!"
"Yeah, I bet he's really tired now."
"He's not even sweating! He beat those twelve people in under ten seconds each!"
"Yeah, but none of 'em were me."
"He beat them all like it was easy!"
"Nah, he's just playing."
"Playing? Against twelve people?"
"He might've taken those twelve losers out, but I'm just built different."
In truth, it was hard for Fang Yuan to fight. Hard without killing that is. He had absorbed about a fourth of a boar's strength, and so had to be careful to not break bones or shatter skulls. Not only that, if he used too much strength, he might end up snapping his own bones or tearing out his own tendons. He also needed to strengthen his body defensively if he wished to use his strength to its full extent.
"Alright, if y'all are scared, I'm going up next. Once you guys get your balls out of your purses, feel free to fight me after him. Ayo - Fang Yuan! Once I'm done with you, you're gonna wish you died with your parents you stupid orphan!"
Five seconds later, said person rolled out of the ring, knocked out cold.
"Bro really thought he was heaven's chosen son."
"Alright, that's enough," the martial arts instructor said, seeing no one else was stepping up despite the prize. He handed Fang Yuan the primeval stones and then took him aside. "Fang Yuan, where did you learn to fight like that?"
"It was all thanks to the guidance of my uncle," Fang Yuan said. "He is extremely good when it comes to hand-to-hand combat, indeed he is a true dragon among men when it comes to martial arts, ah, too bad that my younger brother never saw the use of it."
"Oh, is that so?" the martial arts instructor thought, though it made sense. Fang Yuan had been orphaned at a very young age supposedly- who else but his uncle would've taught him then?
In truth, this was a lie, but Fang Yuan needed to give some plausible explanation for his skills. He couldn't reveal his 500 years of fighting experience, now then could he? His uncle was actually only skilled at beating the two of them back when they were kids.
However, this had another upside- once word got out that his uncle was secretly a martial arts master, people would begin challenging him just to test out their own combat skills.
Fang Yuan smiled inwardly at the thought of people lining up for the opportunity to punch his uncle in the face. The clan always promoted fighting to a reasonable extent between clan members for them to grow more powerful and also to compete.
'Uncle, I hope that this filial nephew has succeeded in giving you some face ah, too bad that it might be bloody and bruised soon,' Fang Yuan thought to himself as he walked away to start cultivating, bag of primeval stones fresh in his hands. 'Though maybe it would've been funnier if I said it was Aunt who trained me instead?'

chapters.title: Chapter 51 - 51: Hot Springs Retreat: Part One
chapters.content:
Once the fighting was done, Fang Yuan returned to his dorm room to begin nourishing his aperture again. Rank 1 Upper Stage was within reach, but it would still take time for him to get there. He could really use some aptitude boosts right now, but the system was as indifferent to that request as it always had been.
A message reached him, and he went outside to accost Fang Zheng at the gate.
"What's going on?"
"It looks like Mo Bei was indeed too badly injured and is resting so he won't be able to do his usual duties today," Fang Yuan said. "As such, you'll be covering for him."
"What! You can't be serious!" Fang Zheng was not looking forward to yet another afternoon of standing around like a guard dog.
"Fang Zheng, it is our duty to help out our fellow clansmen," Fang Yuan said. "Think about it in the future- if one of your team members falls sick, who will help them out in the future? Show some compassion for Mo Bei and agree to do this."
"Compassion? Elder brother, don't you think that you're being too shameless? Who was the one who is responsible for his state right now anyway? Where was your compassion then when you were mercilessly striking him?" Fang Zheng asked indignantly.
"Come on now," Fang Yuan said. "If I had not knocked him out he would've been greatly disappointed that I was not fighting him seriously- one with a pride like his would not want to be treated with kid gloves, after all. Quite frankly, I did him a favor by fighting him."
"But now he's out because of you... couldn't you have gone easy on him?"
Fang Yuan gave Fang Zheng a cold look. "I was going easy on him." For once, Fang Zheng felt that Fang Yuan was actually telling the truth. A chill crept down Fang Zheng's spine - if that was 'going easy' how would it have been if Fang Yuan fought at full force?
"But brother I-"
"Fang Zheng, don't make me remind you of the oath you took while becoming vice-president. Didn't you promise that you were going to work for the good of the student body? What do you think it means to be a hero? To just sit around doing nothing? Fang Zheng, the clansmen next to you is your greatest source of strength, it is only by banding together that we can thrive in this cold world," Fang Yuan said. "And that involves helping each other out when we're down, doesn't it? Tsk, I thought that I had taught you better through example but it looks like my lessons fell on deaf ears. I had hoped that you would aspire to become a respectable gentleman within society just like me, though unfortunately you seem to lack the virtue needed for such."
Fang Zheng realized that he was going to lose this fight. He hadn't gotten into an actual physical fight with Fang Yuan- knowing that he was going to be kicked and humiliated. The others didn't look favorably on this, given he was the only one of the 'big four' as they were now called who hadn't fought. But that was fine, he had just made the excuse that he didn't want to throw hands with his elder brother.
However, in this battle of wits, there was little that he could do. "Why don't you do it then? Aren't you president?"
"I have other duties," Fang Yuan said, waving a scroll before his face with the academy elder's seal on it. "Look at this- it is a task especially given to me. Now, do you want the academy elder to know that you are giving me a hard time?"
Fang Zheng sighed, resigned to his fate as he stood outside Fang Yuan's door while the latter quickly skimmed through the scroll.
'Interesting- is this a consequence of my rebirth? This did not happen during my last time,' Fang Yuan thought as he analyzed what was written before him.
Normally, the students would be given some time off around this time to help them refine their second gu worms. Fang Yuan had been the first to pick his, but there hadn't been anything good within the gu worm storage as it was, and he had ended up taking a Little Light Gu, which could be refined into something special in the future. Also, it would boost the power and range of his moonblades, being a supporting gu worm to the clan's signature Moonlight Gu. Overall though, it was slightly disappointing and there wasn't that much advantage to being the first one to choose a second gu worm, at least, not for someone like him.
It had been too much to expect a good gu worm to be there, like the Black Boar Gu, for example. Expecting something like that would only set one up for disappointment.
Fang Yuan did not need any time to refine his second gu worm given he had the Spring Autumn Cicada's aura to work with, but the time off would help him get ahead with refining to Rank 1 Upper Stage quickly. However, it appeared that they weren't going to get time off - rather than that, the academy elder wanted to conduct a 'retreat' this year in which the class would go somewhere. The usual lessons were suspended, of course, but they would be expected, or at least, this was the point of this whole thing in the first place, that they would start socializing with each other using much of the time they were allotted.
'Is this a scheme by the academy elder because of me?' Fang Yuan wondered. By going back in time, he had changed several small things already. Either it was a direct consequence of him becoming class president or some other change that he had caused.
The academy elder had left it to Fang Yuan to decide where to go. The options were- a martial arts dojo in the village, a hot spring resort, hunting cabins outside of the village, or to just have it here in the academy.
Fang Yuan did not care either way. if it had been the old him, he would've planned on just calling in sick o something to get more time to cultivate. Now though, he was burdened with his new position and had to play along.
'I don't care either way where we happen to go, I'll pawn this off to the vice-presidents and they can choose where to go,' Fang Yuan thought.
Fang Zheng later turned his head ten minutes into his 'shift' to see that Fang Yuan was already done with his 'work' and was now cultivating.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
'AH!' Fang Zheng wanted to scream. The pin on his chest now felt like it was a hundred times heavier, weighing him down and chaining him to the earth. He was going to fall even further behind the longer this continued! All of Fang Yuan's talks of solidarity and helping each other were nonsense, he knew, and were just things he was saying to force him to work harder.
The next day, Fang Zheng and a mildly mollified Mo Bei were discussing on where to go for the upcoming trip. There was excited discussion from a lot of people, and as neither Fang Zheng nor Mo Bei had any particular interest in any of the four locations in particular, they decided to leave it all up to popular vote.
It finally came down to going hunting outside the village, or to the hot springs.
"Man, don't you guys think it would be cool to go on a hunting trip?' some of the boys thought. They didn't want to go ahead with the hot springs plan.
'But wait,... if we choose hot springs there's a chance...' some of the others spoke to them, changing their minds, enticing them with what they could find in the hot springs.
"Alright, hot springs it is then," Fang Yuan said, seeing the majority consensus. As class president, he delivered this news to the academy elder, who was satisfied enough with the response.

chapters.title: Chapter 52 - 52: Hot Springs Retreat: Part Two
chapters.content:
Despite having resided within Gu Yue village for some time in his prior life, Fang Yuan had never been to the hot springs. The main reason for this was a lack of primeval stones at that period of time- he had better things to do than relaxing and bathing in hot water.
There was another reason- the hot springs were located some distance from the village borders, though not so far into the wilderness as the hunting trip would've been. This normally would be a very bad idea given the size of the beast tide- attempts had been made, multiple times, to expand the village though it always ended up shrinking to its current size as it was found that the clan could not defend any larger area effectively.
Because of this, naturally, the village was quite crowded and it was hard to find houses. Rent was high- but there were little options one had if one didn't want to be thrown out of the village.
This hot spring resort had likely been destroyed back in his old life as well- he just hadn't paid much attention to it.
But, it seemed that the owner had a peculiar business strategy. When the beast tide was not around, the area was safe enough, especially given the few Gu Masters stationed there to guard the place. One could charge money for the hot springs, which were constructed with wood and the help of some Rank 1 Gu Worms. The water was heated with Rank 2 Hot Spring Gu, which looked like small piece of coal normally but would turn red and emit a great amount of heat particularly in water when injected with primeval essence. All of these gu worms could be retrieved and stored when the beast tide occurred. The building itself wasn't too hard to rebuild, so the business plan seemed to be to milk it as much as possible during ordinary times, and then to let it be demolished during the beat tide. Afterwards, it could be rebuilt and the gu worms placed there once again.
The cost to rebuild could be considered to just be a 'business expense' and depending on how business was usually, it might still be turning a profit. Though, the scale of the next beast tide would be beyond anyone's expectations, and much of the village itself would also be destroyed.Google seaʀᴄh ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
'Is this really profitable?' Fang Yuan thought to himself as the students arrived at the building. It was quite simple, of course, given that it was made with the expectation that it would be destroyed soon enough. However, there seemed to be a reasonable amount of traffic. not to mention the students, who numbered around fifty. The place of course had not given up all such space for free, but had rather been paid either with funds from the academy or by the academy elder himself, more likely the former rather than the latter.
Fang Yuan was currently standing near the door, with a sheet in hand. He was in charge of attendance- and though he'd normally pawn this off to either Fang Zheng or Mo Bei, he had been asked to do this himself by the academy elder. Those two were currently doing some other things.
"Gu Yue Chi Chen... Gu Yue Li Mei..." Fang Yuan muttered to himself as he crossed names off of the list.
As a consequence of becoming class president he had (unwillingly, mind you) learned the names and faces of all of his classmates. Not to the point of becoming friends with them, of course, but after interacting with them for some time he was able to put a face to each name, something he had not been able to do the first time around.
"That should be everyone," Fang Yuan said as he folded the sheet. Two people were not coming for some reasons- Fang Yuan wished he could join them by playing sick or something along those lines so that he would have more time to do what he wanted, but given how the situation was, he could not do so. Not to mention if he feigned illness the academy elder just might come personally to heal him. it was one thing if no-name C-grade and D-grade talents didn't show up, but all eyes were on Fang Yuan, especially because of his position and deeds this time around.
Being famous and having a good aptitude has its drawbacks, he thought.
He took a look around the place. A group of deer were grazing far off in the distance- and there were trees here and there which speckled the landscape. It could be said that they were as far into the wilderness while still being near civilization as possible- the village itself proper was not too far away. They had not run into any problems as of yet, because it was not time for the beast time to erupt. As it was, they had a Rank 3 Gu Master, the academy elder with them. Although he was specialized in healing, there was no way that he didn't have some method of attack. In addition, the hot springs themselves employed several Rank 2 Gu Masters to function as bodyguards- then again, that was why the price for attendance was proportionately high. Despite this, Fang Yuan saw some people who were not from the academy - many of them couples who were walking into the hot springs. It looked like the place was not doing too bad for itself.
The area inside was divided into a men's and women's section, as well as a shared section (this being the smallest). Fang Yuan walked along the men's section until he reached the door of a large room.
The academy elder had a room to himself, and Fang Yuan knocked on the door. "Gu Yue Fang Yuan requests permission to enter."
"Come in," came the reply.
The academy elder was lounging in a chair wearing slippers and a bathrobe- looking like he was having the time of his life. 'Did he ask us to come here simply so that he could get a paid vacation?' Fang Yuan thought to himself even as he cupped his hands. "I've taken attendance and everything is in order."
"Good, good," the academy elder said lazily. "Well then, I had something for you actually..." He pulled out a small bottle of liquor. "A gift from someone, though I don't really drink. I know you need to feed your Liquor Worm, consider it a gift from me. Oh- I don't mind you taking a few sips yourself, but remember not to overdo it we can't have our class president becoming tipsy now then can we? Ehehe..."
He chuckled to himself as Fang Yuan respectfully took the bottle. "Thank you for this gift."
"It's nothing, just a reward for your hard work," the academy elder said. Arranging for this trip had fallen on Fang Yuan quite a bit since he had to oversee a good portion of the logistics involved.
Given all the time he'd had to spend, this gift was really nothing special. However, Fang Yuan needed those ten stones a week, and without extortion being an option, he couldn't back out from this position. The daily quests had occasionally given him some primeval stones here and there, but they were not enough. More often than not he ended up getting more Human Path dao marks which he did not use, to the point where he was declining some of the daily quests.
"Which gu worm did you pick again?" the academy elder asked.
"The Little Light Gu," Fang Yuan replied.
"Ah, good choice," the academy elder said. One's choice of gu worm said a lot about a person - the fact that Fang Yuan had chosen a supportive gu worm for the Moonlight Gu meant that he greatly valued offensive power. Not only that though, but there was meaning to him choosing a supportive gu worm for the clan's signature gu worm- it was a way of tying him down further with the clan.
Fang Yuan, of course, had no intention of keeping things that way. He knew the Moon Orchid Petals were another way of tying him down to the village, and the Little Light Gu was quickly going to be refined into something more suitable for his needs. Something that could be fed differently.
Fang Yuan took his leave after this.

chapters.title: Chapter 53 - 53: Hot Springs Repeat: Part Three
chapters.content:
During this hot springs retreat, everyone was doing something or the other to either relax or work, usually a mix of both.
First off, starting with the teachers. Although this had been introduced as a way for the students to relax, many of the teachers had tagged along. This was not entirely without reason or justification, as they needed someone to supervise the students as well as to ensure their safety.
The teachers had a room all to themselves- and the academy elder was the only one currently relaxing when the martial arts instructor walked in.
"Ah, greetings," the martial arts instructor said.
"Greetings, how are you?"
The two of them exchanged pleasantries. The academy elder noted that the martial arts instructor's body was covered in sweat- even now, when they were on 'vacation' so to speak, the man was still training.
Although he was inexperienced, one could not say that he lacked dedication to his craft.
"Still training?"
"Yes, I've heard that hot springs help relax the muscles, and if that's the case, why not make full use of it? I was also hoping to whip up some enthusiasm from the students to train but didn't get too far unfortunately..."
The academy elder began to ponder things. He had heard that this batch was rather peculiar in that they seemed to neglect martial arts more than the prior batches. This was not good- while gu were the core of a Gu Master's arsenal, oftentimes being quick with your fists or feet could easily get you out of a sticky situation. Not to mention that Strength Path Gu Masters specialized in turning their bodies into living weapons- there would always be a few among the students who would eventually go on to specialize in the Strength Path, though no one had done so up till now. "What is the issue here?"
he had initially thought it was the martial arts instructor's fault as he was a greenhorn, though that didn't seem to be the case at this point.
"Ah, it's about Fang Yuan..." the martial arts instructor said.
The academy elder was intrigued at that point. "Oh? How so?"
"Oh, he hasn't done anything wrong," the martial arts instructor said, rubbing the back of his neck sheepishly. "He is a natural when it comes to martial arts, to the point where there is nothing to teach him. I ah, kind of feel useless even trying to give him instruction... his uncle must be quite the figure to have taught him so. I was even thinking of challenging him one day to test out his skills! But putting that aside the other students, rather than feeling motivated by Fang Yuan's example, seem to have given up. 'I can't be as good as Fang Yuan, so why bother?' seems to be their motto. It's unfortunate that their morale is going down rather than increasing."
It appeared that Fang Yuan's image had dominated them so thoroughly that none of them thought they were his match- even the other three being Mo Bei, Fang Zheng, and Chi Chen seemed to barely be keeping pace with him.
The academy elder didn't think this was good- competition was of course, essential, but Fang Yuan being too good to the point where everyone gave up was not good either.
If Fang Yuan suffered a defeat at some point, his image would take a nosedive and the others might be motivated. But as it was right now, Fang Yuan had been doing nothing but farming Ws since the year had started.
The academy elder could do little to suppress him as well, though he had hoped that this little excursion would help Fang Yuan mingle with his peers a bit more.
'Hopefully, Fang Yuan will learn the value of his comrades on this trip. Or at least, make some friends,' the academy elder thought.
Meanwhile, Fang Yuan was in his room, deep in cultivation. One of the perks of his position was that he had been given a private room unlike the others.
The Liquor Worm was swimming in the bottle of alcohol he had gotten from the academy elder, and then re-entered Fang Yuan's aperture when it was done feeding. Fang Yuan began giving it primeval stone after primeval stone, watching as the green primeval essence deepened as the Liquor Worm began releasing a sweet, intoxicating fragrance.
He had left the White Boar Gu and the mysterious Rank 3 Gu Worm he'd gotten back in his dorm, with his methods, he doubted either would be discovered.
Right now, in his aperture, other than the Liquor Worm, there was the Moonlight Gu and the Little Light Gu, which he had refined instantly. The Spring Autumn Cicada looked infinitesimally better than before, but it was good that its rate of recovery was not faster for Fang Yuan. He had brought One With Scenery Gu on a whim, thinking that it might've been useful if he ever needed to sneak out, something that was far harder now than in his previous life.
The wall of his aperture was on the cusp of changing as he was about to reach Rank 1 Upper Stage - it was only the matter of a few hours.
As for socializing with the others, or going to relax in the hot springs, he had no time for either of those things.
Eventually his stomach began to growl as his primeval essence was all used up, and he went to go have lunch when a notification flashed before his eyes.
New Main Mission Unlocked!
Shikanoko Nokono Koshitantan
Description: Help the hunter save a baby deer
Reward:
Permanent 3% increase to aptitude
Karmic flag plant regarding above incident
Fang Yuan paused as he went to go take his meal.
A number of thoughts blossomed in his mind.The source of thɪs content is ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
First off, he had no idea what 'Shikanoko Nokono Koshitantan' meant, the system seemed to be using some kind of language that he was unfamiliar with, but no matter how much he thought about it, it didn't give him any further explanation. Did those words have something to do with deer?
Secondly, he was finally getting an increase to his aptitude, which he really wanted from the system. Right now, he was advancing at a pace that was nearly ten times that of his previous life, but it was not enough for him. He had to go further still, and though doing this mission might waste some of his time, the 3% difference would be essential to clutching victories in the future.
Most importantly, although it made advancing for now easier, that wasn't what the main benefit was. The gap between Rank 2 and Rank 3 needed around 60% essence to overcome, and with this, he would have 59% essence. Advancing to Rank 3 would cost him far less and would be much easier even though the increase was only by 3% right now. He was already sure of his advancement to Rank 2, but that was nothing to someone like Fang Yuan who needed to priortize getting to Rank 3 above all so that he could leave and take advantage of a lot of his knowledge since his regression.
Third, although the system mentioned this as a reward, he didn't know what a 'karmic flag' was.
It is something that will be relied up later on.
That was little in the way of an actual explanation, he thought.
It was as if he had used an information-type gu worm as a location appeared in his head on where to go.
Walking out of the hot springs, he was stopped by one of the guards.
"Junior brother, where are you headed?"
"I just wanted to take a short walk to clear my head," Fang Yuan said.
"Alright, but stay close to the trail where it's safe."
"Hang on," another guard said. "Are you Gu Yue Fang Yuan? The student who found the Flower Wine Monk's inheritance?"
The story had spread far and wide, and it was not out of the ordinary for people to recognize Fang Yuan.
This was more of a hindrance than anything given how often people would stop him for now reason, and here was no exception as Fang Yuan found himself exchanging greetings for five minutes longer than he would've liked before heading off.

chapters.title: Chapter 54 - 54: Hot Springs Retreat: Part Four
chapters.content:
While all of this was going on, a group of male students were planning something.
There was a reason that a lot of them had ultimately decided upon the hot springs even though most of them were more interested in hunting. They were just 'hunting' in a different sense.
While the girls wanted to enjoy the benefits of the hot spring, namely, in better skin and the like, the boys chose it for the opportunities it provided.
Namely, they were thinking of peeping on the girls!
Of course, if they went ahead and simply tried to go peer over the wall separating the women and men's sections, they would be caught quite quickly. No, they needed a plan. But a plan needed a leader- a figure that they could all rally behind. Who would be the captain to whom they swore their allegiance?
The first choice, Fang Yuan, was discarded immediately. No one thought that they could convince him to join them, and even if they had tried, it would have gone badly.
The next person in line was Fang Zheng, but he rejected them wholeheartedly.
'If I go ahead with this, I'll probably be caught and end up bringing infamy to the family name,' Fang Zheng thought. 'Not to mention, I have to remain loyal to Cui-Cui! As it is, we can bathe together almost anytime at home. Who cares about these other girls? I only need her in my heart. Besides, I need to work hard right now.'
Mo Bei also turned them down and told them to work harder. He was vice-president and couldn't be caught being involved in something like this. Not to mention he still felt sore from the beating Fang Yuan had given him, as well as the extra work they had to do to organize this trip; therefore lacking the energy to cause any kind of mischief. As it was, he finally had some peace and quiet to refine his second gu worm and didn't want to lose to Fang Zheng or Fang Yuan - he hadn't realized that Fang Yuan was already done refining his 'second' gu worm weeks ago and was rushing towards Rank 1 Upper Stage.
With these targets out of the way, they then approached Chi Chen. Chi Chen considered it for a moment, before saying, "Have you seen the girls in our class? None of them are worth peeping on."
With these four people rejecting them, it seemed that the party of Peeping Toms was demoralized enough that they were about to give up.
"Maybe we should just focus on refining our second gu worms..."
"We'll probably get caught and beaten for no reason anyway..."
"Chi Chen was pretty right too, all the girls are 6/10 at best..."
Among this cloud of despair, however, a heroic(?) figure emerged.
"I can't believe that all of you are giving up so soon," Yu Sai said, walking in on the group. "Are you all not ashamed to call yourselves men? Tell me, can you all really say in your heart of hearts that you don't want to see what's on the other side of that wall."ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
The others were momentarily speechless. It was true, being young boys, they were quite curious as to what the sight on the other side of that wall was like. So what if all the girls were 'mid' at best? Wasn't it the allure of what was forbidden fruit which was really exciting them? Didn't they all want to go venture out and do something like that, and then get away with it? Wasn't that what they were really after?
"Fang Yuan and the rest might be a bunch of eunuchs and refused to join us," Yu Sai said. "But can you all really say that you lack the stones to go where no other man would dare?"
The boy's found their morale raised kudos to Yu Sai's rousing speech, but now they had a new problem.
"But... what are we going to do?"
Some people with a little less self-control had already tried to peep on the girls by just climbing over the wall or such similar measures and had naturally gotten into trouble. They needed a far better plan than that.
"Those people failed because they didn't use their brains and acted as no better than mortals," Yu Sai said. "What are we? Normal people? No, we are Gu Masters! We use, raise, and refine gu! There is a gu worm for every purpose, and this is no exception!"
He then pulled out his 'trump card.'
"Is that...?"
"That's right," Yu Sai said. This had been his choice of second gu. "This is an Audio-Visual Gu! We just have to somehow get it on the other side, and we don't even need to wander there ourselves! We'll get the images right to us! No risk whatsoever! That's how smart people would do something like this."
Audio-Visual Gu was an extremely bizarre choice for a second gu worm given how niche it's use was, but given how bad Yu Sai's aptitude was no one really paid him any attention or had noticed his choice. As it was, it did have the upside of not needing to be fed with anything other than light, allowing Yu Sai to save on a few primeval stones. He had been one of the last to choose his second gu worm, but that had been what allowed him to pick this based on the news of where they were going on their trip.
"Ah, but there is a catch," Yu Sai said. "I need some help refining this gu. Come on, I just need a few primeval stones to do so... either that or one of you needs to refine it for me."
He didn't dare ask Fang Yuan to refine it as it would naturally bring attention to the fact as to why he wanted this gu in particular, and in his eyes Fang Yuan was an upstanding class president and definitely crack down on him.
Some of the boys grumbled but they ultimately agreed to his plan.
Meanwhile, Fang Yuan was making his way down the marked path that the system had set up for him.
He lacked an investigative-type gu worm, but this was mostly just open fields and there was little room for things like wolves or enemies to hide. Not that there couldn't be dangers- some creatures could lurk underground, and there could be wild gu worms. However, this close to the village, this was rather unlikely.
If he wandered a bit further south, he might be able to find a group of wild boar and get some boar meat. However, that would take too long and then his absence would without a doubt be noticed. As it was, he had left the White Boar Gu at home.
He considered using One With Scenery Gu, though it didn't look like anyone had noticed he had left. As it was, he was technically not doing anything wrong so he wasn't afraid of being tailed, if anything, that even guaranteed him a small layer of protection.
A short distance away, a mortal hunter by the name of Ji Han was squatting near a curious specimen.
It was a deerling- barely a few weeks old, but it looked like its parents were either dead or had abandoned it. It was clearly struggling, and the man had found it while surveying the surrounding area.
Suddenly, he felt a chill crawl down his spine. It was as if he felt a great evil was bearing down on him, and his hunter's instincts, without which he would have perished long ago, and he grabbed his weapon- a makeshift spear, as he saw someone approach out of the corner of his eye.
He relaxed and lowered his weapon as he saw who it was that had approached. It was a student Gu Master, but a student was still a Gu Master- the gap between their statuses could not be overemphasized as he lowered his head. "Ah, Young Master, what brings you here?"
Fang Yuan surveyed the man quickly. This was the 'hunter' the system wanted him to help out with, and there was the young deer child that was the main subject of the mission. "Nothing, I was merely out for a walk- but what is this?"
"Oh this," Ji Han began, "it's a bit of a sad story. I think this deer was abandoned by its family. It can't live on its own for much longer... I was out for a hunt, but it seems too cruel to kill something so young." He sighed. Perhaps a hunter should not have that kind of reservations in such a dog-eat-dog world, but he couldn't bring himself to kill the deer. Despite the fact that it was doomed to die soon, he did not want to accelerate that process.
Fang Yuan, however, looked at the deer with great interest. 'Could this be... if I'm not mistaken...'

chapters.title: Chapter 55 - 55: Hot Springs Retreat: Part Five
chapters.content:
An ordinary person would not have recognized anything 'abnormal' about the fawn, but to Fang Yuan's trained eye sharpened by 500 years' worth of experience. The fawn's eyes had slit pupils, and upon examination of its mouth one could barely make out the pointed teeth that would later grow into fangs. Its hooves had the slight vermillion tinge of what would later acquire a sanguineous hue.
The Crimsonhoof Deer!
It was a type of mutant beast.
Normally beasts were divided into ordinary beasts, Hundred Beast Kings, Thousand Beast Kings, Myriad Beast Kings, and Beast Emperors! These corresponded to Rank One through Rank Five Gu Masters in terms of strength. Normally beasts would grow into higher stages over time if they were capable enough, however, the Crimsonhoof Deer was a Mutated Beast. Its strength would soon jump up and rival that of a Myriad Beast King, in other words, that of a Rank Four Gu Master. If it was lucky, it could even turn into the Crimsonhoof Deer Emperor- on par with a Rank Five Gu Master.
The above classification, was of course, only for mortal beasts. For immortal beasts there was a different classification.
Mutated Beasts appeared at random within herds of animals. They were extremely valuable- Fang Yuan would've been able to sell it for a great profit, or, if he was a Blood Path Immortal, would raise it in his aperture. It was classified as a type of Blood Path beast.
But, he had no easy way to sell it.
The next best thing would be to raise it. Although he did not have the strength and power to enslave a Rank Four beast, one did not need to subdue it by force in order to use it. If he was the one to raise it from infancy, it would naturally grow to follow him even when it grew up.
Even humans were similar; Fang Yuan couldn't help but think. Fang Zheng would, if allowed, grow to be not only Rank 3 but Rank 4 later on. And they would still have him on a leash- even a mortal like Shen Cui could make him dance in the palm of her hand. No Enslavement Gu was needed for that.
As it was, Rank One Deer Enslavemnt Gu would not work on this creature. Once it exceeded the boundaries of an ordinary beast, it would break free from Fang Yuan's control.
He could not raise it, however. He didn't even have a room for himself, and was living in the academy dorm. There was no way that he could provide the constant care a fawn like this would need. Pay someone else to do it? He could do so, but that would raise a large number of questions. Not to mention that it would eventually be discovered as a mutated beast, and would likely be taken from him by the clan or cause large amounts of damage and be killed. While he might be able to get the mutated beast to acclimatize to his presence, keeping it in Gu Yue village was out of the question. It would attack the other humans.
These thoughts passed through his mind in nearly an instant. However, there had been a reason as to why he had been called to this place.
"What concerns you so much, Young Master?" Ji Han asked. It was odd to him that a Gu Master would be concerned with something so petty.
"I wanted to find a way to save this fawn," Fang Yuan said. His mind was going through several things as to what to do.
"Truly? I also could not bear to kill it, thinking of it living such a sad life but to think there was someone else who thought the same..." the hunter mused.
"It has always been my philosophy in life that, 'helping someone in need is always the right thing to do,'" Fang Yuan said. "As a matter of fact, if I saw someone in trouble and didn't do something to help them out, I wouldn't be able to eat dinner that day as the guilt within me would gnaw at me relentlessly- that is just the kind of person I am."
The hunter was greatly moved. To think that he had initially pointed his weapon at Fang Yuan because he believed he sense evil- no, this young Gu Master clearly had a heart of gold.
As a matter of fact, now that Fang Yuan was here, the hunter felt that he could not longer just walk away from the fawn. Perhaps, together, they could do something?
"Do you happen to know if there are any deer nearby?" Fang Yuan asked. "Adults, I mean."
"In that direction, about an hour away, but..."
"Can you stay here while I try something?" Fang Yuan asked, wandering away slightly. It didn't look like he was out to hunt the deer, so the hunter wasn't sure what was going on but obliged nonetheless. Something about the way Fang Yuan behaved made him believe that he was quite reliable and could be trusted.
Meanwhile, back in the retreat, Fang Zheng was done refining his second gu worm and decided to take a break.
Some of his newly acquired 'friends' approached him. "Fang Zheng, we had a new idea that we thought could help you?"
"Oh?"
"You were trying to write poems to beat Fang Yuan, right, but, he's a genius when it comes to poetry," someone said. "But there's something else that you can do- something that might get you famous as well in that area. It's called writing novels! Anyone without talent can easily do it! I mean, not to say that you lack talent but..."
Fang Zheng went around this group, who included some people who were not part of Yu Sai's peeping expedition. They had started working on their own stories, and seeing them, and with nothing better to do, Fang Zheng decided to try his hand at it.
Gu Daoist Apprentice
By: Fang Zheng
Once upon a time, in the weakest corner of the weakest region in the world, there was the weakest clan who lived in the weakest village. There, in the weakest family, a child was born with the lowest talent among the family. His name was...
Fang Zheng contemplated what to call his protagonist. He wanted to make it a self-insert, but he couldn't be too obvious about it.Google seaʀᴄh
...Zheng Fang. Zheng Fang had no talent and the people in the village always bullied him and considered him to be less worthy than his older brother. However, he had one person who always supported him- the family maid whose name was Cui Shen. She always supported Zheng Fang, saying "I believe in you Zheng Fang, even if the world turns against you, I'll always keep supporting you." Everytime he would hear those words, no matter how badly Zheng Fang felt, he always cheered up. She had a smile that could light up his day, no matter how dark things were.
However, Zheng Fang had little talent and continued to be overshadowed and oppressed, until one day while running away from some bullies, he ended up falling off a cliff.
"Ouch... that could've really hurt..."
As he was about to get up though, he found something strange on the ground.
It was a small gu worm, which looked like little more than a flea.
"Wow! I wonder what kind of gu worm this is..."
"Welcome, young traveler," a voice echoed from within the gu worm.
"Ah!"
"Relax, I was an ancient master and my soul got trapped within this gu worm. When you fell, you freed me from where I was trapped. I thank you kindly."
Fang Zhen paused before continuing to write.

chapters.title: Chapter 56 - 56: Hot Springs Retreat: Part Six
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan walked through the plains and near a more arborous area. The tree line hide what was behind it from view, though if the hunter was to be believed, there was a group of deer behind those trees.
The deer, of course, being so close to the village and within its walls were all ordinary. There would not even be a single Hundred Beast King among them, otherwise the clan would've sent someone to dispatch of them. These deer were a good hunting resource which is why the hunter had them marked down, and Fang Yuan needed to reach them before they left.
In his previous life, the Crimsonhoof Deer had likely perished like this in the wilderness and never grown to maturity. However, he intended to change that.
As he got closer, he activated One With Scenery Gu. This unfortunately did nothing to hide his scent or noise, which was why 'there was no strongest gu, only strongest Gu Masters.' All gu had their weaknesses, but this would hopefully be enough.
Female deer raised two to three fawns a year, though in the harsh climate of this world, several of the fawns would have died by now. He merely needed to find the appropriate target..ɴet
and found a doe near the edge who was nestling a young fawn with her.
At this moment, Fang Yuan retrieved the Rank 1 Deer Enslavement Gu from his system. This was a one-time usage gu worm, meaning that if he failed, that would be the end of things. That said, this was an ordinary beast and not even a hundred beast king, meaning he was extremely confident in subduing it.
Man is the spirit of all things - how could the soul of an animal compare to that of a human?
As he launched the gu worm at the deer, he felt his soul colliding against the deer's. It resisted, as all living things, it had its own will to live. The two souls wrestled against each other. The rest of the flock noticed its wariness and sudden change of behavior, looking almost ready to flee, but it calmed down soon enough.
Fang Yuan's brows were furrowed. He had not strengthened his soul which was an integral part of enslavement tactics, but his willpower had not been reduced. His soul began to thoroughly suppress the deer's and he won.
This fight felt like it had taken place over a few minutes, but had in reality only lasted for a few breaths of time.
Fang Yuan was then able to lead the doe back to where the hunter was. One With Scenery Gu's power faded on the journey back, as it was, Fang Yuan did not have much primeval essence to keep up with the Rank 2 gu's expenditure. He used primeval stones to restore his essence while they went back.
"Young Master, you are back!" the hunter said, a bit astonished at how obediently the deer was following Fang Yuan.
"I found the fawn a mother," Fang Yuan said. Taking control of the deer and maintaining some manner of influence over it would strain his soul to some extent, but it was a simple enough command to make it take care of the Crimsonhoof Deer. On top of which, once it had taken care of the fawn for a while, it would grow attached to it and start raising it without any prompt from Fang Yuan.
The doe nuzzled the Crimsonhoof Deer, which nuzzled it back. It clearly was looking for someone to care for it- and though this doe's scent would be different from its mother's, it was close enough that it quickly bonded to the doe, which trotted off with her new adopted offspring.
Would the deer survive? The world was quite cruel, and the doe had been orphaned in the first place because its parents had been killed. One could scarcely guarantee one's safety even in the confines of a village, let alone the wilderness. But, even if that was not the case, Fang Yuan still got his reward.
Mission Successful!
Aptitude permanently increased by 3%!
Karmic flag planted!
Fang Yuan wasn't sure what the second prompt did, but he had finally made some progress in increasing his aptitude. For that, this whole excursion was worth it.
Meanwhile, on the girl's side of the hot springs, there was a bit of a commotion.
"Did you hear? Some of the boys were caught peeping on us!"
"I heard some more of them are planning something too."
"None of the peepers were the handsome ones either, just creeps."
While the other girls were talking about this issue, Li Mei sighed.
Even if the hot spring had rejuvenating properties, it would likely do nothing for someone like her who had never had good skin in the first place. And it would do nothing for her looks.
On top of which, she had made little progress with refining her second gu worm. She had chosen the Little Light Gu- though for what could be considered a dumb reason. She had heard that Fang Yuan had chosen it, and being confused about her second choice, went with it, thinking that if it was good enough for the class president it should've been good enough for her too.
Of course, Fang Yuan had different prospects than her- something she should've considered. He had enough primeval essence to make good use of offensive methods. Her- although she hated it when Yu Sai talked about it, really had very few in the way of advancing.
Rather than choosing a combat-focused gu worm, she would've likely done better with choosing one that could heal. Healing Gu Masters had better rates of survival, and for someone like her who didn't like fighting, that was more optimal than trying to get a stronger moonblade.
But, there was nothing that she could do about that now.
As for the peeping incidents, she couldn't care less. If anything, that was at least some form of attention. Something that she couldn't get otherwise.
'Though come to think of it, would Fang Yuan be among the boys coming to peep? No... he wouldn't write?
That didn't stop her mind from going to... strange places.
She imagined walked out of the hot springs, only to be stopped suddenly.
"Ah, class president!" she'd say, noticing for some reason that there was no one around the two of them. At least, no one they could see was around them as the steam completely covered the hot springs and was so thick it was like the two of them were isolated in their own, small little world; just the two of them.
Fang Yuan would look amazing, muscles toned as the beads of water ran down them, accentuating each of the finely chiseled parts of his body. His long hair, wet but neat, covered part of his face but left his intense gaze unveiled. His eyes were like two hypnotizing beautiful pools of darkness that seemed to beckon for her soul to fall into them. His features had a strange grace and serenity about them that she couldn't describe with words. As he always did, he had an aura of near invincibility and aloofness about him - though she knew that in truth, behind the mask of coldness, one of the kindest and most generous hearts in Gu Yue village dwelled.
The towel around his waist covered just enough as he slowly approached her, suddenly seemingly entranced by the rose-like color of her lips as he bent over her and his mouth moved closer to hers...
'NO!' she suddenly thought. 'I can't kiss Fang Yuan, or I'll become pargenant just like mother warned me about! Uh... but what if he was a bit forceful and wanted to kiss me even if I said 'no?' Well... I'd probably resist a little at first... but not too much I guess if he really insisted...'
Her head was filled with all these strange thoughts that she couldn't fully describe- her mother would not tell her what they meant, only that she was a bad girl for expressing them and needed to avoid all contact with boys, and her father stayed out of that conversation altogether.
She could ask the other girls- but something deep within her told her that this was a... rather taboo thing to ask and she wasn't close to any of them as it was. She had had friends before, but they were all mortals and she didn't see them as often now that she was a Gu Master.
And so, she was left blushing and dealing with these odd feelings in her head that she didn't fully understand.

chapters.title: Chapter 57 - 57: Hot Springs Retreat: Part Seven
chapters.content:
"Did you really use a gu worm to save that fawn?" the hunter asked Fang Yuan. He was a mortal and did not have a deep understanding of Gu Master cultivation, but could comprehend that Fang Yuan had paid a rather high price to save the deerling. Although the hunter had been moved somewhat as well, he would not have paid a fraction of the price needed for a gu worm just to save it.
"Don't worry," Fang Yuan said. "I myself was orphaned at a very young age. Given that, my heart was greatly shaken upon seeing another abandoned child who had been separated from its parents. Seeing myself in it, I couldn't help but want to save it."
The hunter lowered his head. He had done so many times in the past to Gu Masters out of fear of retaliation, but this was a bow of genuine respect. "Truly! In all of the five regions and two heavens, I do not think that there is anyone as righteous as Young Master! If it would please you, may I know your name?"
"Gu Yue Fang Yuan..."
"Ah, Young Master Fang Yuan," the hunter said, committing the name to memory.
Fang Yuan easily returned to the lodge after that. No one had really missed him, but he had been gone for some time. The moment he walked in someone came in with a small issue - if he had been just five minutes late, they likely would've noticed how long he had been gone for.
Was this the effect of luck? Or had the system anticipated this?
Regardless, he put a sign outside his door stating that he was refining his second gu worm and to not disturb him unless there was an emergency.
By now his primeval essence had completely recovered, filling in 59% of his aperture. The Liquor Worm began doing its thing, essentially turning it into 118% effective essence which began to nurture his aperture.
'I'm close - very close to reaching Rank 1 Upper Stage!' he thought.
Fang Zheng, on the other hand, was feeling rather delighted when someone told him that Fang Yuan was still working on refining his second gu worm.
'At last- I'm finally pulling ahead!' he thought.
He had been working on his novel for some time, and by now, he was almost done with the outline for the first draft.
He saw that the others were similarly done, and decided to take a look at what some of them had written.
Zhang Long waited outside of the auction house, knowing that his special ingredient was soon to arrive.
"Here it is," Fairy Jin Zhen handed a bottle filled with clear liquid to him. It was very small and only had half a mouthful of liquid, but to Zhang Long it was extraordinarily precious. Zhang Long handed her ten thousand primeval stones and accepted the bottle.
Fairy Jin Zhen was a bit embarrassed which was why this transaction was done quickly and in a darkened alleyway, though there were still those who were watching from the shadows.
'What did that vial contain that could cost ten thousand primeval stones?' they thought.
If they knew that the vial contained Fairy Jin Zhen's bathwater, who knows what kind of expression they would have?
Fang Zheng stopped reading at that point, nearly choking on his own spit. "Bathwater... what's going on?" What was the context behind this paragraph?
"Oh," the writer of said novel said. "In my novel, the protagonist has a special talent. He can use the bathwater of beautiful girls to create powerful alchemical solutions which greatly boost his cultivation. The more beautiful the girl, the better his talent. My working title is 'I Can Use Girl's Bathwater To Make SSSSS+ Ranked Alchemical Potions.'"
Fang Zheng was greatly shook. Was this what they were all working on?
The guy read Fang Zheng's work and said, "This is good - but I think you need to add more 'S''s to the title somehow. The more of those you have, the better your work, you know."
Fang Zheng lost all ambition for working on novels at that point and just chose to give up. After all, it looked like he was winning against Fang Yuan when it came to cultivation, which was what really mattered.
The next day, nothing of note really happened, though Yu Sai and his gang finally managed to retrieve the Audio-Visual Gu they had planted on the women's side the day before. While it was not easy for someone to pass through the barrier between the sides, a small gu worm could do so easily.
"Alright, this is what we've been waiting for," he said excitedly, about to activate it. What kind of exquisite scene were all of them about to see? Their hearts were pounding in anticipation at the wonderous sights the Audio-Visual Gu must have captured.
They were gathered in a room a bit out of the way of the lodge, which made sense given what they were doing.
Before Yu Sai could activate it, however, a voice spoke to him. "So you are the people who planted that gu worm there..."
They all turned around to see a Rank 2 female Gu Master glaring at them. "You kids think that you're real slick? You're not the first ones to try something like that... and you're not the first ones to be caught. Did you really think that we wouldn't have methods for dealing with such?"
Several of them began to sweat. This was a Rank 2 Gu Master- she could really hurt them, but she only smiled. "Don't worry- I won't touch a hair on your heads. Otherwise people will complain that I'm bullying students." Her smile twisted. "But they don't have such restrictions."
She had been blocking the door, their only hope for salvation and also their only escape route, but now moved to reveal pretty much every single girl in the academy glaring at them, while cracking their knuckles.
Using gu worms was still prohibited in for fighting, but with such a numerical advantage over the boys (Yu Sai had only been able to recruit six of them to join him on his 'righteous crusade'), their fists were more than enough.
Needless to say, Yu Sai and the others had learned their lesson by the time the girls were done. They explained their bruises away as the consequence of sparring with each other, something no one believed but no one did anything about either. Fighting was somewhat encouraged in the academy, and this would've been seen as just 'boys being boys.'
Yu Sai thought that the worst part of the whole ordeal was the fact that they had destroyed the Audio-Visual Gu. So not only did he not get any eye candy, he had completely wasted his chance to get a second gu worm from the academy. As someone with bottom-of-the-barrel aptitude, he would not have many chances to buy one later on in the future.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on
And squandering his opportunity here would negatively affect him given how important having a variety of gu were for a Gu Master. He was now the only person in the class who just one gu worm. And though his prospects were low, it was not like he would be able to do nothing at all- but without more gu, his usefulness had dwindled even further.
As it was, the boys had learned their lesson, and Yu Sai could do nothing but nurse his injuries.
And so, the hot springs retreat ended. The academy elder had wanted to set it up so that the students could interact with each other and strengthen their bonds, with a particular focus on Fang Yuan.
Needless to say, the endeavor had basically pretty much failed in all aspects of what it was trying to achieve. Perhaps you could say that Yu Sai and his gang were closer after their ordeal, or that the girls were closer after beating them up, but that was not intentional on the academy elder's part. Oh well, he would have other plans in the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 58 - 58: Assassination Attempt: Part One
chapters.content:
"Fang Yuan, congratulations on reaching Rank 1 Upper Stage," the academy elder said two days after the trip had ended. It had been quite fruitful for Fang Yuan, if not for anyone else. The prize of thirty primeval stones was graciously accepted by Fang Yuan as the others seethed.
'How did brother reach Rank 1 Upper Stage so fast? I thought he was still refining his second gu worm...' Fang Zheng thought. 'Unless... he was pretending to be behind? Elder brother, you're too crafty!' To straightforward Fang Zheng, such a strategy was unfathomable. If anything, he was the type to brag to anyone and everyone about his progress.
The academy elder clicked his tongue- Fang Yuan had pulled ahead yet again! Still, there was nothing more he could do but praise him. "Well done, as expected of the class president. The rest of you, continue to work hard! The mid-year examination will be approaching soon, and this is an excellent opportunity for all of you to show your skills. This year's task will be hunting for wild boar. You may team up in teams as big as three if you wish, and for each boar tusk you obtain, you will get ten primeval stones." Boar tusks were somewhat valuable, but could only fetch one or two primeval stones at most. This was an opportunity for many of them to earn some extra money.
Excited chatter immediately erupted from the student body like the buzzing of a giant beehive.
'This exam is different- is it because of my regression and changing things?" Fang Yuan thought. The task had been to gather honey, as far as he knew. However, this was ultimately good for him. He could gather meat and primeval stones in one fell swoop!
"Do you want to team up?" Yu Sai asked Li Mei. Both of them were trash D-grade talents, and would be hard-pressed to show a good performance on their lonesome. Li Mei hadn't forgotten about how Yu Sai had tried to peep on the other girls, but because they were part of the 'Fang Yuan Alliance' he likely felt that he had at least a moderately good chance of winning her over. The girls hated him, and many of the boys did as well (even if they secretly admired his guts) especially those who had taken a beating with him.
Li Mei sighed. 'How good would it be if I could be paired with the class president... but that's all just a pipe dream.' The four big shots would all be working alone and competing against one another. Because of that, she agreed.
However, even for this contest Fang Yuan was still a favorite to win. He had won everything flawlessly up to this point, and by now, an image of invincibility had been carved into the student body's minds. Even those like Mo Bei and Chi Chen were somewhat demoralized by his success.
There was someone who was having an even harder time because of Fang Yuan's success though- his uncle!
Uncle had ran into several problems lately. For one, people had taken Fang Yuan's comments that he had trained him quite seriously, and because of this random people kept approaching him on the street or when he was outside.
"Sir!" a very muscular Gu Master once asked him in a tavern. "I would like to challenge you to a martial arts contest!"
Uncle began sweating heavily. If he fought this man, he would certainly lose, and so, he took the man aside and said, "Ah, whatever issue you have with me, I'm sure we can resolve it without fighting. If you're in need of primeval stones..."
"No, no," the man said. "I'm not here because I am eyeing your assets! No, I merelly wish to improve myself by challenging the strongest martial artists the village has to offer!"
"Why are you challenging me then..."
"I have heard great praise from the martial arts instructor about the teacher of his best student- Fang Yuan! I wished to see your skill for myself!"
"Ah, no that's not true at all," Uncle said. "I... I don't have much talent when it comes to martial arts."
"Please, there is no need for Sir to be humble. I merely wish to fight a simple bought with you..."
If Uncle fought a bought, he would absolutely be crushed. And sensing weakness, after that, people who were after his assets would soon pop out of the woodwork to challenge him. He couldn't draw attention to himself like that.
"No, no, you misunderstand, I uh, was skilled back in my day but... after my injury and the loss of my Rank 3 cultivation my physical abilities were also sadly weakened... I can do nothing but train the next generation now and I'm afraid I would only disappoint you..."
"Is that so?"
The man left, but that was not the end of Uncle's worries.
Two days later, a man approached him with his son, about ten years old. "Sir! I would like you to train my son in martial arts! He is quite talented, and I wanted to find the best teacher for him, and so we have come to you!"
"Ah no.... my days of teaching are long behind me..." Uncle said wearily.
"Don't worry, Father," the kid said. "I know- this is how martial arts stories always work! The old master refuses to teach his disciple, until he challenges him. What do you want as a test? To take a pebble from your hand? Or to pluck a feather from your belt? Or a direct spar?" The kid, in a rush of exuberance, kicked Uncle in the shin, expecting him to block it.Thɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
Uncle would've beaten the kid on the spot if his father wasn't there! His knee still hurt from that incident.
Uncle confronted Fang Yuan about this while the latter was out and about. "Fang Yuan, stop spreading lies and slander about me!"
"Lies and slander? What are you talking about? This filial nephew is only trying to give Uncle some face."
"Filial my foot! If you were truly filial you would've given up on the inheritance! And please... stop giving me face!" Uncle said.
It was of little use, however. People knew the relationship between Fang Yuan and Uncle was not good- meaning that they took his praise to be the real thing. If Fang Yuan had said negative things about Uncle, it would be easy to dismiss- but praise from an enemy had to be genuine, no? Not to mention people assumed that someone had had to have trained Fang Yuan, and who else could've done so?
