He could dispel their notions by losing, but how would he show his face to the village then? And then he would get a reputation as someone who was easy to bully. He could kiss the assets he had gotten from Fang Yuan's parents goodbye then.
It had gotten to the point where Uncle avoided leaving the house.
He had a bigger worry though- it seemed that Fang Yuan had not made a mistake, and was even rising in ranks rapidly.
If Fang Yuan was still a C-grade talent, Uncle wouldn't have been as worried as Fang Yuan would be easily dealt with. But with his 'B-grade talent', Uncle was under a large amount of pressure.
He tossed and turned in bed for many nights, losing sleep over it. One solution came to mind- only one, but did he really want to go down that route?
The more he thought about it, the more his stomach turned. But, he knew that not only his fortune, but his life would be in peril if Fang Yuan was allowed to advance. If Fang Yuan became an elder wouldn't that be the end for him and his wife? At the very least, they would lose all of their inheritance. As for Fang Zheng, he would be led astray by Shen Cui- that girl had a tight hold upon him, and that meant that Fang Zheng would eventually leave. What would they do without his direct protection, or if Fang Yuan struck at them before Fang Zheng could retaliate?
He was already in this state, it would only get worse as time passed.
'This is just self defense...' he thought to himself, finally steeling his resolve. He had to do what he had to do.
He had to kill Fang Yuan!

chapters.title: Chapter 59 - 59: Assassination Attempt: Part Two
chapters.content:
Of course, even if Uncle had come to the conclusion that he had to kill Fang Yuan, he would not go through with it himself. For one, he had sold most of his gu worms to cut down on the cost of maintaining them. Not to mention he lacked the skillset after being idle for so long- and if he was caught, the punishment would be severe. To be tortured for seven days and nights before being killed- that was the punishment for trying to kill a fellow clan member! After all, blood was thicker than water, and in this world it was through clan ties that one could survive in this world.
As such, those who tried to kill fellow clan members were the lowest of the low- lower than scum! And if he was killed, his wife would be executed summarily as well. She was a mortal after all, and only through her affiliation with him did she have some veneer of protection.
Above all, he was not an experienced fighter even when he had been younger. He was not someone like Fang Yuan who had taken countless lives. He feared that when the time came to strike, he might hesitate with giving the final blow. Especially given this was after all, his own nephew.
The solution, then, obviously, was to get someone else to do it for him?
But who? Who could he trust? He was so secretive with this idea of his that he had not even informed his wife of what he was plotting. You couldn't just go around with a signpost saying 'assassin wanted.' How did people even arrange for these kinds of things?
However, after searching for several weeks in the seedier parts of Gu Yue Village, he was able to find out from a drunkard about how to get in contact with someone who would do something- anything- for the right price. A demonic cultivator who functioned as muscle-for higher. The drunkard didn't even remember the conversation the next day, but Uncle had found out how to contact the man.
And so, one month, under the light of a crescent moon, he wandered out of the village to its outer boundaries, whereupon, an hour later, a shadow jumped out of the darkness behind him.
Uncle froze, feeling the chill of death behind him. "Is... is it you?"
"Yes," a voice said, as someone walked out of the shadows. The aura of a Rank 3 Gu Master emanated from this figure who was dressed from head to toe in black rags. "I do not know you stranger- though the fact that you're here means that you are up to no good."
"Who.... who are you?"
"I go by many names. Dark Claw. Night Shadow. Black Dagger. The Gu Master Formerly Known As Dark Claw after that other demonic Gu Master accused me of stealing his name. For now though, I simply call myself Noir Wings!"
"...never heard of you..." Uncle said.
"Yes, well, I keep changing my name, hoping to find something that's cooler than the last, something that leaves a lasting impression, you know," Noir Wings said. "Something more mysterious..."
"I need a job done," Uncle said, getting to the point.
"Then you have come to the right place," Noir Wings said.
"It's a tough job- and risky."
"I am no stranger to risk," Noir Wings said. "When I was a child, my village underwent a famine, and my parents abandoned me in the wilderness. There, I was adopted by a pack of wolves who took me in as one of their own; but then who also abandoned me two weeks later. Then, I managed to find the inheritance of a Rank 3 Gu Master, but then a Gu Master discovered it too and then beat me up before tossing me aside. But when he did so, I managed to find the inheritance of a Rank 5 Gu Master, and I cultivated until I was Rank 3. I then went to go take revenge on my village for abandoning me, only to see that it had already been destroyed by wolves six months earlier. I then went to go take revenge on the Gu Master who beat me, only to see that he had already been killed by another Gu Master. I then went to go take revenge on the wolf pack for abandoning me, but they had been chased out and killed by a pack of bears. Since then, I have wandered this world, a lone demon on a journey looking for purpose. An odyssey over a phantom sea filled with perils and nightmares, only my own wits and judgement to guide me-"
Noir Wings was stopped in his tracks as there was a loud noise.
"What was that? A bear?" Uncle wondered.
"No, that was my stomach- I haven't eaten anything in several days," Noir Wings said. "Do you have anything to eat?"
"...there's some beef jerky I brought along..."
"Many thanks," Noir Wings said. "Being a demonic cultivator isn't easy... I need food... and oftentimes can't get it... so what is this job you need?"
Uncle gulped, scared to even say it. Were there eyes or investigative gu watching him right now? If so, he would be heavily implicated in a crime. "I need you to kill someone."
"Fine, but my only rule is that I don't do children- unless the child in question is a jerk, for which I'll make an exception," Noir Wings said.
"This is him," Uncle said, handing Noir Wings a sketch of Fang Zheng- which was a sketch of Fang Yuan for all intents and purposes. "Five days from now, there will be an examination out in the fields. He'll be vulnerable then."
This would be the best and only opportunity to strike at Fang Yuan. He had a tendency to wander the village, but no one could get to him there obviously. When he wandered outside of the village, Uncle would not know where and when he was going out. Once he graduated it would be even more difficult as he would gain access to more powerful gu worms, and would be accompanied by teammates. An 'accident' could always happen then, but one could not rely on that. And that would mean collaborating with a few other people, which he absolutely did not want to do.
"The exam will be guarded, but mostly by Rank 2 Gu Masters," Uncle said. "Are you up for the job?"
"Definitely."
"Oh, and one thing- make sure that you target Fang Yuan and not Fang Zheng. They look alike, being twins, but Fang Yuan will have a golden moonlight gu pin on his chest, not silver, understood?"
"Now... about payment..."
"Here," Uncle said, handing over five hundred primeval stones. "This much now, and the rest later."
"Whoa- that's a lot of primeval stones," Noir Wings said, his voice changing as he broke character for a moment. He would've been willing to do it for half of this amount. Being a demonic cultivator really was hard and one had to scrounge and scrape for resources.
"Oh Lord..." Uncle said, beginning to think that he had made a mistake- not in trying to kill Fang Yuan, but hiring this guy to do it. The fact that he was this shocked by that amount proved that he was likely quite hopeless. He had been willing to pay more of course, but
"Wait, say that again?"
"Oh?"
"No, after that."Thɪs
"Lord?"
"Yes, wait," Noir Wings said. "Lord... I wanted a mysterious name... Lord... Mysteries... Mysteries... Lord.... I feel like there's a really cool name there, but just on the tip of my tongue..." Noir Wings said. "I know! Mysterious Lord! Aha! Yes, that's what I'll call myself now!"

chapters.title: Chapter 60 - 60: Assassination Attempt: Part Three
chapters.content:
The second day of the exam was underway. The exam took place over the course of several days, with students vying to be the one who killed the greatest number of boar.
Fang Yuan was currently in the lead, though Fang Zheng was close behind. There had been a few accidents up till now, but nothing serious.
The exam took place in a forest a bit of a distance from the village. Given this, several Rank 2 Gu Masters were scattered about to keep a close eye on the students and make sure that there were no big mishaps. Some Rank 3 elders were even near a central command fort set up by the academy elder.
Hunting boar was naturally difficult, even with the help of moonblades. Most students had chosen to work in groups, and yet, Fang Yuan was still pulling ahead- likely as a result of his Liquor Worm and higher cultivation realm- up till now, only Fang Zheng had managed to catch up to him and become Rank 1 Upper Stage.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
But, that meant that Fang Yuan's advantage with the Liquor Worm would soon be gone.
Fang Zheng was in good spirits thinking of this as he went to the tent reserved for the class president and vice-presidents. It was not very grand, but was more than what the other students got. Which was practically nothing.
"Oh?" he said as he noticed something lying on the ground. A golden moonlight gu pin. "Brother left this lying here..." It was unlike Fang Yuan to drop or lose things, but it wasn't like it couldn't happen.
Immediately, Fang Zheng was struck with a thought. Something that he'd wanted to try ever since he was young, but had never actually done.
He put the golden pin on his uniform, pocketing his own silver pin, and then walked outside, trying to mimic Fang Yuan's behavior.
"Class president, greetings!"
Many people deferred their respect to him. It was quite nice to be though of as 'class president' and not 'vice-president.'
'If brother asks why I'm wearing this, I'll just say he dropped it and I was going to return it,' Fang Zheng thought. 'Is this how it feels like to be him? It feels... like everyone's scared of me! But they respect me too.'
As Fang Zheng walked to go hunt boar, Mo Bei shot him a cold look that surprised him. Right, he looked exactly like Fang Yuan now and the two of them did not have a good relationship.
Fang Zheng wandered away from the central area, always under the watchful gaze of the invigilators.
As he walked further and further away from the beaten track, eyes were locked onto him.
"Ah, I can't believe we're stuck here with babysitting these kids," a Gu Master in the bushes sighed.
"Keep your chin up, we have to be on guard for attacks."
"Puh-lease, who would attack anyone here?"
"There's Fang Zheng you know, the A-grade talent. The others would love to strike a blow against him."
"Yeah, but we're deep in our territory. There's no way that they would strike at us."
As he said that, Fang Zheng felt something swiftly fly over his head and imbed itself in a nearby tree.
The two Gu Masters hiding immediately stood up, feeling the sudden appearance of the aura of a Rank 3 Gu Master!
Reinforcements arrived in the form of two more Rank 2 Gu Masters, who quickly signaled the main headquarters.
"You," a shadowy figure said, leaping out of the woods. Whatever concealment gu he was using was now disabled as he was fully visible dressed almost entirely in black. Fang Zheng looked to see that what had nearly struck his head had been a long white rod- this was clearly some kind of projectile gu worm!
Panic began to set, and the Rank 2 Gu Masters yelled for Fang Zheng to run.
"Ah, the shadows lengthen," the man said. "It seems that fortune saved you from that blow, but I will have your head as of yet. Sneak attack!" He yelled out, striking at Fang Zheng again, though the Gu Masters blocked it. "Hmm...? Who is it that dares to fight the legendary... the one and only... Lord of the Mysteries?" He had realized that that name sounded much better than Mysterious Lord and went with it, striking a cool pose.
Finally, after so long thinking of a cool name for himself- he had found one that he felt that he could commit himself to. 'Lord of the Mysteries'- it was without a doubt very cool.
"If you're going to sneak attack someone, don't announce it before you do it! What's the point of announcing it then?" a Gu Master sneered.
"You make a compelling argument, however, I just emerged from closed door dual cultivation with your mother," Lord of the Mysteries said.
"Why you-"
"I have been tasked with eliminating that boy over there," Lord of the Mysteries said, moving to strike 'Fang Yuan' who had run away out of earshot. "I have no quarrel with you, as a matter of fact, I would rather to leave some witnesses alive so that you may spread word of my fame far and about. What say you? Stand down, and let me kill Fang Yuan and I will spare you."
"Hah- as if we'd ever!"
Two more reinforcements arrived.
"Good, good, good, just like your mother, I have no problem taking on multiple people at once," Lord of the Mysteries said. "Take this! Rank 3 Testicular Torsion Gu!"
A gu worm flew from his aperture, and snaked its way up a nearby Gu Master's pants, who then began screaming.
"Fiend!"
"How dare you!"
Moonblades flew at Lord of the Mysteries, though using a movement-based gu worm he nimbly avoided them and chased after 'Fang Yuan.'
He prepared his next attack. He was using Rank 2 Javelin Gu to attack Fang Zheng, though with the constant movement of running around, not only was it hard for the enemy moonblades to hit him, but also hard for him to hit his own target.
News quickly spread via an information-type gu worm to the Academy Elder. "We're under attack! A Rank 3 Gu Master has emerged to attack Fang Yuan!"
"Who could it be? The Bai or Xiong clan?"
"What does it matter- we'll find out later, let's behead the rascal first!"
"Wait," the academy elder said. With enough numbers, Rank 2 Gu Masters could wear down and eventually kill a Rank 3 Gu Master, depending on the enemy's skill level.
However, that was the question. How strong was this enemy? If they were confident enough to attack in a place like this, they had to be skilled.
But there was something that was off...
"That man is targeting Fang Yuan but... wouldn't the enemy's main target be Fang Zheng? No, what if this is a ploy by the enemy? What if they're actually after Fang Zheng? Both Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng look the same, so this could be the enemy's error. Or do they want to divide our forces to sneak attack Fang Zheng?" Fang Yuan was somewhat valuable, but Fang Zheng more so. Also, the amount of information that could be passed was rather limited- he did not know the full details of the issue such as the fact that the assassin said he was after Fang Yuan and not Fang Zheng. As it was, he would never have suspected so.
There were many irregularities however, in what was going on, which gave him an uneasy feeling.
There was a simple explanation for this all though - the assassin was just really dumb. However, there was no way that a ma like him would rest easy thinking like that.
"Where is Fang Zheng right now?"
"We don't know..."
"Damn it! Keep... keep most of our forces here. Send a small party to reinforce the people shielding Fang Yuan," the academy elder said through gritted teeth. Fang Yuan would just have to hope that he would be lucky enough to survive- between an A-grade and a B-grade talent, it was obvious who was more important. "And most importantly, find Fang Zheng!" It was imperative that they form a defensive core around Fang Zheng to protect him.

chapters.title: Chapter 61 - 61: Assassination Attempt: Part Four
chapters.content:
Meanwhile, Fang Zheng screamed as he had been hit by a javelin in the left leg, leaving it hard for him to move. His eyes widened as Lord of the Mysteries prepared the final blow.
Though, as he was about to skewer Fang Zheng's head, one of the Gu Masters managed to land a moonblade, neatly nicking his left leg, and causing the javelin to strike Fang Zheng's abdomen instead.
If Fang Zheng was in medieval times on Earth, this blow would still be fatal as some of his bowel loops were perforated and he would certainly develop peritonitis. As it was here though, such a wound could be patched up so long as he got to a healer in time.
As for Lord of the Mysteries, he had exhausted his primeval essence in chasing down 'Fang Yuan.' He took out a primeval stone, but would the others give him time to recover?
Of course not!
Moonblades flew at him, many of them now hitting their mark as the Gu Masters rushed to cover Fang Zheng. 'I shouldn't have used my Rank 3 Testicular Torsion Gu so quickly- that was my trump card!' Lord of the Mysteries thought to no avail. Aside from his stealth gu worm, that was his only Rank 3 gu worm. All the rest of his gu worms were Rank 2; there was a reason he was so desperate for primeval stones, after all. He had essentially been stranded near the mountain when his other Rank 3 gu worms had died when he had been unable to feed them.
However, he had greatly underestimated the difficulty of this task.
The other Gu Masters, though only Rank 2, showed excellent teamwork and had a full set of gu worms for the most part. They could also actually recover their primeval essence using primeval stones so long as one of them covered for the other.
It looked like he was cornered.
"You might call yourself Lord of the Mysteries- but the only thing that you'll be remembered as- is the Fool!" a Gu Master declared.
With a swift motion, that Gu Master beheaded Lord of the Mysteries.
While this was going on, the real Fang Yuan leisurely walked into camp. Naturally, he was spotted by someone who had been looking for Fang Zheng. "Fang Zheng- thank goodness we found you! You need to get to safety immediately!"
Fang Yuan frowned, but for the time being, did not correct the Gu Master. If there was danger, why would he loiter around just to correct this guy? Obviously, it was more important that he get to safety!
"Academy elder, we've brought Fang Zheng!"
The academy elder rushed in to ensure that Fang Zheng was alright, and then paused.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
Although someone else might've been fooled at how close the two brothers' appearances were, he had spent enough time with them to be able to distinguish them based on their facial expressions. He said, rather slowly, the gears in his head turning, "You are not Fang Zheng?"
"That is correct, academy elder, I am Gu Yue Fang Yuan," Fang Yuan said. He looked around and saw that most of the other students had already been brought back to the headquarters- though Fang Zheng was not among them. Clearly there had been a case of mistaken identity.
The academy elder's face blanched. That meant that the person he had abandoned to his fate... immediately he felt his heart erupt in anger. "Fang Yuan! Why are you so late to the examination?"
"Oh, an old lady's cat was stuck in a tree on the roadside while I was walking here, and so I stopped to help," Fang Yuan said nonchalantly.
If it had been someone else, the academy elder would've given that student a good lecture and perhaps even a thrashing given his mood for saying such a blatant lie- but this was Fang Yuan, and the way that Fang Yuan said it... he didn't seem to be making it up!
And for that matter, it was 100% true. While Fang Yuan had been walking towards the location where the exam was being held, the system suddenly told him that he could get yet another Red Steel Relic Gu if he helped this old lady get her cat out of a tree.
While Fang Yuan had been regularly delinquent in the past, ever since becoming class president, he had been quite regular with showing up and had rarely if ever shirked his duties. Even Fang Yuan was bound by the role that he had been given and had to play the part. That was because he needed those ten primeval stones a week. However, he was more than willing to be late if the benefits were high enough- and a Red Steel Relic Gu was more than worth it.
However, this kind of action was somewhat consistent with what the academy elder had heard of Fang Yuan, so he moved onto something else.
"And what about your class president pin?"
"That- oh, I think I misplaced it during yesterday's hunt," Fang Yuan said. 'It is odd- several weird things happened today. For one, I woke up late, two, I had forgotten the pin which is unlike how I usually do things. Three, doing something as simple as helping a cat out of a tree got me a Red Steel Relic Gu? Clearly there is something greater at foot here.' By now he had pieced things together enough to the point where he was rather certain as to what was going on, but still chose to play dumb.
The academy elder no longer bothered wasting his time with Fang Yuan-he was the most experienced healer here and he rushed to go find Fang Zheng.
Fang Yuan was filled in on what was going on from the other students. 'Heh... it seems that I got quite lucky avoiding it. Maybe that Luck stat isn't worthless at all. Though, why did someone want to kill Fang Zheng? This did not happen in my old life... is this something that I changed?"
The Gu Masters returned with the corpse of the assassin and Fang Zheng, whose stomach was badly injured.
The academy elder's face paled when he saw this- it was not that the wound couldn't be healed, but it looked like Fang Zheng's aperture had been damaged! That would be far harder to fix than the damaged organs.
It was to such an extent that the clan head himself came to investigate.
"It seems that there was only this lone assassin and no one else," the scouts said after scouring the area. That said, there could still be more Rank 3 Gu Masters with stealth-type gu worms lurking around, and no one wanted to take chances.
Naturally, the exam was cancelled.

chapters.title: Chapter 62 - 62: Assassination Attempt: Part Five
chapters.content:
"What is the status of Fang Zheng's recovery?" the clan head asked the academy elder, worry etched into his face as he saw the latter's ashen expression.
"He will live but... his aperture has been damaged. He's fallen all the way back to Rank 1 Initial Stage, and it looks like his aptitude has fallen from A-grade to C-grade," the academy elder replied.
"Is there nothing that can be done?"
"Perhaps if we had one of the famous four great doctors of this Southern Border, they could do something," the academy elder said with a bitter tone. Such a thing was just wishful thinking. The aperture was a mysterious area and not many people knew much about it, simply because doing research upon it was difficult. Even those four might've been helpless in this situation. "I guess those Xiong and Bai clan bastards are belly-jingling with laughter right about now..."
"I don't think it was either of them," the clan head said. "The evidence doesn't seem to suggest such."
"What?" the academy elder asked, surprised. This was news to him. "Who else but them would have the motive to do something like this?"
The clan head shook his head. "We examined the body of the assassin. He had no markings which would identify him as belonging to either clan. If anything, he was malnourished and looked like he was on his last legs. And the most important part though- after reviewing statements from many witnesses, is the fact that he was extremely incompetent with his job. Were it not the case, he would've succeeded in finishing Fang Zheng off. Now tell me, why would the Xiong or Bai clans hire someone to do this job who was terrible at it and was also so weak? Furthermore, although they didn't have the necessary gu worms to record it, it seems the assassin was after Fang Yuan, not Fang Zheng."
"Fang Yuan? Why Fang Yuan?"
"I cannot tell, and it's only conjecture because the person in question doesn't remember things exactly," the clan head said. This was an era without cameras and the like, and without the appropriate gu worm it was hard to record things exactly.
"But why try to assassinate Fang Yuan?"
"Who knows? We can only ask him."
Fang Yuan was interrogated four times over, but had been able to give them no useful information.
He was allowed to see the body of the assassin, and did not recognize the person in question. The only person that he could think who might have cause to go against him in this timeline were the relatives of that mortal boy he had killed- but if he had the backing of a Rank 3 Gu Master he wouldn't have had to resort to such schemes to win the affection of a mortal woman.
The thought that his uncle was behind it did not even cross his mind- simply because based on what Fang Yuan knew, his uncle lacked the courage to do something like this. He was experienced, but not omniscient, after all.
'This man is a demonic path cultivator, but I had never heard of him during this time. Countless Gu Masters exist, of course... but why target me? Unless they were all mistaken and he just threw around the fact he was targeting me as an excuse?'
The confusion around the incident muddled it even further, to the fact that to everyone's disappointment, no clear answer could be found.
Everyone's disappointment, that is, other than Uncle.
He was sweating bullets almost constantly, jumping at nearly every single shadow around him. He had been genuinely shocked when he received news that Fang Zheng had been injured and the assassin he had hired had been killed.
Any minute now, he expected the clan to put the pieces together and come to snatch him away! He had made a grave mistake hiring that idiot- who knew what kind of clues he had left behind?
The longer nothing happened, the more worried he got.
"Husband, Fang Zheng has been crippled and is nothing more than C-grade trash now, what was the point of raising him then?" Aunt asked, but he ignored her for now.
Right now, he tried to play the part of a caring and nurturing uncle fully, simply to mask his own guilt.
In reality, he had nothing to worry about. Lord of the Mysteries had his headquarters hidden well enough that in the expanse of the mountain, it was nearly impossible to find. And he had left no clues for that matter- the bag of primeval stones that were left behind had been unmarked, after all.
"I can only apologize and bow my head for my failure," the academy elder said to the other elders during a meeting as he lowered his head. He had let an A-grade talent be crippled- the one greatest hope they had of nurturing someone who could rival the Bai clan's Bai Ning Bing. If he had perhaps made a move faster, Fang Zheng could've been saved from his fate. Moreover, he was in charge of the exam, and any mishaps that happened naturally fell on his head.
"Raise your head," the clan head said. "No one here blames you. if anything, the person behind this scheme was too crafty and pulled the wool over all of our eyes." In reality it was the opposite- the person behind the scheme had been extremely dumb and the only reason they hadn't been caught yet was that no one thought that anyone could be that dumb, thereby ironically saving them from suspicion. Nearly everyone was certain that there was a greater conspiracy at foot. "But, we cannot let this matter slide like this. That is why I have reached out to Ti Xue Leng."
"The famous investigator himself?"
The TIe clan was one of the largest clans of the Southern Border, and was famous for upholding justice and had brought countless demonic cultivators to justice. Ti Xue Leng was a Rank 5 Gu Master who wandered the Southern Border, upholding the values of his clan. Naturally, he had many demands upon him, and could not come immediately, but once he was done settling his other matters he had promised to look into their matter.
"Will he really come?"
"Promises are just talk, after all. And what would he care about breaking his word with a village like ours?"The most update n0vels are published on novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"No, I think based on his reputation, he truly wishes to uphold justice," the clan head said. "And, I have offered an adequate price for his aide."
The elders paused. A price that could entice a Rank 5 Gu Master- it could not have been small!
"Is it worth it for something like this? Fang Zheng has already been crippled, what use is it in spending so much over spilt milk?"
The clan head shook his head. "If word gets out that we did nothing, it will be seen that our Gu Yue clan is easy to bully, or that we could not deal with a demonic cultivator ourselves." The other clans, naturally, had denied their involvement- though no one in the room believed them for even an instant.
With time, Uncle's paranoia faded and he was now faced with the decision on what to do with Fang Zheng. He was now a liability, not an asset, to their household.
In some ways, it would have been better if he had died. In this world, which was quite different from Earth, where strength was everything, it was better to be dead than to be crippled. Those who died to save their clans were remembered as heroes. Those who had been gravely injured and remained, while treated nicely initially, would eventually be forgotten and even mocked by those whom they had saved. Without strength to back up their position, they would eventually become helpless.
Fang Zheng felt this acutely. He had earlier been soaring high based on his A-grade talent, even if he had temporarily been suppressed by his elder brother. But, it was as if a new world had now opened up to him. A world that had suddenly turned cold as he was seen as nothing better than average.
He had great difficulty dealing with the fact that he was now considered ordinary, and had reverted back to his former status before the awakening.
To those who had been honored, dishonor was worse than death! His gu worms had all been destroyed when his aperture had been damaged, and he did not even have the primeval stones to buy more. No one was willing to help him anymore, as he was no longer A-grade. His classmates who used to look up to him, now had odd looks on their faces whenever they saw him. Of disdain, of smugness, and worst of all- of pity. Fang Zheng hated the pitiful looks more than anything else.

chapters.title: Chapter 63 - 63: Fang Zheng's Downfall: Part One
chapters.content:
If such a thing had happened to Fang Yuan and not Fang Zhen, he would not have been bothered in the slightest save for the decline in his ability. The scorn or praises of the world meant nothing to Fang Yuan, but Fang Zhen was not like that.
To Fang Zheng, the whispers, the taunts, the mockery- it all was too much to handle.
"Heh, look at him, was so high and mighty- but heaven brought him down!"
"Fang Zheng, you're back to only being Rank 1 Initial Stage? Even the D-grade talents have left you behind!"
"A Gu Master with no gu worms- what a joke!"
"Fang Zheng, you failure, when I was your age I was already sixteen years old!"
"Fang Zheng, why can't you at least be as good-looking as your brother?"
"Fang Zheng, I'm sorry to hear about what happened to you... but I need you to pay me back for lunch that time, okay? Half a primeval stone will do."
The only thing that people wanted to see more than a genius, was to see a genius fall!
His aptitude had fell from 80% to 46%, meaning that his prospects for the future were greatly limited.The most update n0vels are published on ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
He had gone from soaring high in the skies to once again trailing behind in his brother's shadow, like he had been doing until then in life. Was he fated to always be second-best to his brother? Encountering the Lord of the Mysteries had caused him to enter a circle of inevitability- one where he continued to be nothing better than a cheap knockoff of his brother.
Fang Zheng was so worried by all of this that he started having the strangest dreams.
"Fang Zheng, good that you arrived here," the clan elder said to him one day. Next to him was a strange person who had a lot of hair- did they have some kind of disease? The hair covered almost every part of their body, even their eyelids. "Unfortunately, since you're no longer an A-grade talent, you can't protect the village. And so, we needed to find some other way to defend the village. This is a female hairy man, and we've decided to make a military alliance with them. The hairy men are extremely powerful and our only hope of surviving against the Bai and Xiong clan. However, this alliance came with a price. She demanded... your hand in marriage. Please don't resist, Fang Zheng, we need you to do this for the sake of the village."
Fang Zheng was shocked. So, all that hair wasn't some kind of disease?
"What? But... but... I don't wanna marry a female hairy man!"
"Fang Zheng, this is all for the good of the village, please don't resist," Uncle said.
"Yes, we all need to make sacrifices for the village. If only you were still an A-grade talent this wouldn't have to happen, but who can change what fate does? Now, this is the only way that we can reliably save ourselves," Aunt said.
"Also, didn't you always want us to treat you better? Here, we're treating you just like a princess- by marrying you off to secure a military alliance," Uncle said. "You can't possibly complain about that."
"B-But, I always wanted to marry Shen Cui!" Fang Zheng protested. "She's the only woman who'll ever be in my heart!"
"It's okay, my love," Shen Cui said, wiping the tears from her eyes. "I will cherish you in my heart always, even if you marry someone else. For this village, we have to sacrifice our love, no matter how pure and noble it is."
The female hairy man licked her lips as she saw Fang Zheng. He shuddered at the thought of what was going through her mind.
"NO....!"
Three Months Later
Fang Zheng found his lower abdomen suddenly swelling up, not knowing what it was that caused it. He was also nauseous and vomiting constantly. That was, until someone else noticed.
"Oh, husband, it looks like you're finally bearing the fruit of our love!" his 'wife' said. "You're pregnant!"
"What?!" Fang Zheng said, astonished. "But... I'm a man!"
"Don't you know? When it comes to hairy men, the males get pregnant instead of the females!" she replied. "Oh, I hope that it's a boy!"
"NO....!"
Six Months Later
Fang Zheng held his newborn son in his arms. The baby was squirming after he had exited Fang Zheng's belly, drooling all the while.
"Nine months of staying in my body making me suffer- and he looks like his stupid mom!"
"Guague..." the baby said in response, oblivious to what Fang Zheng was thinking.
Five Years Later
"Papa! Papa!" Fang Zheng's son said, watching him leave. "Where are you going?"
"I've mastered a new immortal killer move son- it's called 'Patriarch Goes to Fetch Milk' a technique that combines the profundities of both movement and stealth. Don't worry, I'll be back after I've gotten the milk, okay? Looks like we've ran out."
"Okay!"
Fang Zheng then left, never to return.
Fang Zheng then woke up in a cold sweat.
'That was such a bizarre dream!' he thought to himself. 'It's okay, I can relax... there's no way something like that would ever happen.'
While he was thinking such and rolled over in bed, going back to sleep, there was harsh knocking at his door.
"Fang Zheng! You rascal! Open up!" his uncle's voice could be heard loud and clear.
Fang Zheng felt that he had just woken up, although it had been a few hours judging from the daylight. He opened up the door to see his uncle and aunt there, glaring at him angrily. They had not looked at him like that since before the Awakening Ceremony.
"What's going o-" before he could finish, his uncle slapped him across the face.
"Scoundrel! You dare ask what it is that you did wrong after what you did to Shen Cui?"
"What? What happened to Shen Cui? I didn't do anything to her-" If anything, Fang Zheng became worried that something or someone had done something to hurt Shen Cui- not realizing that this was clearly a setup. He even though that it might've been Fang Yuan disguised as himself.
"Liar! Let's see what she has to say for ourselves!" Fang Zheng was dragged downstairs.
Downstairs, Shen Cui had her face buried in Mother Shen's arms, and she was sobbing. Mother Shen glared at him.
"Shen Cui! Tell us what you told me earlier- don't worry about Fang Zheng, I won't let him harm you... this I swear upon my honor!" Uncle said.
Shen Cui looked up, face bedew with tears. "He... Fang Zheng he.... he used to force himself on me... he's done it multiple times. I... I asked him to stop but... he wouldn't. He said that if I ever... complained, he would kill me. He said that he had always wanted me, and that now... he was a Gu Master... he would make me suffer if I didn't agree... and stand down... as he violated me!" She then burst into tears and then buried her face in Mother Shen's arms once again.
Her performance was so convincing that if Fang Zheng had not known the truth, he would've instantly believed her.
It was only now that he realized that he had been set up.

chapters.title: Chapter 64 - 64: Fang Zheng's Downfall: Part Two
chapters.content:
"No... no... Cui-Cui, what are you saying? Didn't you say that you loved me and willingly wanted to give yourself to me? Didn't you-"
Fang Zheng got no further as Uncle slapped him again. Even if Fang Zheng had gu worms on him he would not have dared to use them at that moment. That was how deeply he had been indoctrinated to fear the two of them.
"Silence! Insolent brat- to think that not only did your aunt and I take you in, feed and shelter you, and even adopt you as our own son- only for you to do this kind of crime!? From now on, we are disowning you! Consider our relationship to be finished!"
"Indeed, husband, we don't need this kind of son! I had always regretted that we had no one to carry on our bloodline- but it's better that we had no children than to have a child like Fang Zheng!"
Fang Zheng protested. "Mother! Father! It's not true! She has no evidence-"
"Her tears are all the evidence one needs! Fang Zheng, if you dare even show your face here again, I'll chop your head off myself!" Uncle said.
Fang Zheng was roughly thrown out onto the street, his few belongings following him. "And don't come back!"
The door to their house was shut as he slowly got up.
"Is that Fang Yuan?"
"Heh- no way; that loser's Fang Zheng."
"Just take a look at him, if I were him I'd have ran into the woods out of shame."
"And did you hear what he did to that poor servant girl?"
"Oh? He's that kind of monster? Good riddance then!"
"Indeed, heaven is fair and balanced, punishing someone with a wicked heart like that!"
As if to add insult to injury, it began to rain.
Fang Zheng was at a loss of what to do. His primeval stones wouldn't be replenished until a few days, and he had nowhere to go. He could stay in the dorm, but then what would he do about food? It was only free for mealtimes during the academy hours. He also had no gu worms, only a C-grade talent, and no friends to rely on. He had asked for the academy to replace even one of his gu worms, but the academy elder had rejected him. If he had still been A-grade, he was sure that they would make an exception for him, but who would for a mere C-grade talent?
Despite all of these setbacks, he had thought that he could carry on so long as he had Shen Cui's support, but she had turned into a viper and bit him when he had been at his weakest.
If anything, he was sure that a good majority of the class were rejoicing at his failure- Mo Bei, Chi Chen, and Fang Yuan most of all.
As he sulked beneath a tree, wondering what his next step was going to be, the rain only seemed to intensify much like the storm within his heart.
In the story he had been writing, the main character also was going to suffer a setback like this, but an obese merchant by the name of Wang would come to help the main character when he was at his lowest. However, reality was cruel and he was not that main character. His girl had given up on him, and no Fatty Wang would come to his aid.
He was now even lower than what he had been previously- the whole village would not hesitate to spit on him. He would never amount to anything more than a Rank 2 Gu Master now, if even that, with his 46% primeval essence.
His stomach growled yet he barely felt it as he heard footsteps approach. He looked up to see his face reflected at him- a calm, cold face. A face that was not at all bothered by the whimsies of fate.
No, that wasn't his face- that was Fang Yuan!
"So you've found me, huh?" Fang Zheng asked, tears now streaming down his face and melding with the rainwater. "Here to have a good laugh at me? Well then, laugh! Go on!"
But there was no laughter. Instead, Fang Yuan said, "I heard of what happened. You didn't have anything to eat since this morning, did you?" He handed Fang Zheng a parcel of rice and warm chicken- he must've bought it from the nearby inn then. "Here."
Fang Zheng had a dozen questions, but right now, his stomach was growling louder and louder, and he wolfed what was handed to him without even wondering whether or not Fang Yuan would've mixed something into it.
"Feeling better?" Fang Yuan asked.
"...yes..." Fang Zheng said. "Brother... I... was wrong... Aunt and Uncle... and even Shen Cui... they aren't who I thought they were. They were just using me... I really was dumb..."
Fang Zheng did not even have the confidence to face his brother after what he'd done. How could he? How could he look his older brother in the face after breaking ties with him and going against him so often?
"It's good you finally realized that," Fang Yuan said, placing a hand on his shoulder. "Listen, Fang Zheng, this is not the end for you. Nor the end of your journey. With setbacks, we only get the chance to prove ourselves, don't we?"
"But... but... I'm only a C-grade talent now..."
"Talent isn't all there is in this world," Fang Yuan said. "You don't have any gu worms, do you? Even your vital gu was destroyed in battle- you're lucky to be alive right now. However, you are alive- and that is no small things. But, like I was saying, talent isn't everything. There are things which can trump talent. Such as this."
Fang Yuan took out a gu worm that looked like a tiny silkworm- Fang Zheng, though he had never seen it before, could instantly guess what it was. "The Liquor Worm!?"
"Indeed," Fang Yuan said, handing it to Fang Zheng. "Take it. I'm going to give it to you- use it, and you'll soon end up catching back up to where you were before."
"Brother... what... how could you... forgive me this easily? I thought you would be furious at me?"
Fang Yuan embraced him. The warmth felt odd against the cold of the wind and rain. His face did not carry the slightest bit of anger- as if he held no grudges against Fang Zheng for what he had done. "I was never angry with you. I was sad because I was afraid you'd lost your way. Ah, for that incident in the inn; I let my frustration get the best of me. I think you can understand and let bygones be bygones."
Fang Yuan wiped away Fang Zheng's tears.
Seeing this, a nearby beggar almost began sobbing himself. He had gotten alms from Fang Yuan many times in the past, and somewhat knew of the strained relationship between the twins. However, seeing this display of brotherly love and forgiveness, he couldn't help but be moved. Truly, there was no one with a heart of gold like Fang Yuan in all of Gu Yue village- that is what he felt!
"But, won't helping me hurt your reputation?" Fang Zheng asked. Most people thought that he had actually done something to Shen Cui, it seemed. Why would someone with his brother's reputation want to be associated with that?
"What is reputation? Something society hands us? And what of it- I know that you're innocent. Don't worry, Aunt and Uncle will soon get what's coming to them," Fang Yuan reassured him.
"But... don't you need it for yourself?" Fang Zheng asked. The Liquor Worm was very helpful to him, but it would be even more helpful for Fang Yuan.
Fang Yuan shook his head. "You need it more than I do. And it's no problem, I'll make do somehow."
"Is that so... are you sure?"
"Of course I'm sure!"Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Fang Zheng took the Liquor Worm, and having been refined by Fang Yuan, it easily entered his aperture. Quickly, it bonded to him and became his vital gu.
"I think you need some primeval stones, right?" Fang Yuan asked, handing him three.
"I'll pay you back once I get the next payout from the academy..."
"No need to bother, consider it a reconciliation gift," Fang Yuan said, waving his hand. "I want you to remember- not everything is over, alright? Your journey has just started, and the future may soon bring suprises that you wouldn't imagine. Ren Zu did not give up so long as he had Hope in his heart, and you shouldn't either. Alright, if you need anything else, just let me know, alright? Now that we two brothers are together again, who can possibly stop us?"
"Oh... okay..." Fang Zheng said.

chapters.title: Chapter 65 - 65: Fang Zheng's Downfall: Part Three
chapters.content:
News of what had happened to Fang Zheng had spread quickly throughout the village- including about him reconciling with Fang Yuan.
Both Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng were rather famous by this point- Fang Yuan for his role in finding the Flower Wine Monk's inheritance, and Fang Zheng for being an A-grade talent (formerly). Not to mention the news of a Rank 3 demonic Gu Master attacking was without a doubt, going to cause quite a stir. Especially as no one knew who had been behind the attack and speculation was rampant. It was the number one topic of discussion for quite some time.
In the academy, people were more interested in the fact that Fang Zheng and Fang Yuan had apparently made up and were now working together. It became news quickly enough that Fang Zheng had been given Fang Yuan's Liquor Worm, and that he was trying to get back on his feet and become Rank 1 Middle Stage once again.
Some people were quite happy to hear this, for various reasons.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ
Mo Bei and Chi Cheng were absolutely delighted- for one, their greatest competition, Fang Zheng, had been knocked out of the ring. Not only that, Fang Yuan had lost his key advantage over them as well, and would now be burdened by having to support Fang Zheng. This was the best case scenario that either of them could've asked for!
Other people were just happy to see the brothers together again.
Some found it odd just how quickly they had gotten over their animosity for each other, but to most of them, it made sense. They were twins after all, how long could they stay mad at each other?
Li Mei found herself in an awkward position. The Fang Zheng faction of the student body had basically collapsed by this point without their leader, and while some of them migrated to the Mo Bei or Chi Cheng factions, most of them followed Fang Zheng and wanted to join the 'Fang Yuan faction.' Li Mei was basically the leader since she was the only one other than Yu Sai who was a member of it, but, the fact of the matter was that she had no real connection to Fang Yuan and when the others asked her for guidance on what they should do, she was tongue-tied.
Some of the girls were worried about the fact that Fang Yuan was supporting someone like Fang Zheng. The rumors of what Fang Zheng had done to Shen Cui had spread far and wide, and some of them believed them.
"I don't believe them, Fang Zheng must've been set up," Li Mei said firmly. "If Fang Yuan says so, it must be true!" She couldn't imagine someone as righteous as Fang Yuan supporting someone who would do something terrible to a woman, even if they were his own twin brother. He was the kind of person who would fight the entire world for what he felt was right, that was her impression of who Fang Yuan was. Moreover, Fang Zheng had not been part of the group led by Yu Sai who had tried to peep on the girls earlier during the hot springs incident, leading credence to her claim.
However, even now, some female Gu Masters would give Fang Zheng dirty looks whenever he wandered outside. What Uncle had done had been a complete fabrication, but it had been somewhat effective nonetheless.
Speaking of, Uncle and Aunt were shocked themselves to see that Fang Zheng had made up with Fang Yuan so quickly. They had tried their hardest to drive a wedge between the two brothers, after all. If he had known it was going to be like that, Uncle might've thought twice about kicking Fang Zheng out.
Even though Fang Zheng had surrendered his claim to his parent's property, they could've still used him somewhat as a pawn against Fang Yuan to restrict him. It wouldn't have been likely to work, especially as Fang Zheng was only a C-grade talent now, but it was still something that they could try.
The reason that Uncle had been so eager to get rid of Fang Zheng was that he had been paranoid that if Fang Zheng stayed around for too long, he would somehow make the connection that Uncle had been the one who ordered the attack on 'Fang Zheng's' life! Either that, or that someone else might figure it out.
As it was, Fang Yuan was a bit surprised that his Uncle would throw out Fang Zheng so quickly- but he was unaware of the true reason behind it. Of course, he had expected that his Uncle would eventually kick Fang Zheng out now that he was a liability rather than an asset, but he had expected a few more schemes from him to prevent him from taking his parent's inheritance before that happened. Fang Yuan still didn't think that his uncle would be capable of ordering a hit like that, and so, could only put this mystery aside for now.
Still, Fang Yuan, even if he didn't fully understand it, took it in stride.
"And this is my reward for the same," he said as he held a Green Copper Relic Gu in his hands. This was the second one in his possession, and he had gotten this reward from the system for relinquishing the Liquor Worm to Fang Zheng.
He had been waiting for the right time to use this, as he would need some time to believably advance to Rank 1 Peak Stage. Now, the time was right as he injected his primeval essence into it, and the walls of his aperture now turned as hard as crystal.
At this point, the Liquor Worm would've been useless to him anyway. He could only rely on his own primeval essence to break through to Rank 2 Initial Stage now. As it was, if he needed it in the future, he had no doubt that he could easily snatch it back from Fang Zheng.
The academy elder and clan head hadn't been happy with the fact that he had given the Liquor Worm away. From their perspectives, Fang Yuan was now one of the most promising talents and he could've used this far better than someone like Fang Zheng was now only ordinary. Even if Fang Yuan had no use for it, it was 'wasted' in their eyes on a C-grade talent like Fang Zheng and would've suited Mo Bei or Chi Cheng better. However, given Fang Yuan's reputation for generosity and the fact that they were, after all, twin brothers, neither of them suspected anything off about the current situation.
With 59% primeval essence, Fang Yuan could break through to Rank 2 far easier than he had in his past life. However, as he no longer had the Liquor Worm's assistance, his progress would be greatly slowed as he no longer had his primeval essence effectively doubled. Right now, it would be good if he could reach Rank 2 before the end of the school year.
He had not been idle while waiting for the right time to use the Green Copper Relic Gu, however. He no longer focused on breaking through and instead on absorbing as much as the White Boar Gu's strength as possible. He had also used that time to stock up on primeval stones to make his breakthrough easier in the future as there was no need to waste primeval essence on something the Green Copper Relic Gu could do easily, and also to prepare for breaking through to Rank 3 as well in the future. He had things set up so that he would soon have 3 Red Steel Relic Gu in the future to go from Rank 2 Initial Stage to Rank 2 Peak Stage nearly instantly- of course, to maintain appearances he would have to move a bit slowly while building up a primeval stone reserve to break through to Rank 3 after that.
Once that was done, he could leave the village, but there were certain things to take care of before that.
The system, for one, had promised him greater rewards for lending even more help to Fang Zheng. He was greatly interested in one of them, though that might take time and some planning to achieve.

chapters.title: Chapter 66 - 66: Fang Zheng's Downfall: Part Four
chapters.content:
In his previous life, Fang Zheng had suppressed Fang Yuan, disregarding their close blood ties and whatever Fang Yuan had done for the former. Even in this timeline, Fang Zheng had shown great opposition to Fang Yuan.
And yet, Fang Yuan had no qualms whatsoever in taking him back or even supporting him. What were minor feelings of grudges and anger before the vast benefits he could obtain? The Green Copper Relic Gu was merely the appetizer when it came to what he could get.
New Main Mission!
Equality Between Twins
Description: Help Fang Zheng reach Rank 2
Reward: Rank 5 Equality Gu (x 1)
Fang Yuan wasn't sure of Equality Gu's effects, but a Rank 5 gu was more than worth the effort needed to nurture Fang Zheng to Rank 2. it would cost some primeval stones, but the output was well worth the investment. If needed he could even inject Fang Zheng with his own primeval essence to make it easier. Knowing what the system did, however, Equality Gu was likely a Human Path gu worm.
But it was the second one which made him truly wish to give it his all when it came to nurturing Fang Zheng.
New Main Mission!
Equality Is A Beautiful Thing
Description: Help Fang Zheng reach Rank 3
Reward: Rank 6 Beauty Gu (x 1)
Fang Yuan had to check and double-check this over and over again to make sure that his eyes were not deceiving him.
An Immortal Gu!
This was the greatest reward he had been offered as of yet by the system.
Immortal Gu were invaluable, and most Gu Immortals did not have even a single Immortal Gu. The reason was that Immortal Gu were unique- there could only be one of each in the world. Such as the Spring Autumn Cicada- now that Fang Yuan possessed one, even if someone tried a million times to refine it, they would fail every time.
Because they were unique, they could not be replicated and spread like mortal gu among clans. The best example was the Moonlight Gu- once it had been devised by the first generation clan head, it could be spread throughout the clan. Any recipe that involved it, from Rank 1 to Rank 5 would not just benefit the discoverer but also anyone who was given the recipe- though naturally it would have to be hidden and kept mostly with clan members. There could be thousands if not millions of the same kind of mortal gu.
But, say if someone somehow managed to find a way to create a Rank 6 Moonlight Gu, only they could benefit from the recipe. That was why Immortal Gu were rare even among sects and super-force clans- while they could be handed down, there could only be one of each. They could also not be traded freely - usually only Immortal Gu could be exchanged for Immortal Gu.
To be given one for raising someone to Rank 3 was a bargain. Even if Beauty Gu was not useful for him, he could always trade it for another Rank 6 Gu Worm that was more suitable for him or he could use it as a core or accessory for a killer move.
It was a bit of a hassle though now that Fang Zheng only had 46% aptitude. This was the most difficult mission the system had given him, as it had given him no way to raise Fang Zheng's aptitude like he could his own. Should he try to refine the Man-Beast Life Burial Gu? For the former leader of a demonic sect, it was an appropriate method, though Fang Zheng would likely not agree to it and it would be difficult to accomplish such a thing without his cooperation. Alternatively, he could drag Fang Zheng with him when he left the village, though he would be left babysitting a Rank 2 Gu Master then which was somewhat of a burden.
If he was still a Rank 6 Gu Immortal it would've been child's play to get a few aptitude-raising gu worms to fix this problem, but alas, this is all that he had to work with.
The allure of a Rank 6 Gu Worm was strong, but not overpowering to the extent that Fang Yuan was blinded by greed. He was someone who knew when to cut his losses.
News of him reaching Rank 1 Peak Stage soon spread throughout the academy- Mo Bei and Chi Cheng who had been in high spirits prior to this now had their moods sullied. 'No wonder he didn't bother giving up the Liquor Worm- now that he's at Rank 1 Peak Stage it won't be of much help to him!' both of them thought.
Thing somewhat returned to normal within the academy after that, though Fang Zheng's fallen status was still a sore point for him.
Fang Yuan was cultivating one evening when he was called by the clan leader. He sighed, while this was an unwelcome interruption he very well couldn't refuse the summons.
He already had a good idea what this was about, but as had become his wont since he had gotten the Goody Two-Shoes System, he was pretending to be a mostly ignorant but vibrant young man in order for his behavior to not come across as suspicious.
The clan head had taken an interest in Fang Zheng before - he was more of a 'neutral' party and wanted to back Fang Zheng secretly as a counter to the Mo and Chi clans. However, after being crippled, that was a pipe dream.
However, Fang Yuan was still in the running in the clan head's eyes. Fang Yuan had accomplished much already, and though B-grade talent was not as good as A-grade, it was still something, and at least Fang Yuan had some hope of perhaps going on equal footing with Mo Bei and Chi Cheng for the time being. Outside the academy, those two would be able to more freely use their resources to pull ahead.
That was why he intended to back Fang Yuan secretly for now - and had to at least give the impression that he was impartial.
"Fang Yuan," he asked. "I wanted to ask you what was the second gu worm that you chose."
"The Little Light Gu."
"Not a bad choice- and your reasoning for the same?"Google seaʀᴄh NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
"There are many evil and wicked people in this world," Fang Yuan said. "And I want to have the power to vanquish them, so that the righteous can live in peace and harmony. What better way to do that than with a strong offense? With it, I can smite any wicked demonic cultivators I come across. When I get older and stronger, I want to wander the whole world. I want to put an end to evildoers, I want to taste the finest foods and wine, bring justice to the poor and destitute and eheh... maybe even court a fair jade beauty or two! I've heard the mermaids of the Eastern Sea are especially enchanting!" These words might've even been Fang Yuan's heartfelt feelings at one point, and so they sounded quite genuine coming from him.
The clan leader had noted that Fang Yuan was a bit more politically astute than he let on, but after all, he was still a youngster and it was not out of the norm for him to have such lofty ideals. He would need to grow out of them though. "A good offense is useful yes, but there are times when defense is needed as well." He held out a gu worm in his hand.
"Is that the Jade Skin Gu?" Fang Yuan asked, though he already knew the answer.
"Indeed it is, its quite a wonderful defensive gu worm."
"And you're giving this to me?"
The clan leader chuckled. "No, this is the reward for whoever reaches Rank 2 first of all." That was him being impartial.
'This Fang Yuan is talented, but he is too kind and generous for his own good. To the point he will easily be taken advantage of- just see how he handed over the Liquor Worm to Fang Zheng,' the clan head thought. For now, this wasn't a problem as he was just Rank 1, but once Fang Yuan became an elder, he would need to be more careful. Being class president hadn't really molded him as much as he would've hoped, but with time, the clan head felt that he could reach out to Fang Yuan and teach him to be more pragmatic.
New Main Mission!
Rank 2 At Last
Description: Get to Rank 2.
Reward: ???
The system also wanted him to get to Rank 2 as well. Fang Yuan was planning to do so since the beginning anyway, he was able to chip away at the walls of his aperture but needed a few days of seclusion and lots of primeval stones to break through in one go.
"I will do my best," Fang Yuan said obediently.

chapters.title: Chapter 67 - 67: Rank 2 Initial Stage
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan took another primeval stone from the bag, which was already half-empty.
He was currently in secluded cultivation, and had asked for time away for the same reason. Things on the academy side had died down mostly kudos to everyone now focussing on the upcoming final exam.
Of course, it would be of immense help to him during it if he could reach Rank 2 before then.
In his prior life, with only 44% primeval essence, he had to sustain a certain amount of essence to attack the walls of his aperture while continuously using up primeval stones over and over again. The process had taken him several days, only allowing for breaks to eat and crap, not to mention costing him around a thousand primeval stones. It was because of this great cost that it had taken him a decade to reach that point.
Now though, his reserves were large enough for him to overcome the natural regeneration rate of his primeval aperture allowing him to slowly chip away at it so long as he did so regularly. He would not even need the assistance of primeval stones for that. However, there were always interruptions it seemed. Either class, or someone calling on him, or his duties as president.
Breaking through to a major realm was far more difficult than to a minor realm. Before, it had been somewhat fine, but he was making frustratingly low progress even now. Additionally, he lacked the support of the Liquor Worm which had doubled what he was able to accomplish earlier. To Fang Yuan, it felt like he had been running but suddenly sprained his ankle and was now limping along.
No longer though- he had feigned sickness the day before and had asked for time off today. That was two days where he could fully focus on breaking through, using primeval stones with what seemed like reckless abandonment just to get through the process earlier.
That said, he was making rapid progress, having cultivated all through last night. 50% of his essence was needed to overcome the natural regeneration rate of the aperture, and the other 9% was used to actually break free. His primeval stones guaranteed that he could do so over and over, and it looked like even the hard crystal membrane was beginning to yield.
'Just a while longer...' he thought to himself. He was not an actual B-grade talent yet, despite what the others thought. The difference may seem small, but he was sure that his difficulties would be reduce to a third if only he had genuine B-grade talent.
Morning turned to afternoon, and finally, the crystal walls shattered and were replaced by a new light membrane.
The remaining green primeval essence was being replaced by light red essence.
This was genuine Rank 2 red primeval essence!
Fang Yuan relaxed. Things would be somewhat easier now given the amount of Red Steel Relic Gu he had accumulated- though once again, he couldn't advance too rapidly or it would get suspicious. He had a few things to test out first.
Success!
Advanced to Rank 2!
Reward: Strength of Ten Men Gu (x 1)
Fang Yuan was puzzled as he hadn't heard of that gu before. This was one of hte few times the system actually seemed to deem to give him information on a gu worm.
Strength of Ten Men Gu is a Human Path single-use gu worm somewhat similar to White Boar Gu. It grants the user the strenth equivalent to ten adult men permanently when used over time, though unlike the White Boar Gu cannot be reused over and over and will dissipate once it has been accumulated. Can also be split among people- one person can accumulate the strength of five men and the other as well, or five people the strength of two men, and so on.
'And what do I need to feed it?'
The gu uses Human Qi as its food. Based on system estimates, given that it is a Rank 2 gu worm, the human qi being released into the air around Qing Mao Mountain should be sufficient to feed it given its population.The source of thɪs content is NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
There was a flaw there, Fang Yuan realized. 'And if I were to move out into the wilderness alone, then?'
Human Qi would need to be extracted in other ways.
The system did not overtly say so, but Fang Yuan knew that it was implying that he would need to kill people to absorb their human qi if he were to go out into a less populated area.
However, that didn't mean that he couldn't use it now.
He took the gu worm out of his inventory- it looked like a small action figure but with ten arms.
There was a great advantage to this type of gu worm, even if it was consumable when compared to the White Boar Gu. Although the strength of animals like boars and tigers was great, their anatomy and physiognomy were quite different from that of humans. Crocodiles had a strong jaw, horses had strong hind legs, and boars had a strong charge. Because of this, despite absorbing the strength of a boar, Fang Yuan was technically weaker than a boar when it came to head-to-head combat as he could not properly express the strength that had been stored within him. Of course, he had his own strength to add on top of that, but the strength of a human was so weak compared to that of a boar that it might have well been zero.
With this though, since it was a Human Path gu worm, he could bring out the full strength of ten men without any restrictions. Of course, he would need a defensive gu worm to use this fully as well otherwise his fists would shatter on impact.
Although this gu worm was classified as a Human Path gu worm, it had Strength Path properties. Many gu worms were like that which had dual-type properties. However, this meant that it would not synergize with other Strength Path gu. He could however, amplify its power if he imbibed more Human Path dao marks on his body.
There was also another drawback- he might not be able to bring out a beast phantom using this Human Path gu worm like he could with the White Boar Gu. That said, on average, the benefits of this were far greater than that of being able to bring about a beast phantom.
Thinking of this, he kept this new gu in his aperture and began using primeval stones to recover his essence before instilling the gu worm with his new red primeval essence. He did this until he began feeling an uncomfortable fire in his stomach, prompting him to stop. He saw that the gu had about a fourth of one arm which had dissolved, meaning he had likely gathered that much strength.
But, that would be his limit for now. He went outside and decided to check up on how Fang Zheng was doing- and found him cultivating in his room.
Fang Yuan did not bother to disturb him. RIght now, Fang Zheng was trying his hardest to advance to Rank 1 Middle Stage once again. Even with the Liquor Worm he was running into some issues as he did not have as large a supply of primeval stones as Fang Yuan. However, it could not be denied that he was trying his hardest after the incident that had happened to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 68 - 68: Pre-Exam Interlude: Part One
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan now turned his attention to other matters. Although he had no need to cultivate further and could spare his primeval essence for other matters, having enough Red Relic Gu to carry him all the way to Rank 2 Peak Stage nearly instantly if everything worked out. He also had several administrative issues he had been putting on hold while cultivating but which he could tackle now.
The biggest issue was the upcoming end-of-year examination the burden of organization some of which fell upon him.
Starting with the list of people who were not contending. Although it was called an 'examination' to call it a tournament was more accurate - and no one actually 'failed' it. That said, it was considered to be incredibly shameful to not participate unless you had a role like a dedicated healer.
With that said, Yu Sai, in typical Yu Sai fashion, had signed up for the list to not participate the moment that it was announced. Li Mei seemed to be somewhat inclined to follow but she changed her mind at the last second.
Fang Zheng's name was now on the list, but that was because Fang Yuan had convinced him to do the same.
"But Brother, the entire clan will look down on me and laugh at me if I don't at least show up!" Fang Zheng had protested.
This was all true- while no one expected anything from Yu Sai in the first place, the spotlight would be on Fang Zheng without a doubt. And while someone without cultivation couldn't do very well, at their level, Rank 1, even one's fists were sometimes good enough.
As it was, Fang Yuan did not care if Fang Zheng's reputation was damaged, however. The more that the clan despised Fang Zheng, the more that Fang Zheng would begin to despise the clan. That would make him far more easily manipulated. And if Fang Yuan wanted to spirit him away from the village in the future, it would be better if Fang Zheng severed all ties with it.
"And with what gu will you fight? The only one you have is the Liquor Worm."
"Brother I- I can still fight with my fists if I focus on martial arts! And I... I was wondering if you'd lend me your Moonlight Gu for a few fights..."
"I don't have an issue with lending you a gu worm," Fang Yuan lied. "However, I am worried that you will divide your attention between cultivating and training martial arts. One cannot try to ride two boats at once - and giving a mediocre performance in the exam will not help you in the future. Only by advancing in your cultivation can you actually succeed in the future. Take my advice and don't bother with the exam and focus entirely on the Liquor Worm to advance to Rank 1 Middle Stage."
"If you say so..." Fang Zheng said. He had been betrayed by practically everyone, and had only realized now that the only one who had ever shown him affection disregarding any kind of benefits that they could reap from him (aside from his parents) had been Fang Yuan. As such, he trusted Fang Yuan completely and assumed that if Fang Yuan was giving him some kind of advice it was good advice.
The irony being that there had been a time when that was correct- in Fang Yuan's first life. If he was still the Fang Yuan back then his support of Fang Zheng would've been genuine unlike now. Then again, Fang Yuan also had a deeply vested interest in seeing Fang Zheng succeed right now. But that 'success' was measured in terms of cultivation, which was why Fang Yuan wanted Fang Zheng to focus on nurturing his aperture.
As a matter of fact, now that he was at Rank 2, Fang Yuan considered whether it was worthwhile to inject some of his own essence into Fang Zheng's aperture. He didn't earlier as the difference was not by much but now that he was at Rank 2 he could help out with Fang Zheng's cultivation and make him a pseudo-B-grade talent much like Chi Cheng. Additionally, Fang Yuan was focused on his own cultivation more than his brother's, but now that he had reached Rank 2 with the help of the Red Steel Relic Gu he could take a breather as he would have to wait a sufficient amount of time before using them anyway.
To inject your essence into someone else's aperture like that would, without a doubt, cause damage to it. Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng were twins and so the damage would be less than that of what was caused to Chi Cheng's aperture and could be reversed in the future using Cleansing Water Gu. That said, Fang Yuan only cared about bringing Fang Zheng to Rank 3 and didn't care about his future prospects beyond that.
However, Fang Zheng's aperture had only recently recovered and was too fragile to take in foreign primeval essence for now. That, and the fact that the Liquor Worm was doing a good enough job meant that Fang Yuan felt that it was better to hold off for now.The source of thɪs content is ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
With the list completed and handed over to the academy elder, he could move on to some other minor issues that had been building up over time.
Meanwhile, things in Gu Yu village were not idle. Especially not when it came to his aunt and uncle, who were constantly worried about their ill-gotten fortune.
"Husband, now that Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng have made up, don't we have a target we can use?" Aunt asked. As it was, before, Fang Yuan had appeared to be invincible as there was no avenue to take him down. Now though, it looked like he had a weakness- Fang Zheng. At least, to Aunt, it appeared so.
"Yes..." Uncle said but then let out a heavy sigh. He had started eating less and less and gotten very few hours of sleep and looked haggard all night. "But... I think it might be in our best interest to lay low and let Fang Yuan take the inheritance..."
Aunt was shocked. "Husband- what are you saying? Without the inheritance, how will we support ourselves?" Uncle looked like someone who had already accepted defeat, rather than his usual vigilant and devious self.
The reason behind it was that Uncle was afraid that if he pushed Fang Yuan too hard, they might be found out. As it was, he was worried that any day, the clan would figure out that he had been the root cause behind the attack. This had sapped his will to fight. On top of which, though he cared little for Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng he was not completely heartless and seeing the damage that his little plan had caused made him want to scheme no more.
The image of Fang Yuan standing before him, a future elder of the clan, made him shudder in horror every single time he pictured it. But he did not have it in him to scheme further, as it was, none of his schemes were going to work regardless. He had heard that the clan head had shifted his attention to Fang Yuan, and any attempt by Uncle to suppress Fang Yuan might attract that man's wrath.
"Our best plan now," Uncle said, downing a bottle of liquor. "Is to simply make sure we have a good supply of primeval stones to last us our lives. And try not to cause any trouble. It would be best if we start tightening our belts right now - dismiss one-third, no, one-half of the servants. Also, we need to stop making large and extravagant purchases- I can't have people thinking that we are swimming in primeval stones. We need to appear poor- our lives depend on it! On top of which..."
Uncle walked over to a corner of the room, picking up a heavy wooden stick. He sighed, and with a swift motion broke his left arm.
"Husband!" Aunt shrieked, thinking that he had gone mad.
"Now," Uncle said, wincing in pain. "That should take care of the idiots asking me to train them or to spar." While the clan did encourage fighting, attacking someone while they were injured would no doubt be looked down upon especially if they were Uncle's age. And now, Uncle had the perfect reason to avoid teaching people as well.
"Why didn't you pretend to break your arm?" Aunt asked.
"Oh... they could tell if I pretended..." Uncle said. "And if anyone asks, we can't afford a healing Gu Master to fix my arm."
He could curse Fang Yuan all he wanted, but a wise man knew when to submit to circumstances. And these were the kind of circumstances he had to deal with. Only by appearing destitute could he survive the coming storm!

chapters.title: Chapter 69 - 69: Pre-Exam Interlude: Part Two
chapters.content:
"Well done, Fang Yuan," the clan head said as he inspected his aperture, confirming Fang Yuan's advancement to Rank 2. "As promised, this is your reward."
Jade Skin Gu- a rank one defensive gu worm, was handed to Fang Yuan who graciously accepted. It had even been refined by the clan head, which meant that there was likely more to this meeting than first appeared.
"But that is not the only reason that I've called you here..." the clan head said. They were back in the small garden that "I'm sure that in a year or two you will be a clan elder! There are many things you need to learn before that, however, and one of them is regarding gu refinement."
Fang Yuan already had Master-level attainment in gu refinement, but he pretended to be ignorant just as the clan head would've expected from someone his age. "Refining gu? Like, controlling them with your primeval essence?"
"That is a part of it, but I am referring to fusing gu to refine them. You have a rank 1 Jade Skin Gu, and a rank 1 Moonlight Gu. Together, they can be combined to form the Rank 2 Moon Raiment Gu!"
"And how do I do that?" Fang Yuan asked eagerly.
"Both of these gu worms have had their own wills removed from them, they respond to you," the clan head said. "You need to take the Moonlight Gu and the Jade Skin Gu, and infiltrate them with your Rank 2 essence. Then, maintaining your consciousness, you need to bring them together."
"Bring them together... I'm sorry, but I don't quite understand," Fang Yuan said.
"Think of it this way, rotate your right hand clockwise," the clan head said.
Fang Yuan obliged.
"Now rotate your left hand anti-clockwise," the clan head said.
Fang Yuan tried to do this, but found difficulty in doing both processes simultaneously. "Ah, I'm sorry I can't do it."
The clan head nodded. "You are trying to do something similar with gu fusion. You are taking two independent thoughts, and merging them together. It is far easier to understand this by doing rather than simply telling you."
Fang Yuan took out the Moonlight Gu and the Jade Skin Gu, and then infiltrated them with his red primeval essence. They both responded, and then hovered in the air, rotating around each other like a pair of planets.
"Now, try to bring them together, maintaining your control over them at the same time," the clan head said.
The two gu began to get closer and closer, until they finally merged together and formed a ball of light the size of Fang Yuan's fist.
"Clan head! Uh- I- what's going on? What do I do now?" Fang Yuan asked, sounding panicked. The ball of light seemed to almost unravel for a second.
"Calm down, this is all according to how things should be," the clan head said reassuringly. "Now, toss primeval stones into this ball, maintaining the fusion at the same time."
Fang Yuan obliged, tossing in a stone, the ball of light growing bigger in response. He tossed in a second, then a third, and this went on. Soon, the ball of light stopped growing bigger and instead condensed back to its original size.
There was a loud sound, and a flash of light as a new gu worm dropped down from the ball of light.
"Excellent! Well done Fang Yuan!" the clan head praised. Despite all he knew about Fang Yuan having natural talent, he had not expected him to succeed on his first try.
Fang Yuan himself was a bit surprised- no matter how experienced he was, there was always a chance of failure. Experience would not help with that.
