There was a way to make this refinement more successful - that was to add in the bones of a jade eye stone monkey during the refinement, but this modification had not been discovered yet and would not be for at least another hundred years.
This was likely thanks to his high Luck, he realized.
The Rank 2 Moon Raiment Gu fell into Fang Yuan's outstretched palm. Now that it had taken the form of the Moon Raiment, it lost its earlier ability to attack. It was now solely a defensive gu worm, but that ability had been greatly advanced.
"Continue doing well like this Fang Yuan," the clan head said. "You've done great things for the clan already, Fang Yuan, and I have high hopes for you." The clan head been astonished by not only Fang Yuan's performance, but by his luck as well. Sometimes, even those who did not start out well could reach great heights if they had fate's blessing. With Fang Zheng out of the picture, Fang Yuan was the new hopeful among the clan's youth.
"I will continue to work hard so as to not disappoint you," Fang Yuan said, cupping his hands.
The next few days leading up to the exam were uneventful until one day, while walking back to the dorm, Fang Yuan noticed a change in his aperture.
"What is this... gu refinement?!"
The mysterious Rank 3 gu that he had been unable to identify was changing, glowing with a pleasant light. As Fang Yuan continued to walk, it continued to glow, and by the time he had reached his dorm it had formed a fourth feather and was now emitting a Rank 4 aura.
He had refined a Rank 3 gu worm into Rank 4!
The only question was- how? He had no idea what had caused this change.
If one of his disciples back when he had been Supreme Elder of the Blood Wing Demon Sect had told him that they had somehow refined a Rank 4 gu without even knowing what they had done to refine it, he would've slapped them across the face for being an idiot.
But now, he was left speechless as to what had happened. The mysterious gu worm had not done anything until that point, not even needing feeding despite being relatively healthy, and had just suddenly had a change today.
'I don't remember doing anything different today...' Fang Yuan thought. He normally kept the gu worm hidden though he would occasionally take it out and place it in his aperture just to make sure that it was doing alright. Also, if he didn't do so occasionally, unless he used special sealing methods it would eventually die.Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
He took out the newly refined Rank 4 gu and took a good look at it. The fourth feather... it was not the length of the others, though the feathers on the gu worm had not been symmetrical to begin with.
"It almost looks like... it's imitating a human hand, or trying to," Fang Yuan thought. Granted, it only had four fingers, but perhaps it would grow a fifth one when it was Rank 5? The 'feathers' were bent in the same way that fingers would be, with only a 'thumb' missing.
If the food that this gu worm changed upon refinement, it would be an issue, yet, there was nothing that Fang Yuan could do about that. He could only hope that it continued to feed on something that was intangible and yet easy to obtain while he pondered what it was that had led to it changing like this.

chapters.title: Chapter 70 - 70: Final Exam: Part One
chapters.content:
"Psst... hey... Fang Zheng," Yu Sai said.
"What is it?"
"I heard you're also stepping out of the contest," Yu Sai said. "Tell you what- I'm not doing anything either way, and I heard you were lacking an attacking gu worm. I'll lend you my Moonlight Gu if you want to participate- all for five primeval stones! Just for the exam, mind you..."
Fang Zheng considered it - that way he would still be at a disadvantage but could make a reasonable showing of his skills.
However, five primeval stones was a lot to someone like him. And his brother's words echoed as he shook his head.
"Really? Oh well..." Yu Sai said, slightly disappointed.
Fang Zheng had reached Rank 1 Middle Stage a few days ago, though he was still was not participating based on what Fang Yuan had told him to do.
The tournament had attracted a large number of Gu Masters, some of them just here to see the fights, while others were here to eye the potential recruits to their teams. The excitement had died down a bit now that the rumored A-grade talent wasn't going to be performing, but even with three B-grades it promised to be quite the show.
Yu Sai, Fang Zheng, and the other losers who had chosen not to participate stayed on the sidelines- if they were lucky maybe one of the more desperate teams might choose them, but more likely than not they would all be relegated to the tasks of being logistics or support gu masters. Much like the people who ran the academy store, for example. While it could be said that in some way this was safer than going on missions as they usually would, when push came to shove, say, during the beast tide, they would have to fight the same. And in times of peace, they were the bottom of the totem pole- there was a reason that Jia Jin Sheng was so frustrated most of the time. These jobs did not pay well at all either, and meant that these people would barley be scraping by when it came to primeval stones. On top of that, any missions that they would take would be considered to be 'failures' further worsening their reputations among the clan.
That was why many students, even if they were just D-grade, still entered the tournament. To at least show that they could do something- anything, to escape that fate.
Many people gave Fang Zheng disappointed looks seeing where he was standing. They had higher hopes from him, and many rumors were being whispered about in the crowd.
"Is that Fang Yuan?"
"Of course, Fang Yuan would not be standing with those failures. That's his brother, Fang Zheng."
"Ah, the unlucky cripple."
"You'd think he'd at least try to make some kind of show with things, but to see him like that..."
"Heh, did you hear what he did to that mortal woman? I think it serves him right that he's like this now..."
The words were like poison to Fang Zheng's ears, but he only repeated what Fang Yuan had told him until now. 'Words are useless, they will not save you if your life is in danger. There are two ways to avoid being trampled upon in this world - become so strong that no one would dare mess with you, or become so loathsome that no one would even bother stepping on you! Fang Zheng, I know it is difficult, but for now, you have to play the part of a failure while gathering strength secretly. Only then will you be able to once again eventually soar into the clouds - don't worry, I promise that the sun will shine upon you once again someday!'
For now, Fang Zheng was only hoping that Fang Yuan, at the very least, gave a good performance.
Before the fighting started, everyone's apertures were inspected. This was the last time for most of them that this would happen in their lives, after this, their apertures would be considered very vital and private areas that they would not let others intrude upon.
Mo Bei and Chi Cheng had both managed to cultivate to Rank 1 Peak Stage. This had not happened back in Fang Yuan's previous life, and was likely a consequence of him rocketing upwards. While those two were happy, there was a tiny commotion when his own aperture was inspected.
"Rank 2 Initial Stage!"
"What?"
"Rank 2 already?"
"He must be at the peak of Rank 2 stage then- like Qing Shu."
"No, this is all because of the Liquor Worm's help."
"Oh right- he's the lad who found the Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance! How could I forget?"
The other students, who already thought that they were not Fang Yuan's match, had sour looks as half of them seemed like they wanted to join Yu Sai if they were to be paired against Fang Yuan.
"Rank 2 huh..." Mo Yan said. She was watching intently- after all, her grandfather was more serious about marrying her off to him and she wanted to see with her own eyes what he was like. She might even extend an offer to recruit him if his performance really lived up to the hype.
She was not the only one who wanted to recruit Fang Yuan. There was Chi Shan, from the Chi faction, who had incredible strength and was a B-grade talent.
Then there was Qing Shu- a man said to have 'pseudo-A-grade' talent who represented the interests of the clan head. Originally he had been planning to recruit Fang Zheng, but after the assassination attempt, the clan head's priorities had shifted.
The matches began. The D-grade talents could do little more than use their fists, but even then there were some good shows here and there. Li Mei was among them but had to concede after three rounds of fighting- with that said she had put up a good show all things considered.
Fang Yuan, as was to be expected, struck like lightning. He won most of his fights without even having to rely on his gu worms or primeval essence. His dominance from the martial arts training sessions was still fresh in everyone's minds, and he had not lost his advantage since then.
This was slightly different in the fact that gu could be used in these fights- meaning that moonblades flew around like frisbees. The issue was that the ones who were using them were extremely inexperienced to using them in actual fights being that most of their training was against stationary targets.
Even if they had been more seasoned, they would not have been able to deceive Fang Yuan. As a demonic Gu Master, he had fought with his own life on the line countless times, in many circumstances opponents with more strength than his own. His battle experience was honed to a base instinct. When one used moonblades, their wrists had to flick, their shoulders moved- and all of these actions betrayed them as Fang Yuan swerved and dived, seemingly not tiring whatsoever as he beat challenger upon challenger and sent them flying out of the arena.
There was a reward of 100 primeval stones for winning, and he intended to claim it. Above that, was the reward handed by the system.
New Main Mission!
Win the final exam!
Reward: 2% permanent increase to your aptitude.ᴛhis ᴜpdated by novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
With that, Fang Yuan would have 61% primeval essence, meaning that he would then be a true B-grade talent. There was no need to be worried about being discovered as a fake, because he was no longer a fake - the lie that he had woven would materialize into something that was fact!
The clan head, however, was a bit disappointed. Since Fang Yuan could dominate things so easily, he had no need to use gu worms. Meaning that he was not showing how he could use the Moon Raiment Gu, which was good for Fang Yuan to keep a card like that hidden, but disappointing nonetheless to the clan head.

chapters.title: Chapter 71 - 71: Final Exam: Part Two
chapters.content:
The clan head was not the only one disappointed by Fang Yuan's tactics.
"Man- why is that kid not using any gu worms?"
"I thought we'd see some cool Rank 2 action from him- but he hasn't even tossed out a single moonblade yet!"
"Yeah man, what's the point of cultivating if all you're going to do and jump and flail around like a monkey?"
Several people laughed, though a voice cut through all of the noise.
"You all cannot see Mt. Tai," Chi Shan said coldly. The laughter stopped. "Many times, Gu Masters run out of primeval essence and have to use their own fists to do the talking. That boy is a natural martial artist."
"Indeed, you're right, Chi Shan," someone chirped up. "I heard his uncle was the one who taught him how to fight like that."
"Oh, is that so?" Chi Shan thought, eyes shimmering. 'Perhaps I should also seek the advice of his uncle then... or maybe ask for a spar sometime later?'
Qing Shu agreed with Chi Shan's assessment. Qing Shu was a renowned Gu Master and considered to be the 'future clan head' by many until Fang Zheng had shown up. His family had been killed by wolves when he had been young, and he had been nurtured by the clan head after awakening his aperture. He had an aptitude close to the upper limit of B-grade, and could possibly cultivate to Rank 4 in the future.
His heart carried an immense sense of gratitude to the clan head and the clan who had nurtured him, and he had bore no ill will towards Fang Zheng when learning that he was an A-grade talent. Instead, he was overjoyed that the clan would have such a powerful clan head, someone who could maybe even reach Rank 5 one day. Fang Zheng's crippling had affected him greatly, though he had been told by the clan head that there was someone else they were nurturing.
"Who is that?" he had asked.
"Fang Yuan," the clan head said.
"Fang Yuan... Fang Yuan... that name sounds familiar."
"Yes, he was the one who found the Flower Wine Monk's Inheritance- I'm sure you've heard of him..."
"No... no... there was something else..." Qing Shu had said at the time, wondering where it was that he had heard that name before.
After some reflection, the answer became clear.
One day, when he had been out on a walk, he had seen a child limping along the road. His leg had been broken, though at the time, Qing Shu had been preoccupied with a mission and could not stop to help. As it was the injury did not place that boy's life in immediate danger. However, once he was done he went looking for that child, intending to help him, only to find that the child's leg had already been mended.
"Big Brother paid a Gu Master to fix it..." the child told him.
"Oh? And what was big brother's name?" Qing Shu had asked the boy.
"Gu Yue Fang Yuan."
'So that was where I had heard his name!' Qing Shu thought. 'No wonder the clan head is interested in him. Not only is he this skilled- but he has a heart of gold. To spend his own primeval stones to help a child whom he had no relation to. Heh- the clan head said that I would have a new contender who could compete with me for the position of clan head. That seems to be true, but at the same time- I feel like even if I lost to Fang Yuan it would be alright. After all, he would be an excellent future leader for the clan.'
Competition brought out the best in people, and so no matter who won between the two of them, it was the village who would be the ultimate winner.
By now, most of the D-grade and C-grade talents had been eliminated. The semi-finals pitted Chi Cheng against Mo Bei, and Fang Yuan against a classmate who was already sweating bullets.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
Chi Cheng and Mo Bei grit their teeth- they had both hoped that the other would be paired against Fang Yuan, but it was their bad luck that they were up against each other.
Mo Bei had chosen the Yellow Camel Longhorn Beetle Gu as his second gu worm, which greatly increased his endurance. Chi Cheng on the other hand, had chosen the Scarlet Pill Cricket Gu which greatly increased his agility.
The two of them danced on the stage, and for once, the whispers died down.
"Finally! A real fight between Gu Masters!"
Mo Bei could strike with precision and could keep up for a long time, while Chi Cheng could evade nearly everything that he did.
Ultimately their fight was decided by primeval essence. Chi Cheng was not a true B-grade talent and so he expended all of his first, and was no longer able to deal with Mo Bei, who tossed him out of the arena.
Cheers erupted for Mo Bei, while the Chi faction was sullen.
However, Mo Bei knew that the real fight had only just started. He was going to go up against Fang Yuan next- a Rank 2 Gu Master! Fang Yuan would be the one with an advantage when it came to primeval essence.
The clan head tapped his finger- perhaps now Fang Yuan would be forced to use gu worms?
The two fighters greeted each other, before Fang Yuan launched himself at Mo Bei.
'Not even using gu worms?' Mo Bei thought as he flicked out a moonblade, which Fang Yuan saw coming from a mile away.
As the fight continued, it was clear that Mo Bei was faltering. He had been struck in several non-vital areas, but it felt like Fang Yuan's bones were made of iron. When had he gained strength like this? Even then, back during the tournament, he had not shown this kind of power, yet Mo Bei could feel like his bones were going to crack.
And this was all without Fang Yuan using any gu worms! How terrifying would it be when he actually started using them?
Mo Bei needed to find a decisive moment to flip this battle around- a moment where he could beat Fang Yuan.
After a while, it seemed that Fang Yuan had faltered. 'An opening!' Though as he was about to strike, a blue glow erupted from Fang Yuan's right hand.
'A feint!' Mo Bei realized, trying to change the direction of his blow. But it was too late, as he was thrown off balance, Fang Yuan took the initiative to cancel his attack and instead strike him on his chest, knocking the wind out of Mo Bei, before striking him on the back of the neck, knocking him out.
Fang Yuan had won!
Mission Complete!
Reward: Aptitude increased by 2% permanently.
The clan head had expected this, but he had a thought in his mind - 'Didn't Fang Yuan use up the Moonlight Gu? Where did he get another one?'
In the crowd, Yu Sai was chuckling to himself. 'Fang Yuan agreed to give me five primeval stones to borrow it. Joke's on him- I would've done it for three!'
New Main Mission!
To Reach Rank 3
Description: Advance to Rank 3.
Reward: The location of a Paradise Earth Immortal Venerable's and Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable's combined inheritance.
New Main Mission!
Elder Gu Yue Fang Yuan
Description: Become an elder.
Reward: For every week spent as an elder, gain 5 Human Path dao marks.

chapters.title: Chapter 72 - 72: Final Exam: Part Three
chapters.content:
"Incredible!'
"He didn't use gu worms until the very end!"
"We didn't even get to see a Rank 2 gu..."
"Pfft- I don't even think he has a Rank 2 gu..."
"As expected as someone being nurtured by the clan head!"
"Is that true- is the clan head really nurturing him?"
"I heard so, and it makes sense, right?"
Fang Yuan heard all of this, but his thoughts were elsewhere.
The combined inheritance of two Venerables?
Just that alone was worth more than anything he had obtained in his last 500 years, or that which he knew of which he could obtain in this life.
Venerables were existences that defied all logic and common sense. A true Venerable inheritance was so valuable that let alone Rank 8 Gu Masters, even super forces like the Heavenly Court would contend for! Not only would it have secrets regarding cultivation that many would kill for, it was likely that there were several Immortal Gu that could be find in such an inheritance. Most Immortals lacked even a single Immortal Gu, but Venerables were titans among Gu Masters and would not lack several Immortal Gu. It would actually be quite surprising if one of their true inheritances did not have a single Rank 8 Immortal Gu.
Fang Yuan had never heard of Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable and Paradise Earth Immortal Venerable working together, but it was not something unthinkable. Genesis Lotus was a righteous path Venerable and Paradise Earth would have no issues working with anyone.
It made Fang Yuan want to immediately use all of his Red Steel Relic Gu to advance to Rank 3 as soon as he could to obtain this inheritance!
With some effort, he calmed his inner heart down. Yes, this was valuable, but the location it was in could be dangerous. He would have to prepare before diving in. It could even be in one of the other four regions for all he knew. Not to mention it might be a minor inheritance and not a true inheritance- but even then, it would be well worth checking out.
Also, there was a chance this was a trap set up by the system. Unlikely given what he had seen so far, but he could not afford to be careless.
Mission completed!
Graduated as class president!
Rank 3 Doctor Gu (x 1) added to inventory!
That should take care of healing, he thought, though he still needed to find something for offense. He considered 'permanently borrowing' Yu Sai's Moonlight Gu- it would not be hard using the Spring Autumn Cicada, but decided against it. The system would likely not agree to it, and it was not worth the trouble it would cause. Stealing a gu worm was not like stealing one or two primeval stones, it was a serious offense!
'Incredible,' Mo Yan thought, even though she was a bit sour that her brother had been knocked out cold. He was being healed, but this had already caused her to develop negative feelings towards Fang Yuan. It would be a hard issue to get over on their wedding night given how many times Fang Yuan had thrashes Mo Bei.
'Outstanding, but just how strong is he?' Chi Shan thought. It was clear to him that Fang Yuan was very strong- but as to how much, it was not apparent as Fang Yuan had not displayed his full abilities in this fight. Did his strength match his own? That was hard to believe. Chi Chan had the strength of an adult even when he had been young- he had beaten a mortal servant to death in a fit of rage when he had been only ten. However, this world had no shortage of geniuses. Anyone who thought themselves to have crested the peak of this world was just waiting to be shot down by someone at an even higher peak. Only the Venerables themselves could be said to truly have reached the peak of their fields, shining like nine suns in the sky above the gu world.
"Very good, very good," the clan head said, coming out of his tent. Mo Bei had already been healed and had come to, but no one was looking down on him. It was clear that with Fang Yuan's skills and higher cultivation level, it was a big feat to have even lasted this long. "Fang Yuan, as promised, here is your reward." He handed Fang Yuan 100 primeval stones, something that seemed paltry compared to what Fang Yuan could potentially get by getting to Rank 3. "As another reward, you can be the first one to choose which team to join."
"Fang Yuan, I would welcome you into our fold," Qing Shu said. His other team members seemed to be less than thrilled to be babysitting Fang Yuan, but given that he reflected the clan head's faction, it was clear to Fang Yuan which place he should go.
He could cause chaos by choosing something else, but with the thought of a Venerable Inheritance in mind, everything else seemed insignificant to him. He saw no use in causing ripples or issues unnecessarily. "Thank you for taking care of this junior."
With that, Fang Yuan had officially become a member of Qing Shu's team!
Fang Zheng watched the applause being showered on Fang Yuan bitterly. If he had retained his A-grade talent, that could have been him!
There was no use thinking such thoughts, but he couldn't help but concern himself with them. After all, right now, the only person who cared for him was Fang Yuan.
Fang Yuan had even handed him thirty primeval stones immediately after the festivities were over- which shocked Fang Zheng. "Brother, this is all your earnings, isn't it? Why give this much to me...?"Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"Don't worry at all, I want to make sure that you're taken care of," Fang Yuan said, as the two brothers walked away from the academy. Fang Yuan gently had his arm over Fang Zheng's shoulders, and the two of them looked like the best of friends to any outsider. "You didn't manage to find a group to work with, did you?"
"No," Fang Zheng said dejectedly. "I couldn't find a group... I don't know how I'll complete the mission I'll get in the future..."
"It's simple then..." Fang Yuan said. "Fail the mission. They can't compel you to go on a mission."
"Fail? Won't my evaluation be poor then..."
"So what if it is poor?"
"But... what about earning primeval stones to support myself...? And if I don't do good, I'll only get trash missions in the future?"
"Earning? Why would you need to earn? Did our aunt and uncle worry about earning? Have you forgotten about our parent's inheritance?"
"Oh that... right, but I'm not able to contest for it..."
"So what? Do you think that I would let you starve?" Fang Yuan asked. "It's just like old times now, you and I against the whole world, remember that Fang Zheng. With me by your side, there's no need to worry."
"Ah..." Fang Zheng was nearly moved to tears. He had doubted initially whether Fang Yuan had truly gotten over the rift that had been formed between them, and it seemed that he had.
"As for a place to stay, we can stay in the dorm for a few more weeks before we have to leave," Fang Yuan said. "But, I already happen to know of a place we can stay."
Fang Yuan led Fang Zheng to an old apartment complex that he knew of.
"Brother... is this really the best we can do?" Fang Zheng asked. It looked quite rundown.
"Don't worry, this is only temporary until we can get our hands on that inheritance. Eventually, I'll become a Rank 3 elder too- but what's needed now is to save our primeval stones as much as possible for important things like cultivating. Use those stones I gave you, try to get to Rank 1 Upper Stage as soon as you can. I'll pay the rent entirely by myself. When it comes to breaking through to Rank 2, don't think about it too much- once I'm an elder, I'll help you break through to that," Fang Yuan reassured Fang Zheng.
This was where Fang Yuan had stayed in during his past life, so he knew it was free from traps and that his aunt and uncle couldn't scheme against him here. As for living conditions- it was serviceable enough.
To Fang Zheng, who had lost all hope of getting anywhere in this world after having his cultivation crippled, his brother's words were like a burst of fresh rain in the desert - pacifying him and calming his heart.

chapters.title: Chapter 73 - 73: Final Exam: Part Four
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan returned to his dorm. For now, he could spend some time here before having to clean up to let room for the incoming class.
Normally he would've been against sharing a room with anyone, but he wanted to keep a close eye on Fang Zheng, whose development was very crucial to him obtaining an Immortal Gu. Also, there was the fact that Fang Zheng was still very stupid and wouldn't be much of an impediment to his plans anyway. Additionally, at this point Fang Zheng was so much of a pariah that he could only rely on Fang Yuan and so the chance of betrayal from that end was nearly zero.
First off, he sent his mind towards the doe he had used the Deer Enslavement Gu on. To his surprise, it looked like she was still alive as he could feel their connection to each other. The Crimsonhoof Deer was also still alive, though it was likely still nothing more than a baby. The time when Fang Yuan could use it to fight was still far off on the horizon.
Next, he had an experiment that he wanted to try. He retrieved a Green Copper Relic Gu from his inventory and was going to try to use his Cultivation Blessing to raise its rank.
Normally such a thing would be impossible. The Relic Gu series could not be advanced, they were only refined naturally in regions where large numbers of humans gathered. However, this was the current common consensus.
Just because something was thought to be impossible did not mean that it would always be impossible. It was considered impossible to refine Lifespan Gu, and yet, that did not stop people from trying. People did not think that a Four Flavors Liquor Worm existed until it was refined by a genius in the future.
There was another reason that Fang Yuan thought that it would be possible to advance the Relic Gu- because Relic Gu were considered to be Human Path gu worms. Given this, and the fact that the system heavily favored Human Path dao marks and methods, as well as gu worms, made him think that it might be possible.
He activated the Cultivation Blessing, which formed a small ball of light that hovered in the air before descending upon the Green Copper Relic Gu held in Fang Yuan's outstretched hand. A moment later, its color had changed.
Red Steel Relic Gu had formed!
If anyone saw this, they wouldn't have been able to believe it. Fang Yuan hardly even believed it as he placed the Red Steel Relic Gu in his aperture and activated it, advancing to Rank 2 Middle Stage instantly.
He had two more Red Steel Relic Gu in his inventory, but he did not use them immediately. It would draw too much attention to himself if he did- as it was, he was going to have a hard time explaining even this small advancement, but it was still within reasonable expectations if people thought he had between a 75-79% aptitude, which some of them did.
With this, his advancement to Rank 2 Peak Stage was guaranteed, he only needed to make sure that he gathered enough primeval stones in the meantime for his breakthrough to Rank 3. Additionally, he needed to gather Rank 2 and Rank 3 gu worms.
He had already purchased another Moonlight Gu using his primeval stones, and was planning on refining the Rank 2 Moonglow Gu once he found another Little Light Gu. Once he reached Rank 3, he would be able to get a Rank 3 gu worm from the clan treasury, but until then, he needed an offensive option other than using his fists. While that was still quite effective given how much he had raised his own strength, in addition to having Rank 2 Moon Raiment which could protect his bones while he used such strength, he also needed a long-range option.
Regarding healing, it was time to see if the Doctor Gu was indeed worth his time as he brought it out of his inventory.Thɪs
Doctor Gu looked like a small figurine in his hand, rather than an insect. As he injected his primeval essence into it, it transformed into the form of an adult man with a gentle smile on his face.
To an onlooker, this person would be indistinguishable from a human.
Fang Yuan himself was shocked- he had never heard of a gu worm taking human form before. Many gu worms could form disguises, but to see one turn into an actual human was something else. Did this mean that humans and gu worms were one in the same? Or that they had been at one point? Or that they would be in the future?
The strangeness did not stop there, as the Doctor Gu talked. Actually talked!
Many gu worms in 'The Legends of Ren Zu' could talk, but that was a fairy tale and many of the gu worms were Immortal Gu, so Fang Yuan wasn't sure if that was actually the case as he had never encountered said gu worms even in his old life.
"I greet Young Master," Doctor Gu said.
"Are... are you a healing type gu worm?" Fang Yuan asked.
"Indeed I am," Doctor Gu said, however, he then showed a sorrowful expression. "But I am afraid that I will be unable to help the Young Master if he is injured."
"Oh? Why is that?"
"Because I am a Family Doctor, and it seems that you are an orphan."
Doctor Gu: ...
Fang Yuan: ...
"Ah, that was a joke, Young Master," Doctor Gu said. "They say that laughter is the best medicine, and I saw that you were already healthy, and so I wanted to see if I could make you laugh... hehe..."
"Alright, jokes aside," Fang Yuan said, unsure of why this gu worm was behaving like this (as if it still retained a semblance of free will) but he took it in stride as something that was just a peculiarity of some Human Path gu worms. "What do I need to feed you?"
"Oh, you will find that my feeding requirements are rather easy to satisfy as I don't require anything too fancy," Doctor Gu said. "For breakfast, I require a delicate yet invigorating start. Starting with a deconstructed Thousand Beast King Crab Benedict, with saffron-infused hollandaise air, nestled upon a cloud of artisanal truffle foam, accompanied by a single, perfectly spherical quail egg poached in champagne, and garnished with gold leaf and microgreens flown in fresh from the alpine slopes of the Northern Plains and naturally, a single shot of Kona Geisha coffee, brewed by hand from beans harvested only at the first dew point."
"For lunch my tastes require something that speaks of both the earth and the heavens. I envision a Pâté de Foie Gras Terrine presented as an edible mosaic, incorporating rare black Périgord truffles and wild morels foraged by moonlit decree. This would be served with lightly toasted brioche points made from flour milled by monks and a confiture of hand-picked, sun-ripened figs, all bathed in a reduction of an old Romanée-Conti. A palate cleanser of perfectly chilled, hand-scooped Bael fruit sorbet should finish this meal."
"For dinner, the grand finale, I need a pan-seared Hudson Valley Foie Gras, served alongside a delicate Long Island Duck Consommé infused with foraged ramps from the Catskills and a hint of saffron grown in the Western Desert. The main course would be a meticulously prepared Dry-Aged Prime Porterhouse Steak from a local, ethically-raised farm, cooked to absolute perfection and accompanied by a creamy Truffle Potato Gratin made with artisanal Eastern Sea cheeses and shavings of imported white Alba truffle. As a side, perhaps a vibrant salad of Heirloom Tomatoes from a local organic farm run by Mushroommen, drizzled with a balsamic reduction aged in small oak barrels and taken care of exclusively by virgin women. To conclude this meal, I require a vintage port from a renowned producer and a delicate fig jam made with locally sourced fruit."
Doctor Gu: ...
Fang Yuan: ...
"Ah, that was another joke, Young Master," Doctor Gu said, taking out a handkerchief and wiping his brow from the sweat that now coated it. "Ah, but it doesn't seem to have amused Young Master in the slightest... the actual answer is that I can eat any food a human can eat, though I require larger amounts at intervals acceptable for a Rank 3 gu worm. Something like plain rice would be fine."
Fang Yuan nodded. That made feeding this Doctor Gu quite simple. Most gu worms required a very specific food, but it appeared that these kind of Human Path gu worms were flexible in their requirements.
It made some intuitive sense to Fang Yuan though - if these gu worms could transform into humans, it would logically follow that they could eat food that humans ate. That was good as it meant that their feeding requirements would be low.

chapters.title: Chapter 74 - 74: Final Exam: Part Five
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan turned the Doctor Gu back into its gu worm form and placed it in his aperture.
That covered healing even when he advanced to Rank 3. Right now, although it was difficult to use it was not impossible to rely upon it in a pinch. He still needed offense, for which he wanted to refine the Moonglow Gu. For investigative methods, storage, and movement - he would still need to either purchase or refine gu himself.
That would require primeval stones- which is why he needed to obtain his family's inheritance as soon as he could. It was a good thing that the existence of the Red Steel Relic Gu alleviated his need for nurturing his aperture right now.
Now that he had graduated, he no longer got Human Path dao marks - though he had not accepted them anyway so that was not much of an issue. But, that meant that he no longer got his regular allowance from the clan.
Instead, he had to undergo missions along with his team.
Speaking of, many people had congratulated him on being accepted to Qing Shu's team, but Fang Yuan spotted it for what it was- a trap.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Not an overt trap mind you, there was an intention to nurture him by placing him in that team. But for Fang Yuan and his goals, it was the equivalent of a trap.
While he would get 'guidance' under Qing Shu's tutelage, guidance that he did not need given his 500 years of experience, he would also be burdened with various tasks designed to drain as much of his time as possible. They would not be presented to him that way, of course, instead, they would be presented as 'tasks of honor' and would also have some decent rewards. None of which would compensate for the time that they took.
Time was said to be more valuable than gold- and to Fang Yuan, who had the Spring Autumn Cicada, equivalent to a ticking time bomb within his aperture, that was especially so.
He could've saved his Cultivation Blessing for a higher-ranked gu worm rather than using it on Green Copper Relic Gu, that was true, but he needed to advance as quickly as possible to Rank 3 and then bounce. Even now, he wanted to get to Rank 3 in order to get the Venerable Inheritance. If that lived up to its potential, it could help him become Rank 5 or even Rank 6 quite quickly. It was the same concept that a starving man would prefer a loaf of bread now rather than an exquisite banquet two days later. His Cultivation Blessing would've been better used on a Rank 4 gu worm to advance it to Rank 5, but he couldn't wait for that.
There was a reason that Qing Shu was not an elder as of yet. He was considered to have pseudo-A grade talent meaning that his aptitude was likely in the 75%+ range for that to be true. He should've reached Rank 3 several months ago - but if he did that, how could the elders make use of him? This was a form of suppression to keep him at Rank 2 Peak Stage for as long as possible. Not that Qing Shu would complain about this, as it wasn't in his nature.
Qing Shu was actually fated to die based on Fang Yuan's previous memories of what was going to happen. At some point, the wolf tide would grow to be more powerful and Qing Shu would end up using a Rank 3 gu worm despite being only Rank 2 to hold back the tide. He would 'save' the village at the cost of his own life- only for it to be destroyed regardless several months later.
Fang Yuan had no intention of following in his footsteps. No, he needed to hoard as many resources as possible and reach Rank 3. By then, the world would be his oyster.
He glanced outside his window. He saw the other students excitedly chatting as they marched away, talking about what they would do in the future.
"That which starts with the blossoming of spring,
Only withers away with the coming of autumn,
For the leaves so verdant crowned with the morning dew,
Fall to the Earth as winter winds blow anew,
Heaven watches their descent impassively,
As the Earth welcomes them in its warm embrace,
Soon to be followed by the snow and the rain,
For new life to sprout forth once again."
Their school lives were over, and new challenges awaited them all. Without a doubt, they would be excited, worried, frustrated, and happy as they marched every forward.
For Fang Yuan, who had already experienced such, it was no big deal. If anything, the aspirations and hopes of these youngsters was far too small for one like him.
The next day, when he would 'officially' graduate, he would go to the clan mission hall in order to accept the mission needed to inherit his parent's fortune.
Soon, it would be in his grasp. As a Rank 2 Gu Master, there was no longer any scheme that would work on him to prevent him from taking it.
His uncle knew the same, which is why Qing Shu found himself with an unexpected visitor that evening.
"Young Master, Gu Yue Dong Tu wishes to have a meeting with you, and apologizes that it is on such short notice," a servant said.
Qing Shu frowned. He couldn't remember that name- was it someone important? "What is this about?"
"He says it is regarding his nephew, Fang Yuan," the servant said.
Qing Shu nodded. "Bring him in then."
Qing Shu had the guest room set up as he sat down to evaluate the man before him. He was old, but somehow seemed to be more sickly than he was pretending to be otherwise, one of his arms in a sling. That was odd as a Rank 2 Gu Master should've been able to fix that kind of injury without much hassle.
"I greet Lord Qing Shu!" the man said, attempting to cup his hands, though with the sling it was obviously hard.
"No need for that, given how much older you are then I am."
"Lord is too kind!"
"Hmm... I was told this is about your nephew- my new teammate?"
"Yes, it is, Lord," Dong Tu said. He had no presence or grandeur in that moment- appearing quite pitiful on the contrary. "It is something that I have been worried about, and I was wondering if Lord could provide his generous aide in that matter."
"Oh, and what seems to be troubling you?"
"It is not an issue with Fang Yuan in actuality, rather, my other nephew Fang Zheng," Dong Tu said. "You see, he was found to be misbehaving with one of the female servants, so I was forced to kick him out. I wished that he would learn some manners from that incident, and he went back to his elder brother. Fang Yuan will soon want to claim his inheritance, and I don't doubt will become an elder one day. However, Fang Zheng, that rascal, continues to be perched upon his shoulder like a parrot. I fear that he will convince my former beloved nephew to turn against me and his aunt- who have raised them both since birth like they were our own children."
"Is that so...?" Qing Shu wondered. He could somewhat understand what Dong Tu was inquiring about. "If that is the case, you can rest assured that I will speak to Fang Yuan tomorrow." Without a doubt, that was when Fang Yuan would intend to claim his family assets- the first day that he was officially an adult!
"Lord is too kind!" Dong Tu said with a gentle smile.
"As for your arm-"
"It was an accident while sparring, ah, pay no heed to it. I'm not as young as I used to be- Lord Chi Shan actually came to challenge me the other day to a bout, though with this arm I obviously couldn't hehe..."
"Why don't you allow me to heal you?" Qing Shu asked. It was odd for the bone to be still broken after all this time, even someone like Qing Shu who was not a dedicated healer could probably mend the bone within a few days.
"Ah, the issue is that I have come to lack primeval stones to afford a healer, and I couldn't possibly impose on Lord any further than I already have! I will let it heal naturally!"
It was odd, Qing Shu thought, as Dong Tu made a hasty retreat - it seemed like he preferred his arm broken.

chapters.title: Chapter 75 - 75: Family Inheritance: Part One
chapters.content:
Early that morning, Fang Yuan climbed the steps up to the mission hall, only to see three people waiting for him.
At the lead was Qing Shu, his new team leader.
Next to him was a female Gu Master by the name of Yao Hong. She was a Poison Path Gu Master and someone who didn't like to think very much- preferring to attack with reckless abandon rather than thinking things through.
On the other side was Qing Mao, a Gu Master with green hair. Qing Mao and Qing Shu were not related by blood, but Qing Shu had been adopted by the clan head as his godson and the two were apparently very close. He was an Information Path specialist who was very good at reconnaissance and espionage and by contrast to Yao Hong preferred to mull things over several times before dedicating himself to a decision.
Fang Yuan knew that this meeting was no coincidence- more likely than not, his uncle had set this up. And as much as he'd loved to tiptoe past them, he couldn't very well blatantly ignore them. Especially not when Qing Shu approached him directly.
"Junior Fang Yuan! What are you doing at the mission hall this early in the morning? We don't even start with missions until next week, you know," Qing Shu said.
"I'm here to accept a mission to inherit my family's assets," Fang Yuan replied, as if he didn't know that Qing Shu must've already known that.
"I see," Qing Shu. "Family is quite important- as well as their legacy." He had been orphaned since the wolf tide had taken his parents away at a young age, so he was more privy to most what the importance of family was. He as a lot like Fang Zheng in that regard without a massive inferiority complex. "Fang Yuan, you and I are not so different. Both of us grew up without our parents, and its only natural to want to look after that legacy. I'm sure that you're quite eager to find out what your parents have left behind for you." He had misunderstood why Fang Yuan wanted the inheritance- thinking that he was after the sentimental value of having his parent's things passed down to him. Fang Yuan could care less about his parent's heritage and was only after the primeval stones that those assets could generate- whether they were from his parents or someone else did not matter in the slightest.
"Of course," Qing Shu continued, "family doesn't just extend to your parents, after all. It extends to your cousins, brothers, aunts, uncles- in a way, the entire clan is just like one huge family, Fang Yuan. I'm sure that you've already realized that."
Fang Yuan nodded. When was this guy going to get to the point? He didn't think that this uncle would be able to convince Qing Shu to stand against him when it came to inheriting his family's legacy. His uncle might be influential, but not that influential.
"Fang Yuan, even if you feel that your aunt and uncle have wronged you and your brother in the past," Qing Shu said. "I'm sure that they only wanted the best for you. Tough love is a thing in this world, and now that you're older and can appreciate how hard it is to live in this world, I think you can understand that seeking 'revenge' for perceived slights is useless, especially when it comes to your own family. It is best to simply look towards the future and to let such things go."
Fang Yuan had no clue what he was talking about, though he agreed with the sentiment that revenge was pointless.
"I... I'm afraid that I don't quite understand," Fang Yuan said. For once this wasn't him acting, instead, it was genuine confusion. Qing Shu was being so roundabout with what he was saying that Fang Yuan couldn't figure out what he was actually getting at.
"What I'm trying to say is that you'll ascend to the rank of an elder sooner or later," Qing Shu said. "When you're an elder, you need to look after the clan's needs first and your own later. With great power comes great responsibility, after all. I think you can understand that it is wrong for an elder to take out his frustration on those beneath him."
"I... guess?" Fang Yuan said.
"I know that you and your uncle have had your differences," Qing Shu said. "But taking revenge on them won't heal the scars in your heart. If your parents were still alive, I don't think they'd like to see you turn on the only family you have left."
"Did my uncle say something to you?" Fang Yuan asked.
"Quite perceptive- indeed, I met him earlier and he expressed worry... that the child he had raised so warmly might one day turn on him," Qing Shu said. "I expressed the thought that someone as magnanimous as Fang Yuan could never do something like that."
"And yet, you want confirmation?"
"It's good that you understand."
"Alright," Fang Yuan said. "I'll forego any anger I have towards my aunt and uncle, if you'll help me with the inheritance mission. How about that?"The source of thɪs content is Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"Why you-" Qing Mao was about to say, annoyed that this newly joined freshmen was making demands of Qing Shu, but Qing Shu just laughed and waved him down.
"Not a problem, not a problem, as your new team members, how could we stand by and watch you struggle with a mission?" Qing Shu asked. He had been tasked with bringing Fang Yuan into the clan head's fold, and this was an easy way to get on the newcomer's good side. Originally this treatment was planned for Fang Zheng, but Fang Zheng had gotten crippled and that had ruined the clan head's original plan. He had pivoted then to supporting Fang Yuan, but that had only taken place over a few months. Who knew if Fang Yuan still resented the clan? Because of that, Qing Shu was being extra friendly and welcoming to Fang Yuan.
"Ah, so we have to go do some silly mission? What a drag," Yao Hong complained, but did not object. It was clear that both of the others followed whatever Qing Shu said without objection.
"By the way," Qing Shu asked as they walked down the hall as a group. "What is your brother, Fang Zheng doing?"
"Right now, nothing," Fang Yuan said. "You could say that he's unemployed, spending all of his time in his room cultivating with the Liquor Worm."
Qing Shu frowned. He had not expected Fang Zheng to fall so low so quickly. The only reason that Fang Zheng could behave like this was because of Fang Yuan supporting him, though Qing Shu genuinely hoped that Fang Zheng would eventually recover his self-confidence. He was not someone who carried ill-will towards anyone.
"Let's see... yes, a mission to inherit your parent's fortune..." the clerk said. "Here is one!"

chapters.title: Chapter 76 - 76: Family Inheritance: Part Two
chapters.content:
"Isn't the difficulty of this mission... a bit too high?" Fang Yuan asked as he was handed it.
There was a Twin-Headed Boar, which was a Hundred Beast King, who had wandered too close to some mortal villages, and the task was to chase it away. The issue was that 'chasing' one away was nearly impossible without killing or severely wounding it.
If Fang Yuan did not have the rest of his team, in ordinary times, he would not have been able to complete such a task. Most Rank 2 Gu Masters would not be able to take on a Hundred Beast King- most teams would also find it difficult to deal with that kind of creature.
Of course, for someone like Qing Shu, such a thing would be easy even on his own.
"Young man, newcomers have to prove themselves," the clerk said. "And this is a mission that has been on standby for several months. You are a Rank 2 Gu Master, aren't you?"
"Relax," Qing Shu said, waving the clerk down. "Fang Yuan, with us at your side, you don't need to fear this wild boar."
Fang Yuan initially thought that the mission's high difficulty was because of his uncle's underhanded dealings, though he realized that this was a scheme by Qing Shu.
After all, if Fang Yuan had refused to relinquish his grudge against his aunt and uncle, he would've had to turn to his team members to help with the task at hand. And then, Qing Shu could've mentioned that as a criterion to offer his teammates help.
Fang Yuan was reasonably confident he could tackle the Twin-Headed Boar on his own so long as he could refine the Moonglow Gu. With it, and his superior fighting tactics, an animal would be of no match against him. The issue was that he was part of a team, and not just any team, THE team among teams, and had to pretend to go along with them.
"As a matter of fact," Qing Shu said. "This would be good training for you. I've seen you fight against other humans, but a lot of your fighting as a Gu Master will be against wild beasts. Once you become an elder, fighting against Thousand Beast Kings will be a big aspect of what you will need to do, and oftentimes, you will have to do it in groups. On top of which, the real danger is against Myriad Beast Kings, which have the strength of Rank 4 Gu Masters, meaning that even the clan head might have an issue against them without support from the elders. With us, you can practice your teamwork before heading out."
The other teammates also reassured him that the task was more than possible as Fang Yuan left- the agreement being that they would meet up in two days to deal with the Twin-Headed Boar.
Fang Yuan returned home. The apartment was deficient in a lot of ways, particularly when it came to keeping the cold out. There were a few holes in the walls which the two brothers had hastily fixed with pieces of bamboo sheets and wood. Before, there had not been a heater in the room, though Fang Zheng had taken some time out to fetch some coal and now for the most part the room was at a somewhat bearable temperature. On top of which, several thick blankets were laid out alongside an oil lamp.
The room was quite barebones, but that was just how Fang Yuan liked it and Fang Zheng, if he wanted to keep living there, had little in the way of objecting. Though he had bought some small comforts for himself with some of the primeval stones that Fang Yuan had given him such as a silk undershirt that kept him warm even without the blanket.
Right now, Fang Zheng was cultivating, the Liquor Worm working its hardest to solidify his primeval essence to the point where he could use it to nurture his aperture walls even further.
Fang Yuan did not disturb him, instead retrieving three gu worms- the Moonlight Gu, and two Little Light Gu. He had managed to get an extra Little Light Gu from someone and bought it at a reasonable price, and now was a good chance to try to form the Rank 2 Moonglow Gu.
Fang Zheng eventually opened his eyes and noticed that Fang Yuan had returned. "Brother, you're back already? Did you manage to complete the inheritance mission?"
Fang Yuan shook his head. "It's a bit difficult- having to deal with a Hundred Beast King."
"What? That's outrageous! It's unfair! How are you going to deal with it?"
"It's not a big problem," Fang Yuan said, waving his hand. He had more than enough primeval stones now that he was no longer actively cultivating to attempt refinement of the Moonglow Gu several times, more than enough to be successful. With it, he could finish the mission on his own, let alone with help. So, he would only try once- but the Moonglow Gu would be extremely useful in the future so he might as well start now regardless. "How is your cultivation progressing? Focus on that above all."
"I-I think I'll reach Rank 1 Upper Stage soon," Fang Zheng said.
"Good, good."
"What are you doing?"
"Refining a Rank 2 Gu Worm- hmm... Fang Zheng, there are a few things that I need you to do to help me out here," Fang Yuan said. He could do this easily on his own, but with an assistant to handle some of the more annoying parts for him, it would make it slightly more convenient. He took out a bag of Moon Orchid Petals- by making sure that his worms were fully fed, it would increase the success rate of the refinement.
Just like he had done earlier, he put his will into the three gu worms which began to rotate around each other before they formed a tiny lump of light. Fang Yuan then began tossing in primeval stones, while simultaneously Fang Zheng added in Moon Orchid Petals. This modification was not a new discovery, but something not widely known as being something that would increase the success rate of this refinement. Since they effect was greatest when they were added simultaneously, it was easier to do this with someone assisting you.
The ball of light became compact, before finally dissipating and a new silvery gu worm dropped down onto the table. It had the appearance of a crescent moon, glowing a light silver.
'Even my second attempt at gu fusion succeeded on the first try,' Fang Yuan thought. The success rate of fusing gu worms was rather high at this low level, but it was still quite a feat.
The Moonglow Gu could shoot out moonblades at 300% strength of a Moonlight Gu, though the range remained unchanged. With Fang Yuan's more condensed primeval essence, it would inflict heavy damage even to the body of a Hundred Beast King.
"That's amazing," Fang Zheng said with wonder in his eyes.
"Don't worry, once you get to Rank 2, I'll show you how to do this myself," Fang Yuan said before turning over to go to sleep and to get some rest.
Fang Zheng tried cultivating for a bit longer before retiring as well.

chapters.title: Chapter 77 - 77: Family Inheritance: Part Three
chapters.content:
When it came to the Twin-Headed Boar, although it would be a problem for many Rank 2 Gu Masters, to someone like Fang Yuan he felt that he would have a 60-70% chance of being able to take it down on his own.
The reason that his estimate was so low was because of two things. One, he did not know what kind of wild gu worms it had on itself. Secondly, he did not have a full set of combat gu worms yet- most crucially he was lacking a relevant gu worm in the movement category which could've been quite helpful.
However, even with those flaws he could've brought that number up to 80-90% if he used one of his Red Steel Relic Gu, and to 100% if he used both. That would've increased his primeval essence reserves fourfold, and with just attack and defense he would've been able to brute force the fight. Were he determined to go at this alone though, he also would've bought a movement-type gu worm before embarking on this mission in case of any unforeseen contingency.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
As it was, for now, he didn't have to go that far. He had team members for now, if only temporarily, meaning that it would also be useful in hiding some of his own trump cards.
"Now, the way that we're going to tackle this is quite classic," Qing Shu said. "I'll form the head of the formation, while the other two will flank the beast. Fang Yuan, since this is your first real fight against such a creature, no need to be scared, but stay towards the back. Any opening you find though, feel free to strike- but don't get too worried. This is more of an introduction to you so you get the hang of such fast-paced fights, you know?"
"Yeah, don't fret about it too much, kiddo," Yao Hong said. "Just stand back and watch the experts do it."
"Indeed, I'll even record the fight so you can view it later," Qing Mao said. He had already been quite helpful in deducing the location of the Twin-Headed Boar and hiding their own traces. It was lounging in the sun in an open field, the perfect place to ambush it. Its brethren were scattered around the area. Fang Yuan was tasked with trying to deal with them should the beast king ask for reinforcements, though they weren't sure of just how good its control over its subordinates was.
"Alright, let's go," Qing Shu said.
They emerged, though once they were twenty paces away, Qing Shu put his hands on the soil.
That was his specialty- he was a Wood Path Gu Master and could transform parts of his body into a treeman. Of course, this came with the risk that if he transformed for too long he would permanently become a tree - although Fang Yuan had not personally witnessed it, back in his old life, he was certain that more likely than not this was the cause of his death.
Vines shot through the soil before wrapping around the Twin-Headed Boar, binding it in placed. Both of its heads immediately woke up, and it snarled, though it couldn't even turn either head towards the people striking it.
Yao Hong took in a deep breath, and then let out a cloud of noxious green smoke. Poison Cloud Gu- while it was quite useful as an attacking option, it carried the major risk of the cloud turning in response to wind and the like, potentially hurting the Gu Master in question who had cast it or their allies. It was a lot like using weapons like mustard gas back on Earth, though they had been careful to be downwind from the cloud as it enveloped the Twin-Headed Boar. It began to screech in pain as the surrounding boar began to come to its aid.
Moonblades flew from Fang Yuan's and Qing Mao's hands, bisecting the ordinary boar in two in a single hit. Qing Mao was reasonably proficient with the moonblade, using a Moonglow Gu just like Fang Yuan was.
Qing Shu had transformed his arms into long branches and was whipping the Twin-Headed Boar as it screeched in pain. The poison seemed to be taken effect as it became disoriented, though it was still quite dangerous in its frenzied state.
Yao Hong's cheek's swelled up as she spat out a gobbet of green acid at the boar, melting its skin and the acid slowly making its way to its internal organs.
The boar shrieked, and a small black dot atop it jumped up and glowed, the acid slowly reducing and eventually turning into nothing as the wound began to close.
It had a healing-type gu worm!
However, Qing Shu had been expecting this, and his arms went from being long branches to being short but sharp claws. His goal now was to decapitate the Twin-Headed Boar, either that, or strike at its heart to ensure its quick and swift death in a single blow.
Fang Yuan and Qing Mao had also joined in at this point, raining Moonblades upon the beast. Fang Yuan was even able to take out one of its heads, though this only made the other head grow angrier as the stump that had been its other head began to heal and turn into stub, slowly growing back.
In a battle of attrition, the boar would have the upper hand, which was why it was crucial that they strike a killing blow now.
Yao Hong shot out another gobbet of acid, melting the skin down to its bones- the healing gu worm it had could not react in time as Qing Shu took advantage of this moment to sneak his hand inside and then rip out the boar's right lung, stomach, and heart.
It squealed in agony, but by now, it was clear that it no longer had any fight within it.
The battle was over within a matter of minutes. Fang Yuan estimated that it would've taken him at least half an hour to deal with it if he were on his lonesome.
Two specks of black jumped out from its corpse- these were the wild gu worms on its body that had abandoned it now that it was dead. If Fang Yuan was alone he potentially could've used the Spring Autumn Cicada to harvest them, but given current circumstances they only watched the two gu worms run away. He was a bit curious as to what the second gu worm was given they hadn't seen any effect from it, but it could've been something like the Black or White Boar Gu which weren't that useful in combat to the Twin-Headed Boar.
The ground was littered with the entrails of the boar, and a rancid odor was emanating not just from its corpse but because of the poisons and acid injected into it, but they had won without much difficulty. Unfortunately, this meant that parts of the corpse were not usable as they had been damaged, otherwise the bones and the meat could be used at refinement materials for various gu worms.
"Well done Fang Yuan, that was good," Qing Shu said. "We only need to tell the local Gu Master about this, and the record of you succeeding will reach the town hall."
The local Gu Master was more likely than not just Rank 1 and ill-equipped to deal with something like this.
Before they headed home back to the village though, Fang Yuan was interrupted by the system giving him a new mission.
New main mission!
Familial Ties
Description: Save Teng Ru.
Reward: Permanent 2% increase to one's aptitude.
Fang Yuan made some excuses to stay behind, saying that he wanted to take in the scenery- and though this got him odd looks none of the others said anything as Fang Yuan headed towards where this supposed Teng Ru was that the system was telling him about.

chapters.title: Chapter 78 - 78: Family Inheritance: Part Four
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan approached the house under the cover of One With Scenery Gu, in case the others were tailing him.
Now, it wasn't like he was doing anything shady at the moment- quite the contrary, but the more that people observed him, the greater would be the risk that the system would be discovered. And as it was, there were several methods that he had that he would prefer remain undiscovered.
He knocked on the wooden frame of the house after dispelling the effect of his gu, but no one answered until he knocked again.
"Come in..." a voice answered.
Fang Yuan took a step in. It was a small hut, much like all mortal houses, and very simple on the inside.
"Oh did you finally-" the woman who said this stopped mid-sentence as she saw Fang Yuan. He was no longer wearing his school uniform but that of an adult Gu Master, which was a uniform that every mortal on the mountain would recognize. It signified his entrance into adult life, and that all mortals were to give him deference when they saw him. She had clearly not been expecting a Gu Master to wander into their shack. "Ah... Lord- you..."
Fang Yuan waved his hand and tried to give her a reassuring smile. "No matter for formalities, I had heard that there was a young lady by the name of Teng Ru in this village who was sick. I came to check up on her. Is there someone like that here?"
"Why- yes, there is someone like that here... I didn't know that news had become so widespread though... but, Lord, I do not have the treasure to pay you back for such a service..." she said. She reached into a secluded enclave in the house and took out one-eighth of a primeval stone, likely her entire savings.
"It is no matter," Fang Yuan said. "Perhaps you have heard my name before- my name is Gu Yue Fang Yuan. I can't bear to see anyone suffering, and whenever I hear of people in need of help, I feel compelled to lend my aide to them."
The woman frowned. She had heard of a Gu Master who wandered around the villages performing miracles, though she had dismissed this as a fanciful rumor. "Then... this one would be eternally grateful for your help."ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
"I take it that you are not Teng Ru then?" Fang Yuan asked. This woman didn't look injured, but he couldn't be sure. Perhaps she had some kind of incurable disease?"
"No, no, my name is Teng Mai," she said. She then led Fang Yuan to the only other room in the house, where there was a sickly-looking woman on a makeshift mat, likely one of the only pieces of furniture in the house.
Fang Yuan looked at the sick woman, and at Teng Mai. Their faces were close... no, not just close, identical. Though the sickness had marred the other one's features somewhat, they looked like carbon copies of each other.
"The two of you are twins?" Fang Yuan asked.
"Indeed, Lord," Teng Mai answered.
Fang Yuan had a good idea as to why that was. There were often hidden meanings behind various things in life even if one didn't see them- he hadn't been able to during his previous life, but with his 500 years of experience it was like he was wearing X-ray goggles and could see things for how they really were.
Qing Shu did not really want to help him- he had 'helped' him but only after amplifying the difficulty of the mission first. And there was also the fact that he wanted to train Fang Yuan for the future. These all were not necessarily malicious hidden intentions, but he hadn't exactly been open with them either. Someone like Fang Zheng might've been blind to such things, but not Fang Yuan.
The same thing for the system- Fang Yuan was sure that it had several deeper ulterior motives. Among them was trying to get him to feel for the villagers and to gain a reputation of being a good person. It likely hoped that if people saw him that way, or that if Fang Yuan continued to act in that way, he would unconsciously become that way. It was ultimately futile, which is why it had given him this kind of mission.
Twin sisters- who were caring and supporting each other. The one who was healthy had not abandoned the other, even living in what was squalor even by mortal standards just to take care of her sick sister. One could assume that the Teng twins had no other family, but they still supported each other as much as they could.
More likely than not it expected him to have empathy for them given how close their situation was with the Fang twins. Or, it could possibly be trying to get him to also care for Fang Zheng in the way that Teng Mai cared for Teng Ru.
"I think that I can help her," Fang Yuan said. "But... I would ask you to leave the house."
Teng Mei was a bit alarmed. "leave...?"
"This healing technique I know is a secret, and I've sworn to not reveal it to strangers," Fang Yuan said. "Don't worry, it will only take a few moments."
Teng Mei wasn't fully sure about leaving her sister with this strange man- but then again, he was a Gu Master. What could she do against him if he turned angry? And maybe he could help her?
She left but resolved to keep herself just outside the door, in order to listen in case Fang Yuan tried something untoward.
Fang Yuan had asked her to leave because he didn't want to reveal the secret of Doctor Gu- it was not an issue to use a strange gu worm before a mortal who would likely not recognize it, but its ability to turn into a human was not something usual and would stand out even to a mortal.
"Alright, I need you to heal her," Fang Yuan instructed. Could Doctor Gu really heal her? He didn't know- but the system hadn't given him a task which was impossible as of yet, so he assumed that he was supposed to use it hear.
"Very well, Young Master," Doctor Gu said, bowed, and examined Teng Ru for an instant. The girl looked sickly with a green tinge to her skin as her eyes were tightly shut- it looked like she was having a fever as well. "Ah... I think I have diagnosed the problem."
"Oh? What is it?"
"It appears that this young miss has an extreme Yin Physique and has gone into a coma because of excess Yin energy. Ah, Young Master, the only way to cure her is for you to use your Yang rod to extract the excess Yin from her body," Doctor Gu said.
Doctor Gu: ...
Fang Yuan: ...
Doctor Gu wiped off some sweat from his forehead. "That was a joke, Young Master, but don't worry, I can patch up this girl as good as new."
Fang Yuan sighed. Perhaps it was a blessing that most gu worms couldn't talk...
Doctor Gu waved his hand, and Teng Rei suddenly looked livelier as the color returned to her cheeks given them a rose-tinted hue.
"That was quick..." Fang Yuan said, transforming Doctor Gu back into a gu worm and placing it in his aperture.
The Human Path is extremely good at healing, host!
It was like the system was trying to push the Human Path on him as much as possible. He still hadn't used any of his Human Path dao marks simply because it would be very hard to get rid of them once he agreed to it, and so, they were all still in his inventory. He also didn't want to commit to an entire path simply because of this system. Though, he had to admit that the effect was quite remarkable, the girl opening her eyes, saw Fang Yuan.
"Are you... an angel...?"
"Yes," Fang Yuan said. "I am an angel- one who wishes to bring peace and happiness to all the members of this world. No need to thank me- I'll get your sister from outside."
Before Teng Ru could thank him, Fang Yuan had already stepped out and let Teng Mei know that his work here was done, ignoring all insistences that she do at least something to pay him back.
"Helping others is the greatest reward in and of itself," Fang Yuan said, trotting off as his aptitude increased to 63%.

chapters.title: Chapter 79 - 79: Family Inheritance: Part Five
chapters.content:
63% versus 61%- the difference was only slight, but it was actually huge for someone like Fang Yuan. 61% would be just enough to overcome the aperture's rate of recovery, but not enough to make more than the slightest progress that would evaporate the moment that he took long breaks between cultivating- something that was nearly guaranteed to happen now that he was paired up with Qing Shu and his team.
Much like when he had been class president, he would be heaped with a mountain of useless tasks designed on the surface to increase his prestige, but mainly to waste his time and keep him occupied. It was much in the same of what they were doing with Qing Shu- else he'd be at Rank 3 as well.
This was the burden of the righteous path and why he had no desire to re-establish the Blood Wing Demon Sect in this life. His goal was to take as much from the clan as possible, and give as little back as possible.
But, that was why being at 63% was important, that small 2% difference would let him accumulate small bits of damage to the aperture wall over time even with short interruptions. Then, he would be able to take a few days out in closed door cultivation to break through in one go, so long as he had an adequate number of primeval stones. Which, once he got the inheritance, he would have access too.
The right time to use the two Red Steel Relic Gu were after the merchant caravan had come to the village, giving him a plausible reason as to where he had obtained them from. There was always the chance that the caravan would not have them, but based on his prior life's memories, there should have been at least one.
As he exited the mortal's house, he did not leave to go back home immediately but instead used One With Scenery Gu after recovering his primeval essence using primeval stones. He was looking for one of the gu worms that he thought he saw escape from the Twin-Headed Boar's corpse. He could've been wrong, but he thought that it was the Rank 2 Rush Gu- a type of movement gu worm that would increase one's speed while moving in one direction for a short duration. The issue was that once one had chosen a direction to move in they could not change it.
It could be advanced to the Rank 3 Rush Recklessly Gu- a gu worm that had higher speed and also increased one's strength while moving, though it had the same weakness.
Wild gu worms were common enough, to the point where they could be hazardous to a traveler wandering around their own if they were not at Rank 3. However, Fang Yuan did not fear the retaliation of a Rank 2 gu worm, not when he had the Spring Autumn Cicada which could instantly refine it. Actually, this difficulty in refining wild gu worms was why none of Qing Shu's team had bothered to try to go after it.
'Whether or not I can find the Rush Gu will be entirely based on my luck,' Fang Yuan thought.
He had thought the worm had moved in this direction, but it was a movement-based worm after all. It could very well be quite far from the area.
Despite trying for over an hour, even expending a good number of primeval stones to do so, he had not been able to find it. It had likely wandered far away into the wilderness. If he had acted sooner, he might've been able to catch it, but the 2% increase to his aptitude was far more beneficial to him than that gu worm. While it would've been wonderful if he could've obtained both of them at the same time, life rarely went the way that one wanted.
Fang Yuan knew when to cut his losses and went back to the village.
Standing near the mission hall was his uncle, dressed up in a Gu Master uniform that looked worn with the colors faded out. Several small tears could be seen in it, he had not had the time to repair it before trying to accost Fang Yuan. His arm was still in a sling, and the overall appearance gave him a pitiful look.
The hall already knew that Fang Yuan had taken care of the Hundred Beast King, and so it was a simple matter for Fang Yuan to obtain that inheritance. Naturally Uncle did not want such a thing to transpire, which is why he had bundled up his courage to confront Fang Yuan, forgetting his earlier fear of possibly being found out.Googlᴇ search NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
"Fang Yuan," Uncle said. "Think about what I've said to you earlier. Clan relationships are quite important. If you forego this inheritance, I am willing to offer you eight thousand primeval stones as well as my friendship."
Fang Yuan was a bit taken aback by the price, but that only made him want it even more.
"Fang Yuan, listen, don't be rash!"
"Fang Yuan, won't you take pity upon your aunt and uncle who raised you?"
"Fang Yuan, is this the disposition of a leader?"
These words fell on deaf ears as Fang Yuan advanced to take the inheritance. He scoffed at his uncle's foolishness- still being bound by the rules of the clan and being unable to do anything other than yell out rancid words at him.
He had not figured out that Uncle was behind the attack on Fang Zheng, even now.
Main mission complete!
Obtained familial inheritance!
Reward:
Rank 4 Doting Mother Gu (x 1)
Rank 4 Traveling Son Gu (x 1)
You have also obtained a small dream realm. Would you like to explore it now?
Fang Yuan took a look at his gains other than the ones he had inherited.
Doting Mother Gu and Traveling Son Gu were a pair- if one person had Traveling Son Gu they could instantly transport to the person who had Doting Mother Gu. That was true for their immortal forms, it was likely that these Rank 4 version had a limited range. While a powerful effect regardless, it could only be used one way and was of little use to a solo cultivator like Fang Yuan.
It had a few other drawbacks. Both of the people using it had to be of Rank 4 for it to have its full effect. It also did not work in reverse- the person with Doting Mother Gu could not teleport to the person who had Traveling Son Gu. The limitations were numerous, but that was also why its range of effect was likewise large.
'Also system, isn't this a bit on the nose? Are you making fun of me? After getting my inheritance from my dead parents you're giving me a gu worm called 'Doting Mother Gu' as if reminding me of what I don't have?' Fang Yuan thought.
The system would never dare do such a thing. Would you like to explore your dream realm now?
'Of course not, we're in the middle of the street,' Fang Yuan thought as he went back home.
The contents of the inheritance itself included a wine store, a set of bamboo buildings, and a Nine Leaf Vitality Grass Gu. No wonder Uncle had been willing to pay such a high price for all of this- to Fang Yuan most of the property would soon be useless, but the Nine Leaf Vitality Grass Gu was worth taking along even with him on his travels. It was a shame that he had been handed another healing gu worm when he already had Rank 3 Doctor Gu, but as a source of income it was not bad.

chapters.title: Chapter 80 - 80: Family Inheritance: Part Six
chapters.content:
The Nine Leaf Vitality Grass was an excellent gu worm, because it could be used to generate the Rank 1 Vitality Leaf Gu in perpetuity so long as it had enough primeval essence given to it. It took the appearance of a small plant, and when injected with primeval essence it would generate up to nine Vitality Leaf Gu. While only a Rank 1 gu worm, considering the fact that it was a healing-type gu worm and in the right circumstances could save one's life if a healer was not at hand, it sold for a very good price.
Of course, Fang Yuan did not have a monopoly on the supply of Vitality Leaves. The clan had a few Nine Leaf Vitality Grass Gu in its possession and some Gu Masters were tasked with the production of Vitality Leaves for the clan, but that was all fine with Fang Yuan. If he had a monopoly it might end up being seized from him for the good of the clan.
The issue was that while it could produce Rank 1 gu almost limitlessly so long as it had sunlight and water, it consumed a large amount of primeval essence to do so. While that was not an issue for now, given that he was going to simply use the Red Steel Relic Gu to advance, it would be in the future. He would need his primeval essence in order to advance, not to generate Vitality Leaves. Also, the more he made, the lower the price would be. On a good day, he could get about fifty primeval stones for each Vitality Leaf, though as the wolf tide crept closer and closer, the price would steadily edge up higher.
In addition to the Nine Leaf Vitality Grass, there was the wine tavern and the bamboo apartments to take care of. Taking care of the bamboo apartments was not too difficult considering the fact that he had moved into one, being close to the others. But the wine tavern and raising and selling Vitality Leaves put a big burden upon how much time he had. This in addition to the various missions that he had to do along with Qing Shu would've left scarce time for cultivating even if he was serious about advancing right now and wasn't biding his time until he could use the Red Steel Relic Gu.
In his previous life, he had only himself to rely upon. However, he now had a lackey who would take care of much of these problems for him.
Fang Yuan's #1 lackey as a matter of fact - Fang Zheng!
Fang Zheng's life followed a simple routine. He would wake up early in the morning, his primeval essence having been replenished overnight.
He would make a quick inspection of the bamboo buildings that Fang Yuan owned, making sure that there were no issues going on with them. Some of the female tenants tried to get close to him, but he rejected them all.
