Many of them were Rank 2 Gu Masters, and for such people to show interest in Fang Zheng was in itself unusual- unless you accounted for how valuable real estate was in Gu Yue village. There was a limit to how far the village could expand, and as such rent was high for those who did not own their own homes.
When these women had realized that Fang Yuan did not care for them, they instead set their sights on Fang Zheng- seeing that he was allowed a place to stay by Fang Yuan without even needing to pay rent. They thought that if they became Fang Zheng's wife, they might also receive such treatment.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
But while Fang Yuan was indifferent to their advances, Fang Zheng actively hated them. Ever since he had been betrayed by Shen Cui, he had started to hate women in general, thinking of them as nothing more than gold-digging hoes. He knew why it was that the women were showing this kind of interest in him.
'Women will only slow down the speed at which I cultivate,' Fang Zheng thought. This attitude of his was subtly encouraged by Fang Yuan, who didn't want him to suddenly run off with some random girl.
As it was, he was currently stuck at Rank 1 Middle Stage and hadn't been able to advance to Rank 1 Middle Stage. The reason for this was that once he was done inspecting the buildings, he would return back to his living quarters and use the Nine Leaf Vitality Grass. It was a Rank 2 gu worm, and so he couldn't use it to its full extent, but with the help of the Liquor Worm he could still produce two or three Vitality Leaves with each session. He would do so in the morning and in the evening, and would only cultivate with whatever essence he had left afterwards.
This did limit the speed at which he could ascend. On top of which, Fang Zheng did not own the Nine Leaf Vitality Grass or the profits gained from selling Vitality Leaves. Almost all of that went to Fang Yuan with little left to him, but he could do little about it.
'Elder Brother needs these primeval stones to advance to Rank 3,' Fang Zheng thought. 'Once that happens, he'll become an elder and then with those extra primeval stones, he'll help me get to Rank 2. For the big picture, it's better if I keep working for him.'
Fang Zheng thought these things mainly to reassure himself more than anything else. There was a small needling part of him which thought- 'What if brother is just using me and will abandon me once he becomes an elder?' Being stabbed in the back by Aunt and Uncle had dealt quite a blow to his ability to trust other people in general.
But, he pushed down this worry away. If he started to doubt everyone, he would have to become the kind of demon that Fang Yuan truly was- though the issue with that was that Fang Zheng did not have Fang Yuan's 500 years of experience of walking down the demonic path.
Once he was done with this, he took the Vitality Leaves and visited the wine tavern.
It was a small building though the effective area could be somewhat expanded so long as tables were set outside.
Fang Zheng was not worried as he walked down the street, even if he was carrying valuable gu worms with him. For one, he looked exactly like Fang Yuan at first glance and no one wanted to mess with the latter. Secondly, Fang Yuan was well known to hang out with Qing Shu, and so no one wanted to find trouble with Fang Zheng either. Third, Fang Zheng was not completely defenseless. While his vital gu continued to be the Liquor Worm, he had bought a Moonlight Gu for himself using a portion of the earnings that Fang Yuan had given him from selling Vitality Leaves.
Speaking of, when he went to the wine tavern he would order a glass of wine to feed his Liquor Worm. The Liquor Worm did not have many paths of advancement, so he felt rather bad regarding having it as his vital gu. Unlike Fang Yuan he did not know the full potential of this gu worm and felt that the Moonlight Gu was better in terms of advancement given how many recipes that the clan had for the same.
The Mist Perspiring Butterfly, which was the advancement path that the Flower Wine Monk had chosen, was rather useless unless it was your aspiration in life to become a serial flower thief. The clan did have a recipe for the Seven Fragrances Liquor Worm but this had a dud Rank 2 stage which was not that useful.

chapters.title: Chapter 81 - 81: Family Inheritance: Part Seven
chapters.content:
'Rank 3 stage, huh,' Fang Zheng thought to himself as he thought about the Seven Fragrances Liquor Worm. Before, he had been nearly guaranteed to not only reach that stage, but possibly even Rank 4 or Rank 5 if fortune favored him. Now though, it was a lengthy struggle to reach Rank 2.
Even Fang Yuan had been stuck at Rank 2 in his old life until he had been lucky enough to chance upon a talent-raising gu worm. Fang Zheng could not count on that luxury, he could only count on Fang Yuan's help to reach that place. That was why although Fang Zheng had some doubts on how much he could truly trust Fang Yuan, he still chose to stick close to his elder brother.
Trying to reach Rank 3 like this was a paper dream. His elder brother told him that it was possible, but everyone else seemed to tell him to give up on ever achieving that realm. Whenever Fang Zheng expressed such doubts, Fang Yuan would tell him to not let the words of other people bring him down. 'I am ready to promise you this, younger brother, I will find a way to get you to Rank 3,' Fang Yuan would always say.
But if Fang Yuan offered him the sun in his pocket the next day, would Fang Zheng believe it? It would be hard for anyone to wrap their heads around such a thing.
Managing the wine tavern was not that much of a big issue. It basically ran itself, and the shopkeepers and workers did not dare do anything to offend either of the brothers. All of the workers were mortals after all and greatly valued their employment in this place, which offered a safe and steady paycheck. Fang Yuan had even increased their salaries by a not-insignificant percentage, and although Fang Zheng could not wrap his head around why his brother thought it was a good idea, he didn't question this decision.
Fang Zhen mainly just did whatever his brother asked, and rarely if ever provided any kind of pushback. He was completely ignorant to many of these businesses, and figured that Fang Yuan had a better grasp on things.
The main reason he would come to the wine tavern was not to drink (although this was a small upside, and also fed his vital gu worm) or to oversee it, but rather to transact the Vitality Leaves with Jiang Ya.
As it was no one dared to cause trouble in this shop. Reason being was that Fang Yuan had been able to use his membership with Qing Shu to his advantage, one day after a tough mission saying, 'Seniors, I must thank you all for your help and guidance over all of these missions - please let me thank you all by treating you some top-quality wine at my inn!'
Even if they refused Fang Yuan once, or twice, eventually out of basic courtesy they were forced to swing by. And once it was known that characters like Qing Shu occasionally came to the tavern, no one had the stones to cause a scene here. As it was, business was also going smoothly thanks to the tavern now having a finer reputation than before.
"Brother Fang Zheng!" Jiang Ya said as he walked in to sit beside Fang Zheng. Jiang Ya did not have a good opinion of Fang Yuan- but that didn't meant that he was averse from benefitting from a relationship with the latter. After all, Fang Yuan now had a small fortune to himself, and Jiang Ya was eager to scoop up some of that for himself.
Jiang Ya functioned as a sort of middleman in their transactions, finding buyers for the Vitality Leaves and keeping a portion of the sales as commission for himself. The brothers could do this on their own if they wanted- but to Fang Yuan it would waste even more precious time and he had no need to go around cavorting with people to earn their favor. Fang Zheng felt he was even more pressed for time and no longer had a good reputation around the village, and saw no need to try and change it currently. All of his focus had to be either on cultivating, or helping his brother cultivate.
Fang Zheng handed him a bag with six Vitality Leaves as Jiang Ya handed him a bag of primeval stones. "Ah, if only Brother Fang Yuan would help us by lending his primeval essence to generate even more- the profits could be even greater!" To Jiang Ya, who treated this enterprise as a risk-free means to earn money, the more Vitality Leaves he obtained, the greater his benefits.
Fang Zheng counted the primeval stones to make sure the amount was right- he was not like Fang Yuan, after all, who could tell by simply weighing it upon his hand. It could be seen as insulting to the seller for Fang Zheng to do this right in front of him even after they had transacted several times, but Fang Zheng knew that Jiang Ya would not terminate this relationship over something so minor.
"I will reach Rank 1 Upper Stage soon," Fang Zheng said. 'Soon' was a bit of a relative term, but it was true nonetheless. "After that, I'll have Rank 1 Peak Stage essence to use to make more Vitality Leaves- I'll be able to make a full set of nine each day." A Rank 2 Gu Master could easily make nine leaves so long as they were willing to expend most of their primeval essence, but Fang Zheng was only Rank 1. It was not as much of an issue to use the Nine Leaf Vitality Grass as some other gu worm as it was not combat-focused and he could use his primeval essence over time to achieve the same effect- something one could not rely up in battle.
"Of course!" Jiang Ya said. "And I assume Brother Fang Yuan is too busy with his duties to the clan to work on something like this- but I'm sure that Brother Fang Zheng will reach Rank 1 Upper Stage and sooner or later even Rank 2 Stage without much difficulties. Ah, I can see that your future is quite bright, Fang Zheng, and I wish you all the luck in the world!"
Inwardly Jiang Ya was delighted to see someone like Fang Zheng fall from grace given he was a trash-tier talent and misery loves company. Outwardly though, he always made it a point to praise Fang Zheng- and as it was, if Fang Zheng did get better and make more Vitality Leaves it would give him a greater commission. In the same vein he didn't mind Fang Yuan's success so much any longer so long as he could benefit from it.
"Thank you," Fang Zheng said, feeling slightly better about himself even if he knew most of the praise was not genuine.
He would then leave the tavern and go back home, primeval essence recovered to start the process of nurturing Vitality Leaves once again. Only once he had finished two rounds like this did he start his own cultivation. Fang Yuan could've greatly increased the efficiency and speed of this if he was willing to lend his help, but he was fine letting Fang Zheng struggle a bit- if Fang Zheng advanced too fast, he might become rebellious, which is why Fang Yuan suppressed him in this roundabout way.
However, this day, Fang Yuan was waiting for Fang Zheng when he returned home. He took the bag of primeval stones from Fang Zheng, setting it aside with the rest of the hoard he was building up for various purposes, the most important of which was ascending to Rank 3. "Fang Zheng, I have an important task for you."Google seaʀᴄh No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
Fang Zheng was a bit surprised when he heard of the details of the request, but was always willing to lend his elder brother a hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 82 - 82: Family Inheritance: Part Eight
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan sat in a meditative pose while Fang Zheng stood to the side.
Fang Yuan was attempting to explore the small dream realm that the system had given him- but he needed to take some precautions first.
Dream realm exploration had exploded onto the scene in the future- but was still several centuries behind in the present day. Dream realms were just being explored and if the prophecy of the Three Venerables was true, would culminate in the development in the Great Dream Immortal Venerable some years later. Fang Yuan, despite his knowledge as a regressor, did not know who the Great Dream Immortal Venerable was as she had yet to emerge.
Dream realms were manifestations of dreams, as the name implied. Their main use was to refine dream gu, and to obtain attainment levels in various paths.
Attainment was oftentimes confused with knowledge of a path- but they were different even if they overlapped somewhat. Attainment was different from knowledge of a path, and more of an instinctual understanding of the methods and ways of that path.
As an example, an experienced doctor might not have as much theoretical or book knowledge as a recently graduated medical student. And still, if presented with a patient, the experienced doctor would be able to diagnose the issue nearly at a glance while the newly graduated student would have difficulty with it despite their perhaps superior theoretical understanding.
In the same way, if someone's attainment level of a path increased, while they would also usually have more knowledge of the path and its various gu worms, they would also be able to piece together new developments or solve problems like the arrangement of gu worms or the formation of killer moves far easier than a novice would be able to. With time they would even be able to think of new aspects or uses for certain gu worms in the path.
Attainment levels were divided into Ordinary, Master, Grandmaster, Great Grandmaster, and Supreme Grandmaster. Between each of these major attainment levels there was a 'quasi' stage such as quasi-Master, quasi-Grandmaster, etc.
The most obvious way of raising attainment levels was by studying the path in detail. Fang Yuan was a Grandmaster in the Blood Path as he had chanced upon one of the inheritances of the Blood Sea ancestor. He was a Master in the Refinement Path from simple experience in refining gu worms, as well as Flying from the same. Most mortals, however, would only remain at the Ordinary level throughout their lives, with less than 1% reaching Master attainment.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
While attainment levels did not increase one's battle strength directly- it was theoretically possible to be a Supreme Grandmaster and only be at Rank 1, they did greatly increase one's ability in multiple indirect ways. They made it easier to deduce new gu recipes, made it easier to make new killer moves, and also made it easier to counter enemy attacks or defenses of the same path. The best part of attainment levels was that they did not obstruct each other in any way, meaning one could raise one's attainment level in various paths and they would not only not interfere with each other but also synergize in some ways with one another, helping one make complex killer moves and giving inspiration for the same.
The best way of raising them, however, was through dream realms. In the future, dream realm exploration would explode, and numerous 'geniuses' would emerge in the world with massive attainment levels in various paths. During that time, Masters and Grandmasters would become commonplace even among mortals.
Dream realms could raise one's attainment level instantly- that which had taken Fang Yuan nearly two centuries and the guidance of an expert in the field could be attained within a few weeks.
That said, there were several dangers to exploring dream realms as well. For one, it could damage one's soul, and if one was not careful enough, one could remain trapped within a dream realm. That, or their soul could be damaged severely to the point that their bodies would remain nothing but lifeless husks.
As it was, Fang Yuan only had an ordinary soul as he had no strengthening methods readily available to him. The best way to strengthen one's soul was the use of Guts Gu obtained from Dang Hun Mountain, a secluded domain of heaven and earth. However, Dang Hun Mountain was currently in the Hu Immortal Blessed Land which would only open up in a few years, after the Three King's Inheritance had. Fang Yuan, despite his knowledge of this would normally not be able to try and obtain Dang Hun Mountain even after regression as his time to advance was limited, however, with the help of the system it might indeed be possible to grow strong enough to obtain Dang Hun Mountain!
'If I get strong enough, Dang Hun Mountain can be mine in this timeline!' Fang Yuan thought. With the increase in the strength of his soul, it would make exploring dream realms even easier in the future. With his knowledge of the future, he could easily outpace other people by leaps and bounds in this field, attaining great heights in various paths.
The system assuaged him that this was a simple dream realm with practically no risks, but Fang Yuan was not one to place blind faith in anyone. He had examined it to some extent himself before placing it back in his inventory- and this is why he had employed Fang Zheng to stand guard of him while he did so. Intense pain could wake someone from a minor dream realm as long as they weren't too deeply entrenched inside, which is why Fang Zheng was instructed to hurt Fang Yuan's arm if he didn't wake up in ten hours.
Fang Yuan removed the dream realm from his inventory- it was barely the size of a pomegranate seed. It looked like a small blob of gel that shone in various prismatic colors like a thin layer of oil upon water that hung in the air. Fang Zheng looked at it with confusion as Fang Yuan entered the dream realm.
He found himself lying on the floor, looking up at a ceiling. He tried moving his arms and legs, but found that his movement was quite limited.
'Hold on... why does this seem so familiar?' Fang Yuan wondered before barely being able to turn his head with great effort to see an infant lying beside him. Whenever one first entered a dream realm, they would usually take a glance at what tools they were given. But Fang Yuan found nothing- he had no gu worms, no cultivation, he could not even move his arms or legs fully as if they were tied down. But they weren't- it was just that they felt heavy as if they suddenly weighed ten times as much as normal.
He was in a crib, and the infant sleeping beside him seemed to be somewhat familiar as well.
'So is this a baby's dream realm? How odd,' he thought. Dream realms gave attainment levels precisely because they borrowed on other people's attainments who had lived in the past. What deep attainment could a baby possibly have?
He lay there for a while before someone entered his field of vision, appearing like a giant given his tiny size.
It was a woman with soft features, one whom Fang Yuan recognized only from a portrait he had once seen long ago at a funeral.
'Mother...?'

chapters.title: Chapter 83 - 83: Family Inheritance: Part Nine
chapters.content:
"Little Fang Yuan... how are you today...?" the woman gently cooed as she examined Fang Yuan, making funny faces at him.
Fang Yuan was impassive, causing her to have a worried look, before she heard someone crying.
Fang Zheng was making noise back in the crib once he saw that Fang Yuan wasn't there- or maybe he just wanted his mother's attention.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
'Even back then, Fang Zheng always wanted to be the center of attention...' Fang Yuan thought as his mother picked up his brother, who stopped crying.
For some time, the dream realm involved Fang Yuan just lying there while his mother tried to coax him into smiling, which he eventually did.
"Both of you will grow up to be so big and strong one day... won't you?" she said in the high-pitched voice people used to talk to babies.
The thing was, this was not actually Fang Yuan's 'mother' per se. After all, he was a transmigrator from Earth, and the people he considered to be his true parents were back there. These two were simply the parents of the body he had transmigrated into. As such, while the dream realm might've been set up to evoke nostalgia within him he felt nothing of the sort.
His mother put the two of them back into the crib, and beside him, Fang Zheng fell asleep.
Fang Yuan in his current state could not see anything as his ability to move his head was limited, but he heard a second set of footsteps approach and a man's voice join the woman's.
"Are you ready to head out?"
"Just a while longer- did you remember to take a sack of primeval stones?'
"Indeed. Do you have enough food for our trip?"
"Of course."
The voices chatted with each other as there were the sounds of furniture being moved around, before the visage of another person filled Fang Yuan's view.
This was of a man in his early twenties or thirties, who saw Fang Yuan and gave a puzzled look. If the other woman was 'mother' then there was no doubt that this man was 'father.' "Fang Yuan isn't sleeping?"
"No," a voice came, slightly worried. "Sometimes it worries me- Fang Yuan doesn't cry like a normal child should, and he rarely if ever smiles. He isn't like Fang Zheng... or how the other babies should behave. At least, not from what I've heard."
"No, there's nothing wrong," the man said, smiling while pinching Fang Yuan's cheeks. "He's just learned to be strong for his brother, haven't you Fang Yuan? Remember, because you're the oldest, we'll be counting on you to take care of Fang Zheng."
"Ah, he won't have to worry about doing that- after all, what are we here for?" Mother retorted.
"Of course, of course," Father replied. "But the world is a harsh place, who knows what the future holds?"
"Even if something happens to us, your brother and sister-in-law won't let them starve!"
"No, but that's why having siblings is so important- its because I have a brother that I know someone will take care of these two little angels if something were to happen to us," father said. "Remember, just like that Fang Yuan, Fang Zheng, I hope that you continue to support each other in the future."
The dream realm then shifted, and Fang Yuan found that he was no longer lying down, but standing up. Examining himself, he could feel an aperture at Rank 2 Peak Stage, though before he could think about this any further, someone shook him on the shoulder.
It was Mother once again, though Fang Yuan looked down and quickly assumed that he had now resumed the role of his father.
Mother was injured, with a foot that was fractured, and Fang Yuan was rather low in primeval essence. He could feel a Moonglow Gu but nothing other than that.
A howl echoed from the right. Even in a dream realm, and in someone else's body, his battle instincts kicked in and he launched a moonblade without even thinking and the sound of a Lightning Wolf taking its last breath immediately echoed.
With that said, even with that small victory it was clear that the two of them were done for.
A quick examination of the surroundings revealed that the two of them were alone and cornered in a valley. The silhouettes of various Lightning Wolves could be seen even in the shadows cast by the setting sun, and if that was not enough, their howls echoed far and wide.
With their backs to a cliff, primeval essence running out, and no one in sight to rescue them, the scene was already dire.
However, there could still be a sliver of hope of them being rescued by reinforcements at the last moment. It was not unheard of, after all. And it was even possible that their teammates would soon arrive in the nick of time to save them.
But, Fang Yuan knew that wouldn't happen. Because this was the mission in which the two of them were fated to die.
With that said, there was usually something that needed to be done in these kinds of dream realms- even when death was certain, how the death was achieved could unravel the issue at hand.
His primeval essence nearly depleted, and with no primeval stones on hand (they were either completely used up, he assumed, or had fallen or something else along those lines) he prepared to fight with his fists. Yet, his father lacked a source of permanent strength like the White Boar Gu, and even Fang Yuan's battle experience could only go so far against so many enemies. Wild animals, of course, were far harder to deal with than humans, given their natural weapons like fangs and teeth.
Fang Yuan assumed that his father had likely died protecting his mother, which is what he did, with little care for his own injuries. Were this reality, Fang Yuan would've naturally taken any opportunity to save his own life, but he was more concerned with solving this dream realm right now.
Eventually he fell to the fangs of the Lightning Wolves, giving one last glance at his mother as he was dragged away, their teeth digging deep into his legs. The pain was intense, though he had gone through greater pain in his own life.
"Ah... I... lov-" before his mother could finish whatever she was saying, her throat was ripped out by a wolf, the words dying in her throat along with her.
"Fang Yuan... Fang Zheng..." Fang Yuan felt himself say, as he too, felt the sharp dagger-like teeth sink into the soft flesh of his neck. A deep sense of sorrow and regret assailed him- though Fang Yuan was unmoved. The main way that people tended to lose themselves in dream realms was by letting their emotions run amok- as it was, dream realms tended to heighten one's emotions.
The dream realm seemed to end at that point, and Fang Yuan had assumed the same. After all, following this the two of them had not survived to tell the tale and only their corpses would make it back to the village, but there appeared to be more to this dream.
Fang Yuan now found himself walking along a long, narrow path in what seemed to be a barren plain. He examined himself and now found that he had Rank 5 Peak Stage cultivation, and numerous gu worms in his aperture which he did not fully recognize- though he did think, based on his experience, that they were Wisdom Path gu worms.
This part of the dream did not seem to take place in the Southern Border, but rather, somewhere in the Western Desert. At least, Fang Yuan felt so- there were many areas in the five regions which somewhat mimicked each other, but the shrubbery seemed to highly suggest so.

chapters.title: Chapter 84 - 84: Family Inheritance: Part Ten
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan walked along as this Rank 5 Gu Master, unable to do anything until he reached a dune. There must've been something special about this dune, even though Fang Yuan could not for the life of him guess what that was, because the Gu Master stopped as if expecting something to happen.
From the sands, the form of an elderly man appeared, who radiated a Rank 6 aura. The Gu Master whom Fang Yuan was playing as bowed deeply to this man.
"Very good- that is the first test of your intelligence out of the way," the man said. "It seems that you are truly ready for your immortal ascension."ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
The gap between Rank 5 and Rank 6 was immense- it was the gap between a mortal Gu Master an an immortal Gu Master. The reason for this was that once a gu master became an immortal, their aperture was instead turned into a miniature world and their primeval essence was converted into immortal essence- a bead of which provided practically limitless primeval essence for the use of mortal gu.
Of course, the process of ascension was quite difficult, even more so if one did not have someone guiding them. Fang Yuan did not when he had ascended, so he had ample experience about the issues one would face while doing so.
"Shall we begin, Father?" the mortal Gu Master asked. So it appeared that these two were father and son- then it made sense as to why the father was so readily helping the son.
"Begin," the Immortal Gu Master said.
Fang Yuan was now in control of this mortal Gu Master's body, and began the first step, which was the shatter the crystalline walls of the Rank 5 Peak Stage aperture. This would completely destroy it, and once this step was done it was irreversible. There was no going back now- either he would ascend to Rank 6 or he would die.
With this, his body began to ascend into the sky as heaven and earth qi began to rush in. It was here that there was a crucial step which the Gu Master had to do on their own and could not rely on outside help- though extensive practice would help.
Their own human qi had to be balanced against the heaven and earth qi. If any of them were in excess of each other, the ascension would fail and they would die. However, during this time they would be able to take advantage of heavenly inspiration- it was said that Heaven knew all, and so for a brief period of time one could gain insights into things like gu recipes and the like during their ascension. Given that it was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for many, one could not squander such and had to make sure to utilize it fully, oftentimes preparing one's questions in advance.
While heaven and earth qi were abundant, human qi was generated from one's own experience. Based on the amount of human qi that this man had, Fang Yuan could guess that he likely only had a few decade's worth of experience and would only get a low or medium quality blessed land.
"Good, good!" the man's father shouted, watching Fang Yuan expertly balance all three qi. The next step was for Fang Yuan to take his gu worms, first being his vital gu, and place it within the fusion of the three qi. The nature of the vital gu would determine the nature of the blessed land one would receive.
Of course, there was an added difficulty to this in the form of an earthly calamity and heavenly tribulation.
The earthly calamity soon emerged as from beneath the desert, a large worm ten times the size of a subway train back on Earth erupted.
Earthly calamity- Desolate Beast Giant Sandworm!
It was here that external help could be provided, as before Fang Yuan turned his attention to the earthly calamity it had already been burst into pieces by this man's father. He had used a gu that manifested in the form of several hundred thousand fiery wisps that rained down upon the Giant Sandworm. Based on the mode of attack, Fang Yuan had likely been correct- this was a Wisdom Path Gu Immortal, and his son was also a Wisdom Path Gu Master.
Next, was the heavenly tribulation. The sky darkened as a the winds howled and raged around them.
Heavenly tribulation- Desert Cyclone!
In response to this, the man's father release several hundred thousand ruby-red orbs, which were likely thoughts though these were designed to be defensive rather than offensive, which formed a wall around the duo as the winds raged on. At multiple points in time it felt like the wall was going to break, but more thoughts went from the Immortal's mind to plug in those gaps.
Eventually the winds subsided. It was at this point that, if there was more heaven and earth qi left, Rank 5 gu worms could be refined into Immortal Gu with somewhat ease, though this part of the dream ended before Fang Yuan could reach that step.
Some time had passed as Fang Yuan looked upon a slightly older version of this man's father, whow as now emitting a Rank 7 aura. They were back in that same dune that he had underwent his ascension in.
"Do you remember this place?" his father asked.
"Yes, father," the man replied. Fang Yuan had once again lost control of this man's body and could only watch on. He could still sense what gu worms this man had- he was at Rank 6 and had one immortal gu whose function Fang Yuan was unaware of.
"This is where you underwent your immortal ascenscion, and so did I," the father answered. He then sighed, a forlorn look upon his face. "My son, there is an important reason that I have brought you here." The father took out two gu worms from his aperture and handed them to his son. "Take these."
Both of them were Rank 6 gu worms- meaning these were likely the highest ranked gu worms that this man had. At Rank 5 and beyond, most Gu Masters only had gu worms of a rank beneath them.
"Father, why are you giving me these?" the man asked in a shocked voice.
"Because, my time has come," the man's father said.
"What are you talking about? You're still young and have many decades ahead of you."
"Child, you have only embarked upon the path of a Wisdom Gu Immortal- and have yet to understand the immensity of heaven and earth. Your father has been able to see but a slice of what is to come, and even that has chilled me to the bone," his father said and then looked at him with a sad look. "There is something that I have never told you- or anyone in our clan for that matter. I am not originally from this world."
"Not originally from this world?"
"It is hard to understand," the man responded. "But I came from a country known as 'England' where I had been but a normal shoemaker. We had things similar to iron sandworms that spat out steam and ran on coal and many other such wonders that you would not easily understand. Gu Masters were not a concept back in that world, and yet, one day, while walking down the street I suddenly found myself in the body of a four-year-old of this world. In other words, I am what is called an Otherworldly Demon. A traveler from another realm."
"I started to cultivate, as that was expected of me, even becoming a Gu Immortal in the process," the man's father continued. "But the deeper I delved into the Wisdom Path, the more I came upon an uncomfortable truth of this world- it is completely deterministic. In other words, fate- Fate Gu-"
"-the same Fate Gu from 'The Legends of Ren Zu?'" The man did not know what 'Ing-Lond' was, so he latched onto the one thing he did recognize in his father's speech.
"Precisely, it governs this world, and none can escape it," the father said. "However, that also means that because fate is fixed, one with enough ability can peer into the future, much as Star Constellation Immortal Venerable could do. And what I saw in the future greatly saddened me- because I am fated to be the cause of your death in the future!"

chapters.title: Chapter 85 - 85: Family Inheritance: Part Eleven
chapters.content:
"Father- what kind of nonsense are you talking? Why would you ever kill me?" the man asked his father, laughing, though his father did not so much as crack a smile in response and the man's laughter died out awkwardly. "Father... you are serious? Do... do I betray you in some way?"
The father shook his head. "No. I have seen the future and I am fated to kill you in an accident during battle. Even if I hope to avoid it, it is inevitable if that is what fate has decreed. Whatsoever fate decrees will certainly pass. I have envisioned endless scenarios but there is no way out of this prediction."
"So what will we do? You just... have to be more careful is all!" the man said, unable to think of anything more profound, despite being a Wisdom Path expert.
"There is no escaping fate," the father said. "However, there is an exception... it turns out that by being an Otherworldly Demon, I am somewhat able to resist fate."ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
"Ah! So the problem is solved then!"
The father shook his head. "It would be if it were a certain event that led to this tragedy- but no, even if I change what I do, the river of fate always corrects its course and one way or another, my child, I cause your death. My child, I have come to realize many things while living for over three hundred years in this world. Back where I came from, men could not survive for longer than a century- but there is a universal truth between both of these worlds. There is no such thing as eternal life, and those who strive for such are fools. What is important is not living forever- but living life to the fullest. Even if I could live for a million years, I would never want to live knowing that I had killed my one and only son. The only reminder of the wife I found in this strange world before she passed away. There are no certain ways to circumvent fate even for an Otherworldly Demon... except for one."
The man became filled with panic as he realized what the natural conclusion to this was going to be. "No! Father! We can think of something else! We can find another solution we-"
The father shook his head as he gently smiled. "There is only one way to be certain that I avoid my fate. I leave my entire inheritance to you, my son. May you lead our clan well." He then sighed. "Truth be said, it is possible fate will correct itself to take your life regardless, but if my actions can buy you even a single more breath of time in this world, I am fine with it. I have taught you all I know, and you are ready now. Once you are Rank 7, feel free to absorb my blessed land for your own aperture. My land spirit will readily acknowledge you as its owner."
The father then self-detonated, dissolving into tiny wisps of light as his immortal aperture fell to the ground.
The man was filled with a sense of sadness and loss.
With that the entire dream realm was finally over. It had been rather straightforward, with very little parts that took his input.
It didn't even feel like he could've failed the dream realm, which meant that the system wasn't lying and it was indeed quite straightforward.
However, it had still strained his soul, which was to be expected given it was just an ordinary level soul. Fang Yuan felt like he could sleep for three days and three nights. Even with his own sense of perseverance he could feel his eyelids drooping.
The effort had been well worth it though- his attainment level in Human Path had gone from Ordinary to Master level in a few hours. If he had been left on his own, such an endeavor would have taken him 50-60 years if he were studying on his own and 5-10 years if he had some kind of guidance (like an inheritance or teacher in the path). With that said, the higher one's attainment level, the harder it would be to increase it. It would be harder to get to Grandmaster, harder still to Great Grandmaster, and few aside from the Venerables had ever reached the heights of Supreme Grandmaster in any single path.
With his newfound attainment in Human Path, Fang Yuan sent his mind to the strange Rank 4 Gu Worm that he had obtained which was resting in his aperture. He was now sure that it was a Human Path gu worm, but the issue was that his attainment level was still too low to be able to identify a gu worm that was completely new to him. He was only able to get a vague idea based on certain clues. If his attainment level in the Human Path were to rise further, he might be able to know its exact name even if he had never seen it before.
"Brother, are you alright?" Fang Zheng asked. To him, it just looked like Fang Yuan had been meditating for several hours and given him some strange instructions. Fang Yuan had woken up before the allotted time period was over, so he hadn't had to try to force Fang Yuan up, but now that the whole ordeal was over Fang Zheng naturally had several questions- all of which Fang Yuan wished to avoid or deflect for now.
"I'm fine," Fang Yuan said, yawning, and waving his hand in a nonchalant manner. "I'm just a bit tired." His soul was fatigued, and the best way available for him to recover it was to sleep. "I might call in sick tomorrow."
"What was that small thing you pulled out? Some kind of gu worm?"
"Don't worry about it, it's not important," Fang Yuan said, stifling a yawn. "But, I wanted to talk to you about something else. I think it's time that I break through to Rank 3 very soon."
"Right now? But you're just at Rank 2 Middle Stage!"
"Yes, but the merchant caravan is coming," Fang Yuan said. "And very soon. There are some gu worms that can help me- and we need to prepare primeval stones for when I breakthrough to Rank 3."
"Understood!" Fang Zheng said.
"I'm going to sleep," Fang Yuan said, wandering off to the place where he could sleep.
He mulled over what he had seen in his dreams. Had the dream about his parents really been theirs? Or had the system generated that dream? As far as he knew neither of his parents would have any talent in the Human Path so it was odd that was the attainment level it gave him.
As for the second half of the dream, involving the Wisdom Gu Immortal who had predicted he would accidentally kill his son, and deciding to preferably kill himself rather than let that happen. Even that felt that it would be more of a Wisdom Path dream realm than anything else, yet it had granted him attainment in the Human Path.
Who were those two Gu Immortals he had seen in his dream? They never addressed each other by name, nor did he know which clan they belonged to. Only that they had likely been in the Western Desert at some point in the past- which was not much to go on.
Fang Zheng meanwhile, started cultivating, though he only did this for a while before once again using the Nine Leaf Vitality Grass in order to generate more primeval stones for Fang Yuan's future breakthrough. Also, he had some idea of what Fang Yuan wanted to buy from the merchant caravan, and they would need loads of primeval stones for the same.

chapters.title: Chapter 86 - 86: Red Steel Relic Gu: Part One
chapters.content:
The wheel of time turned, and the merchant caravan arrived at Gu Yue village once again. It had felt like it had only been a few breaths of time when it had last come around. Normally it wouldn't have made much ripples in Fang Yuan's plans, but because of the new abundance of resources he had thanks to the system he was not lacking in primeval stones but needed some gu worms in certain critical areas.
The same rock gambling den was set up as last year, and a face familiar to most of the people inside walked in.
"It's him again!"
"He won a Mudskin Toad last time, who knows what he'll win this year?"
"Tch, that was just due to luck, there's no way that lightning strikes the same place twice!"
A voice was quite cheerful though, amid the chorus of sneers and whines. "Young Master, you've returned here! Ah, it's as if we only met yesterday! To see that you've graduated now- I'm sure that you'll have a great run this year as well!"
The smile on the female attendant faded slightly as the man she directed this to gave her a quizzical look. "Is there a reason that you're acting so familiar? Like we've met before?"
"Ah- Young Master, don't tease me like this," she replied, pouting in a way that some might find cute. "How could you forget that time you found the Mudskin Toad?"
The man blinked at her, his face unfazed. "You must've met my elder brother Fang Yuan then, my name is Fang Zheng." Fang Yuan had asked Fang Zheng to ease off on making Vitality Leaves to some extent, so he had managed to get to Rank 1 Upper Stage by this point.
"E-Eh?! Why are you joking in that way?" the attendant asked. Needless to say slogging in the shop was hard- and moving alongside the merchant caravan was harder still. While the profits could be extremely high given how constrained the markets and economies of this world were, a worker like herself would see very little of said profits. To be a real player within the merchant caravan one had to be Rank 3 or have a strong backing, neither of which she had. And while the profits were high, the risks of dying along the journey were also high. Who would want to deal with that day in and day out?
However, this attendant had remembered the young Gu Master who had wandered into the gambling den last year and had even taken extra steps to try to be as appealing as possible to him. She had used a different kind of perfume and had taken great pains to adorn herself, something which was not easy while traveling alongside a caravan. Gamblers, naturally, no matter what they told themselves, never quit after getting a big break. The allure of another big payout was too much and she reasoned that that same Young Master would wander into their gambling day almost certainly when it returned.
The other idiots had ruined her chances last time, but she figured that now was an excellent chance to grasp onto this opportunity. After all, with time he would naturally grow into a fully-fledged Gu Master and possible elder of his clan, and just like Mo Chen she thought it would be better to get her talons into Fang Yuan as early as possible before that happened.
However, despite looking forward to this moment for several weeks by now and making all of these preparations, the Young Master in question was completely ignoring her- behaving as if they'd never met.
"Young Master, look closely, I haven't changed that much-" she began to say before a Gu Yue clansmen interrupted her.
"He isn't lying, Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng are twins," he said.
'Twins!?' the female attendant thought, shocked, but based on the way the other Gu Yue clansmen were looking at her, this was not a lie.
'Why doesn't this stupid woman get out of my way?' Fang Zheng thought. Ever since he had been betrayed by Shen Cui, he oftentimes saw the face of that wretched witch in the faces of the woman he would encounter. The fact that this woman had dolled herself up so much only made the resemblance stronger. On top of which, he easily recognized a woman trying to slip into his brother's good graces for nothing but the thought of the benefits that it would provide. He did not voice his resentment, however, as he had come here to do business and making a scene was not on a list of what he intended to do.
Fang Zheng avoided her entirely, going to a male shop attendant instead and dropping a bag of primeval stones on the counter.
The female attendant was shocked by this behavior- and inwardly furious. Not only did this Fang Zheng give her the cold shoulder, he also went ahead to spite her in another way. Now, someone else would earn the commission she would've gotten from selling to him.
"I have three hundred primeval stones and I would like to gamble," Fang Zheng said.ᴛhis ᴜpdated by NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
Immediately there were cries of shock.
"Three hundred! I couldn't make that much in three years!"
"How is that guy so loaded/ He's just a Rank One Gu Master?"
"Tch, he's just spending his parent's inherited fortune. Lucky brat..."
"Hehe... he's Rank One, why not challenge him for a piece of the puzzle and take it for ourselves? As they say, it is a great crime for a beggar to be holding diamonds!"
"Don't you know, his elder brother, Fang Yuan, is part of Qing Shu's team!"
"Qing Shu? Forget it then, we might as well try to steal the meat from a lion's mouth!"
Fang Zheng ignored these outbursts and pointed out the stones that he wanted to buy without hesitation, picking up a mixture of medium-value and high-value stones.
In total, he had bought seventeen. Unlike Fang Yuan, he did not open them up himself, and instead used the gambling den's service to open up the rocks.
Naturally given the amount that he had purchased a large crowd gathered around him, wondering if luck ran in the family and that he too, might find something like the Mudskin Toad.
The first five rocks yielded nothing, but something seemed to be emerging from the sixth rock.
"No way!"
"Could it be that this kid really found a gu worm?"
As the rock was excavated further, there were sighs of disappointment. While there indeed had been a gu worm inside of the rock, it had died and thus was useless.
"Hmm... bad luck to him."
"It's not over yet though, he still has more rocks to-"
Before the sentence could be completed, Fang Zheng suddenly said, "I would like to take the rest of the rocks home and have someone else open them."
He took the other rocks into a bag and then abruptly left.
"Same thing as last year!"
"These two brothers are really alike!"
"No, one is just luckier than the other!"
"Yeah, dumb kid spent 300 stones and has nothing to show for it!"
While Fang Zheng wandered back to their apartment with the other rocks he had, Fang Yuan was examining the gu worms up for sale in the central tent of the place.
Unlike last year, there was a Liquor Worm up for sale. One might not be up for sale even if you waited for a decade, and then you might find two in consecutive years. That was just how scare and unpredictable the supply of the Liquor Worm was.
"Grandma! Grandma! Do you think that you can buy me the Liquor Worm?"
This question was brought up by a young female Gu Master, who had just recently awakened her aperture. Her name was Gu Yue Yao Le, and from Fang Yuan's memories, she would grow up to become a talented healer though would die alongside the rest of the villagers before she could unlock her full potential.
The Liquor Worm's demand was high, after all, who wouldn't want something that could possibly double their progress - and so naturally few people could afford the price. However, this young girl was not ordinary and had a strong backer- Gu Yue Yao Ji, the medicine hall elder, was her grandmother.
"Alright, alright, don't worry," Yao Ji said. "I'll make sure to buy this for you."

chapters.title: Chapter 87 - 87: Red Steel Relic Gu: Part Two
chapters.content:
"But Grandma, what if someone else buys it?" Yao Le asked, concerned.
In this world, most transactions could not be done with the ease of things on Earth. Things like clan ties, loyalty, and the reputation of the seller and buyer greatly restricted how business could be done on Earth. As such, the buying of precious gu worms like the Liquor Worm could not be done in an open auction most of the time, and naturally since the merchant caravan wanted to raise the price as much as possible they would not post a flat price. Instead, they would allow people to place in anonymous bids, and if the price was too low the Liquor Worm would simply not be sold.
Of course 'anonymous' was only a relative term - who knew if someone like Yao Ji had the ability to find out the buyer? and many people feared the wrath of Gu Yue Yao Ji- she had great influence on people's lives being the medicine hall elder. What if they offended her and then when they or their family members needed her, they were overlooked for other people? Who would risk such a thing? Only someone with strong backing- or someone who did not care for clan ties.
Someone like Fang Yuan, in other words. The Liquor Worm would normally be useless to him once he got to Rank 3 given he had one already, but he had a plan in motion which while slightly cumbersome, would require him to have an excuse as to how he had obtained a second one.
New main mission!
Advance Fang Zheng's vital gu to the Four Flavors Liquor Worm.
Reward: A 2% permanent increase to your aptitude.
By this point, Fang Yuan was completely focused on getting to Rank 3. The difference between 61% and 63% made this goal go from extremely to moderately difficult, and the next 2% would make the journey quite smooth.
The Four Flavors Liquor Worm required two Liquor Worm to be fused, and alcohol of four flavors to be mixed in- Spicy, Sweet, Bitter, and Sour. Three out of the four were easy enough to obtain- but he couldn't find bitter wine despite looking around. Even the merchant caravan did not carry any. He knew of locations where it would be found but they were far away, and if he could reach those he could reach other inheritances more easily.
Needless to say though, he could only think of that once he actually had another Liquor Worm that he could openly use.
"Don't worry dear," Yao Ji said. "Your grandmother has seen countless decades, and knows the exact price to buy it at." If someone bid far more than her price, they could be said to be a fool who didn't know how to manage their resources.
Fang Yuan, though, had seen far more decades than she had and already had a good idea of what price she would've paid. He was reasonably sure that he could outbid her by a chance of around 90% if he raised the price he had in his mind by 10 primeval stones, and by around 95% if it was raised further by twenty primeval stones. However, he raised the price by 30 stones, making his bid 99% likely to succeed in his own mind.
With that settled, he turned his eyes to the Cleansing Water Gu. Chi Lian was no doubt eyeing this gu worm for his grandson, but Fang Yuan wanted it for Fang Zheng, if no other reason than to assuage him to let him inject his aperture with his own primeval essence. Like with the Liquor Worm, he already had a good idea of what price Chi Lian would pay and raised it by a dozen or so primeval stones.
While extorting Chi Lian for this gu worm was an option in the future, it would cause him needless trouble and might possibly trigger the system's anger.
Both of these gu worms, however, were nothing compared to the value of the two Rank 2 gu worms being proudly displayed near the center- Red Steel Relic Gu! Able to instantly raise one's cultivation at Rank 2 by a minor realm, it was worth several thousands of primeval stones.
Fang Yuan did not intend to buy either of them given he already had two- but that did not mean that he could not use the fact that they were on sale to his advantage!
Fang Yuan went back home to see Fang Zheng eagerly waiting for him.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"Brother- just like you asked for, I bought some rocks and gambled with them and brought the rest here," Fang Zhen said. He had not tried to open any of them on his own, being worried that he might damage them if there was a gu worm inside.
"Good work," Fang Yuan said. This was all part of his greater scheme.
He sighed inwardly though, despite smiling. This was all an unnecessary headache in his eyes- he would not need to deal with such formalities if he was fully devoted to the demonic path. However, despite the hoops he had to jump through it was worth it simply because the benefits were large enough.
Fang Yuan began dissecting the rocks. This was merely a formality at this point as he was not expecting to find anything within them, though if it turned out that they had something, he would only be pleasantly surprised.
None of the rocks had anything, and Fang Zheng sighed. "I knew it didn't matter... but it would be good if they had one..."
"Don't worry," Fang Yuan said, reassuring him. "As a matter of fact, I have found something interesting in the merchant caravan- a gu fusion recipe that I think could be greatly useful for you."
"Really? You mean- for the Liquor Worm?" Fang Zheng asked excitedly. The only recipe that the Gu Yue clan had for the Liquor Worm's advancement was the Moong Harbinger Gu which was unfortunately not quite useful. While it could eventually become the Seven Fragrances Liquor Worm, even if Fang Zheng managed to refine it it would be useless to him, a Rank Two Gu Master, once he became Rank Two. However, it was important for his development that he advance his vital gu- otherwise he was just wasting one of the most precious tools that a Gu Master had.
"Yes," Fang Yuan said. "But, I have to speak to the caravan head regarding the same. Wish me luck!"
Two days later, Fang Yuan approached Jia Jin Fu's tent.
"Ah, Brother Jin Fu, thank you for gracing this one with your time," Fang Yuan said, the perfect picture of cordiality.
"No matter, no matter," Jin Fu said, behaving as if Fang Yuan and himself were on equal footing despite him being at Rank 4. "I heard that there was a business opportunity that you wished to approach me with?" He had heard a few stories here and there of Fang Yuan naturally the moment he had entered the village, and it was because of his curiosity that he had so readily agreed to this meeting.
The two exchanged pleasantries before Fang Yuan said, "Thank you for your hospitality- coming to the meat of the matter, I was wondering if it were to be possible to set up my younger brother to join your merchant caravan?"
"Oh, you mean Fang Zheng?" Jin Fu asked. When one spoke of Fang Yuan, they could not help but speak of Fang Zheng- especially given the clamor that the assassination attempt had caused. "You wanted him to join my merchant caravan?" It was odd that Fang Yuan would ask for such. Jin Fu was under the impression that naturally, the twin brothers would care greatly for each other. Why would Fang Yuan, who was on his way to become an elder, wish to send his younger brother away instead of keeping him safe alongside himself?
"The truth is... I am greatly worried about Fang Zheng's future," Fang Yuan said, giving an air of awkwardness that made it clear this topic was difficult for him to broach.
"No matter, no matter," Jin Fu said, sending the servants out and leaning closer. "Don't worry- whatever happens here will remain between you and I and not a soul outside the two of us will get to know. Feel free to tell me what's bothering you."

chapters.title: Chapter 88 - 88: Red Steel Relic Gu: Part Three
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan looked somewhat awkward as he spoke to Jia Jin Fu. "You see... the matter is regarding Fang Zheng and his ability to... work in the clan. Now, I love Fang Zheng more than I cherish the air in my lungs," Fang Yuan, who would sell Fang Zheng into slavery without a second's hesitation if the benefits were high enough, said, "as I am sure that you can understand, being an elder brother yourself."
"Ah, no it isn't like that sadly," Jin Fu said, waving his hand. "Jin Sheng... despite my attempts to reach out to him... he doesn't seem to understand certain things. I have other brothers beside him, though I truly wish that our relationship was as good as that between Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng. With that said, no doubt, I can understand and elder brother's concern for the younger."
"I don't know if you've heard of the incident that happened with Fang Zheng," Fang Yuan said. This was an idiotic question as there was no one on the mountain who hadn't heard of it, and would've been one of the first things that Jin Fu would've been told about the moment he came, but he posed it nonetheless.
"Yes, I have, quite tragic what happened to him- did you ever find the perpetrator behind the attack?"
"Sadly, no."
"If it had been something that happened to my family- I would be livid, so I can understand your anger," Jin Fu said. "But then what does this do with trying to send him away?"
"The issue is that he has had a falling out with the rest of the clan because of this," Fang Yuan said, sighing. "As hard as it is to admit, he seems to greatly resent the rest of the clan after his fall in talent. I... I actually think it might be better for him to seek his fortune elsewhere, rather than where such awful memories lurk." Most people would rather choose to stay with their clan compared to strangers even if they were facing hardships for the simple fact that blood ran thicker than water but this was not true for all. Some people joined the merchant caravan because they wanted to get somewhere along the ride, others joined to make a fortune, some joined because they were kicked out by their clans (like Fang Yuan in his first life), and some joined as they wanted to see the wider world. "Of course, I don't intend to send him off on his own right now. I wanted to wait until he became Rank 2 at the very least."
Fang Yuan knew the internal politics of a merchant caravan very well- Rank 1 Gu Masters were little better than mortals and could only work as low-level employees. It was only at Rank 2 that they could gain some semblance of autonomy- and it was the Rank 3 who were usually the top brass within the caravan. Most of them did not have a Rank 4 Gu Master like Jin Fu's did.
"I see, and you want to discuss how he would do so?"
"Yes."
"I can get him started on his own business within the caravan, though this will have to come at an upfront cost, of around one thousand primeval stones," Jin Fu said. "Either that, or if he were to come along with us along with a large supply of Moon Orchid Petals it would also be a different thing."
"Of course, I just wanted to inquire about what his prospects would be like," Fang Yuan said.
The two of them talked for a while longer before Fang Yuan left, thanking Jin Fu as he walked away.
Jin Fu, on his part, had a slight suspicion within his heart. Did Fang Yuan truly think of sending Fang Zheng away for his own good- or was there a more devious reason behind this supposed move? If Fang Zheng's reputation was truly so bad that he could not fit in within Gu Yue village without causing massive issues, it would also greatly benefit Fang Yuan, a future elder, to get rid of his brother and to avoid associating with something that could stain his own name.
Fang Yuan, for his part, did not care for what Jin Fu thought or reasoned- as he had already accomplished his goal.
The results of the auction were soon declared towards the end of when the merchant carvan stayed.
"I was actually outmaneouvered?" Yao Ji said, seeing that the Liquor Worm had been sold to someoen else.
"Grandma!" Yao Le began to whine.
"Don't worry, dear," Yao Ji said. She turned to one of the Rank 1 Gu Masters. "Who dared to buy the Liquor Worm? Tell me?"
"Madame I cannot..." the man trailed off. He did not dare oppose her, but at the same time, he had to follow the rules of the caravan. "...we cannot divulge the information of our buyers."
"Hmph! Let me speak to your boss!" Yao Ji snapped.
The boss, a male Rank 3 Gu Master, immediately walked by and gave her a firm smile. "Madame, we still cannot tell you who the buyer was."Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
"So be it- I just want to know how much they paid," she said.
"That I also cannot freely divulge but..." the manager of the store began to say, but paused. Yao Ji had great influence among the Gu Yue clan, and he did not want to offend her. "...given that you wish to buy the Liquor Worm, I can definitely have one taken out of our warehouse for you. I won't ask for anything higher than your original bid."
Yao Ji shook her head. "No! I demand that the price be the same as the one who bought this Liquor Worm!"
The manager had a troubled look. Since when did customers start haggling the price up? Ultimately though, he agreed to her request, and Yao Ji was shocked to find that the bidding price was just 30 primeval stones more than what she had offered!
'I should've bid a bit higher...' she thought to herself. She did not lack that many primeval stones, but would've felt somewhat cheated if she had paid that price initially given that her offer was already rather generous. Looking at it though, there was someone else within the village who thought that it was more than fair.
A bottle of water might only cost a dollar on Earth, but a man stranded in the desert dying of thirst would give up his fortune for it. Clearly the buyer of the Liquor Worm had a similar thought and did not mind the excessive price.
There was a similar situation with Chi Lian when he found out that Cleansing Water Gu had also been sold, but he did not have the widespread influence that Yao Ji did and could not do anything other than grit his teeth, wondering who else in the village even needed that gu worm. He could only look forward to next year.
The two Red Steel Relic Gu had remained unsold, at least, that was how most people thought of it.
As Fang Yuan wandered through the streets of the village, someone tugged on his sleeve. "Momma! Where are you leading me?"
Fang Yuan turned to see a young girl, who had a confused look upon seeing Fang Yuan's face. "Wah- you're not Momma!"
The child had gotten lost at some point, and thought that Fang Yuan from behind looked enough like her mother to have followed her far from wherever she had originally been. Seeing that she was lost, she began to cry.
Fang Yuan gently took out a handkerchief and began drying her tears. "There, there, are you lost little one? Let us look for your mother together..."
He gently led the girl away, only returning home after finally reuniting her with her mother, who seemed to be borderline panicked at having lost track of her.
"Thank you! Thank you so much kind sir!" she said.
"It was nothing," Fang Yuan said, turning to the child. "Just remember to be more careful in the future, alright?"
"Of course!" the girl said, thinking 'This senior brother is really kind and friendly! I wanna grow up to be just like him!'

chapters.title: Chapter 89 - 89: River Swallowing Toad: Part One
chapters.content:
The Red Steel Relic Gu had been sold, with many people wondering who it was who had bought it.
As for Fang Yuan, his cultivation skyrocketed to Rank 2 Upper Stage in the coming days. If anyone doubted him, he intended to say that Fang Zheng had found a Red Steel Relic Gu while gambling.
Very few people would buy that excuse, which is why he had left a trail of false bread crumbs in visiting the merchant caravan's leader. Some people would make a connection where there was none and assume that Fang Yuan had struck some deal with him in secret and obtained an extra Red Steel Relic Gu from him that way the same way that Yao Ji had gotten a Liquor Worm.
Since no one was entirely certain who had bought the Red Steel Relic Gu, this was necessary. What if whoever was investigating was the one who had bought both of them?
In this way, Fang Yuan was taking advantage of the general 'fog of war' that existed even amongst clan members.
The reason that he had not as of yet used the second one he had to reach Rank 2 Peak Stage was that he wanted to get that 2% extra from refining the Four Flavors Liquor Worm before making that jump.
However, he had run into the first real roadblock in his journey until now.
Who would've thought that despite being the owner of a wine tavern, he wouldn't be able to get his hands on a certain flavor of wine?
The system was surprisingly unhelpful in that regard- not giving him any bottles of wine as part of daily quests even now.
Unbeknownst to him, at that very moment he was worried about that, there was a commotion going on in the elder's hall.
"Quiet! Quiet!" the clan head said, asking everyone to clamor down.
This was an emergency meeting, so naturally everyone was wondering what it was about.
"There is grave news for our clan," the clan head said. "It appears that a tributary of the Huang Long river has led to a River Swallowing Toad to appear near our village."
The River Swallowing Toad was a Rank 5 gu worm- while many gu worms were insects, much like the name suggested, the River Swallowing Toad was a toad though it was the size of an elephant. It was called such as its food was an entire small river. However, not only could it swallow rivers, it could also spit them back out, meaning that it could very easily drown the entire village if it got agitated.
Wild gu worms were a danger that one might encounter while traveling, though it appeared that fate had brought this problem right in front of their doorstep.
Chi Lian spoke up. "Then the situation is quite grave- if we don't deal with this, who knows if those with malicious intentions won't go and provoke the River Swallowing Toad on purpose?"
"Actually, I think that they already might be planning on doing so," an elder spoke up. "I was going to keep this little piece of information under wraps until I was able to delve into it further- but I think that this only confirms what suspicions I had."
"Oh? What is it? Do tell!"Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"It turns out that the Bai and Xiong clans are plotting something sinister," the elder said. "They have secretly been concocting alchemical solutions which they have been dumping in the nearby ponds and rivers with malicious intent- they're doing it to make the frogs gay! That's right, they're mixing in things into the water which are creating gay frogs!"
"Oh no!"
"Those Xiong and Bai clan bastards- they don't even spare the frogs!"
"What if they succeed in turning the River Swallowing Toad gay too?"
"Wait, all of you calm down," the clan head said, and the clamor died. "I have a few questions... how is it that they came across these chemicals that ah... make the frogs gay? And how do they stand to benefit from doing so? And the River Swallowing Toad is not an actual toad, but a gu worm, so... I don't see how these things are related."
"..."
There was a period of silence.
"While I don't have any good answers for that, I do not like the Bai or Xiong clans- so the rumor must be true!"
"Maybe they're trying to transform Gu Yue village into a village of femboys! Both of them have been envious of our position as mountain overlords, and they're resorting to these kinds of underhanded methods to undermine us!"
"Yes! They must be up to no good!"
"Okay, all of you keep quiet and let me talk," the clan head said, already feeling a headache coming on, and not from the problem of the River Swallowing Toad. "There is a way that we can deal with the River Swallowing Toad..."
Animals had different ways of displaying dominance. Male birds would make fancy homes to compete for mates, while others would dance for the same, and peacocks strutted around with their plumage. Wild bison would butt heads- in that same way, various gu worms also had ways of competing with each other.
There was a way to deal with the River Swallowing Toad, but it would need to involve the greatest caution. If it was provoked, they would truly be courting death.
The River Swallowing Toad respected strength- right now it was lying near the village like a giant boulder for all purposes. But if someone managed to shift it using their own strength, it would acknowledge that person as being its equal and hop off without causing a scene.
Of course, one could only use one's strength in this kind of contest. If it sensed even the faintest aura of a gu worm, it would sense that there was unfair play going on and not acknowledge that person. Even worse, it might even get agitated and go on a rampage. In the same vein, multiple people could not go to try to move it- it had to be a single person.
Chi Shan was well renowned for his strength, and so the decision was made to send him to deal with the River Swallowing Toad.
Unfortunately, he returned later that day with an ashen expression on his face. "I'm sorry, it appears that even my strength is inadequate to move it."
The elders who had been hopeful up to this point now began to panic. If Chi Shan could not deal with this- then who could?
"It looks like we need to bring in the Xiong clan to help us with this," one of the elders opined. The Xiong clan was well famed for their physical strength and might have someone who could rival Chi Shan. However, this would mean that the Gu Yue clan would be indebted to them, and would also lower their reputation among the three villages.
"Clan elders, this junior would like to give his opinion on this matter," Chi Shan said.
"Go ahead- speak, Chi Shan. You have some other idea in your mind, it seems?" the clan head asked.
"Yes, there is one person in Gu Yue village whose strength rivals or might even exceed mine," Chi Shan said. "His name is Gu Yue Fang Yuan."
"Fang Yuan?" the clan head naturally already know who that was. "I was not aware that he possessed much physical strength..."
"Clan head, not only has he gotten training from an excellent martial artist- his uncle, he also possesses great strength. Someone bought a Black Boar Gu from the merchant caravan and from the feats I have heard from Fang Yuan, I do not doubt that he has great strength," Chi Shan said.
As a potential rival, Chi Shan naturally kept his ear to the ground when it came to Fang Yuan's exploits.
"If that is the case, call upon Fang Yuan at once!" the clan head said.

chapters.title: Chapter 90 - 90: River Swallowing Toad: Part Two
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan was pondering how he could get his hands on some of the wine he needed when a notification popped up in his view.
New main mission!
They're (allegedly) turning the frogs gay(?)!
Description: Prevent the River Swallowing Toad from destroying the village.
Reward: Hundred Li Earth Wolf Spider (x 1)
At first, Fang Yuan couldn't figure out what on earth was going on with the mission's name.
That said, he had heard of the River Swallowing Toad in his past life. A mortal had managed to become friends with one, before being assassinated later on.
As for dealing with it, Fang Yuan had an easy method for doing so. He merely needed to reveal the Spring Autumn Cicada's Rank 6 aura and it would immediately get agitated. If it was of a more mercurial temperament, it might attack, but it was at baseline a very docile creature unless it was provoked.
As for refining it, that was out of the question unfortunately since the Spring Autumn Cicada was only Rank 6 and not Rank 7, it could not frighten a wild Rank 5 gu worm into submission like it could Rank 4 and below.
Regarding the prize, the Hundred Li Earth Wolf Spider was an excellent mount that would allow one to quickly burrow underground. The Flower Wine Monk had a Rank 5 version of the gu, the Thousand Li Earth Wolf Spider, which he had used to evade the righteous path Gu Masters who trailed him over and over again.
In other words, it greatly suited a future demonic overlord like Fang Yuan!
Before Fang Yuan could even get up from his seat, Qing Shu had arrived along with his other two team members at the tavern's door. "Junior! We've been given a compulsory mission by the clan head himself! I'll explain on the way there- there's no time to waste!"
"Is this regarding the River Swallowing Toad?"
"Junior seems to have eyes and ears everywhere- yes, it is about the same. We have heard that your strength is not inferior to Chi Shan's," Qing Shu said. It was odd for him as a team leader to be unaware of his team mate's capabilities, but he had already felt that Fang Yuan had a number of trump cards up his sleeve. His cultivation had grown by leaps and bounds, and it was all but clear that he was the one who had purchased the Red Steel Relic Gu from the market.
Chi Shan was waiting for them at the mission area, on the pretense of telling Fang Yuan about the mission, while also watching him.
"Do you think you can do it?"
"I can, but I need help."
"Asking for help is out of the question- the River Swallowing Toad won't accept you then."
"No, not direct help, but indirect help."
Fang Yuan approached the giant toad as the gu worms within his aperture hid their aura in fear from the Rank 5 worm, only the Spring Autumn Cicada was unperturbed.
Fang Yuan approached it and began giving it a test push- he felt that his strength was just enough to be able to possibly budge it by a few inches, but that was not enough. He was unable to increase his innate strength any further as his body was still bound by the limits of a mortal without any gu worms.
However, that didn't mean that he couldn't borrow some outside help in some way.
A distance away, Qing Shu was in motion as the river water suddenly increased in intensity and strength. Fang Yuan found himself soaked from the water, though to the River Swallowing Toad this was nothing abnormal. Borrowing on the strength of the water and the tides, the River Swallowing Toad began to move.
Ten feet... twenty feet... as Fang Yuan continued to push it, it finally opened its eyes and let out a loud croak, flipping onto its hind legs.
It then opened up its mouth, and began rapidly drinking the river water. The water disappeared into its stomach despite it seeming too small to carry that kind of capacity. Once it was satisfied, it let out the prawns, fish, and other creatures within the river out by spitting them. It only ate the river water, not the living creatures inside it.
Fish began to rain from the sky, and a strange smell began to permeate the air.
"Is that... wine...?" Fang Yuan thought as he looked around, finding a strange kind of turtle that was letting out that fragrance. 'This is... bitter shell wine! To think that I would find it in this way!'
Qing Shu and the others arrived to see the River Swallowing Toad hopping away into the horizon.
"Great job, Fang Yuan, you really did it!"
However, Fang Yuan paid them no heed, running around to gather as many of the bitter shells as possible.
Word of this reached the clan head. Naturally, as a member of the clan head's faction, Fang Yuan's success increased his prestige.
"Give Fang Yuan a reward of one thousand primeval stones!"
Word of Fang Yuan's exploits quickly spread around the village, and many of them were not surprised as the image of Fang Yuan's heroism had already etched itself in their hearts by this point.
Fang Yuan, however, was unmoved. He had stored away the bitter shell wine for now- the goal was to get Fang Zheng to Rank 1 Peak Stage so that he would accept the fusion of the two Liquor Worms into a Four Flavors Liquor Worm.
Fang Yuan now asked Fang Zheng to stop creating Vitality Leaves, and was injecting his aperture with his own primeval essence. There was a limit to which he could do so, given the damage to Fang Zheng's aperture, but he was able to bring up his aptitude to around 62%.
Fang Yuan now made the Vitality Leaves himself, his greater primeval essence meaning he was able to match Fang Zheng so long as he no longer focused on nurturing his aperture.
He had used the second Red Steel Relic Gu by this time, word of him having bought one of the Red Steel Relic Gu from the market (or both of them) already gotten out.
In truth, one of them had been bought by Chi Shan, and the other by Mo Chen. Being on other sides of a political divide, they didn't know about each other and thought that the 'extra' one was bought by Fang Yuan. And to Qing Shu who did not know at all about either of them, it seemed normal to assume that Fang Yuan was the buyer.
Now at Rank 2 Peak Stage, there was only the advancement to Rank 3 left. His aperture was surrounded by crystal walls, and he was able to make minor cracks in them over time. However, to really break through it would be best to have 65% aptitude.
And for that, it was best for Fang Zheng to advance.
'Finally... I'm at Rank 1 Peak Stage,' Fang Zheng thought.
"Fang Zheng, the Liquor Worm will be of little help to you now," Fang Yuan said to Fang Zheng one day. "Remember when I told you that I had a new recipe to advance your vital gu...? Well, it's time to use it."

chapters.title: Chapter 91 - 91: Advancing To Rank Three: Part One
chapters.content:
"A new recipe? I've been meaning to ask you one thing... where did you get this?" Fang Zheng asked.
"Let me tell you a secret... so long as you can keep this between us..." Fang Yuan said.
Fang Zheng nodded. "When I found the Liquor Worm in the Flower Wine Monk's inheritance, there was an information-type gu worm which detonated after I used it. But I still have the contents with me- it had multiple varying recipes for how to advance the Liquor Worm into higher forms. One of them is called the Four Flavors Liquor Worm- it has the same effect as the Liquor Worm but at Rank 2!"
"The Flower Wine Monk!?" Fang Zheng said. "Brother... are you sure we can rely on a recipe that he left? He was a ruthless demon after all." Fang Zheng didn't know the reality of what had actually gone down during that time, and Fang Yuan felt no need to catch him up to speed on any of the details.The most update n0vels are published on Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"I'm sure that it's safe," Fang Yuan said. "And that's why I-" Fang Yuan removed the second Liquor Worm from his aperture. It had been somewhat annoying to feed the second one, though not overly so given his ownership of the wine tavern.
"Are you sure I should do this now? I'm only at Rank 1 still, won't it be... bad if I have a Rank 2 vital gu worm?" Fang Zheng asked the person who had once had a Rank 6 vital gu worm at Rank 1.
"It's not a big issue as the difference isn't too big," Fang Yuan said. "And I would normally not rush you into trying to do this, but the thing is that the bitter shell wine that I've managed to find which we need as a refinement material will go bad if we don't use it now."
"Oh... is that so?"
