The Legends of Ren Zu... Hope Gu was stored within Ren Zu's heart... Derivation Gu... Ren Zu and his children formed the world of humans... Integration Gu can do this in reverse... Can Integration Gu merge humans together to form something...?
Even as Fang Yuan puzzled these pieces of text together, a voice called from up above.
"Lord Teng Mingyu, time is up!"
The guard came down to escort him back up.
"Wait- I just need a few more minutes to finish up!" Fang Yuan protested. The guard, however, was having none of it.
"No can do, even for an elder, the clan rules are strict. Come back later!"
The guard showed no signs of letting up, and Fang Yuan knew that if he attacked the guard in this dream he would simply be ejected. Even an elder couldn't get away with something like this.
Fang Yuan was then ejected from this dream realm once again regardless, signifying he had failed this portion.
He grit his teeth as his soul sustained a mild injury once again before repairing it with Guts Gu.
Refining an unknown gu worm was extraordinarily difficult given the few clues that he had. It was a process that took much time and experimentation- how could he do so in the span of only a few fifteen minute sessions?

chapters.title: Chapter 136 - 136: Refining Hope Gu: Part Four
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan thought about it for a moment, 'There is no point in charging into the dream realm blindly once again.' If he didn't have an answer in mind, he would just end up wasting more time, damaging his soul and wasting Gu guts.
The real question, though, was where to look for answers. There's no one in the village who could potentially help him, and he did not have access to a place like Yellow Treasure Heaven yet where he might be able to get some information regarding the same. All he had were the clues that he had been given while in the dream realm itself.
'Integration Gu...' Fang Yuan thought to himself.
'In mathematics, derivation and integration are the opposite of each other. If Ren Zu had created the world of humans through Derivation Gu, does that mean Integration Gu could somehow gather all of humanity and then recreate Ren Zu?' That was what Teng Mingyu had seemed to be hinting at in his scribblings.
'Or maybe that isn't it and I'm thinking about things too literally,' Fang Yuan thought. 'Integration could also be thought of as something else: as bringing together a large number of small pieces to make a whole.'
He then decided to do something slightly risky, although it was a risk that he felt would pay off. The system had given him this dream realm for getting 100 Human Path Dao marks, and it had given him Rank Five Integration Gu for getting 200 Human Path Dao marks.
'Could it be that these two things were related?' Fang Yuan withdrew Integration Gu from his inventory. He wasn't sure how to feed it, which was the main problem, and it was Rank Five, which was another issue with taking it out. But as he examined it, he realized that he had seen it before. 'Teng Mingyu had a lower version of this Gu in his aperture,' Fang Yuan realized.
Integration Gu took the form of two worms which were curled and fused in the middle. It had five segments on it; it seemed to imply its rank. More likely than not, the Gu which he had seen, which only had two, was Rank Two Integration Gu. 'So is Integration Gu involved in the refining of Hope Gu?' Fang Yuan thought.
Now that he knew that Teng Mingyu had Integration Gu in his aperture, it made things slightly easier. However, he didn't know what the other gu worms inside Teng Mingyu's aperture were or if they were also a part of the refinement, and there was no easy way for him to find that out.
'I will give this another try,' Fang Yuan thought, 'and if not, then I'll have to leave it for now.'
He entered the dream realm once again. He walked alongside the guard, who reminded him that there were only 15 minutes that he could use. Then Fang Yuan approached the primeval spring. The numerous Hope Gu glittered like specks of gold in the water, calling out to him. Here, he removed Teng Mingyu's vital Gu from his aperture, a Rank One Hope Gu.
He then approached the water. Hope Gu began shining a bit more, and other wild Hope Gu began gathering around it.
'However, this is not enough to fuse them together,' Fang Yuan thought. 'The 'Legends of Ren Zu' was the greatest Human Path inheritance left behind in all of history. From the looks of this, this was a Human Path dream realm, and the answer would likely come from there. If he thought about it a bit more, Hope Gu lied in Ren Zu's heart,' Fang Yuan thought. At first, he thought that the recipe for advanced Hope Gu might involve the hearts of actual Gu Masters or just humans in general, but that did not seem to be the case given he was right here.
The only real clue he had was that Integration Gu was involved somehow.
As Fang Yuan looked at the water, his mind turned in another direction. 'What does it cause for hope to be built up? Can the hopes of many people come together?'
He repeated the last phrase in his mind: 'coming together, integrating together.' A flash of inspiration then struck. He took Rank Two Integration Gu from his aperture, and he also took out Friendship Gu.
Friendship Gu had the will of Teng Ling and Teng Mei within it.Follow current novᴇls on NovᴇlFirenᴇt
'If I can integrate these things together,' Fang Yuan thought. He used Integration Gu and Friendship Gu in succession, bringing the two wills to the forefront where Rank One Hope Gu began joining them.
As a Hope Gu joined with each of the wills which had been manifested by Friendship Gu, Fang Yuan then attempted to bring them all together, all the while pouring primal essence into Integration Gu.
The wills had manifested in the form of short, six-inch-tall versions of their owners. There weren't enough thoughts for a full person to manifest, as could be expected of such a low-ranking Gu worm.
However, both of his "friends" smiled at him as they each held onto a single Hope Gu. They then began approaching his vital Gu worm, and under the influence of Integration Gu, these three lights of Hope Gu began rotating around each other.
As they rotated faster and faster, a ball of light began forming.
'Is this the crucial step?' Fang Yuan thought, tossing in primeval stones while maintaining this. It was more difficult than a normal Rank Two Gu fusion, simply because he not only needed to think about the fusion, but also maintain Integration Gu's function separately while tossing in primeval stones. The ball of light shrunk, and then a new Gu worm emerged from the ball of light and landed on Teng Mingyu's palm.
Rank Two Hope Gu had been successfully refined!
Teng Mingyu then took this Gu worm and walked out of the underground cavern. "I was about to call for you," the guard said. "15 minutes are up."
"Don't worry, my job here is done," Teng Mingyu said. Fang Yuan thought that the dream would be over by this point.
However, it continued, though he had no control over Teng Mingyu's body right now. Teng Mingyu walked back home. The village was bustling with activity, and many people bowed to him once he went back home. He showed his father his new creation. "Look, Father, I did it! I managed to refine Rank Two Hope Gu!"
"Congratulations," his father said, though he had a sad smile on his face. "And what can you possibly do with Rank Two Hope Gu?"
Teng Mingyu trailed off. "Although I have advanced it to Rank Two, it still seemed to have no function. Maybe at a higher rank, it can do something else..." His father shook his head, still not understanding why Teng Mingyu had chosen Hope Gu, of all Gu worms, to be his vital Gu.
Teng Mingyu then went into a room where Teng Mei was. Her abdomen was slightly swollen, indicating that she was at least a few months pregnant. "I managed to do it!" Teng Mingyu said, embracing her.
"That's amazing!" she answered. "How did you do it?"
"The essence of refining Hope Gu is to take the hopes of many people and stack them upon each other," Teng Mingyu answered. "I have to thank you for this."
"Oh, it was nothing," Teng Mei said.
"No, I really do need to thank you and Teng Ling for this."
"Thank us, but what did we do?" Teng Mei asked.
"It was your friendship that let me do this." Teng Mingyu took out Friendship Gu from his aperture.
"You still have that?" Teng Mei asked.
"Not only do I still have it, your wills were still always there with me, and it was thanks to them that I was able to create Rank Two Hope Gu. I think that if I managed to get more people, I might be able to create a Rank Three Hope Gu as well. But first, I need to advance Integration Gu to the next rank."
"You're always so busy," Teng Mei said, wrapping her arms around him. "You should relax a little, you know?"
"Teng Mei," he said, "You know how much work and expectations there are on my shoulders, on top of which I decided to do something as dumb as taking Hope Gu as my vital gu. I have to work hard to compensate for it, don't I?"
"Don't call my husband dumb!" Teng Mei punched him lightly on the shoulder. "I'm sure you had your reasons for doing so, and if it was something unconscious, maybe it was Fate itself that desired you to have Hope Gu and refine it further."
"I don't really see how that's possible," Teng Mingyu mused. "Fate Gu is the enemy of Hope Gu, after all. Isn't it true that one's hope would be to persevere, even if Fate decrees that you have to fail? Even in the direst of scenarios, didn't Ren Zu continue to keep Hope Gu in his heart, which had refused to abandon him even as Fate Gu mocked him and trapped him in his web?" He then went on another tangent. "And Hope Gu is also the first step towards cultivating... every Gu Master awakens their aperture with the tiniest seed of hope... so long as one has that, there is always a chance to succeed..."
"You're thinking too much again," Teng Mei said, rolling her eyes. She then gasped. "Oh, right, you promised to take me shopping this afternoon, didn't you? Don't tell me you forgot!"
"All right, yes, I did," Teng Mingyu said, rubbing the back of his neck. "Sorry, let's get ready and go."

chapters.title: Chapter 137 - 137: Refining Hope Gu: Part Five
chapters.content:
The dream realm shifted once more.
Fang Yuan felt that there was an increase to his attainment in the Human Path once more. However, he was still lacking somewhat to get to the quasi-Grandmaster realm. The dream wasn't over yet, though so there was still a chance to advance even further.
Fang Yuan found himself in the same house, except a portion of it was on fire.
Fang Yuan barely had a moment to take this in when he noticed a pair of beady yellow eyes glaring at him from the darkness. 'Lions,' he realized. He checked his aperture.
He had Rank Three Hope Gu now, meaning that Teng Mingyu had likely succeeded in advancing it to Rank Three as well. However, that would be of no help to him in this fight. As for the other gu worms, there was Rank Three Integration Gu. There was still Friendship Gu. And just like before, there were a number of Gu worms which he was not sure about.
He got out of the way as the lion leaped, but there was little that he could do with his own physical strength.
'There must be an offensive Gu worm among these,' Fang Yuan thought. 'If I picked one, he would soon end up dying.' He knew one of them was a storage Gu worm, so that left only three possibilities.
He picked one, and the Gu worm in question leapt from his aperture into his stomach and began releasing something immediately. Fang Yuan felt something travel up his esophagus and into his throat as he then spat out a massive gush of green liquid, the liquid splashed against the lion, dissolving its flesh and bones as it touched it.
'This is a type of acid-spitting gu worm,' Fang Yuan realized. He felt a sharp burning sensation in his mouth and throat, but he knew that there must also be a gu worm for this as well. Of the other two gu worms, he activated one which generated a protective shield around him and the other which actually healed his wound. 'I should have used the defensive Gu worm first before this,' Fang Yuan realized as his primal essence was rapidly depleted. 'It would've prevented this kind of corrosive effect.' It was like how one had to use defensive gu worms or strengthen one's bones before they could properly use Strength Path gu.
With this lion taken care of, there was much to be done. He ran out of the house to see that the village was infested with them.
'Where did so many lions come from?' Fang Yuan thought. This was not something from a beast tide. No, this looked like the work of an Enslavement Gu Master.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs
Three more lions pounced at Fang Yuan, though he defeated them with ease. Around him, he could hear the screams of the surrounding villagers as well as the roars of the lions.
He began running through the streets, wondering what it was that the dream required him to do. It could be surviving this fight. It could be killing a certain person, or it could even be saving a certain person. You could usually only figure out these things via trial and error, though Fang Yuan only had the resources to try once for now.
As he was walking through the streets of the village, he came upon someone whom he recognized. "Teng Ling!" he shouted out.
Given how close the two of them were, there was no way that Teng Mingyu would have simply wandered off and left him there. Fang Yuan was sure that doing so would lead to the end of the dream realm and him failing.
Teng Ling had been severely injured, and even Teng Ling's healing gu could do little for this. It was likely that his own healing gu was made specifically to counter the acidic effects of his offensive gu, and not for wounds like this. It was not as good as Doctor Gu when it came to healing.
"Don't mind me," Teng Ling said. "Save Teng Mei and... save the villagers. Save yourself!"
"Who did this?" Fang Yuan asked.
As if to answer his question, a voice cut through all of the other noise. It was cold and distant, as the North Wind itself. "Die, die, you Teng clan bastards! Today I take my revenge for my humiliation!"
There was a scream. "No, please! Let us go! What did we ever do to you?"
The cold voice answered, "Your mistake was being born in the Teng Clan. In your next life, don't be surnamed Teng." Then there was a scream that was swiftly cut off by the roar of the lion.
'I see,' Fang Yuan thought, 'so a demonic Gu Master might have been insulted by someone from this village and came back for revenge. Or perhaps it was a mortal who managed to find a way to cultivate and then came back for revenge for some kind of humiliation in the past.' There were numerous stories in the world, though he had personally never heard of the Teng clan.
Fang Yuan then turned his attention back to this person's aperture.
His improved attainment in the Human Path told him there was something that could be done here. Friendship Gu and Healing Gu along with it, Integration Gu, and Hope Gu!
He had formed a killer move, though he had no chance to test it. However, given its simplicity and the fact that it used only a few gu worms, it shouldn't have been too difficult to pull off with his attainment level.
He used Healing Gu and then used the other three Gu worms together.
Mortal Killer Move - The Bond Between Friends!
This turned the original path of the Healing Gu worm to the Human Path. Its effects became apparent as Teng Ling got up as the healing effect was greatly magnified. "That was," Teng Ling said, looking at his healed wounds, "something that you should have saved for someone else."
"Where is Teng Mei?" Fang Yuan asked.
"You mean she's not with you?" Teng Ling wondered. "How could you let her out of your sight at a time like this?"
Teng Ling answered for Fang Yuan. "She had gone for a stroll with my father late at night. I didn't think that she'd be caught up in something like this."
"Then there's nowhere we can just sit around not doing anything!" Teng Ling said. "Let's go!"
The demonic Gu Master in question was riding a Lava Lion Lord, a Rank Four Beast King. Every time it roared, small tendrils of flames would escape its mouth. Its mane was made of scorching flames, which would sear everything in its path.
Teng Mingyu was still only Rank Three, and there was no way that he stood a chance of beating this person. 'Or is there?' Fang Yuan thought. Even if there wasn't, that didn't mean that he had automatically failed the dream realm. There must have been some solution to this problem.
Teng Mingyu's vital Gu shuddered. Fang Yuan barely managed to avoid the claws of a lion who had been waiting in ambush before he killed it.
"No, please!" a Gu Master pleaded before the Lava Lion Lord.
But he died - because he was surnamed Teng!
"Teng Mei!" Teng Ling yelled out. Fang Yuan saw that Teng Mingyu's father was desperately holding off a group of lions, along with a few other elders behind him. Teng Mei looked extremely scared, but thankfully unharmed for now
"Good, good," the demonic Gu Master said. "Your resistance only makes my victory all the sweeter." He then turned his gaze towards Teng Mingyu. "Him, take him out as well!" A group of lions surrounded the two of them.
"We might be done for here," Teng Ling said. "But even if we are, it was a pleasure to fight with you, brother."
"We're not done yet!" Teng Mingyu answered.
'The hopes of the Teng clansmen... Their desire to see the next day... The bonds that had been formed between all of them.' Integration Gu activated, bringing them together.
Their wills combined as numerous small portions of their will were gathered around Integration Gu.
Fang Yuan instinctively realized what he had to do next. He would have liked to practice this killer move before trying it out as well. It was a miracle the earlier one had worked, but there was no time for second chances here.
Mortal Killer Move- Hope of the Clansmen!
The will of the Teng clan gathered around Integration Gu. Before being rocketed out towards Hope Gu, which began shining along with Friendship Gu.
A bright light began to surround the Teng clansmen, and with that, there was a flash of bright light and Fang Yuan found himself back in his room.
'So that was it. The dream realm did not show what the ultimate fate of the Teng clan had been.' Fang Yuan now felt his Human Path mastery finally reached quasi-Grandmaster level. 'So that is what it wanted to show me,' Fang Yuan thought.
Not only had his his attainment level in the Human Path increased, he also had a bit of direct information from that dream realm. 'I learned how one can advance Hope Gu. It looks like there is something else that I will have to add to my things to do,' Fang Yuan thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 138 - 138: Strike Force: Part One
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan exited his room. Now that his attainment in the Human Path had risen to quasi-Grandmaster level, it opened up new avenues for him to pursue. Not only that, he now knew the recipe for advancing Hope Gu.
'However, I can't do anything with the primeval spring right now,' Fang Yuan thought. He did have his own idea to advance Hope Gu, but it'd be better if he became clan head before doing so.
"You're done, Fang Yuan?" asked Fang Zheng who was standing guard outside Fang Yuan's room. If anyone were to ask, he was to tell them that he was in closed-door cultivation and had demanded not to be disturbed. This was true, but Fang Zheng was also waiting just in case Fang Yuan happened to become trapped in the dream realm somehow as a safety measure to wake him up.
"Did anyone drop by?" Fang Yuan asked.
"A couple of people did," Fang Zheng answered, "but their needs weren't urgent, or they were just people wasting time, you know, the sort."
Fang Yuan nodded. "The only thing that I think was important was that there was an elders' meeting tomorrow," Fang Zheng added. "And they sent a messenger to ask me whether or not you would be attending."
"I was going to say that you were in closed-door cultivation, and I didn't know when you were going to come out, so probably not. But..."
"It's not an issue," Fang Yuan said. Although it was late, he had no problem attending the meeting.
It had been ultimately pointless last time, based on his memories, to the point where he had nearly forgotten about what had happened there. It was just a meeting to go over the upcoming wolf tide, and there was a lot of brow-beating and chest-thumping, as well as descriptions of how the wolf tide was getting worse, but very little of practical value was done at the time.
Now, though, Fang Yuan had something to contribute to the meeting so he would without a doubt attend.
"Go to the underground cavern and ask for these supplies for me," Fang Yuan said, writing down some supplies on a piece of paper and handing it to his younger brother, as well as a bag filled with primeval stones.
It may have been late at night, but for someone like Fang Yuan, there was no issue in obtaining supplies, especially right now with the Wolf Tide nearly at its peak.The most update n0vels are published on NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"These supplies are..." Fang Zheng said, reading over them. "Brother, aren't they slightly different from what you thought we were going to use initially?"
"That's right," Fang Yuan said. "I was going to advance my Golden Moon Gu at first. At least, that was what I was thinking. However, I've changed my mind after contemplating. I wish to refine the advanced version of the Blood Moon Gu instead."
In the previous timeline, the clan head had highly suggested that Fang Yuan refine the advanced version of the Golden Moon Gu, and at the time Fang Yuan had agreed, simply because he could not leave the village then. However, now things had changed.
For one, he could leave the village, and feeding an advanced version of the Golden Moon Gu would be a massive headache if he stayed on Qing Mao mountain. Secondly, while he had thought of a potential killer move during the prior timeline, he now had a more firm understanding of the Human Path, and therefore could think of a definitive killer move. However, this was not just a Human Path killer move. It would be a combined Human and Blood Path killer move. For that, he needed a Blood Path gu worm at least at Rank 4, and this was the easiest one to get his hands on.
"Brother, are you sure?" Fang Zheng asked. "Even the clan head and the other elders thought that the Blood Moon Gu wasn't the best path to advance the Moonglow Gu on?"
Fang Yuan waved his hand. "It might not have been for them. In my experience, however, this is a far better gu worm. Go ahead with this. Once you become more experienced yourself, you'll also understand."
Fang Zheng couldn't help but think, 'I know brother's advanced to Rank Four, but he's speaking about things from his own limited experience. How much could he have experienced by this point, even if he is a genius? He's only 16 years old, just like me. A lot of the elders have been cultivating for far longer than he's been born. I wish he would listen to their advice. From this tone, I can already tell that he's not going to change though. Uh, I just hope this doesn't come back to bite him in the future.'
Fang Yuan noticed this reluctance from his younger brother, but didn't say anything. As his younger brother wandered off. What did it matter if Fang Zheng didn't understand so long as he fulfilled his role as a puppet and that Fang Yuan could extract Immortal Gu from him?
'As a backup plan,' Fang Yuan thought, 'in case I happen to fail, I need to find out a way to...' His eyes suddenly widened. 'Could it be that that was the reason that I had been handed that gu worm?'
Running away on his own was fine, but he wished to save Fang Zheng as well, if possible. After all, this was an actual, reasonable way that he could get an Immortal Gu. Unlike that weird mission from the system in which he had to marry Bai Ning Bing, which was definitely not going to happen. The issue was how he would keep Fang Zheng safe.
'Doting Mother Gu and Traveling Son Gu,' Fang Yuan thought. 'The only issue is how I'm going to make it so that he can actually use one of those Gu worms.' While he waited for Fang Zheng to return, he began preparing things for refining Vermilion Blood Moon Gu.
He already had some of the ingredients, but there were also some that he could not pull out in public. It was only when Fang Zheng returned that Fang Yuan started the refinement on his own.
He took out Blood Moon Gu. He was a Blood Path Grandmaster in his previous life, and advancing this would have been child's play at the time, though he did not have much of the resources available to him right now.
However, he did have one thing which he did not have in his original life at this time: the support of the Crimsonhoof Deer. Even if it was not a full-grown deer yet, its blood could still count as a Rank Two refinement material. And after Fang Yuan had visited it, it would soon be able to count as a Rank Three refinement material in this timeline, though he did not have that right now.
To the Blood Moon Gu, he started adding various ingredients. First, he needed the blood from three different Thousand Beast Kings. With the wolf tide going on, this was not hard for him to collect. As he added it to the Blood Moon Gu, it began glowing.
Then, he had to add fifty moon orchid petals. If he had not been granted his increased allowance, doing so would have been financially crippling to him. However, the advanced version of the gu worm would not need moon orchid petals to feed anymore. So, this was a one-time cost.
He then added two Moonglow Gu. The ball of light started growing brighter!

chapters.title: Chapter 139 - 139: Strike Force: Part Two
chapters.content:
The ball of light began shining brightly. He had failed last time he had tried this, but this time he added the blood of the Crimsonhoof Deer. He had messed up last time he had tried to refine this Gu worm because he had changed his mind on what he was going to advance it to before harvesting the blood of the Crimsonhoof Deer.
Refinement depended on various factors. He wasn't sure if going back in time would change the odds if he had failed due to luck. He could only continue tossing in primal stones until the ball of light shrunk, and a new Gu worm fell into his palm. It looked just like the Blood Moon Gu, except it was larger, and the blood was a darker, deeper, richer color. Vermilion Blood Moon Gu! It had been successfully refined!
Fang Yuan had been successful on his first try. This was good because otherwise, he would have to switch up his plan on how to deal with the Lightning Lycan King.
After this, Fang Yuan fell asleep, exhausted.
The meeting of the elders was devoid of the usual pomp and circumstance that it might have had in other times. With the wolf tide going around, no one had time for excessive formalities or pageantry. That wasn't to say that there wasn't anything important going on.
After all, the topic of discussion right now was the fact that the village had a new Rank Four Gu Master, Fang Yuan.
Fang Yuan had paid little attention to the inner politics going on at this time, simply because it had not been worth his notice, and he had been occupied with other things at the time during the previous timeline. The only thing he had strived for was to avoid conflict and he had been able to avoid such without much issue thanks to an old clan legend.
Now, though, he wanted to encourage action and that would require action on his part.
The village currently had 22 Elders. One of them was standing guard at the wall in case there was an emergency that needed someone to stall for some time while the rest of them headed out.
Another one was injured so severely that he couldn't come to this meeting.
That made the total number of people there 20, including the clan head. 'In the coming days, though,' Fang Yuan thought, 'Some of these faces would no longer be here. Two of them had been killed by being ambushed by the Lightning Lycan King, and two more had died afterwards in unrelated incidents.' During this kind of crazy wolf tide, no one was safe.
The village's two major factions, the Mo faction and the Chi faction, were present. The faction which supported the clan head was smaller, though now that they had Fang Yuan, it could be said that they were the strongest faction.
Other than this, there were a few smaller factions consisting of the Medicine Hall Elder, and a neutral faction, which together could maybe rival these other groups.
Fang Yuan glanced towards Mo Chen, the leader of the Mo faction. He had a pensive face, but he was glancing towards Fang Yuan as well as the clan head. Fang Yuan didn't know this, but inwardly, the man was cursing the fact that he hadn't been a bit more aggressive in having his daughter court Fang Yuan.
If only they had been successful in doing so, then the Mo faction would have had a Rank Four Gu Master among their ranks and would have been the domineering force within Gu Yue Village. Against his rival, the Chi clan, this would be both check and mate! But there was no use in dwelling over such matters- it was just that Mo Chen had not anticipated that Fang Yuan would rise to power this quickly. Fast yes, but not blazing through the ranks like he had done so right now.
His only real chance had been when Fang Yuan was still a student, but they had dropped the ball on that.
Fang Yuan then turned his gaze towards Chi Lian. He did have some potential leverage over the Chi faction simply because he knew their secret. The incident in which Chi Cheng's aptitude had actually been revealed had not occurred yet.
For that matter, if things continued as they were, the village would be destroyed before it could happen.
However, Fang Yuan no longer needed to resort to such things in order to get their cooperation. His sheer strength was more than enough.
Lastly, there was the Medicine Hall faction, as well as the neutral faction. Naturally, the Medicine Hall had seen its influence increased during the time of the wolf tide. The neutral faction could not be ignored either, as even one or two more elders could shift the tide of a battle.
The meeting began with a report of casualties. The mortals had died in such numbers, and no one particularly cared for them, so their deaths were not even worth of being reported upon.
What was more important was the loss of Gu Masters. 45 Rank One Gu Masters had been killed in the last two months. 20 more had been incapacitated to the point where they could no longer fight. 30 Rank Twos had died, and five were incapacitated.
In addition, there were about 15 Gu Masters who claimed that they could not bring out their full strength either because of a lack of Gu worms, injuries, old age, or a combination of the above and had requested to be retired from the front lines.
"Bah! These are all excuses!" Mo Chen said. "What do these Gu Masters think, that they can stand by behind the backs of other people risking their necks for them? We should issue a decree demanding that they commit themselves to the field."
He had made the same demand last time. Fang Yuan remembered some of the people who had been forced to the front line because of this had ended up dying when they had encountered the Lightning Lycan King.
Mo Chen had shown no remorse for such during the time period afterwards. 'So what if they had died in a way that actually freed up resources for other people? This was another way of calling out those who are useless.' That must've been his thought process.
It was a bit of a shame that those Gu Masters had died basically without contributing anything, however, Fang Yuan felt. While they were a bit of a burden on the clan (Gu Yue Ye was in this camp), even if they were doing nothing, to send them blindly to their deaths was also a mistake, though now, only Fang Yuan knew this in advance.
Mo Chen's suggestion, however, passed without any resistance. Even his rival, Chi Lian, could not think of a reason to oppose this sort of thinking. When even elders's lives were at risk, how could the rank and file think to hide?ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
With that matter settled, now came the reports on the wolf numbers. It was this opportunity that Fang Yuan had been waiting for before he was going to pounce on it this time around.

chapters.title: Chapter 140 - 140: Strike Force: Part Three
chapters.content:
"Regarding the wolf tide," Fang Yuan Yuan began, once he had been granted permission to speak, all eyes immediately turning towards him. Last time, during this meeting, he had said as little as possible in order to draw the least bit of attention to himself as possible. Now, though, he was confident in his strength enough to openly go around scheming, but he still not strong enough for what he wanted to do on his lonesome.
"We are not just dealing with Thunder Crown Wolves in this wolf tide," Fang Yuan said. "I'm sure that many of you have heard of this, but there's also a Lightning Lycan King among them."
From their expressions, he could tell that many of them had indeed heard of this but for about one third of them this was completely out of the blue.
"A Lightning Lycan King!" one of them yelled out. The elder's pupils shrunk. The mere thought of another Rank 4 equivalent wolf out there was enough to dry his throat.
"Elder Fang Yuan," the Medicine Elder, Gu Yue Yao Ji asked gently, "how exactly did you come to know of this?"
Even those who were already aware that there was a Lightning Lycan King were curious about this. Not even the clan head knew the details.
"I've seen it with my own eyes," Fang Yuan said. "We battled, I almost beat it, and then I gave chase, but it is cunning, as many of you can already assume. When it saw that its defeat was certain, it fled. I did not have an Audio-Visual Gu on me at the time, otherwise I could have presented more direct evidence on the matter."
"There is little need for that." The voice who spoke right now was the oldest among the elders, Gu Yue Han Lin. Fang Yuan knew that two of the elders, other than the clan head, happened to know the secret of the Blood River Graveyard. Without a doubt, this person was one of them. "The words of Elder Gu Yue Fang Yuan are more than enough."
There was some muttering in the background. After all, all they had right now was Fang Yuan's word for it, and no words from other scouts.
As it was, Fang Yuan's story seemed rather fanciful- especially in the way that he described nearly defeating it. It would be difficult for even the current clan head with the help of several elders to defeat the Lightning Lycan King. For Fang Yuan to have nearly done so on his own was difficult for them to stomach - for those who did not think that he possessed the Ancient Yin Desolate Moon Physique it was nearly unimaginable.
"Could the scouts really have been deceived?" Mo Chen asked. The reason why he was bringing this up was because it was his granddaughter, Mo Yan, who had been sent as part of the team to investigate the wolf tide. Of course, there had been other teams, but if someone wanted to, they could bring this up as a failure of his faction to properly investigate the issue.
"It is not unfathomable that the Lightning Lycan King has not been found until now," another chimed in. "It has the intelligence rivaling humans, and its size is only that of an ordinary wolf. It would have, without doubt, blended itself among the pack, and any scout which would have happened to come upon it would have either not noticed it or not lived to tell the tale. Lord Fang Yuan, with his Rank 4 cultivation level, however, would have been able to do so and also live to tell the tale."
Mo Chen relaxed a little. That meant that this matter could not be traced back to his faction and blamed upon his granddaughter.Googlᴇ search Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"I think that everyone here knows the danger that the Lightning Lycan King presents," Fang Yuan said. "Which is why I propose that to deal with this issue, we go ahead and preemptively strike against it. Without it, the wolf tide will have lost its greatest strategist." These words drew several shocked looks and even a few gasps. The clan head already knew of this plan. However, he had not begun introducing it just because of how out of left field it was.
"Lord Fang Yuan?" one of the elders finally managed to get out. This was an elder from the neutral faction, though he spoke with trepidation. "I do not doubt for a second your valor and bravery, as well as strength. However, there is a reason why we wait for the wolves to come to us, and we do not strike out against them. Out there in the wilderness is their territory- we would be leaving ourselves exposed, searching for the Lightning Lycan King fruitlessly for possibly days on end."
"I understand your concerns," Fang Yuan said. "However, we will not be going around marching around the wilderness fruitlessly. I have been able to ascertain certain facts about its routines and habitat. As such, I know where it will appear. If we head out within the next five days, we will be able to find it somewhere around this region." Fang Yuan pointed to a spot on a map that was laid out.
"I want to create a team with me at the head and several elders supporting, so that we can catch the Lightning Lycan off guard. With it removed from the table, dealing with the wolf tide will be far easier."
None of the elders spoke up for some time.
Fang Yuan had declared something - that he knew where the Lightning Lycan King was going to be. This was nearly an absurd fact were it not for the existence of certain gu worms which could allow one to track such a creature.
If it had been an ordinary elder who had proposed such a plan, they might have even been kicked out of the meeting then and there after being harshly reprimanded by the clan head.
Without a doubt, many of them had their own hesitations, but because it was Fang Yuan, a Rank 4 Gu Master, who had said this, none of them wanted to be the first to call him out. Even the elder who had spoken up against Fang Yuan before from the neutral faction had felt like he was walking a tightrope while he questioned Fang Yuan. The only person who could truly do so was the clan head himself, or the leaders of the Mo or Chi factions.
The clan head was already firmly on Fang Yuan's side. As for the Mo and the Chi factions, neither of them wanted to risk stepping on uneven ground. Finally, it was Yao Ji who spoke up.
"Lord Fang Yuan," Gu Yue Yao Ji said. "I appreciate your valor and readiness to sacrifice for the clan. However, I think that this is too risky a matter." Her words were soft, and although many openly shook their heads at them, most of them actually agreed with her inwardly. They simply did not have the courage to voice their opinion. "You are still young and inexperienced, Fang Yuan, despite your strength. Heed the advice those who have seen far more winters than you, and you will continue to live for far more winters than you would otherwise." Yao Ji said these words without knowing that compared to Fang Yuan, she may as well have been a little girl.
It looked like the meeting was about to turn against Fang Yuan's suggestion, with even the clan head being unable to do much with the elders united in this manner.
'It was a borderline insane plan to begin with,' the clan head thought to himself. 'In this political battlefield, Fang Yuan, you need to prove yourself, and I can help you no further.'
However, right then and there, a voice cut through the crowd.
"I support Fang Yuan and will go with him to fight the Lightning Lycan King!"

chapters.title: Chapter 141 - 141: Strike Force: Part Four
chapters.content:
These words were uttered by Gu Yue Han Lin.
The man looked like he could keel over any moment, but there was a strange strength still left within him that could not be underestimated. He had been an elder of the clan for a long time and knew that his time would come sooner or later. He had already settled matters with his son who was prepared to take over the family traditions.
As for why he was volunteering, it was because he knew the legend of the Blood River Graveyard, and he thought that Fang Yuan had the blessing of their first generation ancestor. Were it not for those things, he too would have voiced his disapproval. However, given his age and given the fact that he knew that his time would sooner or later arrive, he wished to be part of the faction that supported the new and future pillar of their clan, the one who would bear the Ancient Yin Desolate Moon Physique.
He did not admonish Gu Yue Yao Ji but upon seeing such an old and frail man volunteer to take this kind of mission immediately, it would cause a great deal of shame to build within the hearts of those who heard it and were fearful.
Well, except for Fang Yuan, that is; he had absolutely no shame. But shaming was one of the best tactics the righteous path had to control its members.
The Mo and the Chi factions then immediately voiced their support simultaneously.
"How many elders will you need?" the clan head asked Fang Yuan upon seeing the motion pass without resistance now.
"Six or seven should be adequate," Fang Yuan said.
Ultimately, a group of eight was assembled. This was nearly half of Gu Yue Village's strength when it came to elders in terms of numbers, not to mention Fang Yuan, who was Rank 4 himself. If this mission failed, without a doubt, it would reflect badly on Fang Yuan.
However, Fang Yuan did not care for his reputation, nor did he think that he would fail in this endeavor anyway.
Once the meeting was wrapped up, Fang Yuan headed out to deal with some other matters in preparation for the upcoming battle. Several skilled investigative Gu Masters would be called upon, on top of which Fang Yuan had been allowed an extra allowance of items from the underground cavern for the upcoming mission. It was for the ultimate good of the clan, after all.
He had gu worms of his own to refine, as well as to purchase. He also hadn't used his Cultivation Blessing to raise a gu worm by one rank yet- and needed to weigh on what the right gu worm for that would be.
And at this point, Fang Yuan had weaved things in such a way that only the clan head could properly oppose him, and the clan head would not do so.
With that said, there was another ally that he needed to rope in when it came to dealing with the Lightning Lycan King
He stopped by a familiar house. The guard posted out front immediately let him in without a word. Fang Yuan found the person who he was looking for practicing in the courtyard of the manor.
Gu Yue Qing Shu's arms had turned into vines, which he was using to strike several grass dummies. He had honed this ability over several years. Were it not for the case, he would not be able to fight Rank 3 Gu Masters even with the help of the Wood Charm Gu.
Despite the spectacular performance, Qing Shu actually fumbled his final blow. Not out of lack of skill on his part, but because he had noticed Fang Yuan in the corner watching him.
"Fang Yuan!" Qing Shu said, immediately canceling the Wood Charm Gu's effect, his arms returning to normal.
"Good evening, and well, how are you?" Fang Yuan said.
"I can't complain," Qing Shu said.
"How is Yao Hong doing now?"
"Perfectly fine, thanks to you. I'll be honest, if you hadn't popped up at that time, I think it's likely that the three of us might have been finished."
"Oh, I'm sure you could have handled it," Fang Yuan said, waving his hand dismissively.
Qing Shu chuckled. "Maybe- maybe I could have held him off, but not without losing control."
"Regarding that, actually," Fang Yuan said. "I wanted to speak to you about something."
"Is that so?" Qing Shu asked. "If that were the case, why didn't you just call me to your house? I would have come running."
"No, it's fine," Fang Yuan said. "As it is, I've already spoken with the elders, and your house was on the way. And it's not a job that I need you to do anything excessive for. Instead, it's more of a... request."
"What is this request."
"I want you to advance to Rank 3!"
Qing Shu paused. "You want me to advance to Rank 3?"
"Yes," Fang Yuan said. "There's a matter of secrecy that needs to be kept around, so I'm sure you can be trusted regarding this. I wanted to take you along with me anyway so there is little use hiding it form you." Fang Yuan told Qing Shu about the Lightning Lycan King and his plan to strike out at them.
"Fang Yuan, I'm not going to mince words here," Qing Shu said. "But I don't agree with your idea. I know that you're strong. I've seen it myself. But tackling the enemy out there in the open, while it might seem and sound courageous, it is more likely than not to backfire. Several elders could also be lost during the fighting."
"I already know that," Fang Yuan said. "Which is why you'll be a far more help if you were to get to Rank 3."
Qing Shu sighed.
The servants began setting up dinner, and the two of them sat down to eat. However, Fang Yuan was relentless in what he was trying to convey.
"Senior Brother Qing Shu," Fang Yuan said.
"Fang Yuan, you don't need to use honorifics like 'Senior Brother' before me," Qing Shu said.
There had been something endearing about Fang Yuan still thinking of him as Senior Brother, but that was back when Fang Yuan had just become an elder. Now that Fang Yuan was Rank 4 and likely to become clan head, he couldn't go around addressing someone like Qing Shu so formally. If anything, Qing Shu needed to start addressing Fang Yuan with respect.
"It does not matter how far I go in my cultivation," Fang Yuan said, "or how strong I get. After all, aren't people worthless if they forget who helped them back when they were weak and young? That is why I felt like I could not take the clan head position right now. I could not bear to be seen as someone who had struck against the current clan head, who did so much to help both me and Senior Brother Qing Shu. Even if I somehow managed to get to the heights of Rank 4 or even Rank 5, for that matter, I will not forget all of the important lessons imparted to me back during those days which I treasure deeply within my heart. And you will always remain Senior Brother, as will my other teammates continue to remain my other teammates."
Qing Shu sighed. He thought inwardly, 'In a way, I think Fang Yuan is too good for his own safety. You need to be a bit more scheming if you want to succeed as clan head. If he continues like this, people are going to take advantage of his generosity. Well, it's fine to be nice and polite. But one must also occasionally be selfish - that is a lesson that only time will teach him.'

chapters.title: Chapter 142 - 142: Strike Force: Part Five
chapters.content:
"Tell me the truth," Fang Yuan continued. "The reason why you are still at Rank 2 peak stage and not at Rank 3 is not because you are unable to reach that stage due to the elders, correct? They wished to suppress you because they could make better use of you."
Qing Shu fiddled with what he was eating. Well, what Fang Yuan was saying was not technically incorrect; however, it was also not the whole truth. "Fang Yuan, in any organization, those at the bottom need to pay their dues before they can advance further. It is true that the elders demanded certain things of me, but then again, I have just barely graduated from the academy. What they asked for was not excessive, and if I can serve the clan better by being at Rank 2 peak stage rather than becoming a Rank 3 elder, I do not see what is the problem in holding off my cultivation for a while."
"As expected of Senior Brother," Fang Yuan said. "There's a saying which is often parroted around teachers: that they, like candles, burn themselves so they can illuminate the path for others. However, if you wish to truly contribute to the clan right now, it needs more strength than it has ever needed before. I want you to become Rank 3 before we set out for the strike force."
Fang Yuan's mission was to keep Qing Shu safe, and he had failed in it last time around. However, he had succeeded in saving Qing Shu this time because he had acted faster than he did before. However, even if he forbade him, he was sure that Qing Shu would find his way onto the battlefield, and Qing Shu's chances of survival were much higher if he were at Rank 3.
The mission required Qing Shu to survive past the Lightning Lycan King's assault, not just to survive that encounter with Bai Ning Bing.
"Tell me one thing, Senior Brother Qing Shu," Fang Yuan continued. "There's another reason why you don't want to advance to Rank 3, isn't there?"
Qing Shu did not answer him, so Fang Yuan continued.
"The real reason why you don't want to become an elder," Fang Yuan said, "is because you dislike the internal politics among them. Isn't it? As long as you're only at Rank 2, you don't need to bother yourself much with them and only listen to what the clan head says. However, once you are an elder, they will look at you differently. You'll be forced to choose a faction, more likely than not, the Clan Head's faction along with me. You'll be embroiled in their schemes, and you feel like that will take away from your ability to work in the village like you want. "
"It isn't just that," Qing Shu said. "All of my friends, my companions... they are still at Rank 2. If I were to go further along this path, I will be leaving them behind. In a way, I will be even more isolated than I am now."
Qing Shu sighed. "I'm sure that you can understand, Fang Yuan. Being a genius is rather lonely."Googlᴇ search
"I can," Fang Yuan said. "However..."
"...you can only be with them if they are still alive. I think you can appreciate the magnitude of the situation. The clan is on the verge of possibly being annihilated, if not, at the very least, many people will die. Neither Mo Bei nor Chi Sheng would've declined this kind of offer."
"I understand what you're saying," Qing Shu said. "However, even if I would like to, to break through to Rank 3 so quickly is..."
Fang Yuan pulled out a bag from the Tulsita Grass Gu. "This bag contains 3,000 Primal Stones," Fang Yuan said.
He had a good estimate of what Qing Shu's aptitude was like and how much he would need to break through.
"Feel free to use it," Fang Yuan said, handing it to Qing Shu. Fang Yuan giving someone else a bag of primeval stones was a strange sight indeed. However, for what was at stake, given the fact that Yellow Gold Relic Gu oftentimes could not even be bought in mortal marketplaces, this was a small price. As it was, Fang Yuan no longer lacked primeval stones. He had either been able to easily borrow some and people had simply given him more Primal Stones after he had reached Rank 4.
"Fang Yuan, I can't possibly..." Qing Shu began to protest.
"It's fine, if you want, you can consider it a loan," Fang Yuan said. "You can pay me back later on, but no more excuses from now on. Use these primeval stones and advance to Rank 3. If you truly want to help the clan, this is the best way forward. And once you get to Rank 3, join me in my attempt to kill the Lightning Lycan King."
Qing Shu looked down at his meal.
He could withdraw himself and entered closed-door cultivation for a few days, and would be tired at the end. People were going to die as he wouldn't be around to finish some tasks.
However, what Fang Yuan was saying, looking at the bigger picture, was correct. Far more people would die if the Lightning Lycan King continued to exist and was able to rally more wolves to its side. To kill it before it could get to them would not be easy, but if they succeeded, the wolf tide would be far less frightening.
"All right, Fang Yuan," Qing Shu said, sighing. "It looks like you won." He took the primeval stones. "I will repay these back to you at some point."
"Next time when we meet, I hope that you'll be Elder Qing Shu," Fang Yuan said.
"And soon enough, I hope," Qing Shu said. "I will address you as Clan Head Fang Yuan."
With their dinner finished, Fang Yuan made his way back home.
The next day, while Qing Shu was in closed-door cultivation, Fang Yuan had taken another visit to the underground cavern to withdraw not only some gu worms but also some refinement materials.
Since he still had his Cultivation Blessing, he needed to raise the Moonlight Chainmail Gu on his own to the Moonlight Plate Armor Gu.
"Finally..." Fang Yuan said as he succeeded on his third attempt after two day's worth of time. This refinement coupled with what he had lent out to Qing Shu had put a dent in his finances, but it couldn't be helped.
A good defensive option was needed for the upcoming fight. He would need it to face the Lightning Lycan King.
As for Charity Gu, though he had tried to delay it- it had ended up refining itself to Rank 5 regardless. That made it more difficult to use.
However, Integration Gu was already showing effects even now. Collecting the wills and experiences of the members of the Gu Yue clan, Fang Yuan could feel it almost filled to the brim right now.
The only question was what he would do with all of this accumulated experience.
Secret mission complete!
'Charity Begins At Home'
Help Qing Shu advance to Rank 3!
Reward: The recipes for Rank 6 to Rank 9 Charity Gu!

chapters.title: Chapter 143 - 143: Strike Force: Part Six
chapters.content:
Without a doubt, this notification greatly shocked Fang Yuan, and he eagerly accepted the recipe, downloading it directly into his mind as if he had used an information path Gu worm.
Normally, the recipes for Immortal Gu worms could go on for pages and pages. However, these recipes for Rank 6 to Rank 9 Charity Gu could have easily fit on one page. That was because the requirements for refining them were rather straightforward.
Rank 6 Charity Gu could be refined from Rank 5 Charity Gu, assuming that no Rank 6 Charity Gu already existed, by donating a Rank 6 Gu to someone, with Rank 5 Charity Gu already in your possession.
There were restrictions on this, of course. You could not just simply take it back, and it had to be freely given to whoever you were donating it to. In the same vein, you could get Rank 7 Charity Gu by donating a Rank 7 Gu to someone else. You could get Rank 8 Charity Gu by donating a different Rank 8 Gu to someone else, and for Rank 9 Charity Gu, you would have to donate a Rank 9 Gu to someone.
Fang Yuan's eyelid twitched. Upon reading this information, he nearly spat out a mouthful of blood in anger. Out of all of the unreasonable things mentioned by the system - this seemed to be the most unreasonable. Even more than that mission requiring him to marry Bai Ning Bing.
What kind of Gu recipe was this? What did this system take him for? Did Rank 9 Gu grow on trees or something? Given how unique Immortal Gu were and how hard it was to obtain an Immortal Gu worm in the first place, with many Gu Immortals not having even a single Immortal Gu corresponding to their rank, this might have been entirely useless, especially given that he had no idea what he was even going to use Charity Gu for or what the Immortal version of Charity Gu did.
Essentially, these recipes did not suit Fang Yuan at all!
He was sure that he could eventually find a workaround to the stipulation that they had to be freely given. He was sure that there was a way to fool it in such a way that he could still donate the gu worm and have Charity Gu refined to the next level.
However, even with that in mind, this was an awful deal. The more he thought about it, the more annoyed he got, because usually the highest-ranking gu worm a mortal would have would be their Vital Gu, and naturally, you cannot give your vital Gu away. And to swap it out from the position of it being your Vital Gu would cause backlash and also make it far more difficult to refine advanced versions of said Gu worm.
He quickly calmed his heart - perhaps in the future there would be a use for this. However, regardless, the tiny bit of information was still useful.
This showed that his plan had been successful at the very least however. Qing Shu had advanced to become an elder, and would be far more useful in the upcoming fight.
A crowd had already gathered around Qing Shu's house even as Fang Yuan made his way there later that afternoon. The crowd completely parted upon seeing him, many of them bowing deeply before him.
"Elder Qing Shu," Fang Yuan said.
"Elder Fang Yuan," Qing Shu said, standing near the entrance of the house. There were dark bags under his eyes, and he looked like he hadn't had enough to eat or drink in the past few hours. He had only recently come out of closed cultivation, after all.
Of course, the moment that he had advanced to elder, there were numerous people who had gathered around his house, asking for various kinds of favors. The fact that the wolf tide was increasing in intensity lately only made such a situation worse.
Fang Yuan had, of course, experienced something similar when he had advanced to Rank 3. In the case of Qing Shu, though, it was even worse simply because he had a reputation that spanned far longer than Fang Yuan's, and many people wished to see if he could solve some of their problems.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"Everyone!" Fang Yuan yelled out to them, using the kind of words which Qing Shu felt uneasy saying himself. "Elder Qing Shu is tired. Currently, he needs his rest before an important issue that he must attend to. All of you disperse!" At his words, the crowd thinned out until it was just the two of them.
"Qing Mao and Yao Hong were here," Qing Shu said. "To congratulate me. Though I don't think Qing Mao or Chi Shan will be happy to hear about this."
"It's good," Fang Yuan said. "Maybe knowing that you've gone to Rank 3 will spur them to work harder. Get your rest," he then added, his face a bit more serious than before. "We have a big day ahead of us tomorrow."
"You don't need to tell me twice," Qing Shu said. The advancement to Rank 3 must've left him feeling somewhat invigorated, but at the same time, exhausted as well. At the very least, he had not failed to break through to the next major realm. The worst feeling in the world- one that Fang Yuan himself had experienced in his prior life spanning 500 years was to put in all that effort to advance and then fail due to some reason or the other.
"But before that," Fang Yuan said. "Go and get a Rank 3 gu worm from the underground storage. Without one, your strength will be lacking. I'm sure that whatever Senior Brother picks, it will without a doubt be the right choice."
"Alright, and I haven't forgotten the fact that I owe you 3,000 primeval stones," Qing Shu said.
"No need to worry about that at all. You can even consider it payment for being such great help."
"Hah- as if I could do such a thing! I could only get this far thanks to the generosity of the clan head. How could I do such a thing without paying it forward? On that note, how is Fang Zheng lately?"
"He is doing as well as one can be during these dangerous times," Fang Yuan said. "Though, he won't be joining us in tomorrow's fight." Fang Yuan wasn't going to risk losing Rank 6 Beauty Gu like that.
"Ah, that is to be expected, I suppose. I can only hope that your plan is successful."
News of Qing Shu's advancement spread rapidly throughout the village with there being barely a soul who had not heard of it.
The elders, however, had something else on their minds. The fighting that was going to take place tomorrow- that is.

chapters.title: Chapter 144 - 144: Strike Force: Part Seven
chapters.content:
Gu Yue Mo Chen was once again practicing one of his paintings. While his paintings tended to be of scenic, sunny landscapes (he might even add in a rainbow from time to time depending on his mood), lately, the sky above whatever landscapes he etched out onto his easel tended to be cloudy, either a thunderstorm or a heavy burst of rain upon the grassland below.
His back was towards the door, and someone knocked, but then he immediately heard footsteps coming in. The fact that they had knocked first meant that this was not Mo Yan. The fact that they had stepped in after knocking, as if it was just a courtesy, meant that it was not one of the servants either.
"Mo Bei, how are things?" he asked without even turning his head.
"Things are well enough, my grandfather," Mo Bei said. "I just wanted to see how you were doing."
"Well, I'm fine, as always," he answered. "What could possibly go wrong with me? But I take it that's not the only reason that you came here."
"Yes, Grandfather, actually, I..." Mo Bei began. "I was wondering if I could accompany you on the mission tomorrow?"
"Denied," Mo Chen said without any hesitation. "You are the future of this family," he continued. "If I die tomorrow, so be it. But if we lose you, the hope for continuing our clan will be extinguished. And as it is, you are not yet ready. You've just broken through to Rank 2 Initial Stage, haven't you?"
"No, that's not true," Mo Bei retorted. "I just managed to get to Rank 2 Middle Stage."
Mo Chen nodded satisfactorily. While the looming wolf tide was a cause of huge concern to the village, it also meant that people were spurred on to work harder.
People oftentimes only show their true natures when put under duress, and while some people would break under pressure, others would begin to shine and show their true talents. He was happy to know that Mo Bei used this opportunity not to lock himself in his room and become depressed, but rather to better himself.ᴛhis ᴜpdated by NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
That was good- that was exactly what was expected of the heir to the Mo family name.
'Perhaps if I die tomorrow,' Mo Chen thought, 'I can very easily leave things to him.'
Mo Bei did not fully understand what the mission was, but there was no way that the village could hide the fact that several elders were heading out tomorrow from everyone. The fact that Fang Yuan himself was also leaving leaked through the grapevine to Mo Bei. In truth, it was Mo Yan who had told him this. She had also stipulated that he not tell anyone that she had told him that.
Still, he understood the kind of firepower such a force would be packing. He could only assume that they were out to hunt a Thunder Crown Wolf or another beast on its scale. Given the inherent danger involved, he also realized this was one of the last times he might even be able to see his grandfather.
And naturally, he did not want to lose out to Fang Yuan. Nor did he want to just stay on the sidelines. He wanted to contribute to the battle, no matter how little it was. Of course, thinking it through with a cool head, the fact remained that he could do very little to change the outcome of such a fight, and they did need to be someone to inherit the family name.
"Sister is also there to inherit the family name."
" a woman?" Mo Chen asked. "She would essentially have to sell herself to a suitable fiancé. She does not have your aptitude. She would not be able to reach Rank 3. No, you are far too precious for us to risk in the upcoming fight."
"Grandfather, I've been meaning to ask," Mo Bei said. "How did Fang Yuan manage to rise to Rank 4 so quickly? Even if he had A-grade aptitude, he wouldn't have been able to do so."
Mo Chen scratched his chin. 'Should he tell him the truth? Or should I deflect the question entirely?'
"The fact is that even I am not sure,' he answered his grandson. "However, the clan head has taken it in stride as if nothing, or rather, as if he was expecting such. Right now, at the height of the wolf tide, we cannot inquire into this too further, especially with the clan head already backing him. It's only when the wolf tide ceases that we'll be able to get some proper answers from Fang Yuan."
"So you don't know either?" Mo Bei asked, shocked.
"What, do you think I'm lying to you?" Mo Chen asked.
"No, no, I would never insinuate that," Mo Bei answered. "I just thought that there was a chance that, you know, you weren't telling anyone."
"The most obvious cause," Gu Yue Mo Chen said, "would be that he had somehow found some kind of inheritance or some other kind of fortuitous encounter, which allowed him to reach Rank 4 so quickly. However, were that the case, the clan head would have immediately demanded answers from him, instead of protecting him like he is now. There's something else going on, even if I cannot fully fathom what it is."
He stopped painting, turning towards his grandson. The painting depicted a typhoon over a stormy sea, with a ship upon the rocky waves that looked like it was in danger of capsizing.
"Regardless, once all of this is over, we will be able to inquire into this matter further. If it is indeed something, such as an inheritance, without a doubt, the Mo family will be able to ask for a stake in the same. When that happens, I will hand it over to you. However, even if I'm not still alive," he continued, "you must find your way to get your hands on it. It would have been better if you had been able to reach Rank 3 by now, but fate limits us."
"And don't worry, Grandfather," Mo Bei said. "I'll definitely work as hard as I can. If anything, I'll reach Fang Yuan's level, or even surpass him once we figure out what his secret is."
"Good, good," Mo Chen said. "On that note, although I've already told your sister of this, I think it is prudent that I tell you as well. In case something happens to me, I have reached an agreement with Gu Yue Yao Ji, the medicine hall elder. You should be able to rely upon her in the meanwhile while you get to Rank 3."
In times like this, it was important to know who they could trust once the chips fell.
Of course, the Mo faction had its own group of elders. But it spoke volumes to the fact that Mo Chen had decided to trust an outsider rather than them. The reason was simple: Mo Bei was still young and could easily be led astray by one of the others in his faction. They would have been happy to have a puppet that they could control easily heading their faction, even if it would sacrifice the Mo family's interests.
"I understand," Mo Bei said. Inwardly, he thought, 'Fang Yuan. I don't know what your secret is, but you better not mess up tomorrow. If I find out that my grandfather died because of your carelessness...' He clenched his fist. 'I'll make sure that you regret it!'

chapters.title: Chapter 145 - 145: Strike Force: Part Eight
chapters.content:
Meanwhile, in the Chi household...
"I'm afraid this is the maximum that I can do for now," Chi Lian said to Chi Chen. He had supplemented the latter's primal sea, ensuring that he could reach Rank 2. However, much like with Mo Chen, he was concerned as to what would happen tomorrow.
"So, Grandfather, you don't happen to know how it is that Fang Yuan reached Rank 4?" It was the talk of the town, naturally, with many people expecting an answer, like a grand inheritance. However, instead, the clan head had simply accepted this and went on as if there was nothing wrong with Fang Yuan becoming Rank 4, no doubt questions buzzing through everyone's minds. However, if the clan head accepted it, and if the Elders weren't doing anything about it, there was little that small fry like the rest of the Gu Masters could do about such.
"I don't know the secret," Chi Lian said.
"Regardless, I am heading out to battle tomorrow."
"Does it have to be you?" Chi Chen asked.
"If it's not me, then who else?" came the answer. "It has to be someone of Rank 3 or higher, and if Mo Chen himself is wandering off, what will people think of the Chi family if we stand on the sidelines like a massive amount of cowards?"
"Isn't it better to be seen as a coward and be alive rather than be seen as brave and die?" Chi Shen asked.Follow current novels on ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"That may be so," came the reply. "However, don't worry, your grandfather isn't that easy to kill! I have seen my fair share of battles. "
Inwardly, he thought, 'This blasted plan of Fang Yuan's. There are multiple ways that it could go wrong. However, with the clan head agreeing with him, with other elders backing him, there's little that I can do except ride the tide.' "The question now," he continued, "is what to do should I pass away... this little secret of what has happened between us cannot go beyond the two of us. I hope you understand.'
"I understand."
"Do you, Chi Chen? Not even Chi Shan could know?" Although Chi Chen would be relying upon the latter in the meanwhile, in case his grandfather died, he could not know about their subterfuge.
"Who knows where the chips will fall?" Chi Lian said. "However, remember to attempt to get a Cleansing Aperture Gu for yourself, even if you cannot continue to supplement your own primeval essence like we are doing now. And if discovered, do not hesitate at all to throw me under the bus. Say that I coerced you under the pain of death to go along with this plan. If you must throw my name into the mud in order to save yourself, do so." What did reputation matter from beyond the grave? If it would save his last living descendant, so be it.
"I hope that will not come to that," Chi Chen said, clenching his fist. He once again cursed fate. He had been given a C-grade aptitude, falling behind the others and being forced to resort to such trickery in order to keep up with them.
Although he had managed to keep such a thing hidden for some time, without his grandfather, there was no hope of this ruse continuing. He would literally be thrown to the winds in such a case. With that said, there was a small glimmer of hope.
He didn't know how it was that Fang Yuan had managed to reach Rank 4, but it was clear that he had some manner of external help. If he could get his hands upon such, he might be able to reach Rank 3 or even Rank 4 as well. 'Fang Yuan! What kind of secrets are you hiding?' Chi Chen thought.
Had not the four of them- Chi Chen, Mo Bei, and the Fang twins started the academy at the same time? Then how was Fang Yuan soaring so high out of their reach, to the point where he now even exceeded the strength of their grandparents and could stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the clan head himself?
'Did he find an aptitude-raising gu worm and get A-grade aptitude? Or is this the effect of multiple relic gu?'
There was little other than speculation that he could do in the moment, other than praying for his grandfather's safe return.
The dawn of the next day, Gu Yue Yao Ji had woken up early. "Grandmother, shouldn't you be resting a bit more?" Yao Le asked her.
"Not today," Yao Ji said. She was not going along with the others for this mission, but she knew that the likelihood of them being injured was very high today.
"We have to wait for and be prepared for what's coming."
Yao Le didn't fully understand what was going on. However, she understood from her grandmother's expression that there was a high likelihood that things would be going south.
"All right, thank grandmother. I'll have everything ready. Everyone will be alert and ready to respond to your command."
"That's my granddaughter," Yao Ji said.
As the strike force to deal with the Lightning Lycan King headed out; some of them were disguising themselves using Aura Restraint Gu. Fang Yuan himself had reduced his own cultivation to Rank 3 using the Training Weights Gu.
Their goal was to kill the Lightning Lycan King, after all, and for that they needed it to appear and not run away.
One thing surprised everyone who went on the mission along with Fang Yuan: that was the fact that he not only knew the rough location of where the Lightning Lycan King was, or at least claimed to, he also seemed to know all the gu worms that it had.
One of the biggest uncertainties in dealing with a wild beast king was the wild gu worms they could use. The fact that they knew for sure what this thing had made it somewhat easier to deal with in their mind. It was not out of the question for Fang Yuan to know this however, if he had truly fought with it like he had claimed to.
However, those Rank 4 Gu worms could only be countered by someone like Fang Yuan and not by them.
Their forces were arranged in such a way that it appeared multiple factions had been sent out to deal with various pockets of wolves. However, they were also clustered in a way that would be easier to coordinate and coalesce together to form one big whole. A large number of investigative Gu Masters were employed in this on the battlefield. They were skilled in all sorts of investigative measures. However, before the might of a Myriad Beast King, these measures might fail.
Fang Yuan was quite optimistic about this project succeeding. He was leading one of the groups, Mo Chen led another one, and Chi Lian led a third. The fourth was led by Gu Yue Han Lin.
"It will be an honor to fight with you today," he had told Fang Yuan before departing for his assigned position.
Both the leaders of the Mo and the Chi factions were quite warm towards Fang Yuan. They were not only relying upon him during this battle, but also hoping that he would show their families clemency once he had become clan head in case either passed away.
"Everyone! Thousand Beast King!" one of the scouts shouted, sounding the alarm.

chapters.title: Chapter 146 - 146: Strike Force: Part Nine
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan shifted through his memories. This was how it was said that the fighting had begun last time.
A Thousand Beast King had been spotted, and then a second one as well. When the elders went to go deal with it and were nearly about to kill it - that is when the Lightning Lycan King had revealed itself. Fang Yuan told them that this would likely be its plan. He only hoped that they would cooperate with each other and that his regression hadn't changed things to the point where something different would happen.
New main mission unlocked!
Five tigers one lamassu, three hounds one molossus, ten wolves one lycan!
Kill the Lightning Lycan King.
Reward: Yellow Golden Relic Gu (x1)
Fang Yuan narrowed his eyes. Last time, it had been a Rank 4 Stone Aperture Gu which he had gotten, and the system had also kept this reward hidden until he had completed it.
The system did not seem to think that the Rank 4 Stone Aperture Gu was necessary this time around.
If everything worked out like last time, he would be able to save Qing Shu and Yao Le as well, meaning that he could boost himself to Rank 4 peak stage.
Even the clan head was Rank 4 middle stage, having not been able to progress much since becoming Clan Head. That was the issue. When one became the leader of an organization, one which Fang Yuan knew all too well, he was sure that the clan head could have been Rank 4 Upper Stage at least by this point, if he had only focused on his cultivation rather than on clan affairs.
At Rank 4 Peak Stage, he would've had to seriously worry about the clan heads of all three clans moving against him... were it not for the prophecy of the Ancient Moon Desolate Yin Physique.
Now, with that foreknowledge, he could move freely.
"I'll go deal with one of them," Fang Yuan said. He motioned to Qing Shu, who nodded to lead the team against the other one.
The Frenzy Lightning Wolves were nearly as large as elephants, though it was still difficult to maneuver close to them with so many of their lackeys guarding them. The Bold Lightning Wolves could be dealt with by someone like Fang Yuan in a single blow, but the Frenzy Lightning Wolves usually needed two or three elders to deal with them safely.
There were exceptions to this of course- fighters like Fang Yuan (with his true Rank 4 essence and battle experience) and Qing Shu could deal with them confidently on their own.
That wasn't to say that the other elders did nothing.
"Don't let them escape!" Mo Chen said, when he noticed several lightning wolves trying to regroup and ambush another team from behind.
"I will take care of it," Chi Lian communicated to him.
They might have been rivals, but out here, on the battlefield, they moved in near-perfect synchrony. Each of them knew each other's moves quite well, which is how such synergy could be achieved.
Fang Yuan approached one of the Frenzy Lightning Wolves. It snarled at him, unleashing a bolt of lightning as a tiny speck leaped out from its back. Fang Yuan deftly avoided it before unleashing the power of the Rank 4 Vermillion Blood Moon Gu.
At this distance, the Rank 4 aura could not leak too far, though its effect was immediate upon the Frenzy Lightning Wolf which began hemorrhaging profusely. It soon realized that its days were numbered if it continued to fight.
Howl!
It called for the lower-ranking members of it species to hold the line while it attempted to retreat. A tidal waves of wolves appeared at the beckoning of its call, though it was of little use as the Frenzy Lightning Wolf found its pathway blocked.
"This is...!" someone shouted out.
"A group of deer?"
Not just any group of deer, there was one at its forefront which radiated a dense Rank 3 aura, rivaling that of the Frenzy Lightning Wolf.
Karmic flag has been triggered!
The Crimsonhoof Deer has answered your call!
Fang Yuan only needed it to buy some time as he unleashed moonblade after moonblade upon the wolves. Where the moonblades were unnecessary, his fists easily crushed their skulls and made indentations in their chests- throwing them around as if they weighed nothing more than pillows before his increased strength.
Fang Yuan had exchanged the Rank 3 Stone Aperture Gu that he had obtained from Bai Ning Bing for a Rank 3 Beast Mutation Gu from the Bai clan. He had wanted to obtain this during his past life but lacked the necessary resources to trade for such at the time and felt that he had other priorities- but in this timeline, he knew its value.
Rank 3 Beast Mutation Gu, much like its name stated, could drastically increase the growth rate of a beast, whether deer, wolf, bear, tiger, or anything else. It had a drawback- namely that if used, the beast in question would be weaker than it ordinarily would have been.
But that was fine with Fang Yuan- he only needed it to stall the Frenzy Lightning Wolf for a while.
On the other side of the battlefield, Qing Shu had bound the wolf he was fighting in vines, making escape impossible as the elders bombarded it with Rank 3 gu worms.
Gu Yue Han Lin was surprisingly useful here, despite his age he weaved and slashed without restraint, taking the lives of countless wolves and ultimately dealing the fatal blow against the Frenzy Lightning Wolf.
As for Fang Yuan, he quickly caught up to the one he was chasing. Seeing that it had only two ways of escaped, it chose to turn around and lash out at Fang Yuan, sending crimson droplets pouring all around itself as if it were raining blood upon the battlefield.
It shot out another bolt of lightning- though Fang Yuan simply took this head on with the help of Moonlight Plate Armor Gu before decapitating the Frenzy Lightning Wolf and going to examine the Crimsonhoof Deer.
It had been lightly wounded, though that was nothing that Fang Yuan couldn't fix. Even as he healed its injuries, he was actually using this opportunity to surreptitiously check on what gu worms it had.
'No Rank 3 gu even now,' he noticed bitterly. Ah well, it was thanks to the Beast Mutation Gu that it had even managed to reach the equivalent of Rank 3 in such a period of time. It would still take time before Rank 3 and then later on Rank 4 Blood Path gu worms would be attracted to it for Fang Yuan to harvest.
Fang Yuan had a plan that involved getting as many high-ranking Blood Path gu worms as possible- he was not sure how many the clan had, and so he had been hoping for something to come out of this, but not everything could go the way you wanted in this life. That was something he had learned long ago.
