This painting had indeed not been intended for Fang Yuan, but had been intended for Bai Ning Bing all along!

chapters.title: Chapter 158 - 158: Dollhouse: Part Six
chapters.content:
Bai Ning Bing was in a state of shock as she was dragged inside the Gu House. Although Fang Yuan had managed to save her life, he had not resurrected her gu worms. Her aptitude had fallen to ninety percent now, and it seemed that the Northern Dark Ice Soul physique had indeed been suppressed for the time being.
However, she noticed a problem immediately as she examined herself further: "she" had been a "he" just moments before.
Before she could dwell on this point any longer, a doll in the room she was in jumped up and walked over towards her. The doll had massive eyes and curly brown hair and was wearing a pink bow along with a blue dress. Its head was far larger than the rest of its proportions should have allowed for.
While it was clearly a well-made doll, it seemed slightly unsettling with an uncanny valley kind of effect as it moved around and talked.
Bai Ning Bing put up her hands defensively, but it did not attack her.
Instead, it hopped all around her excitedly. "Fairy! Fairy!" the doll yelled. "You look so pretty, fairy! Without a doubt, you'll be a great inheritor for this Gu House!"
Bai Ning Bing narrowed her eyes. "What's going on? Inheritor?"
"Why, yes, indeed," the doll said. "Fairy, this place was created by my master."
"Only an Immortal could have created this kind of place," Bai Ning Bing mused, sensing the aura of over a thousand gu worms all around her.
"That is correct, fairy," the doll answered. "This place was created by my master, who was a Rank 8 Gu Immortal in the Western Desert. I am this Gu House's guardian spirit."
Bai Ning Bing tapped the doll on its forehead. "You're not just a spirit, though."
"Indeed, fairy, I'm one of the puppets that my master used which has a portion of his intent sealed within, the spirit of this Gu House," the doll answered. "My master was rather skilled when it came to the puppet path. However, he ended up failing his second Myriad Tribulation and passed away. However, he wanted to leave this house to an inheritor. There's even more to inherit other than just this house, fairy, so long as you meet his other requirements."
'Meet his requirements...' Bai Ning Bing thought to herself. "What requirements did I meet right now? As in, why are you giving me this Gu House? Or do I need to do something else to prove I'm worthy of it?"
"Oh, the requirements to inherit this Gu House are simple," the doll answered. "You see, my master was quite heroic when he had been alive. He fought many battles for his clan and led his clan to prosperity. He was a loving husband and caring father. However, even though he was thought of as extremely brave, he always felt like he was a great coward inwardly."
"He felt like he was a coward?"
"Because he could not reveal to the world who he truly was... or that is, who he truly wanted to be. My master wanted to become a woman," the doll answered.
Bai Ning Bing blinked.
"However, even though he always felt like a woman despite being born as a man, he had never had the courage to live as his true self while he was still alive. And therefore, he wanted to entrust this Gu House to someone who could and had the bravery to do what he could not do. In other words, fairy, this Gu House can only be inherited by a man who is currently in a woman's body, such as you."
Bai Ning Bing: ...
"Fairy, I knew that the person who would inherit this Gu House would be a woman," the doll continued. "However, I never imagined she would be as beautiful as you. Without a doubt, you could easily be ranked as one of the top beauties in the entire world! We have many clothes which I think would greatly suit you, fairy. And if you have any other people who also want to join us after seeing your example, then that's even better. As my master said, in the future, we, the Dollhouse Sect, will rule over the five regions and two heavens!"
By this point, Bai Ning Bing had heard enough and kicked the doll across the room where it hit its head against the wall. "Stop calling me fairy! And shut up with your nonsense! I didn't choose to become like this!"
Bai Ning Bing had no idea if the doll could feel pain, but small teardrops formed around its eyes as it got up. "Fairy, why did you hit me? I didn't say anything mean to you, after all..."
"And you're going to obey my orders, right?" Bai Ning Bing asked.
"Yes, fairy."
"First of all, stop calling me fairy," Bai Ning Bing said. "Second of all, turn me back into a man."
"Oh, I can't do that," the doll said.
"What do you mean, you can't do that?"
"You were turned into a woman by Yin-Yang Rotation Gu, it appears. That means you need the Yang portion of the Yin-Yang Rotation Gu to turn back into a man," the doll answered. "It's only that specific Yang Gu which can turn you back into a male. Another Yin-Yang Rotation Gu won't work either. But fai- Senior Sister, if you want my advice I think you should remain as a woman."
Bai Ning Bing gritted her teeth. "Outside, there are two people, Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng. Bring them inside." Fang Yuan was the one who had started this, and he was likely the only one who could fix it as well.
The doll obliged, and Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng were both transported inside the Gu House.
"So this is what Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable wanted me to pass on to someone else," Fang Yuan mused as he arrived inside. Although it was still just a mortal Gu House, one could not even mention his Blood Chariot Wheel and this Gu House in the same sentence together. This house was incredible- being skillfully made form thousands of mortal gu worms. By comparison, his creation seemed like a crude stack of rocks before an enormous and extravagant palace.
Clearly, this Gu House had not been made in a rush with limited resources. It had been designed by a Gu Immortal who did not lack mortal gu after much thought and experimentation.
Even if Fang Yuan had been a Rank 6 Immortal, he still could've found a use for such a structure depending on what it could do, though he would've quickly outgrown it the moment he reached Rank 7.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"Senior brothers, senior brothers," the doll said, hopping around Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng. "Have you considered becoming senior sisters instead?"

chapters.title: Chapter 159 - 159: Dollhouse: Part Seven
chapters.content:
"What's going on?" Fang Yuan asked, and Bai Ning Bing quickly explained the situation to him before he began laughing loudly.
Fang Zheng backed away from the doll. "Why would I want to degrade myself by becoming the less useful gender?"
"Oh, but senior brother," the doll said, approaching Fang Zheng, "I think you would look extremely good in a dress."
Fang Zheng kicked the doll, sending it flying to the other side of the room where it hit its head again.
"Quick, Fang Yuan, give me the Yang Rotation Gu!" Bai Ning Bing said.
Fang Yuan glared at him devilishly. "Why, certainly, Bai Ning Bing, but there are certain things we need to take care of beforehand. We still have a very angry Rank 5 Gu Master hovering above us, and no way to deal with him."
"What do you mean? We have this Gu House," Bai Ning Bing said.
The doll got up slowly, nursing its head.
"You may have a Gu House," Fang Yuan said. "But do you have the essence needed to use any of its Gu worms?"
'Primeval Essence...' Bai Ning Bing thought to herself. With just a little bit of Rank 3 Peak primeval essence he could not even power up a corner of the Gu House. "Isn't there any primeval essence lying around? How are we supposed to make this work?"ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
The doll shook her head. "My apologies, fai- senior sister, but my master thought that the one who discovered this Gu House and the inheritance would be an immortal, and so he had not planned for anything like this."
'That person must have had a connection to Genesis Lotus somehow. Either that, or Genesis Lotus found this inheritance and kept it, thinking that it would be useful in the future,' Fang Yuan thought to himself.
"Bai Ning Bing, quickly hand over control of this Gu House to me. I have a way that we can use it."
Bai Ning Bing turned toward him, frowning. "It only needs to be temporary," Fang Yuan added.
"All right, then," Bai Ning Bing said. "House spirit, this person is now in control of the house for a while."
"Alright, then, fairy," the doll said, before being kicked by Bai Ning Bing again.
"How many times have I told you not to call me fairy?!"
Fang Yuan smiled inwardly.
As he released his will and the drop of Grape Green Immortal Essence from his inventory, his will condensed and took the form of another Fang Yuan making it seem like the Fang brothers were triplets instead of twins.
It was holding a bead of immortal essence as it flew towards one of the walls.
In an instant, as the new owner, Fang Yuan refined all of the Gu worms within the house and obtained complete control over it. Even though the requirements to inherit the place were that the inheritor had to be a woman who used to be a man, once that requirement was met, that person could transfer the inheritance to anyone they wanted.
In that way, the House Spirit seemed to be like a Land Spirit: quite easy to fool and quite straightforward.
The Grape Green Immortal Essence filled the Gu House as it now began to rise into the air. Outside, Lord Sky Crane's pupils shrunk.
Two doors on the side of the Gu House opened up while it flew, and numerous small figurines flew out. Many of them looked like porcelain dolls, but others looked like tiny soldiers, some looked like cooks or butlers, etc.
However, there was one thing in common with all of them: they were all puppets. And they were all rapidly rushing towards him.
"This is... the Puppet Path!" Lord Sky Crane muttered. Even in all his years, he had barely heard mention of it.
It was an obscure path that was a branch of the Human Path which in and of itself was a rather underdeveloped path.
As the Human Path contained the profundities of all paths, the puppet path was a sub-branch of it which combined the essences of the Enslavement Path along with the Human Path.
Man is the spirit of all things, and men were not easy to enslave. Enslavement Gu itself was a Rank 5 Gu worm, after all.
However, by combining the Enslavement Path and the Human Path, or at least in an attempt to do so, it was rumored that the Puppet Path had been created.
But that was all that Lord Sky Crane knew about this path. It was so esoteric that he had never seen it with his own eyes before, nor did he think that anyone in the Immortal Crane Sect had either.
These puppets were all Rank 4 or Rank 5 gu worms. None of them were immortal, but their coordination was excellent. They began downing his cranes left and right, and he only had a small amount of primeval essence left. Gritting his teeth, he knew he had to cut his losses as he flew away.
"Should we chase them?" the doll asked Fang Yuan.
"No," Fang Yuan said. There was no guarantee that he would be able to kill Lord Sky Crane, even if he rushed out with this Gu House. Although it was powerful, it was only a mortal Gu house and still had the deficiencies of a Gu House, namely, that its moves were somewhat limited, and once they were found out, one could start to avoid them. He also was not experienced with using it either- much of its motion as it moved through the air was erratic as he tried to get a handle on it. It would take him several hours to be able to operate it properly.
As it was, there were other things he needed to do right now on the mountain, especially given that so many of the Gu Yue clansmen were buried under the ice.
Main mission complete!
Stupid birds!
Reward: Aptitude increased by 4%.
"House spirit," Fang Yuan said to the doll. Unlike the others, he was easily able to accept its existence- Blessed Lands had Land Spirits, and formations could have Formation Spirits. The creator of this house had managed to make a House Spirit- so what? It could be dealt with in the same way that he would deal with any Land Spirit. Bai Ning Bing was unaware of this and so still treated it with some suspicion, but Fang Yuan knew of its straightforward nature. When it came to such things, usually, 'yes means yes and no means no.' It had also likely inherited an obsession from its creator, which is why it behaved the way it did and there was little use attacking it to get it to change. It was here that his experience as an Immortal was paying dividends as he knew how to optimally utilize the Gu House and the House Spirit. "Is there a way to get rid of the ice covering the mountain?"
"Indeed Senior Brother - there is the killer move 'Man's Triumph Over Nature' that can deal with the environment and weather as well," the doll answered.
"Activate it for me."
Mortal Killer Move - Man's Triumph Over Nature!
The ice began to thaw out rapidly in a massive area around the peak of Qing Mao Mountain. The base was still somewhat encased in ice, signifying the limited range of this skill - but given how thick the layer of ice at the top near where Bai Ning Bing had detonated had been, and how it would've likely remained unthawed for several weeks if not months even under the assault of the summer sun, this was no small feat.
Next, Fang Yuan used Doctor Gu in conjunction with Charity Gu to heal the injuries of those down below, prioritizing those of the Gu Yue clansmen.
"The ambition which blooms in spring withers in winter,
Whether winter comes from within or without,
The flame of humanity continues to smolder,
Until fanned by ambition into a raging inferno,
Burning as bright as the midsummer sun,
Thawing through even the coldest of embraces-
-death."
The doll clapped. "Senior Brother, that was wonderful! If you were a fairy, you'd be renowned as one of the greatest wordsmiths in the Five Regions!" Once again, it was letting its obsession show.
Speaking of, that seemed to snap Bai Ning Bing back to reality.
"Fang Yuan!" Bai Ning Bing snorted. "Hand me the Yang Rotation Gu!"
"Sure, sure," Fang Yuan said. "I just need you to do a few things for me first," he said, grinning wickedly. "I need your help rebuilding my clan, after all."
"Why you-"
Even if Bai Ning Bing attempted to turn the house against Fang Yuan it was useless. By this point, he controlled the entire mortal Gu House as his will had overwritten every single one of the gu worms.
The doll, while it seemed to know much about the house, had also realized that it had lost control over the gu worms there. Fang Yuan smirked to himself. 'Genesis Lotus, you said this was destined for someone else? No, I think I'll be keeping this Gu House to myself, thank you very much.'
His will joined up with him, injecting some information into his brain before leaving to continue controlling the Gu House. There were several Information Path gu worms in the house itself that revealed its secrets, though these were probably only for the rightful inheritor. For one, this was only a part of the inheritance that its creator had set up.
This Gu House in and of itself was actually a downgraded version of what used to be a more sophisticated Gu House that had several Rank 6 Immortal Gu worms in it, though they had been removed at one point. Still, Fang Yuan now knew of the places where they were supposed to be put if he could find them in case he wanted to recreate the Rank 6 Gu House. Not only that, but most of the mortal gu which were already here were Human Path gu worms and there were several that he could remove for his own usage without significantly compromising the strength of the Gu House.
Fang Yuan even found a blueprint for a Rank 7 version of this Gu House, though it had never been completed as the creator had been unable to find the proper Rank 7 gu worms. There was a blueprint for a Rank 8 version of this Gu House as well, but that was only 50% complete.
Still, that meant that there were several Immortal Gu that were out there, somewhere in the world, waiting for him to claim them! He just needed to follow the clues that were left in this Gu House.
There was also the matter of the creator's Grotto-Heaven in question, which was also somewhere out there, the clues hidden within the walls of this Gu House.
Fang Yuan laughed before stepping out of the Gu House, noting the villagers around him coming to and wondering just what it was that was going on.
There was quite a lot of work to be done.

chapters.title: Chapter 160 - 160: Volume One Epilogue
chapters.content:
It is said that there are no lessons in victory, but there are a thousand lessons in defeat. As Lord Sky Crane made his way back towards the Central Continent, he couldn't help but ruminate over these words.
He thought dejectedly about the kind of lesson he had just learned - or might have been supposed to learn anyway. What was there to learn from his recent encounter? That you should always be prepared for your enemy to pull a Gu House out of what appeared to be their lower digestive tract just when you were about to win? What kind of a lesson was that?!
Even his joy at finally subduing his old rival was muted by the fact that the job was left unfinished. That was a massive stain on his honor, as well as the honor of the Immortal Crane Sect. The former was somewhat acceptable to him, but the latter was not.
The crane he was riding upon let out a weak cry. Its beak had been badly damaged when it struck it against that Immortal House. Out of the ten thousand cranes that he had brought to the Southern Border, less than a thousand remained. Most of them were ordinary cranes, with very few Beast Kings among them.
Still, it could not be said that his journey had been entirely unfruitful. After all, he now knew of the existence of a very complex mortal Gu House. Even if he lacked the strength to take it, that didn't mean that the Immortal Crane Sect lacked the required strength. He could get a lot of contribution points for donating it to the sect.
Even if that Gu House was strong, before the might of an actual Gu Immortal, it was nothing. A mortal could never hope to compare to an immortal, even if they had a Gu House like that. However, without a doubt one would be able to dominate the mortal realm with its aid. Depending on its power, even a Rank 6 Immortal might find such a thing helpful.
The Gu Yue Clan was now like a beggar who had found a diamond necklace. They were committing a crime just by possessing it. It was only for the best that the Immortal Crane Sect take it from them before someone else did.
Lord Sky Crane had also gained something else.
He took a gu from his aperture to admire it; one that looked like a skull carved out of a giant ruby: the Blood Skull Gu! He had managed to snatch it from first gen Gu Yue completely intact during their fighting.
As for the other gu worms, first gen Gu Yue had detonated them with his final breath when he realized that all was lost. Lord Sky Crane had used a special method on the Blood Skull Gu to ensure that it didn't meet with the same fate.
The gu worm that he had found among the Blood Sea Ancestor's Inheritance and had always been rightfully his; that had been stolen from him by the man who called himself Gu Yue and had once been his senior brother - it was finally back where it truly belonged, in his hands!
There's a reason that betrayal hurt the most; it came from those who you knew and trusted. Even now, after a thousand years, it felt as if the wound had been made just yesterday in Lord Sky Crane's heart.
But never mind that now.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs
Even if it had taken a thousand years, he had finally retrieved his property. The Blood Skull Gu, although mortal, was extremely valuable. It could cause a commotion in any of the Five Regions for how it could be used to raise the aptitude of mortals. Immortals had their descendants and mortals whom they needed to raise, after all.
A force like the Immortal Crane Sect would find less use for it given the lack of tight blood relations between most members, but that didn't meant that they couldn't make use of it in some way or the other.
He had no doubt that this in itself could gain him quite the amount of contribution points from the sect. The sect might even be able to find a way to prolong his life even further in recognition of what he had done.
His cranes had to rest after the battle, and so they stopped by a nearby stream. With his Rank 5 strength, Lord Sky Crane did not need to fear wandering anywhere in all the five regions. However, his flock had just fought a difficult battle and was quite exhausted himself.
The journey back home was extremely long given the distances needing to be covered, as well as the fact that he needed to find food for his entire flock whenever they landed.
Another third of his flock either died out or were culled simply because they had been too injured to keep up with the rest, or because they had fallen prey to all sorts of animals which Lord Sky Crane couldn't deal with in time as these threats gnawed away at the fringes of his flock.
They eventually reached the Miasma Regional Wall that separated the Southern Border from the Central Continent. As they crossed through the barrier with relative ease, being mortals, Lord Sky Crane felt his cultivation fluctuate as he had already somewhat adapted to the Southern Border, and now this adaptation was going in the opposite direction.
He was still far stronger here than in the Southern Border, however.
As he was about to send out a missive to the Immortal Crane Sect, he immediately felt a sudden sense of danger as the hairs on the back of his neck stood up.
An impossibly strong aura burst out from the clouds as the Gu Immortal in question revealed himself. Lord Sky Crane did not recognize the man, given he was wearing a mask and did not wear anything that would betray himself as belonging to any organization in the Central Continent. A demonic or lone cultivator? Or a righteous path cultivator pretending to be acting on his lonesome? Immortals rarely bothered with mortals, but there was no mistaking the killing intent that this person was radiating.
Lord Sky Crane knew that he had no real chance of fighting or fleeing against such an enemy. "Sir, whoever you are, I can assure you that the Immortal Crane Sect will give you adequate compensation in exchange for my life if-"
"There are two things I want," the Immortal said, interrupting him. "The first is the Blood Skull Gu you're carrying. The second would be your life. Neither are negotiable."
Several days later, the Immortal Crane Sect would find Lord Sky Crane's corpse atop one of the nearby mountains. His soul had been extracted from his body, and the only clues they could find regarding what had caused his death was that a Blood Path attack had likely been responsible for dealing the finishing blow. It was a bit hard to tell given that bits and pieces of him had already been devoured by some of his cranes.

chapters.title: Chapter 161 - 161: Make Gu Yue Village Great Again: Part One
chapters.content:
In the Southern Border, atop Qing Mao mountain, there was a man who exited a scaled-up version of dollhouse. This man had long black hair and had a gentle expression, despite this his pitch-black eyes betrayed him for what he was: a demon. This was Gu Yue Fang Yuan, who had used the Spring Autumn Cicada to go back in time 500 years ago - and this is Fang Yuan's, a regressor's, tale of cultivation.
The soft soil crackled like rocks under Fang Yuan's footsteps. Although the ice had melted, bits and pieces of it were still lying around and most of what had been in contact with the sheet of ice still retained its coolness. The bright sun overhead would need to work overtime to get things back to a normal temperature.
In this case 'things' included people as well. Most of them were shivering with very little idea of what was going on. Some of them still had frost covering them in certain areas, and many of them were discovering the fact that while they had lived; their gu worms, sadly, had perished away with the cold. Human Path methods could do nothing for such.
Many people stumbled around like zombies, calling out for the names of their loved ones or trying to find them. Others were looking for shelter, still glancing at the sky as if thinking it would fall down on their heads and crush them.
Given the scale of damage done to the buildings, such a scene could've been taken right out of a war photograph after a town had been ravaged back on Earth, Fang Yuan thought to himself.
The door to the dollhouse opened and another person stepped out who looked identical to Fang Yuan, but had only Rank 2 cultivation and a much softer gaze. This was Fang Zheng.
"Let's gather everyone up," Fang Yuan said.
People began gathering all around Fang Yuan once he had used a gu worm to tell everyone in the village that it was safe to come out. "Relax, our ancestor is dead, and that demonic flying Gu Master from the Central Continent has fled."
"So you mean that he isn't dead?" several of them asked, immediately looking towards the sky, as if expecting another flock of cranes to arrive.
"Don't worry, don't worry, he was heavily wounded and is unlikely to come back," Fang Yuan said. "Additionally, I have a way of dealing with him even if he does. Regardless, we can't continue to keep hiding like scared little turtles, now then can we?"
"Where did all of this ice come from?"
"It was another attack from the demonic gu master," Fang Yuan said, not mentioning the Northern Dark Ice Soul Physique.
To say that casualties were high was an understatement. In Fang Yuan's first life, fewer people had died when the wolf tide had struck the village. Human Path methods, despite how good they were at healing, were still limited in their capacity to bring people back from the dead particularly when a long enough time interval had passed.
About 4,000 people in total had survived the events of the day. Gu Yue Bo, their former clan leader, had perished at the hands of Lord Sky Crane, being especially targeted for his high cultivation. Qing Shu was still alive as was Han Lin, along with four other elders; but there was no word of the others. In other words, more than half of the clan's elders were dead.
Gu Yue Yao Ji had technically survived, but the cold and her age had damaged her aperture to the point that she was now Rank 2 Peak Stage, and could no longer be counted upon as an elder.
Speaking of, most of the elders could not fight or function properly because they had lost some of their key gu worms.
In such a scenario, they could only turn towards Fang Yuan to lead the village and rely upon his strength.
Most of the survivors had been either the very old or the very young, simply by the nature of those near the top of the mountain being the last to be targeted. These people could not fight either, and those who could were mainly logistics Gu Masters who were only Rank 1 and occasionally Rank 2.
Needless to say their combat strength had dropped a great deal. While their population was less than one-fifth of what it had been before, their offensive power was less than one-fiftieth of what it had been before.
Other than the Gu Yue clansmen, about 1,000 mortals had also survived. To Fang Zheng's great delight Shen Cui was not among them. For that matter, the Fang twins agreed that there was no need to look too hard or try too much in order to save their aunt and uncle.
Fang Yuan had his own plans for them, but that was only after he took full stock of the situation at hand.
Since he was relatively confident in his ability to deal with any threat that might appear, the next aspect to deal with was food.
The frostiness had damaged some of the stored food, and taken the moisture from some of it- while it would no doubt taste bad, it would do for the upcoming months.
The nearby farms, however, had been completely decimated as specks of ice were still embedded in the soil. The fish in the streams were nearly all gone, and the soil would not be ready to be tilled for another year even if they could find enough hands to work them.
The primeval spring itself had been damaged, though hopefully it could recover. Many of the gu worms within the clan's storage had also perished, and of those which had survived, there simply wasn't enough food to feed them. Several of them would have to be culled simply for the clan to survive and feed the more important gu worms.
The biggest casualty of this would no doubt be the clan's signature Moonlight Gu - many of the Moon Orchids were already withering away as the intense frost had permeated deep underground. Neither Fang Yuan nor the Dollhouse had any Wood Path methods to counter this. While there would always be enough for them to plant another stock, it could take months for the supply to reach the point where it would be enough to feed their gu worms given the high demand for the same. Almost all Gu Yue clansmen who fought relied upon the Moonlight Gu or one of its more advanced variants, after all, which also required Moon Orchid Petals to feed.
Fang Yuan had the survivors gather near the clan leader's pavilion in the afternoon. They had sent runners to the Bai and Xiong villages - which had fared far worse than the Gu Yue clan as they had been the first to be attacked by Lord Sky Crane. They each only had about 1,000 survivors.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"Good evening, fellow clansmen," Fang Yuan began. All eyes were on him- he was one of the few Gu Masters with a complete set of gu worms who could actually fight, and he had Rank 4 Peak Stage cultivation to boot. Naturally they were all drawn to him in this time of crisis like moths to a flame. "Today was a dark day- the darkest in perhaps all of our clan's long history. A demonic Gu Master descended from the heavens to kill us, and our ancestor, rather than being our saving grace ended up adding to our misery. However, the important thing is not what has happened up until this point, but rather what the future holds. The important thing is that we survived, and so long as we survived, we can continue. Where there is life, there is always hope. It is time for us to rebuild. To my Gu Yue clansmen, you must not look at this as the end. The foundation of our village still stands - many of the buildings are even intact and there are those which only need to be repaired to a slight degree. We can still rebuild. I promise you that this is merely the start of a bright, new, radiant dawn. We, together, will make Gu Yue Village great again!"
There were cheers at his proclamation before they died down.

chapters.title: Chapter 162 - 162: Make Gu Yue Village Great Again: Part Two
chapters.content:
"For this, we will be needing to make certain changes in the way that we operate," Fang Yuan continued. "Some of these may be... unorthodox, but a wise man submits to circumstances. First, our food supply needs to be secured. We will be fine until next spring, but if we don't plan the appropriate seeds now they will not be ready to be harvested by then. Secondly, in order to bolster our numbers, we will allow the surviving mortals to awaken their apertures."
There was dead silence at this proclamation. Those who were not of Gu Yue lineage may have had the aptitude to cultivate, but they could not go down to the primeval spring to attempt to open their aperture. The reason for this was simple clan cohesion- blood was thicker than water of course, and even if in some cases some mortals were allowed to visit the primeval spring if they married into the clan or as a reward this was done quite rarely.
The mortals were quite excited at this announcement of course, but it was the Gu Yue clansmen who spoke up first.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
"Clan leader, please reconsider!"
"Those who do not share our bloodline cannot be trusted with that kind of power!"
Many of the elders were also in disagreement.
It wasn't that Fang Yuan was unaware of these issues- it was just that he had far different priorities than the other Gu Yue clansmen. He wanted as many Gu Yue clansmen as possible to continue harvesting Human Path dao marks. While there were enough right now, in the coming months, some of them would not survive.
Furthermore, he was an individual confident in his own strength. Rebellion? Perhaps that might be an issue - the Gu Masters had suppressed the mortals for a long time and many of them carried bitter memories after all. However, before Rank 4 strength they could do little even if they wanted to cause turmoil.
Not only that, but Fang Yuan was accustomed to such a kind of structure being the leader of a sect in his past life. Out of the mortals, only about thirty or forty percent would have any talent based on his estimations, and the majority of them would be good only as foot soldiers being D or C grade talents. With that said, the clan needed all the manpower that it could get at this point.
These new Gu Masters would immediately be elevated in status compared to the other mortals. In time, they would see themselves not as former mortals, but as new Gu Yue clansmen. They would then suppress the other mortals as well.
"Naturally though, this will not come without stipulations," Fang Yuan said. "Any mortal woman who wishes to start cultivating will have to either marry or become the concubine of a Gu Yue clansmen and bear at least two children before she can have access to Rank 2 gu worms if she manages to awaken her aperture. Any mortal man who wishes to cultivate will have to adopt one of the orphans and raise them as their own for five years before they can access Rank 2 gu worms."
There were a number of orphans from this incident. Families had been torn apart, with many new widows and widowers. Some of the orphans had already been taken in by families who had lost their own children, but there were quite a few left.
Many of the mortal men's faces twitched. Fang Yuan was asking them to raise other people's children as their own, though many still felt that this kind of a deal was worth it even if they were going to be worked to the bone as Rank 1 Gu Masters.
"I think those restrictions are fair," Fang Yuan said. "Additionally, I think that we should also allow any willing Bai or Xiong clansmen to become Gu Yue clansmen."
There was a much bigger uproar at this suggestion. Fang Yuan raised his hand and there was immediate silence.
"I know that there is quite a bit of bad blood between the three clans," Fang Yuan said. "However, we must also look at our own situation. We are too few in number to populate without there being a large amount of inbreeding and will need outside blood to make sure that we can continue to flourish." Inbreeding was quite common in the gu world - the Mo clan's long horse like faces were the result of several generations of the same. While many people in this world wouldn't bat an eye at such a thing, Fang Yuan knew the dangers of inbreeding from his time on Earth. Also, these new Bai and Xiong clansmen could bolster their manpower.
"Will they even want to join us?" Qing Shu asked a rather pertinent question.
"They might not want to," Fang Yuan said. "As it is of course, I will demand several things if they wish to assimilate into our clan. The Xiong clan's Bear Strength Gu is rather useful given it does not need primeval essence to be used. The Bai clan's Stream Gu is useful in raising fish and can help with our food situation." These were those clan's trump cards, so naturally they would not be easy to snatch. "However, do remember that both of these clans have lost their leaders. They don't have a Rank 4 Gu Master like myself to serve as the pillar of the clan. In the coming months, they will realize the difficulties of life in such a scenario and likely see reason and agree to come under our yoke." It was technically still possible for the Bai and Xiong clans to rebuild with only around a thousand members - for that matter most of the clans were founded by a single strong individual who had taken multitudes of wives and concubines such as first gen Gu Yue. The only issue was that they would need this strong individual to appear before the wolves could recover.
Say, if another Thunder Crown Wolf appeared in the coming decade, wouldn't they be little more than meat on the chopping block without someone like Fang Yuan to protect them? Not only that, but there were other dangers like wild gu worms and the weather that the clans had to deal with. Even if they had someone with A-grade potential that genius would need to be reared and nurtured for several years before they could see the fruit of their labor. Otherwise they would end up like Fang Zheng, crippled because of an accident, or killed before their prime.
"In the meanwhile, I do have a temporary solution to our manpower issues," Fang Yuan continued.
From behind him, several puppets walked out. They were dressed in various uniforms - cooks, guards, soldiers, dancers, etc. but most of them could still function so long as they were given primeval essence. "Fortune and misfortune seem to come together. It turns out that our evil ancestor was hiding this right under our noses- he had obtained an inheritance in the Puppet Path. We have professions like soldiers and farmers covered for the time being." There were also some Human Path gu worms related to professions like Soldier Gu and the like within the Dollhouse which Fang Yuan was using, and he showed these to those gathered below as well.
Someone in the crowd asked: "Is there also a Prostitute Gu? Asking for a friend."
"Can someone slap whoever asked that for me? I can't reach them from here," Fang Yuan said.
SLAP!
A loud and crisp noise cut through the evening ambience.
"Good work Fang Zheng," Fang Yuan said. "Now, like I said, these will assist us in rebuilding the village. Starting with rebuilding our wall- we need it to keep undesirables outside like bears and wolves." It had been damaged in the prior fight, though the basic framework still stood there were numerous holes in it. It was the most basic defensive asset the village had and needed to be a priority when it came to thinking of things to repair.

chapters.title: Chapter 163 - 163: Make Gu Yue Village Great Again: Part Three
chapters.content:
What Fang Yuan had said earlier in front of the crowd was simply for the sake of the general populace. There was another meeting after that in the Clan Head's Pavilion. This was of necessity, as the central Clan Hall, the usual meeting place, had been damaged to the point where it could no longer be used for that purpose. This was the only building in the village which had a room that could be used for such a purpose. This meeting was only for the elders - what few of them that remained.
"Gu Yue Yao Ji is not here," one of the Gu Masters said. There was an uncomfortable silence, as many of them knew what to say but lacked the courage to speak it. Yao Ji's cultivation had now fallen from Rank 3 to Rank 2, and so she was no longer an elder.
However, given the fact that she had dedicated many decades of her life to the village's fortune, none of them would feel right about tossing her out, especially as it appeared that her life was coming to a close. It was the equivalent of kicking someone while they were down or adding insult to injury.
"For the moment," Fang Yuan said, "we do not need to revoke her title of elder until we get a clearer idea of what our situation is. If she ends up passing away shortly, there's no need to do so. As a matter of fact, as long as she does not do anything to 'rock the boat,' so to speak, there's no need to do anything about her." Human Path methods could do quite a lot, but they could not reverse ageing. At least, Fang Yuan had not found something which could do anything like that. The only thing that could cure aging was Lifespan Gu. If Yao Ji did pass away, they would allow her to be buried as an 'elder.' If she survived, they would consider that matter another day.
"There's another matter that we must discuss," Fang Yuan said, "which is why I've called all of you here. And that is regarding the truth of what happened that day." Fang Yuan gave them a very abridged version of events. Some of them had overheard Lord Sky Crane's words, but many of them did not want to believe it. And of course, Fang Yuan left out certain details, such as that of the Northern Dark Ice Soul Physique and Bai Ning Bing's detonation.
"The point which I wish to come to," Fang Yuan said, "is that we cannot let information like this leak outside of the village. Otherwise, we will be the ones who are considered in the wrong."
"Considered in the wrong?" Qing Shu asked. "We are the ones who were attacked by Lord Sky Crane!"
"That is correct," Fang Yuan said. "However, the righteous path is entirely about justification. Even the worst of atrocities can be justified as long as one has the correct reason. The righteous path can sometimes be even more underhanded and despicable than the demonic path in the way that it acts, so long as one can save face. Demonic cultivators will simply attack, but righteous cultivators will attack while claiming that it was you who harmed them in the first place!"
Many of the elders had a strange feeling as Fang Yuan spoke like this. He was speaking as if he was not a member of the righteous path himself.
Then again, most of them shook these feelings away. If a noble hero like Fang Yuan could not be said to be righteous in this world, then who could be?
"Lord Sky Crane can simply use the justification that we were harboring a demonic cultivator, and then he will brand all of us as demonic cultivators as well by extension. The fact that the first generation Gu Yue engaged in Blood Path cultivation is an even bigger stain upon us. Even demonic path Gu Masters stay away from the Blood Path," Fang Yuan said. "Of course, we have our own slight advantage in that regard. The first generation Gu Yue is dead, and so are his Blood Path Gu worms. Most of the evidence can be hidden, thanks to the destruction of much of the mountain. In a way, it is a double-edged sword, a blessing and a curse as well. Furthermore, this Lord Sky Crane hails from the Central Continent, and it will be difficult for them to mount a large-scale attack upon the Southern Border. We can brand him as a foreign invader wanting to infringe upon our benefits." Fang Yuan said this, though he knew this was only true temporarily. In the future, there would come a time when the five regional walls would vanish and the Central Continent would invade all of the other regions. However, that time had not come yet.
While it's one thing for Lord Sky Crane to enter the Southern Border on his own, the Immortal Crane Sect could not send their Rank 6 or higher Gu Immortals after them. Such a thing would attract the attention of every single Immortal within the Southern Border, and they would be preempted to act if only to preserve their own interests. Immortals of a different region were always suppressed when they went to another region, with perhaps one exception being the Eastern Sea. Because of this, Fang Yuan knew that they were temporarily safe. As for mortals, the Immortal Crane Sect could not send a large number of them into the Southern Border either.
"Why even discuss this matter? No one other than Lord Sky Crane knows of what happened here, and the other parts of the Southern Border will not care," an elder scoffed.The source of this content ɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"Do you think so? Have you all forgotten about the Tie clan?" Fang Yuan asked.
"The Tie clan? Why would they be interested in investigating?"
"Because Gu Yue Bo invited them," Fang Yuan said, having found out about this from the former clan leader himself. "To investigate the case of the demonic Gu Master attack earlier. No doubt, the Tie clan would not care for the woes of a medium-sized clan like ours, nor would anything that could be offered sway the heart of famous Tie Xue Long. But when word of this strange anomaly gets out, naturally other clans will come to investigate. Even if the famous investigator thought of ignoring our request or postponing it for several decades, this might arouse his interest."
They were silent as Fang Yuan said this. Now that all the evidence was gone, there was little to no chance that the origin of that demonic Gu Master could be found out. However, they had inadvertently invited trouble into their own house by asking for Tie Xue Long's help.
"Furthermore," Fang Yuan continued. "When word gets out of what happened, nearby clans and the like will start circling the mountain like vultures. There are still many resources upon the mountain that others might covet - like our own signature Moonlight Gu and Moon Orchids. Either that, or the prospect of easy slaves might be enough for them to come swooping down on us."
"Selling human slaves is something only demonic cultivators would do..."
"Are you sure?" Fang Yuan asked, his eyes flashing. "The righteous path, so long as it can justify it, will find any number of reasons to 'capture' us should we show weakness. They would call us prisoners or the like. But this is why we can't show weakness or give them a reason to strike out at us."
The subtext was also clear to everyone there who was experienced- 'You all want to survive? Then you're going to have to rely upon me, the only Rank 4 Gu Master in the village, Gu Yue Fang Yuan!'
There was no need for Fang Yuan to openly state something like that - the others understood, after all, that was just how the righteous path operated!

chapters.title: Chapter 164 - 164: Make Gu Yue Village Great Again: Part Four
chapters.content:
"And what about this strange house?" Han Lin asked. Fang Yuan's explanation did not mention it at all, and it was clear to all of them that it was quite powerful even if they didn't understand the full extent of such power.
"The house was one of the relics that the first-generation ancestor was keeping," Fang Yuan said. "I'm not entirely sure how it works. However, I've managed to make part of it function. Of course, we will also need to keep it hidden."ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
There were those who wanted to delve further, but one hand motion from Fang Yuan told them that was all that he would hear on the matter. If these had been normal times, even the clan head couldn't escape such kind of scrutiny. However, these were not normal times.
Some of them, such as Qing Shu, were even fine and approved of something like this - they saw it as Fang Yuan keeping a potential weapon secret so that it could be used during times of crisis.
Seeing as that this line of questioning was going to get them nowhere, they moved on to other matters.
"Regarding our benefits..." one of them piped up.
"Oh, given the current state of affairs, we can continue with the increased allowance of 300 primeval stones a week," Fang Yuan said. With so many of the elders deceased as well as ordinary clan members, maintaining this level for now was not an issue.
However, that did not solve the real problem on the elder's minds.
"About the Moon Orchid Petals..."
"We have about ten thousand currently in storage," Fang Yuan said. While that sounded like a large amount, when taking into account how many Gu Yue clansmen there were, that would normally only last them all about one or two months. Given the number of clansmen who died and the many dead gu worms at well, things might last two or three times as long.
The shortage, however, would impact these elders the most. Who else had Rank 3 gu worms and needed the largest amount of Moon Orchid Petals? Not only that, it was their battle strength that mattered far more than even ten Rank 2 Gu Masters.
What did it matter if they had an increased share of primeval stones if there were no gu worms to use them on? It was the equivalent of being stranded on a desert island with nothing but a huge pile of money - you would starve to death regardless.
Some of them were thinking that Fang Yuan had the right idea in going for the Blood Moon Gu for his advancement of the Moonglow Gu- all he needed to feed his own gu worm was fresh blood.
"What about the flowers themselves?" one of the elders asked.
"Does anyone have any idea on how to save them?" Fang Yuan asked.
"The method through which the Moon Orchids were planted and maintained was devised by our first generation ancestor himself, much like with the Moonlight Gu," Han Lin said.
They very well couldn't ask that person for help, now then could they?
"Are there any Wood Path experts who might be able to lend us a hand there?" Fang Yuan asked.
"There was Gu Yue Yi Fei... not an expert by any means but an amateur who studied the Wood Path."
"He was killed by the wolf tide two weeks ago?"
"Is that so? I had no idea..."
"No, that was Gu Yue Fei Yi who was killed by the wolves two months ago... Gu Yue Yi Fei was killed when he ate some unripe fruit and had uncontrollable diarrhea..."
"Oh right, how could I have mistaken the two?"
"Regardless," Fang Yuan said, interrupting them all. "Almost ninety percent of the Moon Orchids seem to have been damaged to some extent. The other ten percent might still have signs of damage that we cannot detect- though as you all can understand, we can't continue to harvest any more until the batch grows back without risking the fact that they might turn extinct." They had done their best to defrost any areas of the underground cavern that were still icy, but that didn't mean that the temperature there had returned back to normal.
Fang Yuan did know a Wood Path Gu Master as a matter of fact - the Wood Path Gu Master when you got down to it, but whether or not that person would be of the slightest help had to be seen.
"Given this," Fang Yuan continued, "we will need to restrict the sale and purchase of Moon Orchid Petals in the clan. Elders, naturally, should get the first pick, though I would advise you all to consider changing which gu worms you wish to rear to something which is more sustainable in the future. Speaking of, the Moonlight Gu are the biggest fraction of the gu worms the clan feeds, but not the entirety. What else are we running low on?"
The clan spent up to over a thousand stones in order to keep the gu worms in their storage fed. However, in the current environment, money was not the issue- many of these things could not even be bought from the Xiong or Bai clans simply because they wouldn't have them either.
"Lightwood Soil, Clay Earth, Rainbow Water, Red Crickets..." one of the elders read out a list of materials they would be short on. There was little in common with these materials, so there was no single source they could work on to get them all. Red Crickets were found in the wilderness, though many would have died after Bai Ning Bing's explosion. The Lightwood Soil and Clay Earth might recover to some extent once the ice had melted, but there was no use in trying to defrost the Rainbow Water.
"Additionally, there are many Gu Masters petitioning us asking if we can assist them with the feeding of their gu worms," Qing Shu said.
Such a thing would've been scoffed at in the past, one's gu worms were one's own and had to be fed by oneself, but in this scenario with such widespread damage they would no doubt want some kind of answer.
"Stall them for now while we consider things further," Fang Yuan said. "In the meanwhile, we need to send envoys to the Bai and Xiong clans giving them an offer of assimilating with us."
"You were serious about that? I thought that was a joke..."
Fang Yuan sighed. "Look around you - how many people and gu worms do we have left? The threats on the mountain might have perished along with us, but with this kind of void other animals will soon move in to fill in the gaps. Even if the surrounding Gu Masters do nothing, we will need greater strength to deal with what will be coming up ahead."
There was a good chance that those two clans would reject them, but if that were so, so be it. They would soon see the harsh realities of this world.
"Any other issues to touch upon?" Fang Yuan asked.
For now, while there were a pile of other mundane things to deal with, but they would only pop up in the coming days as people realized that they needed to be dealt with in the first place. Given the widespread extent of damage that threatened even the foundation of the clan, many weren't even sure how much things they needed to deal with.

chapters.title: Chapter 165 - 165: Make Gu Yue Village Great Again: Part Five
chapters.content:
The Gu Yue Clan's envoys reached the Xiong and Bai clans.
Both of these clans had found it easier to reorganize after the recent events, simply because there were fewer survivors among them. However, this was ultimately not a good thing.
The Gu Yue Clan heavily outnumbered both of them combined, whether one spoke of numbers or in terms of power. With Fang Yuan having Rank 4 Peak Stage cultivation, even if their clan leaders had survived, they still would have been placed in a difficult spot and would have been suppressed to some extent.
But now, without any Rank 4 Gu Masters and barely a few elders, they were like people adrift at sea, desperately clinging to the nearest piece of driftwood to stay afloat. The slightest storm could have easily set them adrift, and their survival was on the line with every passing minute.
The Xiong Clan considered the Gu Yue Clan's proposal.
Many of them wanted to outright decline it. "The Gu Clan wants us to become one of them? Impossible!" someone said. "More likely than not, they want to make us their slaves," another pointed out.
Even if that were not the case, nearly every person in the Gu world operated with the mindset that one could not trust others who are not like them.
Humans discriminated against variant humans. Humans discriminated against other humans from different regions. Humans discriminated against other humans from different clans. Even within a clan, humans discriminated between each other based on family ties.
Many of them felt that they would not be fairly treated under the Gu Yue Clan's banner. Furthermore, there was also the issue of their pride. Their clan had stood for several hundred years. How could they bow their heads and erase their surname, becoming part of the Gu Yue clan instead?
Even if they were willing to do so, they would be looked upon with suspicion by the other Gu Yue clansmen. The reason they knew this was because they would do the same if it were the other way around!
As for becoming vassals rather than assimilating with the Gu Clan, while this would still greatly wound their pride, it was more acceptable than changing their surnames.
However, Fang Yuan had demanded the secret of their Bear Strength Gu, something they were unwilling to hand over. One of the benefits of the Bear Strength Gu was that once it was used, the Gu Master in question could fight with little to no primeval essence, even if all of their Gu worms died. Because of that, they had a slight advantage when it came to fighting in a resource-depleted Qing Mao Mountain.
Not only that, but this had remained their clan's secret weapon since it had been founded. How could they give this up? In the future, if they happened to rebuild and regain their earlier strength, the Gu Yue clan would have a clear idea on what their strengths and weaknesses were.
That said, this advantage in fighting was only slight, and they would not be able to withstand a full frontal assault from the Gu Yue clan.
"If we refuse, won't they attack us and just enslave us eventually anyway?" one of the Xiong Clan members asked. This was the only reasonable thing to consider.
After all, with resources being scarce currently, if the Gu Clan limited the other two clans, they would be able to get their hands on better feeding grounds, more primeval stones, and the like.
"I doubt that's the case," one of the Xiong Clan members said. "The Gu Clan might be stronger than us, but they also need time to recover. If they expand their territory recklessly, it will only open them up to attack."
Furthermore, another Xiong clansman chimed in, "Don't forget that they're currently led by Gu Yue Fang Yuan. He is a true righteous hero in the truest sense of the word. He will not attack us without reason."
Many of the Xiong clansmen were a bit skeptical of those words. Fang Yuan's reputation had indeed traveled far and wide, to the point that some of them even felt that they might not be mistreated if they were under his banner.
Of course, Fang Yuan was only one person, even if he was the strongest Gu Yue clansman. He likely had his own issues now that he was clan head, and power tended to change people's minds as well. For now, the Xiong Clan decided to delay giving a reply to this missive, saying that they needed to think things through. In the meantime, they had their own issues to deal with.
Meanwhile, the Bai Clan had a similar reaction to Fang Yuan's missive as the Xiong clan.
However, there was one burning question they had that the Xiong clan didn't.
"Where is Lord Bai Ning Bing?" one of them asked. Although the other dead elders and the Bai clan head were accounted for and were being buried with full funeral rites as much as could be accommodated, Bai Ning Bing was nowhere to be found. Even if the cranes had eaten him, many of them had been subsequently injured so they felt that an arm or leg belonging to Bai Ning Bing should've turned up at some point, but nothing of the sort did.
Given his renowned strength, which was said to rival even Rank 4 Gu Masters at one point, they doubted that he had simply died without any trace.
However, despite looking far and wide for Bai Ning Bing, they could find no trace of him. Anyone within their clan who knew the secret of the Northern Dark Ice Soul physique was already dead, and so they were left ignorant on this matter.
"I kind of feel bad for him, though," one of the Bai clansmen said. "He did quite a lot for the Bai Clan, and we never even listened to his suggestion."
"Which suggestion?"
"The suggestion in which he said we should spread a rumor that there were chemicals we were throwing in the rivers that made the frogs gay."
"That's right!" one of them said.
"You know what? In his honor," another person chimed in, "I think that we should go ahead and start spreading that story as much as we can. It's what he would have wanted, even if he is dead."
Many of them nodded in approval of this, and also decided on waffling on sending the Gu Yue clan a reply for the time being.
Fang Yuan had been expecting such a decision, though he was sure that the other clans would see the clarity of their positions soon enough.
In the meantime, once he managed to get some free time away from his clan duties (which was not easy mind you given recent events and how much everything seemed to now depend upon him), he activated the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider to pay some old friends a visit.
Last time he had visited the inheritance, it had not opened for him, though as he did this time around, the Spring Autumn Cicada in his aperture began humming once again and the Blessed Land opened up slightly to allow him inside.
If things went well, he could solve most of his problems by leveraging the benefits of this Blessed Land. The Blessed Land had changed little since the last time he had visited, and much like last time, as he approached, a figure materialized before him.
"Welcome back, Fang Yuan," Paradise Earth Immortal said. "I see that you've been well. Come, take a seat and have a cup of tea with me."

chapters.title: Chapter 166 - 166: Make Gu Yue Village Great Again: Part Six
chapters.content:
Paradise Earth led Fang Yuan to the same table they had set up before. Given how little the Blessed Land had changed, it felt as though they had sat there just yesterday. Of course, this had not been yesterday, and quite a bit had happened since the last time the two of them had spoken to each other.
"This is a slightly different variety of tea," Paradise Earth said. "Rather than going for sweet, like last time, I decided to change things to a bit more bitter and darker flavor by adding coffee beans to it, creating a slight mix of tea and coffee. If I were to add some special Earth Path ingredients I could even have it give you a few Earth Path dao marks, but I sense that will be a hinderance to you right now. How do you like it?"
Fang Yuan took a sip. Being prepared by an immortal, it undoubtedly tasted excellent. However, neither the driest of wines, nor the most gorgeous of jade beauties, nor the tastiest of food, could deter Fang Yuan's mind from his goal. He was as fixed to his path of attaining eternal life as the North Star was back in Earth's sky - the other stars might dance about it, but it alone remained true to itself.
"Is that all you have to say, Paradise Earth?" Fang Yuan asked. "I didn't think that the man renowned as one of the most generous and most righteous Immortal Venerables in all of history would be this shameless!"
"Shameless, me?" Paradise Earth asked with feigned surprise. "Oh, Gu Yue Fang Yuan, what makes you think that?"
"Last time I was here, your compatriot Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable attacked me," Fang Yuan said. "Not only were you unable to do anything about it, but now that I come back, you don't give me any words of apology or even ask how I'm doing. Instead, you act as if nothing happened. Shouldn't you be compensating me for what I had to go through, Paradise Earth? It is only right that I demand such given what I was forced to go through at your hands and due to your negligence. You can start by handing me control over this Blessed Land."
Paradise Earth laughed. "Oh, Fang Yuan, why are you in such a rush? Don't you know? The most beautiful things in nature cannot be sped up, no matter how much humanity wishes. Nine women cannot create a baby in one month, no matter how much you urge them. This Blessed Land will eventually belong to you. The keyword there, of course, is 'eventually.' When the time is right, I will hand over this Blessed Land. But that is only after you become an Immortal. Coming to that, how has your time been since we last parted?"Thɪs updatᴇd by NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
"I suspect that you're already aware of what happened," Fang Yuan said. "However, in case you want me to tell you, we were attacked, and my clan has nearly been wiped out."
"Hmm, yes," Paradise Earth said.
"Think about it this way, Paradise Earth," Fang Yuan continued. "Their deaths could have been prevented if only you had given me more help in the past. However, now they're dead. Their blood is on your hands. How can you, the most Peaceful Venerable in history, so-called, sit there and so relaxingly drink tea while knowing this? It is not without reason that I just called you shameless."
Paradise Earth shook his head. "Oh, Fang Yuan, they might be dead, but death is certainly not the end of the line, not when it comes to the Human Path. As you will soon see, they might be dead now, but who says that they cannot come back and ask for suffering? Even if I wanted to, I could not alleviate the entire world's suffering."
"No," Fang Yuan said. "However, there are things that you can do right now. Such as by handing me over this Blessed Land, or some Immortal Gu, or helping me ascend to become an Immortal myself."
"Regarding that, actually," Paradise Earth said. "Have you been able to obtain the Righteous Virtue Physique? I had told you that it was quite important that you do so."
Fang Yuan shook his head. "I've not reached Rank 5 yet." Although he had Rank 5 Charity Gu and had enough Human Path dao marks to fulfil the refinement conditions, he had not reached Rank 5 itself and so could not move forward with that refinement.
"And yet I see that you have several of the ingredients needed already," Paradise Earth said. "I can give you a hint when it comes to refining the Righteous Virtue Physique. Like I said earlier, the aid of one of the Ten Extreme Physiques would help you in obtaining the same. You have a gu worm within your system which you can use with your ally Bai Ning Bing in order to make things easier on yourself."
"Well in that case," Fang Yuan continued, "I would like to move the people of Gu Yue village to this Blessed Land."
"That, I'm afraid, is not possible," Paradise Earth said.
"Why not?" Fang Yuan asked.
"Because, Fang Yuan," Paradise Earth said. "Part of your journey is learning how to care for your fellow man. I have a feeling that, despite everything you've done up till now, your inner nature has not changed. It is only by becoming a true clan head that you will be able to advance and learn."
"I am trying to be a true Clan Head," Fang Yuan retorted. "My clan can only remain safe and away from danger if they were in a place like this. Why wouldn't I want them to experience one of the paradises that you had created?"
Paradise Earth smirked. "There are a number of additional reasons why I cannot accommodate humans in this Blessed Land for now. However, I know that that what you are saying is without a doubt not true. I know that you, with your ingenuity, can indeed find a way for your clan to survive. Continue to follow the Goody Two-Shoes System, and you will soon find success. When it's time for you to ascend to Immortality, that is when I will be lending you more aid."
By now, he had finished his tea. The flavor had been so enrapturing that the two of them had actually sat there for four hours without Fang Yuan even fully realizing it. Of course, within the Blessed Land, with its accelerated rate of time, this was not as apparent as it otherwise would have been.
"So then, what is next?" Fang Yuan asked.
"What is next is that you will continue to lead your clan," Paradise Earth said, "and you will try to refine the Righteous Virtue Physique. Only once you have refined it should you attempt to ascend to immortality. Fang Yuan, with your foundation increased like that, the gains you will be able to obtain upon becoming an immortal will be all the greater. That is all that I have to say to you right now. However, there's someone else who wishes to speak to you, of course. Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable."
Fang Yuan scoffed. "You want me to speak with him? Why would I willingly put my head in the lion's mouth?"
Paradise Earth shook his head. "While what had happened earlier was indeed... unforeseen, Fang Yuan, I'm sure that you already know that he wishes to see you succeed. He also has a heavy hand when it comes to the construction of the Goody Two-Shoes System. Even if he had tried to achieve them through means I would not approve of. He still cannot harm you directly in this Blessed Land, and won't be pulling any tricks like last time - that I will assure you."

chapters.title: Chapter 167 - 167: Make Gu Yue Village Great Again: Part Seven
chapters.content:
With a wave of his hand, Paradise Earth Immortal sent Fang Yuan elsewhere within the Blessed Land. Genesis Lotus was not where he had been last time. Instead, his will was lounging just outside a small but elegant bamboo building in its shade.
Fang Yuan approached, crossed his arms, and waited for him to say something.
And then he waited...
And waited...
And continued waiting...
Ultimately, Fang Yuan gave up and just asked Genesis Lotus, "How have you been?"
"Oh, I've been fine. I can't complain," Genesis Lotus said. "I am just a will, after all. I've been working on a few more paintings. Also considered finishing another version of my memoir to give to the Heavenly Court so that its members can learn from my experiences."
"Really, is your memoir called 'My Struggle' by any chance?" Fang Yuan asked.
"No, it isn't," Genesis Lotus said. "I was actually thinking of calling it something like 'Seeds of the Future' or 'Harvest of the Heavenly Lotus' or something good like that. 'My Struggle' doesn't really seem to suit my memoir, Fang Yuan. As it is, I think something like 'My Perseverance' would probably roll off the tongue better if that was something you were considering for your own memoir."
Fang Yuan grunted and glared at the will. "Genesis Lotus, how can you possibly be so shameless?"
"Shameless? Me?" Genesis Lotus asked, then scoffed. "And who's asking me this question- Fang Yuan?"
"What else do you expect me to call you other than shameless?" Fang Yuan asked. "You attacked me last time we were here-"
"No, no, I didn't attack you," Genesis Lotus said. "I merely helped you out with your cultivation. See? You're already Rank 4 peak stage. How could that have happened without my help?"
"Because of you, I had to go through multiple hardships, and the Spring Autumn Cicada had been taken from me! Not only that, I was trapped on Qing Mao Mountain like a prisoner!" Fang Yuan shouted.
"But did you die?" Genesis Lotus asked. "And as far as I can see, the Spring Autumn Cicada is still in your aperture. It isn't my fault you let it go..."
"You attacked me and I demand compensation!" Fang Yuan shouted.
"You know, I'll tell you what," Genesis Lotus said, pulling something out of thin air. "Here, I made a portrait of you. Why don't you take this as an apology?"
He handed the portrait to Fang Yuan, who frowned. The portrait did depict someone who looked like Fang Yuan, but there was clearly something off.
"Why have you drawn me as a woman?" Fang Yuan asked. It depicted Fang Yuan with softer features in a bright red dress with a lily in his long, flowing hair, and while that could be taken either way there was no doubt that this person was supposed to be a woman when one noticed the size of the breasts that Genesis Lotus had painted on her, which rivaled even Bai Ning Bing's.
"Oh, I thought that you would have taken that Dollhouse's offer," Genesis Lotus said. "And that you'd have turned yourself into a woman by this point. I guess I was wrong. Anyway, in anticipation of that, I decided to prepare that portrait for you. What do you think about it, Fang Yuan?"
Fang Yuan: ...
"I'm waiting for an answer? Or did my brushwork truly make you speechless?"
Fang Yuan replied by putting his fist through the portrait.
"Now, come on, Fang Yuan, you're no fun at all," Genesis Lotus said, taking the portrait away from him. "Now, what can I do for you?"
"Several things," Fang Yuan said. "You can start by actually giving me appropriate compensation, starting with this: I have an issue regarding plants back in my clan. They're called Moon Orchids and-"
"Yes, I know what Moon Orchids are," Genesis Lotus said with a wave of his hand. Fang Yuan didn't know how that was possible, given that first gen Gu Yue had been the one to develop them. But then again, he wasn't going to sit here arguing with a Venerable about how they knew something. "Oh, I think I can, as a matter of fact, help you with that. A very small matter, as a matter of fact for someone like me. But there's something else that we have to discuss. You still have that painting of mine, which was a blank canvas, correct?"
Fang Yuan nodded.
"I don't see it with you, however," Genesis Lotus said.
"That's because it's back in Gu Yue village," Fang Yuan said.
"Right, now, Fang Yuan, I'm sure that Paradise Earth has already spoken to you about your immortal ascension," Genesis Lotus said. "And that painting was supposed to help you with your immortal ascension. However, there is more to it than that. If you want to ascend as a Human Path Gu Master, you must do it in a place which is filled with Human Path dao marks for best results. I want you to take that painting to a large populated area, like Shang Clan City, for example. Once you do, you will start to understand what it entails, and then it truly will help you ascend to immortality."
"Is that it?" Fang Yuan asked. "You're not even going to give me anything else for what you did?"
"Fang Yuan, you know what they say about greed - it is like a bottomless well that will never be filled no matter how much you throw into it," Genesis Lotus said. "Don't be so greedy..."
"How can I not be? When the future of my clan is at stake? When Lord Sky Crane could return with reinforcements at any time? When the Dollhouse will be discovered it will attract the attention of every single-"
"No need to worry about Lord Sky Crane," Genesis Lotus said. "Or the Dollhouse being discovered. At least for now. That little bit has been taken care of, you're welcome, by the way. As for your little Moon Orchid issue." He materialized in his hand what looked like a long, dark blue colored vine, about one meter in length with some white flowers growing on it that glowed with a slight silvery hue. "This is a Moon and Stars Support Vine Gu, a Rank 4 Gu worm. Put your primeval essence into it, and it will grow all over the place where you're growing the Moon Orchids. As long as it's given enough primeval essence, even if that's given by multiple Rank 1 Gu Masters, it can sustain and nurture the growth of moon and star-based plants, such as the Moon Orchids. It needs nothing for food other than to be kept in the dark and given enough water."
Fang Yuan took the vine and placed it in his aperture. Needless to say that he was still unsatisfied with everything. He then began saying, "Is this it? Just a single Rank 4 gu worm? I didn't expect the former leader of the Heavenly Court to be so poor as to-"
Before he could finish his sentence, Genesis Lotus had already waved his hand, and Fang Yuan found himself outside the Blessed Land.
"Fang Yuan, take a look at that painting again, perhaps you will understand something!" a voice echoed in Fang Yuan's head, but there was no other response from Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable.
Fang Yuan got on the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider and began burrowing his way back to Gu Yue village.

chapters.title: Chapter 168 - 168: Make Gu Yue Village Great Again: Part Eight
chapters.content:
When Fang Yuan returned to the village, he didn't immediately go back to his pavilion. Instead, he first went to the Blood River Graveyard.
Although first gen Gu Yue was dead and many of his secrets had passed away with him, Fang Yuan had been inspecting the area to see if there was anything useful for him. The corpse of the Blood River Python lay near the river. Sadly, it had perished during the fight with Lord Sky Crane.
Fang Yuan did not have any methods to bring the gu worm back to life. However, it was still covered in Rank 5 Blood Path dao marks.
If he had still been a Blood Path Immortal, he would have added the corpse to his own aperture, increasing the amount of blood path dao marks in the environment within. However, right now, all he could use it for was as material for possible refinement of Rank 4 or Rank 5 Gu worms.
Near the Blood River Graveyard was the Blood Chariot Wheel.
Now that Fang Yuan no longer had a method to obtain a bit of immortal essence its usefulness to him had greatly declined.
He also could not continue to take it out on a whim, based on the simple fact that it was a Blood Path Gu House, and it would give his identity as a Blood Path Gu Master away. For now, the Blood Chariot Wheel was soaking in the blood river, feeding upon it. Fang Yuan released Vermilion Blood Moon Gu from his aperture to allow it to feed as he looked for anything else that might have been useful.
Very few clues were left.
Fang Yuan did not have the necessary methods currently to soul search the body of first gen Gu Yue. He began to think- there was apparently a method through which he had concentrated his bloodline and had awaited the appearance of someone with the Ancient Moon Desolate Yin Physique. First gen Gu Yue had Blood Skull Gu, but that had been taken by Lord Sky Crane.
Still, it was not impossible for Fang Yuan to obtain an extreme physique with his own methods, especially once he ascended to become an Immortal.
Although Paradise Earth had greatly urged him to refine the Righteous Virtue Physique, Fang Yuan was not one to put all his eggs in one basket, especially when that basket belonged to Paradise Earth Immortal Venerable, whom he still did not fully trust.
Comparing the Righteous Virtue Physique and the Ancient Moon Desolate Yin Physique; it was clear which one was superior in his eyes.
Although Paradise Earth said that the Righteous Virtue Physique had no drawbacks, Fang Yuan had difficulty believing such. More likely than not, it had no drawbacks for someone like Paradise Earth, but likely had some requirements on how the user was supposed to behave in order to work properly.
Fang Yuan did not know first gen Gu Yue's attainment level when it came to the Blood Path. It was safe to say that it was likely no more than Master level attainment given how few mortals could even reach that point in their lives.
With his own Grandmaster level attainment in the blood path, Fang Yuan thought that it would be possible for him to improve upon the method used by first gen Gu Yue in order to awaken the Ancient Moon Desolate Physique. There was a reason why he had attempted to save so many Gu Yue clansmen, after all.
However, even this time, his search was ultimately fruitless. Even with a high attainment level, he could not make something out of nothing. He needed some clues to build upon.
He did find something interesting while exploring the nearby area, however. 'This is...' Fang Yuan thought to himself, dismounting the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider to see a gu worm that was encased in a thin layer of earth some distance from the Blood River Graveyard. The Thousand Li Earthwolf Spider, a Rank 5 Gu worm, just sitting out here in the open for him to take.
As for the person who had left it here, that could only be the Flower Wine Monk. Obviously, as it had been his signature method of travel as per the clan records.
'However, why did it end up here?' Fang Yuan thought to himself. This was nowhere near where he had found the Flower Wine Monk's inheritance. 'Could it be that there had been something else to the Flower Wine Monk's inheritance?' Fang Yuan thought. 'Perhaps the Audio-Visual Gu had had more to it before it had been destroyed...'ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ
Fang Yuan put these thoughts aside for now.
As he injected his primeval essence into the Thousand Li Earthwolf Spider, putting the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider inside his aperture, the spider awoke, broke through its casing, and then began devouring soil hungrily. It looked like it had been placed in a state of hibernation for some reason much like the gu worms used in rock gambling were. Fang Yuan felt that he was still missing something, but with the recent destruction to the village, any clues that might have been left behind were likely gone.
Once the Thousand Li Earthwolf Spider was done eating, having consumed nearly half a metric ton of soil, Fang Yuan mounted it and instructed it to dig towards the surface. However, while doing so, he was quite interested in exploring this area.
Perhaps there were more clues left behind by the Flower Wine Monk?
However, something happened as Fang Yuan began to emerge towards the surface: the Thousand Li Earthwolf Spider suddenly began... there is no other word for it... misbehaving. It moved in directions that Fang Yuan did not want it to go. It would sometimes stop, and then sometimes start attacking part of the wall with no provocation whatsoever.
It eventually got to the point where, although it was a Rank 5 Gu worm, he was actually traveling slower than if he had just used the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider. Part of this could be explained by the fact that he still only had peak Rank 4 essence and had not yet advanced to Rank 5. But something like this should have absolutely not been happening.
