Fang Yuan felt something approaching near him. There were hundreds of centipedes being used as a literal wall as the Chainsaw Golden Centipede hid among them.
They could do nothing before Fang Yuan's defensive methods, and the Rank 3 gu worm finally showed itself when it realized that its human wave tactics were futile.
As it made to rear its fangs to try to attack him, before it could even come near him, Fang Yuan unleashed the Spring Autumn Cicada's Rank 6 aura.
The Chainsaw Golden Centipede was a Rank 3 Gu worm. While it was not completely suppressed by Fang Yuan's Rank 4 aura too much, before the might of the Spring Autumn Cicada, it could only shudder as it became completely dominated.
Fang Yuan refined it instantly.
'If I could advance this to Rank 4, it might be a worthy additional offensive option for me.'
Still, the Chainsaw Golden Centipede was mildly useful to him even if he got it to Rank 4. He simply had better options right now.
He could keep it in the clan's storage and consider it as him giving up something towards the clan. He could consider those to be 'merit points' in case he wanted to exchange something later on. He could also give this to Fang Zheng once he reached Rank 3 or Qing Shu if he wanted to increase their battle strength.
Advancing it to Rank 4 would take up too much of his time and resources which he felt were better spent elsewhere.
"I wonder what else is beyond here?" Fang Yuan thought to himself.
There were still numerous ordinary centipedes following around the cave, but in a way, this was good for him because wherever they scurried about meant that there were no traps there.
He still used his investigative methods as he walked forward, noting that the tunnel opened up into a place which showed signs that it had been modified by a person.
Then, he heard the sound of running water reach him before he happened upon a crystal wall.
Beyond the wall was a stream of water that seemed to merge into their clan's primeval spring. It was free flowing and untouched by ice this deep within the mountain, but that wasn't what caught Fang Yuan's gaze.
There was a gu worm located beyond the crystal wall. A novice might not know what it was, but with his 500 year's of experience there was no way that it would escape his notice.
The Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus!
Immediately the puzzle pieces fell together within Fang Yuan's mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 180 - 180: Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus: Part Four
chapters.content:
The Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus was an invention of Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable. It was a portable primeval spring, and once placed within one's aperture, it would generate primeval stones which could either be sold or used by the Gu Master in question for either combat or cultivation.
Its value could not be understated to either a mortal or immortal Gu Master. To a mortal, it would allow them to essentially never run out of primeval essence during combat and also to generate primeval stones which could be exchanged as a medium of currency. To a demonic cultivator it had all kinds of benefits.
If advanced to an Immortal Gu, it would become even more valuable as it would produce not primeval stones, but Immortal Essence instead! Immortal Essence Stones were far more valuable than primeval stones - not even a million primeval stones could compare to a single Immortal Essence Stone. There was a reason that it was also considered one of the Top Ten Immortal Gu, alongside the Spring Autumn Cicada.
The downside to refining it, of course, was that one needed a spirit spring in order to do so.
The Flower Wine Monk had managed to find the recipe for the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus. However, in order to refine it, he needed a primeval spring. Being a demonic Gu Master, one who wandered the world on his lonesome and lacked resources, he did not have the access needed to refine this gu.
Come to think of it, even if he had been a righteous path Gu Master, there was no way that he could be allowed to use a clan's own primeval spring in order to refine a gu worm for himself like this. To a clan, a primeval spring was far more valuable than a single Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus.
The Flower Wine Monk had evidently chosen Gu Yue Village as a target for this. He had been betrayed by the fourth generation clan head, but had managed to escape and then slowly made his way to this location to try and refine it.
However, while going towards the spirit spring, he had likely run into first gen Gu Yue. After running into first gen Gu Yue, he had been killed in that encounter, not from the encounter with the fourth generation clan head, as everyone had assumed.
He had then left his inheritance here to see if anyone could get revenge for him on his behalf.
After all, if someone refined the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus, it would mean the consumption of the clan's primeval spring, and the destruction of the clan.
Fang Yuan extended his hand towards the crystal wall, finding that he could move through it as if it were made of air. The crystal wall existed as a means to visualize the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus, as it was said to be ephemeral and oscillated between the astral and physical worlds until refined. It was only through this crystal wall that one could see it.
Fang Yuan did not touch the water itself - he could not pollute his own clan's primeval spring, after all. He instead tossed a primeval stone through the barrier, with the gu worm greedily taking it in.
Fang Yuan did not know the recipe for this gu worm, but he had heard rumors on how it could be refined.
It was said that it needed to be kept in a fresh primeval spring for nine days and nine nights, and when it bloomed with nine leaves, only then it could be moved else all of one's efforts were for naught.
Fang Yuan saw that it had eight and a quarter leaves on it - it had been sitting here for centuries, and had bloomed fully some time ago. However, the primeval spring slowly lost its vitality over time, and the lotus began nurturing the spring instead.
If anything things must've gotten worse recently after Bai Ning Bing's detonation had damaged the primeval spring, meaning that this process of reverse nourishment was accelerated.
Fang Yuan looked at the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus for some time, weighing his options.
If it had been him from before, he would have undoubtedly wanted to refine this gu.
However, it was only Rank 3 currently, so it offered limited help to him right now. Now that he was at Rank 4 Peak Stage, its primeval essence regenerating ability was but a drop in a massive lake.
Disregarding that, the main problem was that he needed a primeval spring in order to refine it.
The primeval spring in question had to be a healthy and fresh one, not one which was dying or had been damaged. Bai Ning Bing's detonation had caused damage to all three primeval springs on Qing Mao mountain, used by each of the three clans. This had become evident over time as the harvest of primeval stones had decreased somewhat.
The clansmen naturally hoped that the primeval springs would recover with time, and as far as Fang Yuan knew, the possibility of this was quite high. However, that meant that they were not the ideal candidates to be used for refining this gu.

However, he could not just leave the clan like this.
There was also the matter of attempting to advance it any further. You needed multiple spirit springs to do so. To get it to Rank 4 where it would be useful to him, he would need seven primeval springs. To get it to Rank 5, a realm where he was at the cusp of, he would need eleven.
'I can't refine this right now,' Fang Yuan concluded.
However, when he announced the location of this place to the village, he would need to first think of a way to hide this place from the rest of the village. Either that or translocate this gu worm without damaging it.
Such was not impossible, but he had not brought the required gu worms needed for that kind of endeavor.
He got on the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider and burrowed further.
Much as he had expected, the tunnel merged into a location that was near the clan's underground cavern before ultimately opening up in the same area where he had found the Thousand Li Earthwolf Spider.
This opened up into the Blood River Graveyard eventually.
The mystery had been solved, and all of Fang Yuan's questions had been answered.
He had made significant gains, it could be said, though there had been nothing which would improve his own strength by a large measure.
Despite being a Rank 5 inheritance, most of the Flower Wine Monk's Rank 5 gu worms had been killed or died out after so long. As such, to the current Gu Yue Fang Yuan, there was little of value that he could use for himself.
He spent some time investigating the Blood River Graveyard further, wondering if there were any clues that would now show up that he had uncovered the full extent of the Flower Wine Monk's true inheritance. If he could uncover the secret behind the Ancient Moon Desolate Yin Physique, it would make all his gains from earlier seen inconsequential. The entire trip might've actually been worth it to him in that case.
Nothing else seemed to have changed, however, and he could only make his way back to the underground cavern, whereupon he placed several of the gu worms that he had found in the clan's storage before returning those he had borrowed.
He estimated that he would need about sixty thousand primeval stones in order to nurture the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus completely. In lean times like this, even someone like Fang Yuan would have difficulty ponying up that kind of amount. Before that, he needed to find a suitable primeval spring to use in order to refine it.
Once he successfully moved it, though, he would be able to announce his discovery to the rest of he clan.

chapters.title: Chapter 177: Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus: Part One
chapters.content:
"With this, we will be the strongest clan on Qing Mao mountain!"
This sentiment echoed throughout the village.
The Bai and the Xiong clans were still recovering, but of course, those two clans also had their resources to manage.
Since the Gu Yue clan had managed to recover far more quickly than them and had stabilized the resources needed to feed their key gu worm, their position was even more advantageous than before. Before, they were like soldiers without arms - now, they had managed to secure a continuous supply of weapons.
It was easy enough to conceptualize that the cause for this was because they had Fang Yuan to rely upon.
Under his umbrella, they could take greater risks. They also had more people around in part because of his actions.
Because of this, these small advantages slowly snowballed into larger ones, resulting in a massive difference in their village's condition right now. Many people felt that it was only natural that soon the two villages would capitulate to Gu Yue village's demands to either assimilate or become vassals of theirs.
The villagers sang Fang Yuan's praises as they dispersed.
***
In a corner of the village, Yu Sai was resting after a long day of work when someone walked in to meet him.
"Yu Sai," Li Mei said. "Here, I wanted to pay you back." Li Mei handed him a set of Moon Orchid Petals. This was supposed to be repayment for how he had helped her out earlier. Li Mei had been one of the first people lucky enough to get a small ration of Moon Orchid Petals promised by Fang Yuan.
"Thanks," Ye Zan said. He didn't seem to be nearly as happy as Li Mei thought he would be. If he had sold them during the time he had given them to her, they would have fetched a much higher price than they would now. Although Li Mei had technically paid him back with the same number of Moon Orchid petals, it could not be said that their value was the same simply because of the differing times they had been exchanged.
Of course, there had been risk associated with selling them at the time, which is likely why he had just handed them over to Li Mei and let her use them with an I.O.U., but still, Li Mei couldn't help but feel she might've shortchanged him slightly.
When she brought this up, Yu Sai simply waved his hand. "No problem. We're good. Don't worry about it."
There was more to it than that, of course. Li Mei felt that Yu Sai had suddenly become rather frosty towards her over the past few days. She didn't know why - although they never had the best sort of relationship even back during their school days. They had never been antagonistic towards each other. 'Is something bothering Yu Sai?' she wondered to herself. If there was, he wasn't exactly opening up about it.
For the time being, Yu Sai and Li Mei were "living together" in the same house.
Space was quickly becoming a premium within the village once more, at least space which did not have its walls or roofs riddled with holes.
They slept in different places, of course, and the house was somewhat divided between the two of them.
Li Mei had come a long ways from thinking that you could get pregnant by kissing, but she still knew that this kind of arrangement between unmarried men and woman was quite unorthodox.
They hadn't been asked by any of the elders to vacate the place they were staying in. Li Mei had a feeling that day would come soon. The place where they were staying was technically owned by a Gu Master who was a distant relative of the landlord who had died here.
The clan only needed to go through various records to confirm this before they would be forced to leave. 'Maybe that's what's bothering him,' she thought to herself. They needed to find a place once they left here.
She paused her train of thought.
She was still thinking of them needing to find a place together, as if she had naturally assumed that they would be living together even after they were done here.
Her cheeks flushed slightly at the idea.
But from what she could tell, Yu Sai did not return the same feelings towards her that she had developed for him ever since he had rescued her. Since the time that he had saved her, she had seen him in an entirely different light.
Li Mei had dropped as many subtle hints as she possibly could towards Yu Sai. These included placing a small flower for him while she handed him a breakfast tray, stating how she would 'have no problems cooking for him for the rest of her life' when he had complimented him on something she had made for him, or any other number of signs she had attempted to flash his way.
However, he seemed to be ignoring all of them completely.
From what she had heard from him back during the academy, he had never intended to get married simply because it was "too much of an effort," or so he said.
'So maybe he really doesn't like me,' Li Mei thought to herself. The only other thing she could think of to do was to literally scream "I love you!" at him.
However, from what her mother had told her before she had passed away, that was not a really appropriate way for a girl to tell a man that she liked him.
Her mother had said that a real lady would use more subtle hints, and any man worth his salt would be able to pick up on them. Likely, that meant that Yu Sai had picked up on them, and he simply chose not to respond, meaning he was not interested.
'Oh well,' Li Mei thought to herself.
In the coming future, several mortal woman might get the chance to become Gu Masters. Maybe Yu Sai was waiting for that opportunity to snatch a beauty for himself - Li Mei was well aware that her looks were bottom of the barrel.
If Yu Sai ever did change his mind in the future and decided to find a wife for himself, why wouldn't he choose one of them over her? There was no shortage of pretty mortal woman, and he would be guaranteed at least two children from them.
Perhaps their love was just not meant to be, she thought as she rolled over and went to sleep.
Yu Sai, for his part, was grumbling as he arranged the Moon Orchid Petals into his storage Gu worm. He had no use for them as he did not use the Moonlight Gu or any of its derivatives, but he could still sell these on the open market or to someone else. He would not invite censure now if he did so.
As he saw Li Mei's retreating frame, he once again couldn't help but feel frustration rise within him. This girl... despite him trying to drop several hints that he liked her (in spite of the fact that he knew that she actually liked Fang Yuan he decided to try to shoot his shot so to speak) she had given him no response.
I guess our love really isn't meant to be, Yu Sai thought as he turned over and tried to fall asleep. Really, he had been stupid to even entertain the idea in the first place. It was clear that Fate did not favor him when it came to nearly any aspect of life.

chapters.title: Chapter 178: Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus: Part Two
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan was wrapped up in his duties as clan head most of the time. That didn't mean that there weren't times where he had a break, or at least that there weren't times where he could tell everyone that he was busy doing something and they needed to handle things on their own.
He had thought about using these brief periods to raise Fang Zheng's cultivation initially, but that had failed, and he still hadn't accumulated enough Human Path dao marks, nor had he reached Rank 5 to try that again with any assurance of success.
Instead, he chose to use this time to delve into something that had been tugging at the back of his mind: namely, the Flower Wine Monk's inheritance. Or at least, what he thought was the 'true inheritance' left behind by the Flower Wine Monk.
Fang Yuan wandered over to the same place where he had found the nearby waterfall, which still had chunks of ice - a remnant of Bai Ning Bing's detonation - that was still prevalent even after all this time.
Fang Yuan went back to the same place where he had found the Audio-Visual Gu. There was nothing abnormal about the area upon first glance, but this was still quite a distance away from where he had found the Thousand Li Earthwolf Spider earlier.
'I had thought that the inheritance only consisted of a few primeval stones and the Liquor Worm,' Fang Yuan thought to himself, 'as well as the Audio-Visual Gu. However, there might have been more to it.'
This actually confirmed one of the suspicions he had had long ago: the system had seemed a bit too generous when giving him the reward for turning over the details of this inheritance to the clan. It seemed that there had been more to the inheritance which he had not uncovered initially which he might have been able to had he not turned it over to the clan head.
He had borrowed several investigative-type Gu worms from the clan's storage and activated them. There was something odd about the earth in a specific location, as if it had been shifted ever so slightly.
He took out the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider and then began commanding it to dig. It turned out that his suspicion had been correct. He ended up in a tunnel which was definitely man-made, likely having been made by the Thousand Li Earthwolf Spider. He found an Earth Treasury Flower Gu, a storage-type Gu worm, which had another Gu inside: White Boar Strength Gu. This gu worm seemed to be on the verge of death, and Fang Yuan refined it instantly before placing it in his aperture.
Some distance further ahead, there was a boulder which was blocking his path. By now, Fang Yuan had fully utilized the Strength of Ten Men Gu, as well as the system's White Boar Gu and he began to push it.
Fang Yuan continued to push it forward, all the while using his investigative methods. This was a demonic inheritance, after all; it would not be out of the ordinary for there to be a trap that could possibly kill the inheritor.
As he rolled away the boulder, eventually, he came upon a spot where the incline flattened out, and it seemed he had succeeded in this part of the 'test'.
There was a section of the soil nearby which also looked like it had been modified slightly. Fang Yuan, after he confirmed that it was safe, dug up the soil to see that there was another Earth Treasury Flower Gu, and within it was a Jade Skin Gu.
This would have been extremely helpful for him back when he had been at the academy, though by this point, the Moonlight Plate Armor Gu naturally far outclassed it. It was not even worth giving to Fang Zheng to increase his battle strength at this point.
What intrigued Fang Yuan far more than this sort of reward was what lay beyond.
There was a massive cavern which he doubted had been made by the Flower Wine Monk. More likely than not, this was a natural cavern that already existed within Qing Mao mountain, which had been used for this purpose.
There was a great deal of greenery within the cavern as a cool breeze met Fang Yuan.
This place seemed deep enough that it had escaped most of the damage caused by Bai Ning Bing's detonation. Then again, Fang Yuan thought that if he had not used a method from the Dollhouse to melt most of the ice, likely this place would not have survived either.
There were numerous stone pillars which stood out amongst the greenery. They extended from the ceiling and went down towards the earth, forming an inverted forest. There were small holes within each of the pillars, and his investigative methods told him that there were certain things living inside.
Fang Yuan approached one of them cautiously, and something leaped out at him. It was a monkey, almost looking like a statue, but there was nothing statue-like about the way that it moved. Its entire body was grey but something stood out among its nearly uniformly dull appearance; namely, that its eyes were two bright green orbs.
'Jade eye stone monkeys,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. 'To think that there was a colony of them beneath Qing Mao Mountain all this time.'
Fang Yuan had no need to even use Moonblades; his fists were more than enough to shatter the monkey into pieces. He retrieved its pair of eyes - two jade stones.
These actions, however, had attracted the attention of even more monkeys. They had been watching the actions of this one, which may have been a particularly adventurous fellow amongst all of them.
Though, upon seeing their comrade killed, more of them began to venture out towards Fang Yuan, who crushed them all with ease. As a Rank 4 Peak Stage Gu Master, enemies of this sort were nothing compared to him. Even if there were thousands of such opponents, he would mow them down as easily as grass.
He was sure that even a Rank 1 Peak Stage Gu Master could deal with several of these monkeys so long as they had the appropriate gu worms.
Fang Yuan investigated more of the pillars.
It seemed that the monkeys were quite territorial but were otherwise not very violent. They would attack only if someone came within fifty meters of one of the pillars, and they would retreat if he managed to move a great distance away. Not that Fang Yuan had a need to retreat; he was merely trying to understand how this place worked.
'These enemies are weak, but in a way, this is good,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. Although the jade eyes were currently useless to him as he didn't need to use Jade Skin Gu, it didn't mean that they would be useless to other people.
These jade eyes could be used to feed a variety of gu worms and could also be used in Gu refinement. Not only that, they could be sold.
Normally, the Gu Yue Village made a good portion of its revenue by selling Moon Orchid Petals. However, it was always good to have several sources to rely upon. Say, for example, if Fang Yuan had not managed to find a way to save the Moon Orchids, they would have been out of luck as their major source of income would've withered away.
'I could also set this place up as a training ground for new Gu Masters,' he thought to himself.
That was why he did not kill all of the stone monkeys, even though it would have been easy for him to do so. Rank 2 Gu Masters could gather around this area and kill some of the jade stone monkeys, thereby harvesting the jade eyes.
It could become a moderately lucrative endeavor for the Gu Yue village so long as they could claim this area. Given their current status as the strongest village upon Qing Mao, he had no doubt that they would easily be able to secure this resource point.

chapters.title: Chapter 179: Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus: Part Three
chapters.content:
By the time Fang Yuan crossed the seventh pillar, it seemed that the jade eye stone monkeys seemed to have realized that there was little point in trying to fight him.
They must have had their own methods of communication between each other, as they did not challenge him, instead cowering behind their pillars and making nervous sounds.
Fang Yuan found a central area among the stone pillar forest. There was a cave within it which looked like it had been made artificially, and Fang Yuan could already guess what lay within.
There was likely a monkey king inside it - given the huge number of jade eye stone monkeys in the area it would be unusual for there not to be one.
Given the fact that the jade eye stone monkeys which surrounded him had attacked in a rather haphazard manner earlier that meant that there was no one strong ruling over them.
The chances of what lay within being a Thousand Beast King were rather low, but it wouldn't be odd for it to be a Hundred Beast King. Regardless, a Thousand Beast King or a Hundred Beast King -both were of little consequence to Fang Yuan as he advanced.
The monkey king, upon sensing that its territory had been invaded, immediately leaped out towards Fang Yuan.
Swoosh!
A single Vermillion Crimson Moon Blade bisected it, killing it instantly.
'It looks like I wasted that attack,' Fang Yuan thought to himself now, seeing that it was indeed a Hundred Beast King.
He had used the Vermillion Crimson Moon Blade on the off chance that it was a Thousand Beast King, simply to settle things quickly.
However, he could have just as easily solved this with his fists.
The monkey king dissolved into small pieces leaving behind only its eyes.
Given enough time, the jade eye stone monkeys around here would repopulate the area, and another monkey king would appear among them.
'This indeed would be quite a good training ground,' he thought to himself.
If this had been him earlier, when he had first found the Flower Wine Monk's inheritance, something like that wouldn't have concerned him whatsoever.
He would have only been thinking of getting as many jade stones as possible for his own use. Right now, though, even if this wasn't useful towards him, as clan head, he could find a use for it in order to strengthen Gu Yue Village.
Within the cave he came upon some writing on the wall.
'Golden Chainsaw Centipede's cave is precarious. Earth Communication is the way to avoid disaster.'
He found another Earth Treasury Flower near there within which there was an Earth Communication Ear Grass Gu. This would have been very helpful to him back in the day, though currently it could not fit his needs. While Earth Communication Ear Grass could be considered a first-class investigative gu worm, that was only considering its rank. It could not match the might of a higher-ranking investigative gu.
Fang Yuan used some more investigative methods near the cave.
Piecing together what was written on the wall, he could guess what lay inside. The Chainsaw Golden Centipede was a Rank 3 gu worm, and could reign over a large number of ordinary centipedes much like a beast king would.
The Flower Wine Monk clearly intended for the Earth Communication Ear Grass Gu to be used by whoever reached up to this point in order to try and avoid the Chainsaw Golden Centipede to progress further.
Based on Fang Yuan's estimations, someone at Rank 2 cultivation could've gotten to this point with some effort. No wonder there would be the consideration of them struggling to deal with a Rank 3 gu worm. The Flower Wine Monk, despite being a demonic cultivator, seemed to have set up his inheritance so that even a weak Gu Master could pass through it after a few attempts.
More likely than not, this was for some kind of nefarious purpose and not out of benevolence.
However, Fang Yuan did not have to worry even if he had only been Rank 2 as he possessed a trump card - the Spring Autumn Cicada.
He wandered near the entrance and let out his Rank 4 Gu Master aura. If he was at Rank 5 currently, the Golden Chainsaw Centipede would've shuddered and retreated, though with what he was doing now, it had likely become agitated, sensing that another 'wild beast' had invaded its territory.
Would it fight or flee?
Fang Yuan felt something approaching near him. There were hundreds of centipedes being used as a literal wall as the Chainsaw Golden Centipede hid among them.
They could do nothing before Fang Yuan's defensive methods, and the Rank 3 gu worm finally showed itself when it realized that its human wave tactics were futile.
As it made to rear its fangs to try to attack him, before it could even come near him, Fang Yuan unleashed the Spring Autumn Cicada's Rank 6 aura.
The Chainsaw Golden Centipede was a Rank 3 Gu worm. While it was not completely suppressed by Fang Yuan's Rank 4 aura too much, before the might of the Spring Autumn Cicada, it could only shudder as it became completely dominated.
Fang Yuan refined it instantly.
'If I could advance this to Rank 4, it might be a worthy additional offensive option for me.'
Still, the Chainsaw Golden Centipede was mildly useful to him even if he got it to Rank 4. He simply had better options right now.
He could keep it in the clan's storage and consider it as him giving up something towards the clan. He could consider those to be 'merit points' in case he wanted to exchange something later on. He could also give this to Fang Zheng once he reached Rank 3 or Qing Shu if he wanted to increase their battle strength.
Advancing it to Rank 4 would take up too much of his time and resources which he felt were better spent elsewhere.
"I wonder what else is beyond here?" Fang Yuan thought to himself.
There were still numerous ordinary centipedes following around the cave, but in a way, this was good for him because wherever they scurried about meant that there were no traps there.
He still used his investigative methods as he walked forward, noting that the tunnel opened up into a place which showed signs that it had been modified by a person.
Then, he heard the sound of running water reach him before he happened upon a crystal wall.
Beyond the wall was a stream of water that seemed to merge into their clan's primeval spring. It was free flowing and untouched by ice this deep within the mountain, but that wasn't what caught Fang Yuan's gaze.
There was a gu worm located beyond the crystal wall. A novice might not know what it was, but with his 500 year's of experience there was no way that it would escape his notice.
The Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus!
Immediately the puzzle pieces fell together within Fang Yuan's mind.

If he could uncover the secret behind the Ancient Moon Desolate Yin Physique, it would make all his gains from earlier seen inconsequential. The entire trip might've actually been worth it to him in that case.
Nothing else seemed to have changed, however, and he could only make his way back to the underground cavern, whereupon he placed several of the gu worms that he had found in the clan's storage before returning those he had borrowed.
He estimated that he would need about sixty thousand primeval stones in order to nurture the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus completely. In lean times like this, even someone like Fang Yuan would have difficulty ponying up that kind of amount. Before that, he needed to find a suitable primeval spring to use in order to refine it.
Once he successfully moved it, though, he would be able to announce his discovery to the rest of he clan.

chapters.title: Chapter 181: Blood Tiger: Part One
chapters.content:
Several hundred li away from Qing Mao Mountain, out in the wilderness, far from any clan, a man by the name of Zuo Ming carried about his daily tasks.
Zuo Ming was a lone cultivator and possessed Rank 3 Middle Stage cultivation. While that was sufficient to survive in this world on one's own, it didn't mean that it was easy.
Since procuring resources was difficult, he had to be careful with the kind of gu worms that he raised. Because of this, he had, out of necessity, become a Strength Path cultivator, despite his greater proficiency when it came to using Metal Path gu worms during his earlier days.
Zuo Ming had not always been a lone cultivator. He had once belonged to a small but lively village until he had been forced into this situation after his village had been annihilated.
It was a tale as old as time: two different clans occupied the same mountain, and one of them faltered and was defeated by the other. Zuo Ming had only been Rank 2 at the time, but he managed to escape with a small group of allies who had helped him survive until he had ended up getting to Rank 3.
He then had a falling out with these people, which is why he currently lived his life as it was currently.
'I wonder if it will rain again today?' he thought to himself.
Back when he had still been living in the village, he had enjoyed the rain as it would often provide a respite from the hot and humid weather that tended to linger where they used to live.This text is hosted at .ɴet
Here, however, the rain only made life worse. The soil became wet and slippery, making it hard for him to move. He did not have a proper Rank 3 movement-type gu worm and had to make do with a Rank 2. As such, there was a high probability of him becoming stuck in the mud while traveling with very few ways of getting himself out of that kind of situation.
There were all sorts of dangers that could get to him if he were trapped: giant frogs which could traverse the mud much more easily than he could; poisonous snakes which tended to bury under the soil and only came out when it rained as the water filled their underground nests; certain plants which were poisonous and difficult to avoid if it became muddy.
If it only rained for a short while, it was not much of an issue. However, if it rained for too long, he would have to make his move anyway.
The only alternative was to starve, both for him and his gu worms. Thankfully, the clouds above passed away soon enough with only the lightest drizzle, and he was able to safely wander outside.
Day-to-day life was difficult and oftentimes tedious.
Someone like Fang Yuan would have had no problem living this way, but the majority of people would have found the isolation nearly unbearable.
Zuo Ming had considered joining another clan as an external elder many times, but that pathway was now cut off from him because of incidents in his past.
He found a herd of goats nearby. There was a Hundred Beast King among them, which glared at him even from a distance; likely the effect of some kind of investigative gu.
However, a Hundred Beast King was of little threat to him. There probably was a Thousand Beast King somewhere, but this section of the flock seemed to have separated from the main herd.
Whether it was wild beasts or humans, both had immense difficulty surviving in the wilderness.
Zuo Ming quickly activated his only Rank 3 gu worm, Tortoise Armor Gu. He had managed to win it after a long and hard battle with a Thousand Beast King giant tortoise. It fed upon tortoise meat, and there was a colony nearby which would usually visit a nearby lake once a month, which provided the adequate food needed for the gu. He needed a defensive Gu worm to use his strength properly without shattering his bones on impact.
While the Hundred Beast King had noticed him, it had still not alerted all of the flock in time.
He grabbed a goat from the periphery and snapped its neck in a single blow before the rest of the herd could properly react.
He was already dragging his kill away by the time that they could mount some kind of response.
He had no intention of fighting all of them; he only needed to fill his stomach.
By the time a few goats were chasing after him, he was already long gone. While goats were very good at traversing the nearby mountains, they had difficulty traversing the loose soil which was scattered around where Zuo Ming lived.
Just as he thought he had enough meat for the next couple of weeks, disaster struck him on the way back to his cave.
If it weren't for his Rank 2 investigative gu worm, he wouldn't have been able to notice it at all and may have very well died on the spot.
A shadow leaped out from the nearby greenery: a Dark Panther King, the equivalent of a Thousand Beast King!
Dark Panthers were known to be quite violent and very good fighters unlike the goats which tended to be less ferocious. It would not be as easy to get away from it as with the goats.
Its entire body was as black as night and was as a matter of fact covered in a small amount of Dark Path dao marks. Normally it would only venture out at night, but something, likely hunger - had motivated it to stay up late.
Its irises were entirely black, but were speckled with small spots like stars. One could not let this deceive them however, as its eyesight was perfectly fine.
The Dark Panther King wanted the kill that Zuo Ming was dragging along, and Zuo Ming immediately had to make a choice.
He either could try to fight the panther off, or he could abandon his meal.
He chose to do the latter, abandoning the carcass he was dragging along and running in the opposite direction.
He was not confident enough in fighting this Thousand Beast King, and he figured that he would be able to find food some other day. It was not worth the risk.
The goats might've backtracked a bit after what he had pulled today, but they were likely still in the same vicinity and he could probably still find them even later.
The panther did not let him go, chasing after him even as he abandoned his kill. He could almost feel its hot breath as he sprinted for his life and kept his defensive gu worm active.
However, after a hundred paces, it turned around, realizing that it couldn't get both things that it wanted at once, and seized the carcass that Zuo Ming had been dragging along before anything else could get to it.
After all, it was not the only hunter in this area. There was a reason why it was so desperately looking for food. If it chased too far after him, someone else might snatch up what it had very rightfully stolen.
It retrieved the goat and then took it away, likely to its lair in order to consume later.
And so, Zuo Ming was left to walk back home empty-handed.

chapters.title: Chapter 182 182: Blood Tiger: Part Two
chapters.content:
'If only I had a storage-type Gu worm that I could use,' Zuo Ming thought to himself as he trudged his way back with nothing to show for all of his effort. 'I wouldn't be in this situation in the first place.'
He wouldn't have lost the carcass had such been the case - nor would he have been a somewhat vulnerable target while traversing the wilderness lugging it behind him which had led to the panther discovering him.
His storage-type gu had unfortunately died three months ago during a fight, after which he had been unable to feed it.
The panther was gone from his sight, but he did not let up until he reached the place he called home as there was always a chance it could come back. "Home" was a quite generous term to describe it, given that it was little more than a cave which could be somewhat reasonably defended.
'I hate living like this,' he thought to himself. Living out here in the wild, like some animal, where everything was struggling to feed itself. Where one could find Rank 4 and Rank 5 beasts wandering around at times and could do nothing but cower and hope that they would eventually pass you by. Where nearly everything wanted to kill you. Where it lacked the comfort of either warm food, a friend, or a wife.
There's a reason that many lone and demonic cultivators developed mental illnesses. The isolation was torturous for those who did not seek it.
As Zuo Ming was about to enter his cave he had resigned himself to having to scout the nearby area for wild turnips later that evening unless he wanted to sleep hungry that night, his pupils suddenly shrank.
There were markings near the entrance of his cave, meaning that someone had been there other than him.
Although he didn't have a specific gu worm that could accomplish this, he had set up things using mortal means that would alert him if someone had entered the cave. He would hop into the cave in a specific pattern, which would not disturb any of the things he had left outside as markers.
'Did someone find my cave?' he thought to himself. He saw a single human footprint. Was there a demonic or lone Gu Master out in the area? Zuo Ming had no desire to fight anyone.
And while he did have some spare belongings he had managed to accumulate within, he was not going to cling onto them at the cost of his own life. Humans die for wealth and birds die for food.
Zuo Ming knew when it was time to cut his losses, such as when he had encountered the panther earlier.
As he turned around though, a shadow leaped out of the wilderness. At first, he thought it was the panther which had followed him all this way.
But instead, it was a Gu Master. A pit formed in Zuo Ming's stomach. He may have been decrying his loneliness just a while back, but he absolutely did not want to meet this person ever again. How had this person even found him? He had done his utmost to cover up his tracks to make sure that this man of all people wouldn't be able to trace him.
Rank 4 aura emanated from this Gu Master. His name was Zuo Chen.
Zuo Chen was the reason that Zuo Ming had had a falling out with the other survivors from his clan.
Zuo Chen had been a Rank 2 Gu Master, much like himself at the beginning. He and a group of other followers had tried their best to survive in the wilderness, wondering how they could possibly restart their clan, until one day Zuo Chen had a fortuitous encounter.
He found the inheritance of a Rank 5 demonic Gu Master. Two other people had gone with him to explore that inheritance, but he was the only one who came out alive. Whether that was because he had killed them himself or because they had died while exploring the demonic Gu Master's inheritance was a mystery.
The problem was that it wasn't just a demonic inheritance, but that it was a Blood Path inheritance. Zuo Ming had pointed out that if Zuo Chen tried to cultivate it, he would end up drawing the ire of every single righteous and demonic cultivator in the Southern Border.
However, Zuo Chen had been rather charismatic and had convinced many of the others to side with him.
By this point, Zuo Ming had managed to reach Rank 3, and he separated from them, but his name was still associated with that group.
Because of that, he was also considered a demonic Gu Master by extension, even though all he did was live alone and try to keep to himself. He had no chance of joining up with a righteous path faction as an external elder because of this; a fact that he greatly resented Zuo Chen for.
"Greetings, junior brother," Zuo Chen said, as if there was no degree of animosity between them, but his eyes betrayed his murderous intent.
Zuo Ming backed away, only for someone else to block that part of the path.
"Zuo Lin?" Zuo Ming asked.
Zuo Lin was part of the group which had decided to follow Zuo Chen long ago, but now Zuo Ming could feel a Rank 3 aura coming from him.
"Relax," Zuo Chen said. "We're not here to fight you."
"Why did you sneak around like this then?" Zuo Ming asked, wondering if there were even more people waiting to jump in.
"Oh, we just thought that you wouldn't be that cooperative if we came knocking, we know how much you hate guests," Zuo Lin said, snickering. "But rest assured, we are just here to talk."
Zuo Ming did not believe that for a second.
But at the same time, he did not have the appropriate tools to try and escape. He didn't know what kind of gu worms that Zuo Chen had, but the main upside of the Blood Path was that it required relatively few resources.
It would not be out of the question for Zuo Chen to have a Rank 3 or even Rank 4 movement-type blood path gu worm. If that were the case, Zuo Ming would have almost no chance of escaping. For now...
"So, what is it that you want to talk about?" Zuo Ming asked.
"We wanted to make you an offer you can't refuse," Zuo Lin said.
"We wanted to invite you back into our group," Zhu Chen said. "I'm willing to bury the hatchet and forget your treachery and welcome you with open arms." Zuo Ming's mouth twitched - he had committed no act of treachery, he had just wanted to be left alone!
Zuo Ming snorted. "And just how many people remain in our group?"
Zuo Ming had his answer from how the two others faltered.
These two people were all who remained of the Zuo clan other than himself!
That was why Zuo Chen had come to recruit him into his group.
However, Zuo Ming knew that mingling with them would only bring ruin.
Getting involved in Blood Path matters, even tangentially, would be a death sentence. He had been forced to live in the woods like a hermit because of that, just because his name was associated with this group, after all.

chapters.title: Chapter 183 183: Blood Tiger: Part Three
chapters.content:
"We have a bit of a numbers... problem," Zuo Chen said. "However, we find ourselves in need of new members, and I think that you would find joining with us to be quite profitable. Junior brother, it is your good fortune that we happened upon you and happen to need fresh people to bolster our ranks. Else, you would be left here in the wilderness "
Zuo Chen did not say the "or else" part out loud, although it lingered in the air regardless.
"Relax, we don't want you to do anything too terrible. It's an easy job. We just need another Gu Master to make sure that things go smoothly," Zuo Lin said.
"What kind of job?" Zuo Ming asked.
"Have you heard of Qing Mao Mountain?"
Zuo Ming had heard the name once or twice. "Why? What of it?"
"There was a massive disaster that occurred there," Zuo Chen said. "They were attacked by a demonic Gu Master, apparently, and they are in dire straits. However, one of the villages atop there has managed to recover."
Zuo Ming could already tell what Zuo Chen was plotting. He wanted to extort them.
If the village had survived, it was likely not possible for a lone Rank 4 Gu Master like Zuo Chen to annihilate them wholesale.
That was why he would prefer extortion over direct violence.
"Exactly. See, you always had a good head on your shoulders," Zuo Chen said, smiling wickedly as he realized that Zuo Ming had caught on. "We just have to go there and knock on their door. Remind them how terrifying we are, and claim this as an easy payday. We'll even give you ten percent. How about that?"
"Ten percent of what? What makes you think that they'll surrender so easily?"
Zuo Chen laughed. "You've been living in a cave for too long, my friend. My reputation has soared throughout the Southern Border as the feared Blood Tiger! Not only that, I am a Blood Path Master now! Ah - and after the events on the mountain I doubt that they're eager to fight someone when they're barely scraping by."
Zuo Ming's eyebrows raised. To become a Master in any path was something almost unheard of for mortals.
Blood Path Gu Masters were dangerous as is, but if one were to become an expert in the Blood Path, he was extremely dangerous.
Merely dropping this as a fact would cause most Gu Masters to flee instantly.
"Why do you even need me then?" Zuo Ming asked.
"Because you being there would make us look better," Zuo Lin said. One Gu Master extorting the village was rather difficult unless they were Rank 5. Zuo Chen likely wanted the two of them as backup in case anything happened and also to increase the pressure on the villagers.
"No need to think about it too hard," Zuo Chen said, slapping Zuo Ming on the shoulder. "Just agree to join us, and things will go smoothly. You must be running low on supplies - right? We can fix those up for you."
Zuo Ming glanced towards another direction where he could run, but then ultimately gave up.
He wasn't sure how it was that these people had found him in the first place, but if they had been able to, they would likely be able to track him even if by some miracle he managed to get away.
He would need to make sure, however, that he disguised himself properly. "I don't want to use my actual name then."
"Oh, that's fine," Zuo Chen said. He, of course, would be using his own name simply because of the notoriety it generated. It was not worth taking half-measures as a demonic Blood Path Gu Master. Zuo Ming also wanted to wear a mask in order to hide his identity.
"Don't worry about the job, m'kay?" Zuo Chen said. "I've heard that the leader of the clan that we're going to target, the Gu Yue Clan, is a very kind and righteous man by the name of Fang Yuan - wet behind the years maybe, but very caring. He's a real bleeding heart who cares for the welfare of his clansmen. I know those types well - all we need to do is generate a small amount of noise, kill a few of his clansmen, and he'll likely pony up whatever we ask from him to save the rest of his villagers."
Zuo Ming doubted that it'd be so easy if they were trying to extort him to join them this badly, but he could only nod as they prepared to leave.
If there was one small benefit of being recruited by them, it was that he actually had something to eat.
The major downside, though, was that they had a long journey ahead of them.
Twice, they had had to attack mortal villages along their journey simply to feed Zuo Chen's Gu worms. There's a reason why the Blood Path was so reviled, after all.
Zuo Ming's stomach still turned at the memories of the screaming mortals as they were slaughtered wholesale.
Not even the chickens and dogs were left alive. Once again, Zuo Chen found no use in applying half-measures.
'What kind of crime did I commit to be forced to go along with these savages?' Zuo Ming thought. He wanted to see if there was a good chance to flee on their journey, but the other two watched him closely.
"You can go to sleep, leader, I'll keep watch," Zuo Ming volunteered.
"Nonsense, you need your rest - let your leader take that burden," Zuo Chen said, not falling for the obvious trick.
It was a long and hard journey, even with Zuo Chen's Rank 4 skills to help them. Nothing was as easy as it seemed out here in the wilderness.
"There's so much ice here," Zuo Ming noted as they reached the foot of Qing Mao Mountain. While most of the ice at the top had melted away, there was still quite a bit towards the bottom for some reason. "Was there some kind of freak snowstorm?"
"No, apparently, this was the action of a demonic Gu Master," Zuo Chen said. "Now, to the mountain! Let's get to work." They rested for one night at the foot of the mountain before ascending.
The village's hidden locations somewhat. However, there was only so much that you could do to conceal such a large group of people who had to move out and about.
Zuo Ming saw why it was that Zuo Chen had chosen to extort this clan and not the other two present on the mountain. It was the largest clan, and more likely to have something that was worth taking.
"Good news boss," Zuo Lin said. "It looks like the other two clans have lost their chiefs - there isn't a Rank 4 Gu Master with them. We might be able to sack them completely if we play our cards right."
"Hmm..." Zuo Chen thought to himself. It was highly doubtful that those villages would be entirely defenseless. They must have their trump cards if they had survived up until this point, and there was also the possibility of the leader of Gu Yue village coming to their aid if they were attacked.
For now, he did not want to do something so reckless. He was here to do an easy job.
While members of the demonic faction loved taking risks, he was not bullheaded enough to just launch himself into danger. Were that the case, he would've met his end quite some time ago.
"We'll see about that. Right now, let's spread some chaos! What did you find out about Gu Yue Fang Yuan?"
"You were right on the money boss, he's a very kind and caring village leader," Zuo Lin said. "The kind who would do anything for his village."
That was excellent news, as that meant that the likelihood of their plan succeeding was extremely high.
They decided to ambush a group of Gu Yue village Gu Masters while they were on patrol.

chapters.title: Chapter 184 184: Blood Tiger: Part Four
chapters.content:
Yu Sai took a glance at his new 'companions.'
He wasn't familiar with any of them, but with the recent events gutting much of the village's population, most teams were no longer intact.
Before, teams were usually divided based on the experience and age of their members in order to minimize friction between them as well as ensuring that proper nurturing of new Gu Masters occurred. Now, it was basically just whoever they could find for the job.
"What's got your mood so down?" one of his teammates asked. The man in question was in his early fifties and was probably the only one among them with a jovial look on his face. 'Glad to see someone's enjoying things,' Yu Sai thought.
"Nothing. I just don't really like going outside the village," Yu Sai said.
To be more accurate, he didn't like going outside his house either; going outside the village was a step further.
He also didn't see a reason for this mission. They were supposed to be going outside to scout things, though, from what he could tell, there was nothing to scout. Even if he didn't know what the actual cause of the ice was, it had killed most of the living things on Qing Mao Mountain. The few that had survived were not numerous enough to be of any threat to Gu Yue Village, at least not now. So why even bother sending them out like this?
"Oh, it's good to get some experience once in a while and some fresh air as well," the man who had been speaking to Yu Sai said.
"Or is this about something else?" another one of his teammates asked. "Judging from your age, is it about a lady, Yu Sai?"
Yu Sai tried to keep a poker face, but something must have given it away. "Aha, I knew it! So, it is about a girl. What happened? She rejected you or something? Don't worry, my lad," the old man said, with a dismissive wave. "With the current situation, we'll soon have enough mortal beauties to... satisfy us, if you know what I mean?" Then, he added, "Even I'm thinking of picking up a girl, or maybe two if they allow it."
Yu Sai shook his head. 'Oi! Aren't you too old to be lusting after young girls like that? Shouldn't you have learned some kind of restraint by now? Stop literally salivating at the thought, goddamn it!'
He wanted to say something, but someone else piped up before him. "Oh, stop it."
There was another member of their group, a man who had recently lost his wife and children. No doubt he didn't want to hear such talk.
The old man shrugged as they continued trudging along.
Their patrol was rather simple. It was only a short distance away from the village. They would go, examine the surrounding area, camp there for a night, and then come back to Gu Yue Village.
An easy enough mission in ordinary times. A Rank 1 Gu Master like Yu Sai would not have been picked for something like this; he would have been doing some kind of boring, but usually safer, logistical task.
However, there was a shortage of manpower, especially when one had to cover such large distances as the surrounding areas of Gu Yue Village.
'It's like walking into a wasteland,' Yu Sai thought to himself. He had not enjoyed the fact that he had been chosen for this mission, but with the current situation, Gu Masters no longer had the choice of rejecting a mission as they did earlier. Back in the day he could just decline missions and lounge around while his social standing degraded, not that he cared about that. Now, all missions were considered mandatory.
'What a drag,' Yu Sai thought. There really was nothing else beside the perimeter of the village. Without any Gu Masters to take care of them, the plants had pretty much all withered away from the cold, or wouldn't blossom until next spring. Since the plants were gone, none of the animals who fed on them, even if they had survived, stayed in the area.
And since none of the grazers were there, none of the prey animals were there either. In short, there was just a whole lot of nothing all the way from the village wall to the place where they were going to set up camp.
Once they reached the appropriate location, they then split up. Yu Sai was not asked to split up along with them, simply because he was Rank 1 and was asked to stay behind with their luggage. He didn't necessarily mind that, as he slumped down, trying to get his thoughts away from Li Mei.
Dinner was an unappealing meal of dried meat.
He couldn't help but remember that times Li Mei had made him something and was already missing her cooking.
This fact only made the dried meat taste worse, and he barely got any sleep that night.
Needless to say, he was rather tired when they woke up the next morning, finished their reconnaissance efforts, and then set out for the village. He was in such a mental haze that he was the last one to notice when it happened.
The man who was scouting out in front of them had a gu worm which allowed him to see much further ahead, and as such, was looking out for danger, even though there was basically none currently.
However, as he took two steps forward, a fountain of blood suddenly erupted from where his head had been.
It was clear that none of them were experienced fighters, because they were all slow to react.
Yu Sai had difficulty even processing what had happened. 'How had he died so quickly? What could have possibly killed him?'
The answer came soon enough, as a Gu Master leaped out from behind them. Two more leaped up from in front of them. Rank 3 and Rank 4 aura permeated from all around them, meaning that they were severely outmatched.
Yu Sai looked at what they were wearing. Nothing identified them as a member of any village, let alone one on Qing Mao Mountain.
As it was, there was no way that they were from the Bai or the Xiong clans. That could only mean that they were demonic Gu Masters.
"Well, look at what we have here," Zuo Chen said. "A couple of sheep ready for the slaughter!"
Finally, the oldest among them managed to get his senses together, and he ordered them to form up. What was the point of forming up against enemies who were this powerful, though? They were killed with barely any time to react.
Soon, it was just Yu Sai and another member standing there.
"I'm out of primeval essence - damn it! Kid, any cards you have up your sleeve?" the other Gu Master asked Yu Sai.
"I don't have any offensive Gu worms on me," Yu Sai muttered. It was true. He no longer had his Moon Gu.
"Are you serious?" the other guy said incredulously. He had not been expecting Yu Sai to pull out a miracle from somewhere, but he hadn't been expecting nothing either.
"Relax," Zuo Chen said, stretching his arms lazily. "We're not here to kill you, or at least we're not here to kill all of you. And, as it is, we do need some people alive. We have a message for your leader, Gu Yue Fang Yuan."
Yu Sai stiffened slightly at the mention of that name.
"Let him know that the legendary Blood Tiger, the Blood Path Gu Master who has slain countless villages, has decided to pay him a small visit. I looked around this mountain and thought that it feels like a nice place: nice scenery, nice weather, nice animals, nice living targets to practice my techniques on, you know... everything a man could want in a place like this. I was thinking of maybe even camping out here for a while. With that said, we could certainly be... encouraged to leave. Tell your clan leader that we want 100,000 primeval stones, three thousand Moon Orchid Petals, or else this kind of slaughter will continue."

chapters.title: Chapter 185: Blood Tiger: Part Five
chapters.content:
Zuo Chen then waved his hand around at the surrounding bodies and then glared at the two remaining survivors. "What are you all waiting for? An invitation? Get on and get to your village!"
Yu Sai and the other person suddenly came to their senses and high-tailed it for Gu Yue Village. The comrades they had left behind... they would have liked to bring their bodies and gu worms back to the village, but there was no way that they could do so at this time.
"Boss," Zuo Lin said. "How many people does it actually take to deliver a message?"
Zuo Chen smiled. "Only one." He then killed the Gu Master next to Ye Zan.
Yu Sai, to his credit, did not stop at all, not until he was at Gu Yue Village.
"Check their corpses if they have anything," Zuo Chen said.
While normally people would have detonated their gu worms, there's a chance that they had either forgotten to, or thought that their plan would be able to retrieve them.
"Nothing here," Zuo Ming said. They did have some primeval stones on them, as well as some food, but Zuo Chen was honestly disappointed by their haul.
"Do you even think they have something worth stealing?" Zuo Ming asked. From whatever they had seen, the surrounding area was rather barren. There might be a possibility that they were trying to get milk from a dead cow.
"Don't worry, I have no doubt that they must have something worth taking at the very least. Their clan head must have at least a modest treasure hoard," Zuo Chen said. "In the meantime, let's go relax and wait for the response."
Later, in Gu Yue Village, Ye Zan had already spoken about what had happened to the clan hall elders several times.
"How many people were there again?" The one who was asking this was Gu Yue Fang Yuan, who had just arrived.Chapters first released on novelꜰire.net
"There were three of them. One of them was a Rank 4 Gu Master, and the others were Rank 3."
Some of the elders' faces paled.
Demonic Gu Masters usually did not work together which was one of the advantages the righteous path had over them. The demonic path was a solitary path by its very nature, after all. One demonic Gu Master was bad enough, but a group of them was downright terrifying. Demonic Gu Masters tended to have greater battle strength than righteous path Gu Masters simply by the harsh nature of rising up the ranks of the demonic path.
To see that three of them had gathered to challenge and extort Gu Yue Village no doubt unsettled them.
"Can you describe what kind of gu worms they had or their techniques?" Fang Yuan asked Yu Sai.
Yu Sai stuttered- truth be told was that he had blanked out many of the details of the attacks and couldn't give much useful information regarding their enemy's battle strength or stratagems to Fang Yuan.
This encounter had been scarier than anything he'd had to deal with during the wolf tide, after all.
"There was just a lot of blood everywhere-" Yu Sai continued his nonsensical spiel before actually remembering something useful. "Wait- the blood- it started to move in an odd way once they were dead. Like it was flowing into a weapon before striking someone else."
"Blood Path..." Fang Yuan said. "Any information we can dig up on them based on their appearances?"
He had never heard of someone called 'Blood Tiger' before, but there were countless demonic and lone cultivators in the world. This person was likely a nobody who had died without much fanfare back in his previous life.
"No," Qing Shu said. "I've asked the other clans as well, the name isn't familiar to them."
Yu Sai was dismissed and the elders began talking among themselves.
"Who knew that it would come to this..."
"We were already short on manpower and now this happened..."
"Asking for 100,000 primeval stones, are they out of their mind?"
"There's no way we can agree to that - or else every single idiot will be at our doorstep asking for more..."
"Do not worry," Fang Yuan said, waving his hand, ending the meeting quickly. "I will deal with this."
It was a pity that the Tie Clan had not come by to investigate yet, else he could've used them as a pawn to deal with this person.
News of what had happened to the mountain had clearly spread to the point that now there were sharks circling the water. Whoever this demonic Gu Master was, they had clearly smelled blood and had, therefore, thought it was a ripe time to try to gain some benefits.
Fang Yuan could not really blame them. He might have tried the same thing himself in his previous life.
That didn't mean that he wasn't going to kill them. He only needed to be sure of their strength first, and to whether or not he needed to bring the Dollhouse with him when attacking them.
Fang Yuan made his way down beneath the underground cavern to the Dollhouse. "Greetings, senior brother!" the House Spirit called out to him as he walked in.
Fang Yuan made his way to Bai Ning Bing's room. Bai Ning Bing was still in somewhat of a depression. She did not want to go outside or show her face to anyone, and therefore had spent nearly all of her time lounging here, like some kind of jobless recluse.
"What is it?" she asked, seeing Fang Yuan walk in.
"I want to kill some people," Fang Yuan said simply. "I have a feeling you might be interested..."
Bai Ning Bing's pupils dilated slightly. There was nothing more that she enjoyed more than excitement, something that had been sorely lacking.
"And just who are these people?" Although she had very little attachment to the Bai Clan, she wouldn't want to go around wantonly slaughtering them.
"Idiots who think that they can extort me," Fang Yuan said, giving Bai Ning Bing a very short rundown of what had happened.
Bai Ning Bing frowned. "How are you going to find them in the first place?"
"I was going to ask you that question," Fang Yuan said. "Don't you have this Immortal Gu House? Don't you think it has a way for tracking them?"
The doll, the House Spirit, walked in at Fang Yuan's voice asking for it. "What is it?"
"Do you have any way of tracking someone?" Fang Yuan asked.
"There is indeed a way, but it's not very good," the House Spirit replied.
Gu Houses were usually dedicated to one certain aspect and could do that aspect better than they could other general things. Most Gu Houses could do things like healing, attacking, defending, and fleeing, all to some extent, but there was generally a specialization that they excelled at.
This Gu House was a Puppet Path Gu House, which specialized in sending out puppets for attack. Who knew what kind of tracking capabilities it had?
"I would need something, though, to narrow down our search," she replied.
"They have the blood of my clansmen on their hands," Fang Yuan said. If this had been him back in his previous life, there was a blood path method that would have solved this conundrum rather easily. However, he lacked the requisite gu worms right now.
The other issue was that many people in Gu Yue Village shared his bloodline as well. If he tried to use that kind of investigative method here, it would likely just lead him to a living Gu Yue clansman who had been sent out to do some kind of task, if not back to the village itself.
"I know!" the House Spirit said. "We can send out Tracker puppets after them, as well as Hunter puppets! They might be able to scout it out!" As she clapped her hands, other puppets began emerging from the recesses of the house. The Tracker puppets were dressed in simple clothes made of fur. The Hunter puppets, on the other hand, carried weapons with them whether being swords or spears.
"Get out and find these people!" the House Spirit said as the Hunters and Trackers saluted before marching out.

chapters.title: Chapter 186: Blood Tiger: Part Six
chapters.content:
Once he left the Clan Hall, Yu Sai immediately went back to his house.
Although the elders had tried to keep word from spreading, things eventually began to leak out, especially when, later that afternoon, they canceled most of their patrols and ordered many of their Gu Masters who had been sent out to turn back to the village.
Rumors of the other clans attacking were the first to arise; after all, that was the natural conclusion many of them would draw. However, it soon became evident that the other clans were not attacking and so the discussion went to other places. A fifth Myriad Beast King wolf? Some other kind of calamity that was near the village?
Or, as some of them considered, a demonic Gu Master.
But those were all rumors for now. Where were they going to get answers from?
Yu Sai, for his part, stayed in his house, trying to forget everything that happened. They certainly weren't going to get anything from him.
It had indeed been more brutal than anything he had seen during the wolf tide.
At least during the wolf tide, they had been able to fight back.
But before an enemy like that, not just him, they had all been powerless. 'Rank 4, huh?' he thought to himself. He had always known that he was worthless in the grand scheme of things, but it had been one thing to know it and another thing to have felt it like that.
He lay there on the floor, occasionally shivering like a puppy and at other times as still as a statue. He had not eaten anything since the morning, nor did he have any appetite to spur him to do so.
He didn't even notice when Li Mei walked in. "Yu Sai," she said, noticing his state with shock. "Your clothes, they're covered in blood!"
Yu Sai looked down at his clothes. Right. They were.
The blood of his comrades. He had only known those people for barely a day, and yet... he could not forget their faces.
He had been so entranced by the shock of all that had happened that he had neglected to wash himself. "Right, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to get the floor dirty," he said, apologizing before he got up.
"Forget the floor!" Li Mei said. "What on earth happened to you?" Her eyes were filled with worry, though that only seemed to paradoxically aggravate Yu Sai further.
"It's all fine," Yu Sai said, uninterested while pushing her away.
"What's that supposed to mean?" Li Mei asked.
Maybe it was the near-death experience that did it, but Yu Sai no longer felt that he could keep his feelings in check. So what if Li Mei laughed at him or told him that the two of them couldn't be together?
He had nearly died.
There was no guarantee that the next day would come in this world. He might as well go out with it.
"What I mean to say is, we're just friends, right?" he asked.
"Yes, we are," Li Mei said, confused. "Doesn't that mean we can share things with each other?"
"But the thing is," Yu Sai said, "I want to be more than friends with you, Li Mei."
"Yu Sai..." Li Mei stiffened.
"Yes, I know that you love Fang Yuan," Ye Zan said. "And I know that I can't hold a candle to him. However, I also... I think I'd feel even more like a worthless loser than I actually am if I never got my feelings across. I've loved you, even if I know that you don't return those feelings to me."
Li Mei clasped her hands over her mouth. These were the words that she had been longing to hear for some time. But where was all of this reluctance coming from?
"Yu Sai, Yu Sai!" Li Mei felt the same way about him. "I also love you... but the thing is, I never said anything because you always told me that love was a waste of time, that you would never want to get married because it was too much of a drag. So, I kept quiet."
Yu Sai looked at her oddly. "Wait, what do you mean? I thought you loved Fang Yuan?"
"I used to have a crush on Fang Yuan," Li Mei replied. "But that was a long time ago, back during our school days. I've seen what he's done and... I know that he isn't the right person for me, no matter how heroic he is." She tapped her chest. "I've fallen for another man. There's another person here in my heart. I've truly fallen for another one by the name of Yu Sai."
The two of them embraced, Li Mei not caring for the bloodstains on Yu Sai's robes.
"Now, tell me what happened," Li Mei asked. Yu Sai began narrating things. He tried to keep his voice straight and to keep a poker face like he had before the village elders.
However, he found that his facade soon broke under Li Mei's warm embrace, and he was bawling like a small child. Li Mei, however, did not rebuke him or shove him away. Instead, she only embraced him more tightly and wiped away his tears.
"Don't worry. Don't worry," she said. "What's important is that you returned home safe to me. And whatever happens in the future, we'll go ahead and try to tackle it together."
***
"We've gotten a response!" the House Spirit announced to Bai Ning Bing and Fang Yuan. The Hunter and Tracker puppets had returned, drawing a map on a piece of parchment where they had spotted the traces of the demonic Gu Masters.
It had taken them four hours to find the demonic Gu Masters. They were resting near an area by a pond, some distance away from Gu Yue village's normal routes.
"How many of them are there?" Fang Yuan asked.
"Three. One Rank 4 and two Rank 3 Gu Masters."
Yu Sai had said as such, but Fang Yuan wanted to be sure before going out into battle.
Bai Ning Bing was pacing back and forth near a hallway. She was restless, itching for a good fight. "Do you intend to take the gu house with you?"
"Hmm..." Fang Yuan considered things. Unless there was an Immortal backing these three, there was a low likelihood that they could deceive their methods. And taking the Gu House out was somewhat of a risk that he would like to avoid. "No. I'm confident we can deal with them on our own."
"Then let's head out!"
Zuo Chen was lounging near a pond. It was one of the few areas atop this mountain that still had some greenery- possibly because the local topography (a hill was near this pond) had shielded it from the frost.
'What kind of attack could do this kind of damage?' he wondered to himself. They said that it was a demonic Gu Master who had caused so much of the mountain to be frozen over, but he had never seen an attack like this before. If anything, the actual blow must've been far greater than what he was seeing, merely because a good portion of the ice had melted.
Zuo Lin and Zuo Ming were out scouting the area, but were still close by if they needed to group together to attack.Google seaʀᴄh novel·fire·net
"Hmph... what's this?"

chapters.title: Chapter 187 187: Blood Tiger: Part Seven
chapters.content:
Zuo Chen at first thought that there was something akin to a minor earthquake happening.
His investigative Gu worms were being set off by some kind of tremor.
However, that was all the forewarning that he received before he could react further or even think a breath's time more.
Something jumped out of the soil fifty paces away from him. He immediately paused, seeing that it was a giant spider, the Thousand Li- no, the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider. Rank 4 aura emanated from the gu worm and the Gu Master who stood atop it.
Zuo Chen looked around. He was not afraid of fighting, but naturally, against a single enemy, if he had the aid of those two, it would have been helpful.
'If only I hadn't sent them both out to scout the surrounding area. And if only Zuo Ming was more trustworthy, I wouldn't have had to send Zuo Lin to go and essentially babysit him.'
But there was no regretting that now.
"Good morning," the Gu Master atop the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider said with a gentle smile. Despite standing before a demonic Gu Master, his face was tranquil, as if he was simply going out on a morning stroll and admiring the weather today. "My name is Gu Yue Fang Yuan, and I am the Clan Head of the Gu Yue Clan."
"I had some idea that such might be the case," Zuo Chen said, relaxing a little. There was reportedly no other Rank 4 Gu Master on Qing Mao Mountain.
"I came here to discuss terms," Fang Yuan said. Zuo Chen had expected that. 'Quite bold of you to come here alone,' he thought to himself.
However, that was not necessarily true. There are countless ways of hiding, and Fang Yuan could simply be delaying him and waiting for reinforcements to arrive. There could be other Gu Masters hiding around the place. His investigative Gu worm was not as good as his others which is why he had nearly been blindsided by the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider, and there were ways that a single gu worm could be fooled.
"So, I take it then that you're here to express your willingness to surrender unconditionally?" Zuo Chen said, laughing.
"No, actually," Fang Yuan said. "My offer was completely different. Hand over all of your Blood Path Gu worms to me, and I might consider sparing your life."
Zuo Chen stopped laughing, glaring at Fang Yuan, who did not so much as flinch, still wearing the same calm expression on his face. "Do you really think that you can kill me? Me, a Blood Path expert, who is a Master in terms of attainment? The legendary Blood Tiger! You dare try to extort me?"
Whenever Zuo Chen mentioned the fact that he was a Blood Path Master to most people; their faces would pale and they would begin sweating bullets. However, Fang Yuan simply smirked and said, "Blood Path Master? How cute."
'So, you're bluffing.' Zuo Chen assumed.
Even though he himself was only Rank 4 Upper Stage and Fang Yuan was Rank 4 Peak Stage, Zuo Chen was fully confident in his own ability to win.
Cultivation level was not all that mattered when it came to fights, and the Blood Path was an excellent path when it came to combat. Not to mention, he had a trump card up his sleeve: a mortal killer move that he had invented after meditating upon the profundities of the Blood Path for much time.
Fang Yuan sighed. "How unfortunate that you wouldn't listen to reason, then." Fang Yuan gave no further warning before striking out at Zuo Chen, who immediately leaped back.
'This rascal,' he thought to himself. 'Attacking someone without even stating that they were going to fight, when they had been negotiating terms just a while earlier. Righteous Path hypocrite!' Zuo Chen still had his eyes not only on Fang Yuan but on the other parts of the battlefield as well.
Gu Masters like Fang Yuan wouldn't have come to fight him unless they were completely confident in their ability to win. He might be rumored to be righteous and virtuous, but that did not mean that he was an idiot. Meaning he probably did, as a matter of fact, have some kind of ace up his sleeve.
So, the best thing was to simply kill him as quickly as possible before he could use anything like that. Zuo Chen activated his killer move.
Rank 4 Blood Claw Gu, a gu worm that took the form of a pair of retractable claws around the Gu Master's fists, causing the enemy to hemorrhage heavily wherever they struck.
Rank 4 Blood Fangs Gu, which did the same, erupting a pair of fangs from the Gu Master's mouth.
Rank 4 Blood Agility Gu, a gu worm which greatly increased the Gu Master's speed depending on how much blood was stored within it. At Rank 4, it needed about 100 liters to show its full effect.
And finally, Rank 3 Bloodlust Gu. It greatly improved the offensive power of the Gu Master in question; however, it caused a corresponding decrease in defense. Not that Zuo Chen minded. His battle style was to go all out, to kill the enemy in a single strike before they could even react. His philosophy was that the opponent couldn't hit you so long as they were dead.
All of these Gu worms combined to form the mortal killer move - Blood Tiger!
He leaped at Fang Yuan, intending to separate his head from his shoulders.
His speed and strength were such that even a Rank 5 defensive-type gu worm would have difficulty defending against the blow.
Fang Yuan did have an answer for this however, retreating ten paces so that the first strike missed.
