"Is that so? I don't think so," Fang Yuan said. "It was very odd for him to target my brother specifically and to attack in the way that he did. Someone had clearly put him up to the job. More likely than not, one of the other two clans. However, we never got to the root of the issue. Have you really been unable to find any clues?" There was disappointment in his voice, which took the two of them abck.
But even if that was not why they were actually here, if they walked away without having completed the job in question, it would look like they were incompetent to some extent and Tie Xue Leng might end up losing face. "The issue," Tie Xue Leng said, "is that it's been a long time since the incident occurred. Many of that person's Gu worms are gone, and as such, there are no leads to go off of."
The person in question who was responsible, Fang Yuan's uncle, was dead and buried. So there really was no chance of them being able to unearth the culprit.
"Actually, we wanted to ask you about something else," Tie Xue Leng said.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ novｅlfire.net
"Oh, do please go ahead."
"It was said that there was a Blood Path Gu Master on Qing Mao Mountain before the attack of the Gu Master who wielded several cranes. Did you happen to know anything about that?"
"Perhaps the old Clan Head did," Fang Yuan said. "However, I only became Clan Head a few weeks before that incident, as I'm sure you're well aware. If there was a rumor regarding such, I..." Fang Yuan paused. "With that said, it's possible that Zuo Chen, the Blood Path Gu Master whom I killed recently, had scouted the mountain beforehand for some reason or the other, and that he only returned later on because he was familiar with this area. So, perhaps he was the Blood Path Gu Master you're thinking about?"
While that was a plausible explanation, neither of the Tie clansmen thought that that was the case.

chapters.title: Chapter 200: Tie Clan Investigators: Part Nine
chapters.content:
"Regarding this matter," Tie Xue Leng said. "Fang Yuan, I have a request of you. I would like to be able to access some of the clan's records. Of course, I realize this must be done in the presence of an elder. But we were hoping to find some information there."
Fang Yuan pretended to be in deep thought. In truth, there was nothing that he could really do to stop them. If he said no to Tie Xue Leng right now, the force of the Tie Clan might fall upon them. Fang Yuan knew that they weren't really here to investigate Lord Sky Crane but rather the rumors of first gen Gu Yue. With that said, he did want to appear that he was overly pleasing.
"To ask to look into our records is..."
"Ah, your village was the one who invited us in the first place to dig into things - but we can't do that without information, Fang Yuan."
"Could I give you the answer by tomorrow morning? I need some time to think about it."
"Certainly," Tie Xue Lang said.
'If I had been Rank 5 right now, I might have been able to pull a bit more weight,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. Rank 4 peak stage and Rank 5- there was a massive gap between the two of them, even if he could somewhat bridge the distance with the help of Human Path methods temporarily. No one would truly acknowledge him as being a Rank 5 Gu Master's equal.
That night, Tie Ruo Nan and Tie Xue Leng discussed their findings.
"Father, what do you think really happened?" Tie Ruo Nan asked. Despite interviewing several people in the village, she had not managed to come across anything that might lead to some kind of deeper revelation. "It seems that if there is anyone who knows what really happened, they're keeping quiet. Do you really think that there is something in the clan records which can help us?"
"We have no other choice but to attempt to do so as there is no other place to look," Tie Xue Leng said. "What are your thoughts up till now?"
"The biggest thing which bothers me," Tie Ruo Nan said, "is the layer of ice around the mountain. It doesn't seem to match with what happened with an Enslavement Path Gu Master." Gu Masters at one point would usually specialize in one path. And if this person in question had been an Enslavement Path specialist, it was odd for them to carry a gu of the Ice or Snow Path that could cause this level of destruction. It was not impossible, just highly improbable.
"In truth, I've seen something like this before," Tie Xue Leng said. In his long life, although he had not encountered someone else with the Northern Dark Ice Soul Physique, he had witnessed the aftermath of the explosion of a Gu Master who had the Myriad Gold Wondrous Essence Physique in his earlier days. "Was there someone on Qing Mao Mountain with an extreme physique?"
The most obvious candidate for that would be Gu Yue Fang Yuan. Advancement to Rank 4 was extremely rapid, even if he had been greatly nurtured by his clan and even with explanations like the Liquor Worm.
However, investigating a random clan member and investigating the Clan Head himself were two completely different things. If it was Gu Yue Fang Yuan who was behind all of this, it would be a tough nut to crack.
And that was disregarding the most obvious issue with this kind of thinking: if Fang Yuan was responsible for what happened on the mountain, how was he still alive? Resurrection was not unheard of, but was extremely difficult. And as far as he understood, even after resurrection, there would be the issue of him possibly detonating once again.
"You're right," Tie Xue Leng said. "The destruction which happened. It almost seems like it was from the detonation of a Northern Dark Ice Soul Physique."
Tie Xue Lang told his daughter about the ten extreme physiques in a few words. At first, while Tie Ruo Nan had been excited to hear this, her face gradually dropped. "But Father? Doesn't that mean that whatever happened on the mountain was completely unrelated to the crane-wielding Gu Master? It might have been just someone else within any of the three villages then."
Other than Gu Yue Fang Yuan, the only other notable, extremely talented Gu Masters included someone from the Bai Clan by the name of Bai Ning Bing.
This meant that their line of questioning was essentially going to hit a dead-end in that regard.
The net day, Fang Yuan agreed to their request, though he demanded to be in the room when they looked through the records. "And I can only allow you to see through relevant records."
"We might not know what's relevant or not until we see it."
"I can't let you see through anything, you have to understand," Fang Yuan said.For original chapters go to novel※fire.net
His 'resistance' was only nominal - the actual records were kept deeper underground which had many of the true details that were omitted in these. But if he didn't act like these were important, it might give something away.
"So be it," Tie Xue Leng said, going through recent records.
"Another elder killed by Bai Ning Bing..." Tie Ruo Nan noted.
"Yes, he had been quite the nuisance to our village back when he was still alive," Fang Yuan said.
The reason that Tie Ruo Nan fixated on this was because fighting people stronger than your own rank was said to be another identifying feature of the Ten Extreme Physiques.
'So it was him detonating that really caused the ice on this mountain...' she thought to herself. 'Why then would he say something else?'
"Lord Fang Yuan, did you happen to see the demonic Gu Master who attacked your village use a gu worm to encase it in ice?" Tie Ruo Nan asked.
"No, but I don't see who else it could've been," Fang Yuan said.
Tie Ruo Nan felt that there was something that she was missing here. She trusted Fang Yuan's words - a mistake, to be sure, but that meant that there were still unanswered questions.
Tie Xue Leng, meanwhile, was looking for anything that might be related to the clan having a Blood Path Gu Master, though he came up with nothing. Not even the slightest rumor - and of course he couldn't, first gen Gu Yue's secret was well hidden from everyone save himself.
"Not much more here," Tie Xue Leng said as the exited.
"Father, can we go back to Bai clan village? There is something that I think I've stumbled upon," Tie Ruo Nan said.
"Back there?" He couldn't see any link between the Bai clan village and this issue, but he was supposed to let his daughter take the lead when it came to this investigation. "Alright then, so be it."
The two of them traveled to Bai clan village to look for more leads. Tie Ruo Nan wanted to ask more questions about Bai Ning Bing.
"The clan's genius..."
"Very good with Ice Path Gu Worms..."
"And elder within a year of leaving the academy..."
"What did he look like, well, I don't have a portrait or anything but..."
"...say, doesn't Lady Ling Ding Ching look kind of like him?..."
"...you're right! Yes, that's the best example I can think of if you don't have a reference to go off of!"

chapters.title: Chapter 201: Tie Clan Investigators: Part Ten
chapters.content:
"Have you thought of something?" Tie Xue Lang asked. It seemed that Tie Ruo Nan had come to some kind of conclusion after interviewing the Bai clansmen.
"Yes, I see the puzzle pieces in my mind, but Father, I just can't seem to bring them together in a way that will make sense." She then turned to him. "Can I have your permission to use Cactus Pointer Gu?"
Cactus Pointer Gu was a Rank 3 Gu worm. It was a kind of Gu worm that could give the Gu Master who used it inspiration when they were stuck with a problem. It was a single-use gu worm and quite valuable for someone in their line of work.
"Are you absolutely sure? Because I only have one, and you will not be able to get another one if this fails," Tie Xue Leng said. "I want you to think about it very carefully. While the Cactus Pointer Gu can give you a small bit of insight into something you're unable to solve, if you start out with the wrong clues or don't have enough information beforehand, it might, on the contrary, lead you astray."
"I understand, Father," Tie Ruo Nan said. "But I don't think that we can get any further information from somewhere else. I think that this is the time to use Cactus Pointer Gu."
"If that is what you wish," Tie Xue Lang said. He removed it from his aperture. The Cactus Pointer Gu looked like an ordinary cactus with a small flower on top once it was mature. It started out as a seed that one would plant into the soil, and as one injected their primeval essence into it, it would mature into its full form as a cactus. The 'flower' on top was not an actual flower, but a folded piece of paper which would give the Gu Master insight into what to do further.
"All right, let me try this," Tie Ruo Nan said.
"Think of what you wish to ask," Tie Xue Lang said.
The seed bloomed into a cactus with a flower on top of it. Tie Ruo Nan removed the flower, after which the gu worm began shriveling immediately and then died off within a matter of seconds. On the piece of paper was a single word written on it. That word was 'frogs'. To someone else, that might not have meant anything; however, to Tie Ruo Nan, it was what she needed to put the pieces together.
"I've got it!" she said. "Lady Ling Ding Ching is actually Bai Ning Bing!"
"How did you reach that conclusion?" Tie Xue Leng asked, startled.
"You see, Father," Tie Ruo Nan said, "the rumors that people were concerned about demonic Gu Masters putting chemicals in the water, making the frogs gay, were not unsubstantiated. There's a reason why Lady Ling Ding Ching looks similar to Bai Ning Bing. That's because he somehow happened to be exposed to those same chemicals, but in a large quantity, thereby turning him into a woman." Tie Ruo Nan was not finished, however.
"Bai Ning Bing detonated on Qing Mao Mountain and died, or at least that's what we thought. However, what if there was a way to save him? The demonic Gu Master who must have been polluting the water with those chemicals might have found Bai Ning Bing after he detonated. He had a way to bring Bai Ning Bing back, but it involved copious uses of those chemicals. And that's why he was experimenting with those chemicals in the first place, because although they might feminize a person, they would also be able to bring them back to life! This is all the result of demonic Gu Master experimentation."
Tie Ruo Nan took a deep breath as she ended this monologue. Tie Xue Leng looked out into the distance. Before, he had just been thinking about it, but now this confirmed it.
He really had wasted the Cactus Pointer Gu, and Tie Ruo Nan was led completely astray by the rumors on Qing Mao Mountain. 'How does any of this pertain to the Blood Path demonic Gu Master that we were supposedly chasing?' was a question which still remained in his mind, which he wished to ask her.
Her eyes widened when posed with that question.
"Well, that you see, Father..."
"Even if Lady Ling Ding Ching is Bai Ning Bing..." "Tie Xue Lang said, "How does that change anything?"
"Uh, that is..." Tie Ruo Nan began to say before clutching her head in shock. "Ah, Father, I realize I got sidetracked there!"
Tie Xue Leng sighed. His daughter was clearly still inexperienced and needed to learn more about the world, and that's fine. This was a very complicated case anyway. "Perhaps I shouldn't have given it to you as your first case. Allow me to take the lead now."
For the next few days, he continued investigating on his own. Although he didn't get much further, he did, however, scout the surrounding area and was able to find his way into the Blood River Graveyard.
'What a peculiar place. This is without a doubt the signs of the Blood Path.' However, while it was a sign of a Blood Path Gu Master having been there at one point, there are no traces of anyone having been in this place for a while. It was built some distance away from the Gu Yue Clan's primeval spring. However, that in itself did not mean anything.
Ultimately, despite their investigation, they were unable to find anything concrete, at least not without more drastic measures.
"I think that it's time we leave Qing Mao Mountain - I don't think that we can uncover anything, not without potentially tearing the mountain apart," Tie Xue Leng said.
"Right, father," Tie Ruo Nan said. "I'm just sorry about everything..."Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on novᴇlfire.net
"Don't apologize - the journey to becoming a true hero of justice is long and filled with countless ups and downs. I have not succeeded in every mission that I took. You mustn't let this deter you," Tie Xue Leng said.
"That's right father- I'll do better next time!" Tie Ruo Nan said.
"And just remember, simply because a lot of people are saying it - doesn't mean that it is true."
Tie Ruo Nan still thought that there was quite a bit of weight behind her theory that Ling Ding Ching was Bai Ning Bing only exposed to chemicals causing him to become feminized, but she didn't want to argue with her father any further. As it was he was right about one thing - even if they were right, it would not change the status of what they had been called here to find.
"What did you think of Gu Yue Fang Yuan?"
"He does look as heroic as they say but," she began. "There's something off about him. Something... cold and distant."
Tie Xue Leng also agreed there was something odd with him - but that was hardly enough for him to justify staying her to dig deeper into matters.
With that, the Tie clansmen headed off of Qing Mao Mountain.
"Good riddance," Fang Yuan said. His brother was still a bit downcast that they hadn't found anything - Fang Yuan himself had been wondering whether they would've found the person who hired Lord of Mysteries or not, but there was no answer on that. His brother, however, would have something to look forward too soon - advancing to Rank Three!
Now, he could finally get to getting some actual work done.
Starting with getting himself to Rank 5 first of all! Enough time had passed, and he had accumulated enough Human Path dao marks to make another try worthwhile.

chapters.title: Chapter 202: Breakthrough To Rank Five
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan was sitting opposite to Bai Ning Bing. They were using Equality Gu once more. The increase in Human Path Dao Marks had made a significant difference to its effectiveness while using it this time.
Speaking of Human Path Dao Marks, other than the five Human Path Dao Marks per day, the Goody-Two Shoes System had been rather silent recently.
Very few rewards were being handed out as compared to before, though today he had received a notification saying,
New Main Mission Unlocked!
Rank 5 Cultivation Rank
Description: Advance to Rank 5
Reward: ???
Now, with Equality Gu's heightened power, Fang Yuan felt his aptitude rise: first to 90%, then 95%, then 97%.
Both of them were sweating heavily as their free hands fumbled with the scales of Equality Gu at times.
Fang Yuan was no stranger to pain, but it was becoming unbearable even by his standards.
Bai Ning Bing too was feeling the nastiness of using Equality Gu for so long. However, she didn't want to be the first one to say that she couldn't continue further. Ever since venturing out into the world under her newfound identity and obtaining the Bai clan's ancestral inheritance, she had become bolder and did not want to lose that to Fang Yuan in this regard.
Right now, Fang Yuan had a hold over here because he had the Yang Rotation Gu, as well as control over the gu worms in the Dollhouse. If they fought over the latter, he could detonate them all at will, even though she was supposedly the 'true inheritor' Fang Yuan was not about to let something like this slip out of his hands. As such, to maintain some form of control, Bai Ning Bing didn't want to appear inferior to Fang Yuan in any way, shape, or form.
Finally, however, she realized that she could not continue any further.
"Fang Yuan, that's enough," she said.
Fang Yuan was also at his limit; if it had gone on for even five breaths of time longer, he would have been forced to withdraw. Then again, this took a greater toll on him than her since he also had to power up Equality Gu.
He took in a couple of deep breaths now that he had removed the effect of Equality Gu the pain began .
'Perhaps I had been a bit too greedy,' he thought to himself. His body felt sore all over, and the kind of pain that Equality Gu inflicted was not the kind that was very receptive to Doctor Gu's treatment. If it was going to make it difficult for him to concentrate on trying to breakthrough to Rank 5, it might have been worth it to abandon its use a while earlier so the subsequent breakthrough would be easier.
However, there was a reason why he had done so. With every percent increase in aptitude, especially at the higher levels, it could make a massive difference. It could be the difference between breaking through or not breaking through; breaking through within three days or five days and also in the amount of primeval stones one would have to spend to do so. Even if he was clan head, there would always be competition for resources, and it wasn't like he had limitless primeval stones.
Right now, his aptitude sat at 98%. He had used a great deal of primeval essence in order to power up Equality Gu, and now had to use primeval stones to rapidly increase his reserves. Even as he was doing so, his aptitude slowly started to decline.
With using Equality Gu more often, he had managed to learn a few more things regarding how it functioned. For one, the rate of decay of aptitude after one had used it was not constant; it was higher the greater one's aptitude was compared to their actual aptitude.
As such, by the time he had managed to fully replenish his primeval sea, it had already dropped down to 97%, but from experience, he knew that this would hold out for at least another 14 hours until it went down to 90%, which was more than enough for him to attempt to break through.
To break through to Rank 5 needed 90% primeval essence to break through on your own without external help, though it was still somewhat possible depending on how many primeval stones one had at around 80% or so.
His deep golden-yellow essence assaulted the walls of his aperture. The crystal walls began cracking, with the cracks rapidly expanding under the deluge of a 97% aptitude. Any progress he had made before this day had already vanished given the gaps during which he could not cultivate.
So that he could continue cultivating without having to rest, Fang Yuan was using several Gu worms that reduced one's need to sleep, eat, and drink. He had managed to get many of them from the Dollhouse.
And while the House Spirit had been somewhat upset that he had removed some gu worms from it, ultimately, there was little she could do unless Bai Ning Bing herself protested. Bai Ning Bing, for her part, went back to the Bai Clan while Fang Yuan continued cultivating.
Much as he had expected, by the time his aptitude dropped down to 90%, about 14 hours later, he had made a massive deal of progress.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ .net
'This time, things are different,' he thought to himself. 'This time I can indeed break through to Rank 5.'
More and more of the deep golden essence assaulted the walls. The rate of recovery of his aperture walls was slowly but surely going to reach the point where it would outpace the damage he could do. However, that was why the first assault that he had carried out at 97% was so important. Because although the rate of damage he was doing was higher in the beginning, the aperture walls also had more damage to recover from.
After four more hours had passed, his aptitude had dropped down to 87%, still more than enough in his experience to get through so long as he kept up at it.
Another 24 hours of non-stop cultivating later, after which his aptitude was now 80%, the final push was made, and the crystal walls of his Rank 4 aperture finally broke and small droplets of deep purple primeval essence began to condense, mixing in with what golden-yellow essence was left.
Main mission complete!
Advanced to Rank 5!
Reward: A dream realm has been added to your inventory.
Would you like to explore it now?
Fang Yuan stopped cultivating and nearly collapsed from the strain this had placed on his body.
Doctor Gu emerged from his aperture, examining Fang Yuan.
Fang Yuan felt like he was about to pass out. The room that he was sitting in was spinning around him, and dark edges seemed to be forming at the corner of his vision.
He had cultivated non-stop, not even stopping to eat or drink, which is what had made this possible within 48 hours. If he had tried to take breaks, it likely would have taken much, much longer. Each moment that you were not cultivating was giving this output your time to recover and for his aptitude to be pleased. There's no way that Fang Zheng could do something like this. Otherwise, he would have been able to reach Rank 3 back before.
"Oh dear, young master," Doctor Gu said, examining Fang Yuan. "It looks like we have a problem."
"What... kind... of problem?" Fang Yuan asked between deep breaths.
"The issue lies with your stomach, I daresay. I've been examining your kidneys. Unfortunately, despite how old you've gotten, they haven't evolved into adultneys, you see!"
Fang Yuan: ...
Dr. Gu had said the joke in order to see whether it might cheer Fang Yuan up, but it looked like he had instead been so bad that Fang Yuan had indeed passed out.

chapters.title: Chapter 203 203: Mysteries of the Immortal Puppet Master: Part One
chapters.content:
As it was, Fang Yuan did not have any injuries on his body that Doctor Gu could say anything about it, so he simply called the House Spirit for some food.
The way that Human Path gu worms ate could be very odd indeed. Although they looked human, they were not bound by the same rules of physiology as people. Doctor Gu needed a lot of cooked rice to function, and the way he ate it was by unhinging his jaw and opening his mouth impossibly wide - like how some snakes ate, before stuffing it down his gullet in one go.
"Thanks for that."
"No problem," the House Spirit said. Feeding the gu worms in the Dollhouse had been something that Fang Yuan had been worried about, but most of them fed on human qi or had easy feeding requirements. The house had many food path gu worms and had its own stored food supply as well as puppets like Chef Gu that could assist with the house's feeding.
Once Doctor Gu was done eating he simply went back into Fang Yuan's aperture.
Six hours later, Fang Yuan awoke still feeling very tired but he needed to show his face to the clan by this point. Otherwise, strange rumors would begin to circulate about him dying or something or the other.
He looked outside. It was actually in the middle of the night as he emerged from the clan's underground storage. The guard who was stationed in front of the Clan Head's Pavilion was awake - no one would dare sleep if they were guarding this place - and saluted to him as he walked in.
Fang Yuan woke Fang Zheng up. "Oh, who is it? Brother, you..."
"Yes, I'm done with my closed-door cultivation," Fang Yuan said. It was only then that Fang Zheng noted his Rank 5 aura.
"Oh wow, Brother! So you succeeded! That's fantastic!"
"Yes, I did," Fang Yuan said. "I'm going to sleep now, and don't wake me up unless it's something important. Feel free to tell everyone in the morning that I've reached Rank 5, however."
"As you say," Fang Zheng said. Fang Yuan went to sleep and awoke in the afternoon the next day, feeling fresh but extremely hungry. He asked for some food.
"Good news, Brother!" Fang Zheng said, walking into his room. "The Xiong Clan have finally decided to submit to us!"
Fang Yuan did not say anything, but he had been expecting this.
The moment word got out that he had reached Rank 5, the other clans must have known that their time was soon up.
The only thing was that the Bai Clan felt that they could hang on longer to their independence because they had a new external elder with them who had managed to gain the approval of their old ancestor. While they could see the writing on the wall, they probably wanted to wait things out so that they would have greater leverage down the road.
Fang Yuan could pressure Bai Ning Bing to bring them under the Gu Yue Village's wing right now. However, there was no need to do so currently.
The next few days were quite busy as the logistics of how the Xiong clan would be assimilated into the Gu Yue clan needed to be worked out. They had their own elders who would be accepted as external elders.
The Gu Yue Clan had many elders, but even if they outnumbered the Xiong clan, the Xiong clan still had three of them. That was more than enough to make its own tiny faction within Gu Yue Village's political system, which naturally the other elders did not want.
For that matter, the other elders were somewhat disappointed to hear that Fang Yuan had reached Rank 5 - not those in his camp, of course, like Qing Shu and Han Lin, but the others who had bemoaned their lack of authority.
Given how much Fang Yuan wielded near-absolute power, with time as the village improved, although it was a good thing, it also carried the downside of decreasing his influence. The more stable the village was, the less he could unilaterally make massive decisions like trying to assimilate the Xiong and Bai clans.
However, that changed now that he had become Rank 5. It was a qualitative change that put him head and shoulders above all of the other elders. Just at Rank 4 peak stage, there was nothing that they could really do to him, even if they tried to gang up against him.
At Rank 5, it was completely out of the question. Normally, there would have been a large feast and ceremony celebrating Fang Yuan as the third Rank 5 Clan Head within the clan's history. Many people had bemoaned the fact that the clan's bloodline was thinning away with time, and that the fourth gen Clan Head had died without leaving any offspring resulting in such a scenario. If he wanted, he could order a massive military parade or the like in his honor.
However, he had ordered that such things be kept short.
It had been one thing regarding the funeral- that would have been for the sake of the other villagers.
However, he had no desire to massage his own ego with a grand festival. As it was, this was only the beginning.
'And now that I am at Rank 5, it is only the beginning,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. 'I still need to refine the Righteous Virtue Physique, or find a way to possibly obtain the Ancient Moon Desolate Yin Physique, before I ascend to immortality. As long as my foundation is good, the rewards of becoming immortal will be even greater.'
The Spring Autumn Cicada, his vital Gu, was still quite weak. What he had done last time, by forcing it to travel back a few weeks, had depleted any signs of recovery that it had made up until that point. Its leaves were back to their withered grayish state and its body had lost the luster it used to have.
With his new Rank 5 aperture, he could contain its Rank 6 power for longer. He estimated that it would be about five years before it reached the point where he would be forced to advance because of its recovery. That was assuming that he didn't enter some place like a blessed land, of course.
Although he was kept so busy in the next few days that he could not resume cultivating, that did not mean that there were not other ways that he could improve his battle strength.
The reward for advancing to Rank 5 had been a dream realm, but he still thought that he had not fully recovered from his breakthrough to Rank 5 to do that. Without proper rest his soul would be even more vulnerable to damage if he happened to fail so he was putting it off for now.
So, he instead focused his attention on mastering the Puppet Path. The creator of the Dollhouse mentioned in his own records not by name but as 'The Immortal Puppet Master' had been a Human Path Gu Master when they had been a mortal. Once they had advanced, they had begun forming an entire, the Puppet Path, a very niche path which combined the Human Path and Enslavement Path.

chapters.title: Chapter 204: Mysteries of the Immortal Puppet Master: Part Two
chapters.content:
The creator of the Dollhouse had left a great deal of information regarding his findings on the Human Path, as well as the Puppet Path.
There were multiple Human Path killer moves, as well as refinement recipes for certain Human Path gu worms. The majority of Human Path gu worms, however, was noted to come from a Human Path Immortal's aperture as per what Fang Yuan could find out.
As for the Puppet Path, a good deal of the creator's findings were kept in his 'true' inheritance, but even the small amount which was left here was of immense help to a mortal.
It was to the point that Fang Yuan had now achieved quasi-Master level attainment in the Puppet Path simply from studying this information. He had initially relied up on his will stored in the house to study it for him which was quite convenient as it could do so even when he was busy; but found that consumed too much of it and that he had to start looking at things himself since he lacked the methods to replenish his will. Since he had Grandmaster level attainment in the Human Path and Master level in the Enslavement Path from his prior life, the two of them had combined together along with this information to bear this quick advancement.
Still, he had to continue practicing if he wanted to get any further.
A room filled with 100 puppets stood in front of him. Puppets were a strange kind of Gu worm. Although they looked very much like Human Path Gu worms, such as Doctor Gu, which was kept within his aperture, they were different in a few key ways.
One was that they had no gu worm form of their own; they simply remained as puppets constantly. Secondly, they did not require feeding in the traditional sense.
However, they required a large amount of primeval essence to be active and to move about. Given this, it was not possible for most mortals to use the Puppet Path to any real extent because of the amount of primeval essence that was needed to command them.
This distinguished it from the Enslavement Path. Although the resources needed to feed one's army would be large, primeval essence expenditure was usually at a minimum. Each animal in one's army was a soldier, but that soldier did not require primeval essence, only food. Not so with the Puppet Path. Conversely, so long as one had enough primeval essence, say, they were an Immortal - they could easily make a mortal puppet army with great strength.
So long as the puppets were within the Gu House and acting as per the Dollhouse, they were being powered by the drop of grape green Immortal Essence that Fang Yuan had managed to obtain from the system.
However, those that he took outside and had given to the clan members to use had to be powered with their own primeval essence.
Fang Yuan could only command about five or ten of them at once, depending on what rank they were.
Unlike something like Grass Puppet Gu, which might have 'puppet' in the name, these could not be produced by continuously using primeval essence. How had they been made then? There was no information regarding this from what Fang Yuan could find, and so, if he wanted more puppets he would need to discover the owner's true inheritance it seemed.
The reason why he had gathered 100 in this room, regardless, was simply to get a handle on how to actually command them without using his soul directly. He instead wanted to see if he could exploit their intelligence that mimicked those of humans.
He did not need to control all of them directly. As long as the Dollhouse controlled them, and he controlled the Dollhouse, he could still give them all verbal orders, and they would understand and respond.
Much like with enslaving animals, although there weren't any Beast Kings or the equivalent, he could find several of them and make them 'officers', so to speak, giving them authority over the others.
It would then make his job easier to command them so long as he spoke to those officers.
The puppets' intelligence, therefore, was a double-edged sword; although they could understand instructions far more clearly, it also meant that there was occasionally some pushback. They might misinterpret commands. Some of them were like Doctor Gu and had strange eccentricities.
'Once I become an immortal, this might be useful,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. As a mortal, one could only use a handful of puppets. As an Immortal though, their intelligence could be exploited to manage one's aperture. He could have them perform small tasks such as overseeing resources or managing inventory as a workforce without worrying about them betraying him.
As they did not need to rest or eat, they were far preferable to slaves. Which made Fang Yuan wonder why they were not more prolific when it came to Immortals - back when he had been a Rank 6 Blood Path Gu Master, the slave market was quite profitable in Yellow Treasure Heaven. Yet, he had not heard of anyone using puppets to make their work easier.
Was it because that the Puppet Path was kept secret and confidential? Or was there some other reason behind it?
He searched through his memories during his prior life, and he had only heard the term 'Puppet Path' thrown about once or twice, no further details of it. Not only that, but there were no significant figures who used it. It might have been a very esoteric path, but you would expect some kind of news from somewhere. He even knew more about the Food Path than he did the Puppet Path.
"Line up!" Fang Yuan yelled out.
The puppets fumbled a bit at his instructions before he clarified - "I mean, make rows!"
They did so as he desired, though not without there being some slight chaos as they bumped into each other looking for a spot.
'That was quite slow,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. He would need to clarify his intentions beforehand. "Alright, assemble yourselves by order of height. Make it so that the shortest are on that side of the room, and that the tallest are on the other side."For original chapters go to novel_fіre.net
The puppets looked around at each other, confusion on their faces as they struggled to do what he told them to do.
"The person on your left should be shorter than you and on the right should be taller than you," Fang Yuan said.
He felt like Sun Tzu when asked to train the Emperor's concubines for battle - only that he knew there was no solution like killing off the commanders here. He didn't want to damage the puppets as he didn't know how to repair them.
They finally did as he said, standing proudly. One of them coughed and another one couldn't seem to help but break into giggles.
And when that puppet started laughing, so did the others until laughter echoed throughout the room. If they had been actual people Fang Yuan would've punished whoever did so, but they were all gu worms - what was the point?
'I feel like I am missing some crucial aspect here,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. "Alright, I want you to pair off against one another!"
The puppets found partners and stood in front of them.
"Back away so that there is at least five paces's worth of space between the two of you," Fang Yuan said. "And then bow."
They did as he told them too.

chapters.title: Chapter 205 205: Mysteries of the Immortal Puppet Master: Part Three
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan continued to instruct the puppets for a while, but gained no new insight regarding how they worked. He left the dollhouse, passing by the House Spirit on the way. "Any update on the actual true inheritance?" Fang Yuan asked.
The House Spirit shook its head. "Senior brother, I don't know about the details of the true inheritance, only that when the requirements are met, the location will reveal itself to the inheritor."
The House Spirit could very well be lying, but there was very little Fang Yuan could do to try to extract the information from it. If it had been instructed not to reveal something until certain requirements had been met, then it would not do so. House Spirits were rather straightforward like that. As it was, he was not even the current inheritor of the house; it was Bai Ning Bing, though she also had not found anything.
Given the fact that it was an Immortal inheritance, Fang Yuan highly suspected that being an immortal was likely part of the process, or that there was a requirement so cumbersome that only an immortal could fulfill it.
The rest of the inheritance, including the Immortal Puppet Master's Blessed Land (or Grotto-Heaven, depending on its cultivation rank), as well as the gu worms required to turn this into a proper Rank 7 Gu House, were extraordinarily valuable to him.
Compared to the Dao Marks he was getting right now, this was the second most valuable thing that he had. There was no way that he was going to let it slip from his hands! It was more valuable than the Three King's Inheritance that would be opening up in a few years, or that of the Hu Immortal Blessed Land in the Central Continent.
Even now, it served as an excellent deterrent against any mortal threats.
***
Two Xiong Clan Elders approached the gates of Gu Yue Village. Accompanying them were some of the more promising Xiong Clan Rank 2 Gu Masters. There weren't many of them left after the events on the mountain, but with their most promising talents having been some of the first to be killed by Lord Sky Crane they had to make do with what they had.
The elders were here in order to negotiate the terms of the Xiong Clan fusing into the Gu Yue Clan. Assimilating smaller clans was not unheard of, but it was usually done via violent means when one clan had nearly annihilated the other. Many cultivators would prefer to 'pull out the grass by the roots,' eliminating all of their enemies.
However, there were times when this was not possible or preferable. The Xiong Clan in this case had willingly submitted, and as such, they also had to be treated better as per the decorum of the righteous path.
A young man greeted them at the gates. He had a plain face and deep, dark eyes. His Rank 5 cultivation was immediately apparent when they approached. This was Gu Yue Fang Yuan. He had come here to negotiate this deal on his own for the simple matter that the mere presence of a Rank 5 Gu Master would greatly hasten the process. Also, it was good for them to feel his Rank 5 aura on their own, lest they think that they had been deceived in some way by the news that was no doubt spreading about his cultivation.
"I greet the Xiong Clan Elders," Fang Yuan said with a gentle smile. The Xiong Clan Elders quickly recovered from the oppressive Rank 5 aura, cupping their fists, and then Fang Yuan did likewise. Fang Yuan had come with two other elders with him.
Neither of them were technically from his faction, but that didn't matter. Those from his faction were busy with other things and it was these kinds of people that really needed to be told that they
"Come, let us take a tour of the village before we settle down." As the Xiong Clan ambassadors traveled through the village, one thing stood out to them above all others.
Not only was the village far stronger than their own, not only was it in a better state than their own, and not only were the people more content and hopeful than their own, it was the presence of the numerous puppets around the place which was the most striking.
'They look creepy' was a common sentiment among the Xiong members when they saw them. The puppets were designed to be like oversized dolls, meaning that their heads were far larger than the rest of their bodies, and they had massive eyes, nearly as big as one's fist. Perhaps mortals might find this sort of thing to be cute, but the thing was that, given the fact that they were moving around, some of them even talking, it gave them all a very uncanny feel.
"These are all of your clan's puppets?" one of the Xiong Clan Elders asked casually, when seeing a puppet who was repairing one of their roads.
"Yes, these are treasures left behind by our ancestor," Fang Yuan said. "They've been quite helpful in the repair of the village."
While there were several things that puppets could not do, there were many menial tasks that they could be assigned to. It was almost like increasing the workforce of Gu Yue Village several-fold without having to invite other people, though this did come with its own downsides.
Many of the Gu Yue clansmen saw the Xiong clansmen while they were walking. In earlier times, if any of the foreign clans had come to Gu Yue Village, there might have been something akin to a show of strength between the two.
Given the fact that the Xiong Clan prided themselves in their Bear Strength Gu, this would usually be contests of strength.
Gu Yue Chi Shan had been rather good at those before he had passed away along with the rest of the Chi Clan. This, however, was a far more somber affair. When the Gu Yue clansmen saw them they were initially startled, but when they saw Fang Yuan among them they immediately realized what was going on and did not panic.
Fang Yuan led them to the Clan Head's Pavilion where they would be staying for the next few days. This was considered something honorary to the Xion Clan ambassadors, but could also be considered to be a case of 'keep your friends close and your enemies closer.'
The Xiong clansmen could not speak freely while in Gu Yue Village. When it came to Gu Masters, there were numerous ways of spying on people, and in a place like the Clan Head's Pavilion, which had been prepared by the Gu Yue Clan, there was no way that they could speak without wondering if they were being eavesdropped on.
Fang Yuan did not think that the elders would be dumb enough to reveal anything. However, there were some more inexperienced members among them. They would normally not have been trusted with this kind of mission, but due to the clan's deficiency of manpower, they had no one else to choose from.
These Xiong clansmen were not wrong in their paranoia to think that the Gu Yue Clan was spying upon them. Fang Yuan had spies and investigative gu worms scattered all throughout the Clan Head's pavilion, hoping that one of the more inexperienced members might end up leaking something to him.
For now, though, he continued to play the part of gracious host as they sat down for dinner. Back in the day, this may have been a more elaborate affair, but the Gu Yue Clan's resources were not as bursting as they used to be. From reports that he had gotten about the Xiong and the Bai clansmen, many of them seemed to have been showing signs of malnutrition, meaning those two were in even worse of a state.

chapters.title: Chapter 206: Clan Assimilation: Part One
chapters.content:
The specifics regarding how the Xiong Clan would be integrated needed to be discussed. There were a number of issues. For one, they did not want to change their names, which might lead to friction in the future. However, Fang Yuan was fine with that.
Right now, given how many more Gu Yue clansmen there were, they would eventually be assimilated into the village at one point or the other, within a few generations. As for the recipes for their Beast Strength Gu, while they were willing to hand it over, they were demanding a price as an initial upfront investment.
"When we're already doing you a favor by allowing you into our village, why this sort of price?" Fang Yuan asked.
"Lord Fang Yuan, we might be coming into this village, but we will not have resources that we would otherwise need to start up properly," the Xiong Elder said. "We would need some kind of founding seed in order to ensure our future prosperity within the Gu Yue Clan. Please understand. A price of 100,000 primeval stones is quite the bargain, actually, for our signature recipes." The Xiong Clan was worried about being ostracized when they joined Gu Yue Village - but even were that the case, the one thing that someone could rely upon were resources. They were intending to use this as a foundation whereupon to nurture future Xiong clansmen. The price was high, but given the fact that they were handing over several Rank Two recipes and gu worms was not necessarily unreasonable.
The two sides began haggling over the price well into the night before deciding to resume the negotiation in the morning.
As for his spies, Fang Yuan did manage to find out something rather interesting from them later that evening. One of the Rank 2 Gu Masters had brought along his younger sister, a Rank 1 Gu Master, and the two of them were talking near a hallway.
"Primeval stones? Are we asking for them?"
"Yes, we did. 50,000 as a matter of fact."
"That's good."
"Do you think it'll be enough now that our primeval spring-"
"Shhh!" the other brother said, not wanting her to say something else.
Fang Yuan was able to discern something from the conversation, namely, that the Xiong Clan's primeval spring seemed to be dying.
Since the three clan's spirit springs were located in different areas, it made sense that the damage to each one was slightly different. The Gu Yue clan was located at the top of the mountain, where 'Man's Triumph Over Nature' was most effective. The Xiong Clan, at the foot of the mountain, still had to deal with the ice until this day as well as hazards like mudslides.
For that matter, Fang Yuan was not even sure if the Gu Yue Clan's primeval spring would continue to flourish. It seemed to be showing signs of recovery, but that could very well just be wishful thinking on the clansmen's part. All that could be said based on his own assessment was that it was holding steady - neither declining nor getting better significantly. It was only with time that one could tell if it would really recover or not.
This was just the confirmation he needed, however, to help him orchestrate his plan.
The next morning, as they gathered to negotiate, Fang Yuan requested to speak to the other Xiong Clan elders alone.
To their surprise, Fang Yuan even sent out the elders of his own clan when negotiating. He did not say anything for five minutes, letting them stew while wondering what it was that he was up to as he sipped his tea.
"Hmmm..." Fang Yuan began. "I sent everyone out as there is a matter that is rather sensitive. I don't think that you would want it slipping out either. Namely, regarding your primeval spring."
The elders began sweating. Had news managed to slip out? How - they had only found out about a month back? Did someone betray them?
"Lord Fang Yuan, please understand our position - the price of our Bear Strength Gu can be negotiated."
Fang Yuan waved his hand. "No matter. I don't intend to use this method in order to force any kind of change in that price. If you want, you can sell those recipes at 50,000 primeval stones."
The elders were dumfounded for a moment.
Such generosity?
Fang Yuan's righteous nature truly shone through even now wh-
"There is something else entirely I am interested in," Fang Yuan said, interrupting their train of thought. "Namely, the Xiong Clan's secret Rank 5 methods."
"Ah - Lord Fang Yuan, I'm afraid that we don't entirely understand what you're talking about," one of the elders said nervously. There was no way that news of that could have possibly gotten out - Fang Yuan had to be bluffing.
"Back when the wolf tide was near its peak," Fang Yuan said. "The plan of the Xiong Clan was to hide themselves if the Lightning Lycan King happened to strike, deceiving it with your Rank 5 methods and allowing us to take the brunt of it, no? Thankfully I dealt with that problem without involving your clansmen, but to think that you were thinking of such a dirty trick..."
The elder's expressions froze.
What the hell?!
How could he possibly know this?Follow current novels on Nov3lFɪre.ɴet
There were hardly any elders on their side who happened to know about this plan. While it was somewhat feasible that news of their primeval spring dying leaked out, this was incomprehensible.
Fang Yuan's expression changed from being gentle to being rather domineering.
Fang Yuan was using memories from before he had used the Spring Autumn Cicada to his advantage here. Although he had advanced to Rank 5, what was a Rank 5 Gu Master without a Rank 5 gu worm? The Gu Yue clan had lost its own Rank 5 gu worms thanks to first gen Gu Yue - that Blood River Python could've been quite good now, but it was dead.
Fang Yuan could refine one himself. But it was more profitable to simply extort one.
"If I do nothing and reject your offer," Fang Yuan said. "Imagine what happens to your clan - without a spirit spring even if I do nothing the Bai Clan will make its move. Or someone else like Zuo Chen will come knocking on your doorstep. Your clan will truly be finished given enough time."
The elders were silent. They might have been seething - but they were considering what to do next.
That Rank 5 method was their clan's trump card - if the Gu Yue clan tried something even after they had joined, it would be one of their few assurances that nothing untoward might happen. A last resort of sorts.
However, not only would they be handing this over to the Gu Yue clan, but they would be giving it to Fang Yuan, someone who could fully make use of it being at Rank 5. It was handing their enemy a weapon that could be used against them. It was not a matter of primeval stones but of power.
"A wise man submits to circumstances," Fang Yuan said simply. "Take your time to think about it."
"Fang Yuan, I think we have offered up enough," one of the elders retorted. "Surely there is no need to go this far?"
"Why, what you can you keep doing with your Rank 5 method anyway?" Fang Yuan asked. "Won't you still have problems feeding it? No doubt you intend to leave certain people behind to take care of it and make sure it has sufficient sacrifices. But how long can that continue? Isn't it better that the Gu Yue clan take it off your hands and feed it instead?"
Fang Yuan left, allowing them to stew regarding the current situation. He was already certain of what their answer might be.

chapters.title: Chapter 207: Clan Assimilation: Part Two
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan's guess had been incorrect, the Xiong Clan did not cough up their secret the next morning.
Instead, given the oppressive offer, they first tried to reach out to the Bai Clan to see if they could strike some alliance with them. Given how powerful the Gu Yue clan was, their only hope of even offering a token resistance is if they worked together.
No matter how bad a second option was, it was, at the very least, an option when it came to negotiating so that one could not be extorted for that first option. If they had even the semblance of something else that they could do, Fang Yuan would not be able to bully them so.
They delayed negotiations, but Fang Yuan had an answer for this as well.
"What do you make of this?" one of the Bai Clan elders asked.
"Hmph!" Bai Ning Bing said during their meeting.
"Lady Ling Ding Ching, you don't think that this is worth considering?"
"Why would we? It's clear that they are desperate and this is a death rattle of a dying clan," Bai Ning Bing said. Her eyes flashed ruthlessly. "If anything - we should go ahead and use this to our advantage!"
Even though 'Bai Ning Bing' had only been an elder for a while, she had already dominated the Bai clan's political system. She was the strongest Rank 3 Gu Master there, at Rank 3 Peak Stage, her Rank 5 gu worm notwithstanding. If she managed to reach Rank 4, there would be no doubt that she could become their clan head immediately despite being an 'outsider.'
Faced with this kind of domineering personality, the remaining Bai clan elders felt a spark of fear - which was somewhat uncannily familiar in a way. It was as if Lord Bai Ning Bing had returned to them, only slightly mellower.
The Xiong clan elders nearly coughed up blood when they saw the response from the Bai clan.
'You're demanding our Bear Strength Gu recipes for free and 20,000 primeval stones upfront in exchange for our help?!'
This was even more outrageous than Fang Yuan's demands.
'Oi! What are you thinking? Can't you see how strong the Gu Yue clan is? Is this really the time to extort us? Can you not see Mt. Tai? Once they are done with us they'll come for you next!' - that was what the Xiong Clan elders felt.
When seeing someone bullying someone else, rather than siding with the victim, you chose to help the bully instead!?
"No wait..." one of the elders said. "What if... the Bai Clan and the Gu Yue Clan are already in cahoots?" It explained everything going on.
"You don't mean..."
"If the Bai Clan has agreed to assist them in tormenting us, what can we do?"
Both of them cursed their fates, but soon realized that there was nothing to do.
Two days later, Fang Yuan was standing near the mouth of a deep cave near Xiong Clan village.
It would've ordinarily been covered with ice, however, the Xiong Clan had taken great pains to clear this area.
"So this is where your Rank 5 secret is kept?" Fang Yuan asked.
Both of the elders nodded.
Fang Yuan approached the entrance of the cave, noting the bear bones that littered it. Whatever gu this was, it was bear-themed, fitting in with the history of the Xiong Clan.
Fang Yuan walked in cautiously, on guard for traps. Although he was strong, he did not have full Rank 5 strength yet for the lack of gu worms. His investigative methods told him there was something buried deep within the cave, only what that was was unclear.
It was only when he went in some distance that he saw it.
"This is our Rank 5 secret at the hear of our clan," one of the Xiong clan elders said.
Fang Yuan took a look at a gu worm that took the form a giant bear's mouth that had seemingly embedded itself into the cave.
Rank 5 Bear Stomach Hibernation Gu!
Although it was called 'Bear Stomach', and the inside of the gu worm very much felt like that, it did not have any digestive liquids within it. Instead, it emulated the way that bears hibernated. It opened up into a space where people could hide out and weather any passing storm. Once it closed its mouth, it would fuse with the cave and be nearly indistinguishable. It was an inferior way of hiding in a Blessed Land, mildly put.
Fang Yuan had thought that their method had to be some kind of stealth-type gu worm, but this was, as a matter of fact, a storage-type gu worm being used in a way that
It came in a Rank 3 and Rank 4 variety as well.
Fang Yuan: ...
"I see, thank you for showing me this," Fang Yuan said.
The two elders were speechless.
Didn't he want to take this gu worm from them? That was what they had initially thought his intentions were.
However, Fang Yuan quickly realized the impracticality of this gu worm.
It had one major weakness - it took far too long to set up; several hours as a matter of fact. That had been fine for the Xiong Clan when they needed to hide as they planned it from beforehand. Not only that, it could not be moved casually and needed very specific gu worms to do so. The Xiong Clan ancestor did not intend for it to be moved anyway, only for his clan to use it.
For Fang Yuan's purposes though, it simply would not do.
It was not like taking it was entirely a win for Fang Yuan. He would need to feed it, and also there was the aspect of refining it in the first place. He no longer had an 'auto-win' button in the form of the Spring Autumn Cicada - it could make refining this gu worm somewhat easier but it would still take copious amounts of time and effort that were not worth it.
It really would be easier just to refine a Rank 5 gu worm himself!
'All of that scheming for nothing...' Fang Yuan thought.
But it couldn't be helped.
In his previous life he had once fought off two other Gu Masters for an inheritance only to finally realized that it had already been taken by the time he got to the end of the inheritance.
Extortion was not always successful - he had 'failed' in this endeavor because he had not know the true nature of the Xiong Clan's secret. If he did, he wouldn't have bothered with this in the first place!
It was like breaking into a 'bank' back on Earth, only to later realize far too late that it was actually a sperm bank. What were you going to do even if you had the cashier at gunpoint?
This was still useful to the clan, but he could let the Xiong Clan keep it for now. If he ever had need of it in the future, it was a simple matter to extort them for it.
With that done, they finalized the deal between their two clans. It would still take some time, but the Xiong Clan would start to become integrated with the Gu Yue clan. They sent a trickle of people first - only about twenty, and would increase it as time went on. One of their elders accompanied them and sat at the elder's meeting of Gu Yue village as an external elder.
Even if his extortion had somewhat failed, he had still succeeded in his original mission.

chapters.title: Chapter 209 209: Fang Zheng's Advancement: Part Two
chapters.content:
The Legends of Ren Zu, Chapter Five, Section Thirty-Nine
After struggling for a long time, Ren Zu had finally found Self Gu once again.
Even if Self Gu was extraordinarily small, Ren Zu and his children were delighted upon having found it. Their journey, which had gone on for so much time, had finally come to fruition. So what if Self Gu was tiny and insignificant in the eyes of Heaven and Earth?
For humans, there is nothing more important than being able to recognize oneself.
However, they had very little time to rejoice.
As after they had managed to obtain Self Gu, they found themselves sinking into the block of floating truthful ice that they had been standing upon. "What? What's happening?" Ren Zu yelled out as he, Carefree Wisdom Heart, and Great Strength True Martial all fell along with him inside the block of floating ice.
"What is this? What's going on?" Ren Zu wondered, staring at Self Gu.
"Oh, human," Self Gu said, "You recognized yourself, and still have me. So long as you have me, how can you possibly look at the truth objectively? You have sunken into the situation instead of being able to observe it. In order to observe the truth, one needs an objective outside perspective. One who has no sense of self."
Now that Ren Zu had found Self Gu, he had sunk into the block of truthful floating ice. Thankfully, the inside of the block was not fully filled up. It only partially filled up inside spherical ice, which was surrounded by a crystal wall. That gave them some room to move about, but only slightly.
Great Strength True Martial immediately roared in anger before he started striking out at the crystal wall, attempting to break them with his fists. However, he found that even if he damaged them, they slowly began repairing themselves. Whatever cracks he made in them healed over. "No matter how fast I make these," he said to himself, "I cannot break through them in time, even with my ability gu."
Rules and Regulation Gu called out to them. Both of these gu worms were still outside the sphere of truthful floating ice, but had been able to avoid being trapped within the floating ice. So long as one understood Rules and Regulations, they could not be easily bound.
"Oh, Great Strength True Martial, you are very strong and can break through almost any situation, and that is why, as per the rules and regulations of Heaven, the situations you have to encounter will also be even more difficult to get out of." While the weak envied the strong thinking that they could break out of any situation, it was not so! The stronger one was, oftentimes, the greater the problems they would face in life.
"The crystal walls are too strong, brother," Carefree Wisdom Heart said, examining the wall, looking for an egress out of there. "While using Practice Gu, you made the walls of this ball of truthful floating ice too strong. Now, you can't get out of them because you made them too tough!"
Oftentimes, the worst situations that one had to face were caused entirely by oneself.
Ren Zu gnashed his teeth in frustration. 'How can we get out of this?' He looked for Cognition Gu. However, Cognition Gu had already gone to help Myriad Wondrous Gold Essence with her predicament regarding Blazing Lightning Glory Brilliance.
The ball of floating ice continued to flow along the River of Time.
"Father, if we abandoned Self Gu, will we be able to emerge from here?" Great Strength True Martial asked.
"Nonsense!" Ren Zu yelled, "We went through all of this trouble just to find Self Gu, did we not? How could we possibly abandon it at this crucial juncture? We would all end up going back to square one."
It was easy enough to say that one should be detached from one's sense of self in order to see the truth. However, in practice, it was extraordinarily difficult. What kind of human could truly be detached completely from their sense of self?
A voice came ringing from outside the ball of truthful floating ice. "Hahaha! Did I not tell you, human, that you were bound by Heaven and Earth? I have decreed that you will never be reunited with your other children, and so will be the case!"
Ren Zu recognized this voice immediately. It was Fate Gu. Fate Gu had planned all of this all along! The crystal walls of this block of truthful floating ice were meant to restrain them, to keep them trapped here forever.
As the three people inside thought of what to do, coming up with no solution in sight as the walls of crystal could repair themselves faster than even all three of them could damage it even with their efforts combined together, a voice emerged. "Let me out! Let me out!" a voice cried out from somewhere beneath them.
"Who is it?" Ren Zu asked.
"Who am I?" the voice answered. "I am someone who wants to see the entire world. I want to explore every single nook and cranny of it. I want to accumulate every single coin of wealth this world has. I want to read every single book and absorb every single page of knowledge that there is in this world. I want to soar higher than the heavens. I want to burrow deeper into the Earth than anyone has ever done before. I want to swim in the seas and explore every single drop of water that there is within its depths. I wish to be with my family, to have countless wives and concubines, and to completely cover the Earth with my descendants. I wish to live forever. I want to be able to soar beyond the boundaries of this world and see if there is anything beyond it. In short: all I want is everything!"
After some searching, the three of them found the source of this voice. "This Gu is huge and magnificent!" Great Strength True Martial said. He saw a massive flame somehow still surviving inside the ball of ice.
"No," Renzu said, "It is only medium-sized."
Carefree Wisdom Heart disagreed with both of them. "It is extremely tiny, but still warm."
"Oh, Gu, what kind of Gu are you?" the humans asked.
"I am Ambition Gu," the gu replied. "I was born from Great Strength True Martial's Heart of Ambition!"
Depending on one's skills and aptitude, depending on one's wishes and desires, their ambition could be either large or small.
For Great Strength True Martial, an expert, his ambition could consume the whole world.
For Ren Zu, his ambition was simple - to reunite with his children.
For Carefree Wisdom Heart, her ambition was the smallest of all - only wanting to help her family.
Ambition Gu rose up from the floor and seemed to radiate anger as it glared at the crystal walls. "How can such things restrain me? How can the will of Heaven possibly restrain me? Oh, human, use me! And let us break through this prison of crystal together!"
Ren Zu took Ambition Gu, and it launched itself at the crystal wall of the sphere of truthful floating ice. It started to develop cracks within it, which started being larger, getting bigger and bigger.
This time, the crystal walls did not repair themselves, and soon enough they were able to shatter it and climb outside the sphere to the outside world.

chapters.title: Chapter 210: Another Awakening Ceremony
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan had not heard of Beauty Gu, only that it was mentioned in passing sometime during his earlier life.
He had plans to try to integrate it within the Dollhouse to make it a Rank 6 Immortal Gu House, but that would have to wait until he was an Immortal.
As for Ambition Gu, its effects were not very clear. From the story, it seemed to help Gu Masters in breaking through the crystal walls of their apertures. However, it was an Immortal Gu - that seemed like a wasteful thing to have at that point. Or was its use more metaphorical?
Many of these issues would only be solved once he underwent Immortal ascension.
***
Once Fang Zheng had gotten up and recovered somewhat from breaking through to Rank 3, Fang Yuan called upon him.
"Oh, elder brother, what's going on?" Fang Zheng asked, wondering why he was here visiting him this early in the morning. Fang Yuan also looked like he was dressed up for some kind of grand occasion.
"Oh, you've been cultivating for so long... did you lose track of time?" Fang Yuan asked him. "Today is the Awakening Ceremony."
"Oh wait, that's today?" Fang Zheng thought.
News of him becoming an elder had still not spread throughout the village, but this was, without a doubt, more important. Fang Yuan announced to his brother his advancement to Rank 3 in the underground cavern.
"Everyone, I've got news. We have a new elder with us: Gu Yue Fang Zheng!" The other elders congratulated him briefly before the events of the Awakening Ceremony began.
Normally, there would be a bit more pomp and circumstance, but his advancement had coincided with the Awakening Ceremony and that took precedence for the time being. Any celebration could be done afterwards.
Still, Fang Zheng was not too upset about this. He had matured to the point where he no longer felt he needed recognition from other people; he knew he had advanced to Rank 3 and had done something great, which was more than enough for him.
"All right, then, let the Awakening Ceremony commence," Fang Yuan said.
'There are so few people here,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. He cast his mind back to his own Awakening Ceremony.
There had been a hundred or so hopefuls gathered on the other side of the spirit spring.
Now, however, there were only 23 youngsters. In addition to these 23 youngsters, though, there were 10 people who were far older: seven women and three men.
These were the mortals whom Fang Yuan had decided to give a chance to open up their apertures. Seeing how anemic the new class was, he could understand why.
Although Fang Yuan had opened up this opportunity to everyone, for now, there would only be opening it up to 10 people in order to still maintain original Gu Yue clansmen as the majority.
As it was, given they were mortals and did not share the first gen Gu Yue Ancestor's bloodline, it was expected that out of these 10 people, at maximum, maybe four or five would become Gu Masters.
Fang Yuan had his own reasons for trying to expand the clan.
For one, the more blood relatives he had, the easier it was to use - Blood is Thicker Than Water.
Secondly, it made collecting human wills either to use Hope of the Clansmen and for refining Hope Gu.
Third, he had a new mission.
New Main Mission Unlocked!
Village As Before
Description: Increase the Gu Yue clan's size to its prior numbers.
Reward: The daily Human Path dao marks you have for being clan head will be increased to ten.
Double the reward... without a doubt that was enticing.
He stood near a large platform. Fang Zheng took a glance at him. 'Just a while back it was us who was down there, wondering what the elders were thinking.' So much had happened since that Awakening Ceremony - so much that he still felt like it was an odd sort of dream. If someone had told him what the future was going to hold he wouldn't have believed them during that time.
Qing Shu glanced at Fang Yuan. "Who should go first? The mortals or the Gu Yue clansmen?"
Fang Yuan pondered the question for a moment before saying, "Let the Gu Yue clansmen go first!"
He still had to maintain the image that the Gu Yue clansmen were being treasured above all, and this was the best way to ensure it.
The youngsters nervously stepped forward as Qing Shu called out their names. The first hopeful found that he could only move three steps - he was not a Gu Master, and could only return to his family, ashamed.
Fang Zheng watched this all with a sense of apprehension. Although it wasn't him undergoing any of this, he couldn't help but feel a great deal of pity for all of them. With a chuckle, he remembered how he had tripped over his own feet before he had been encouraged to walk as far as he could. At that moment, he had felt mortified, but now, he could easily laugh at his former self.
No one did anything like that now, though some of them looked like they were close to it.
"Gu Yue Luo Mei - C grade talent!"
"Gu Yue Shi Lin - D grade talent!"
Many of the Gu Yue clansmen had not talent at all, and when all was said and done, there were only C and D grade talents in this new batch. Not even a single B grade talent could be found.
"What is going on here?"
"Only one in two had the capability to become a Gu Master..."
"Has the bloodline really thinned so much?"
Fang Yuan's best guess was that most of the children with talent had been killed in the fight with Lord Sky Crane - and it was only because of their bad luck that they had been left with these kinds of people. When there were usually only one or two B-grade and higher talents per class, it was easy to see how pure, random chance could lead to this kind of skewed result.
Still, his main problem was one of numbers, and they would do well enough to bolster them.
Now, the question moved on to the mortals.
They had been specifically selected after several rounds of vetting. After all, they were Fang Yuan's own pet project and if anything went wrong it would reflect badly on him. These were people with no reason to despise the clan, and were all hard-working. Additionally, there was an age limit - none of the men were over forty and none of the woman were over twenty-five. He had also not chosen any woman who already had living children.
Seven out of ten of them had no talent. The oldest among them, a man who was forty years old, happened to awaken his aperture and was found to have D-grade talent. It was bottom-of-the-barrel aptitude, but the man looked like he had just struck gold, eyes shining with newfound hope.
So what if he would have to adopt a Gu Yue clansmen? He could still find a mortal wife, and have children of his own! The fact that none of the other men had succeeded only made his victory, no matter how tiny, all the sweeter!
In one swift moment, his fate had greatly changed!
The other two people who were successful among the mortals were woman. Both of them were C-grade talents, but one of them was more promising than the rest as her aptitude was at 55%. This was technically still just C-grade in terms of talent, but was at the cusp of where one could potentially advance to Rank 3. This woman with long eyelashes actually had the highest aptitude out of everyone that had been tested today.
'We will need to keep an eye on her,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. As it was, with the restrictions he placed, her growth would be severely limited until the point where the clan would already begin recovering.
This ceremony had been for lack of a better word, rather boring. Without the usual faction fights between the Mo and the Chi clan given they were gone, there was no political maneuvering to watch, and none of the youngsters were promising. One could only look forward to next year's batch.

chapters.title: Chapter 211: Taming the Crimsonhoof Deer: Part One
chapters.content:
All in all, things seemed to be going smoothly, Fang Yuan noted.
On the political side of things within Gu Yue Village, there was very little for him to do.
Although he was experienced in such matters, things were basically falling into the palm of his hand to the point where even someone like Fang Zheng could've done this job.
His own faction was emboldened now by the presence of another elder joining its ranks; Fang Zheng.
Any attempt by the others to form a counter-faction was muddled by the fact that there just weren't enough of them, and the fact that Fang Yuan had reached Rank 5 in terms of cultivation.
It had really turned into a 'you're either with Fang Yuan or against him' political situation.
In a way, it was kind of boring for someone like Fang Yuan, who was used to navigating complex political issues. Still, he wasn't going to complain about things being easy, and despite things being easier than normal, he still did not have much free time on his hands given all that he had to do.
This was the great paradox of the righteous path: in order to advance, you needed resources, for which you would need to maintain a high rank within the organization. However, to maintain a high rank within the organization, you also needed to contribute to it. Right now, Fang Yuan had reached Rank 5.
He was, without a doubt, contributing far more to the clan than he got out of it, especially given the clan's anemic state. Were it not for the fact that the Goody Two-Shoes System was giving him Human Path Dao Marks, he would have abandoned the place entirely, as it was only the Dao Marks which made this venture profitable to undertake.
Now that the new academy students had been selected after the Awakening Ceremony - they had 12 Gu clansmen and 3 mortals totaling 15 students, a far cry from the usual number which reached the fifties.
After some discussion, it was decided to teach the mortals along with the Gu Yue clansmen, though the mortals would have to find some way to fulfill their obligation before the year was over. In other words, the two women were currently looking for Gu Yue clan husbands and the man had adopted an infant.
There would no doubt be some kind of friction between the Gu Yue clansmen students and these mortals. In later years, when the Xiong and Bai clans also integrated into the Gu Yue clan, they would have even more problems.
However, that was why the position of Academy Elder needed to go to someone capable of handling such a thing. And it was here that Fang Yuan found himself faced with an issue: who could he entrust to be Academy Elder?
Since there were only 15 students this time, and because none of them were A or B grade in aptitude, none of the elders could see any profit in becoming the Academy Elder. The position usually went to someone who was interested in the field, that is to say, someone interested in molding the minds of the future generation. However, none of those present had any sort of inclination or experience regarding that.
Fang Yuan's hands were somewhat tied here.
He could not send Fang Zheng, as Fang Zheng had just become a Rank 3 Master and was not yet capable of teaching others the intricate details of Gu Master cultivation yet given he had barely grasped them himself.
Qing Shu could have been an alternative as he had the experience to do so. However, Fang Yuan relied upon him greatly, and sending him away to a different position would make him even more burdened with clan duties.
As for Han Lin, although he was experienced enough, his health was declining, and he would not be able to have the energy to go about the day-to-day duties of the academy.
The other elders waffled on the issue. The Medicine Hall Elder, of course, could not be sent. None of the others wanted to take the job, even with Fang Yuan increasing the Academy Elder's allocation of resources by 25% and then 30% as an incentive.
Fang Yuan could've forced them, or did some kind of political maneuvering to guide them into this position - it was not that they were impossible but those things took far too much time for his liking. Not to mention would it be worthwhile to send someone like that to teach the new generation - someone who might have a reason to despise Fang Yuan and possibly cause issues with the integration of the mortals who had been allowed to cultivate? He needed to find someone willing to do this role.
Finding someone from outside the clan was, of course, unthinkable for this kind of role. This person had to guide the future minds and talents of Gu Yue Village. How could they possibly trust it to someone from, say, the Xiong or Bai Clans?
Fang Yuan, of course, could not take the job himself.
With little other choice, he ultimately decided on picking an unconventional choice.
"Clan leader, you called?" a Gu Master approached the door to the clan head's pavilion.
"Indeed I did," Fang Yuan said, turning to Gu Yue Ye. He had paid little attention to the man during their prior encounters when he had asked for Vitality Leaves, but he could find some use for him here. "I have a possible job for you, if you'd be willing to take it."
"What kind of job?" he asked rather apprehensively. The man did not want to offend Fang Yuan, but at the same time was worried about what 'job' this would be. He had been wanting Vitality Leaves to preserve his own life, after all.
"If I'm not wrong, before your children died, you must have taught them yourself," Fang Yuan said.
"Indeed I did..."
"Hmm. Then could you continue to train other Gu Masters?"
"I... I can do so, yes."
"The position of 'Academy Elder' is currently vacant, though there are only 15 students this year," Fang Yuan said. "Would you be willing to take the job?"
Gu Yue Ye's eyes lit up. A job away from the frontlines and fighting? Of course he would want it!
The Academy Elder position was sometimes seen as nothing more than a glorified babysitting gig with little in the way of advancement - though people who wanted to teach would agree to it regardless.
