To an actual elder, this was not worth the hassle. To an ordinary Gu Master, however, it was a dream job - very safe and many of your needs would be provided for.
"With that said, since you're no longer an elder," Fang Yuan continued, "the position will be known as 'Academy Head' for now and the benefits will be adjusted down accordingly."
Gu Yue Ye's face fell slightly - but this was not a big deal for him. It was too much to expect to be compensated as much as an elder when he was only at Rank 2. Fang Yuan had to make this distinction as well as changing the name of the position simply to placate the current elders that they were not having their own benefits eroded.
"I thank Lord Clan Leader for this opportunity, I will not let Lord Clan Leader down," Gu Yue Ye said.
Some of the elders protested this appointment as well as the parent's of a few of the new students. The parents were appeased easily upon knowing that Gu Yue Ye had been a former elder at some point, and for the elders this was a minor concern.

chapters.title: Chapter 212 212: Taming The Crimsonhoof Deer: Part Two
chapters.content:
With this matter settled, and with Fang Zheng beginning to become more accustomed to his duties as a clan elder and absorbing some of Fang Yuan's responsibilities, Fang Yuan turned his attention towards his own cultivation. There was that dream realm that the system had given him that he wanted to look into. But before he could do that, a messenger arrived at his doorstep. It was odd for someone to come this late in the evening, which meant that it must have been urgent.
"Clan head, permission to enter?"
"Come in!"
"Lord Clan Head, I pardon the intrusion, however, you have asked to be notified of this the moment that it happened."
What's going on?" Fang Yuan asked. There were a number of emergency issues that he might be notified of at any time. Say, a Demonic Gu Master who had appeared near the village, or some powerful Gu worm, like the River Swallowing Toad, or had the Xiong Clan pulled some sort of odd political maneuver.
"The Crimsonhoof Deer was spotted at a location one day ago."
Fang Yuan's eyes widened. He had instructed all the Gu Yue clansmen to tell him if the Crimson Deer could be found. He had thought that it was likely that it had died after Bai Ning Bing's detonation, and if not from that, then perhaps from starvation. However, it looked like that mutant beast was not that easy to get rid of. It had managed to survive, though none of the scouting Gu Masters dared to go anywhere near it.
"All right, this is good," he said. "You may leave," he said to the scout. Although he did not have Rank 4 Deer Enslavement Gu, that did not mean that there were no ways to enslave the deer in question. There was only one Immortal Enslavement Gu after all, and yet Gu Immortals regularly enslaved all kinds of creatures.
Before, Fang Yuan had not had the appropriate cultivation level, nor the required gu worms to do so. However, now with preparation, he had a way of binding that Rank 4 beast using a Blood Path method.
A warm breeze washed past his face, signifying the first signs of an early summer.
The ice was almost completely gone by this point from Qing Mao Mountain.
In this scenario...
The next day, Fang Yuan left the village atop the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider. He told the villagers that he needed to deal with this Rank 4 Beast King.
None of the elders objected simply because this could potentially be a threat to the village. Fang Yuan knew better, of course. The Crimson Hoof Deer was not an overtly violent animal, although it was, without a doubt, strong. But this was a good enough pretense for him to leave the village to bring the deer back.
He found its tracks. And from there, he was able to use a Blood Path method to discern its location. He still had a small amount of blood left over from his earlier refinement of it, though it was too small to detect anything that was further away than ten li.
"There you are," Fang Yuan thought to himself as his wings burst from his back.
The Crimson Hoof Deer was not doing very well. Its ribs were showing, a clear sign of the lack of food on Qing Mao Mountain. Most of its brethren had died out or had simply separated from its care. Even though it was a full Rank 4 mutated beast now one could not get blood from a stone, and it still needed sustenance.
With a jolt, it suddenly smelled something- something that tasted good. It wandered off towards an area where it sniffed at a block of ice. With the sun beating down on it, it was feeling thirsty as well. While the streams had quenched its thirst, there was something different about this block of ice as it approached. It was not just a block of frozen ice, but a block of frozen blood. The deer began to eagerly lick it after it smelled it and noted that there was nothing wrong with the blood.
Fang Yuan watched this spectacle from a distance, hidden from its sight.
This tactic was something that had been used by one of his disciples in the Blood Wing Demon Sect. They took care of many Blood Path beasts on his behalf during those days, and during the height of summer, many of the Blood Path beasts would begin to become agitated from the heat.
The frozen block of blood was a simple enough invention, but very useful. The disciple in question had been a Rank 1 Gu Master; Fang Yuan didn't remember that person's name right now, but at the time, they had been awarded 1,000 primeval stones for their contribution to the sect.
Although deer were herbivores, they would have no problem taking meat or other things if there were carcasses lying nearby, and for a Blood Path beast, there's almost no better nutrition than blood itself.
There was another block of frozen blood lying near it. The Crimson Hoof Deer wandered over to it. Fang Yuan pondered his next move.
He wasn't sure how close his relationship was to this Crimson Hoof Deer, or how much it trusted him to put it simply. If the trust was good, this would be an easy enough affair.
If it wasn't, it would strike back with all of its strength. He did not know what kind of gu worms it had on its body now that it was Rank 4. It was entirely possible that it had multiple Rank 4 Gu worms. Of course, in a way, that only bolstered his desire to tame this deer. After all, those Rank 4 Blood Path Gu worms could be very useful for him.
The Crimson Hoof Deer noticed a piece of cloth near the next block of frozen blood.
It took a sniff. The smell reminded him of someone. The cloth had been imbued with Fang Yuan's scent, and he wanted to see if it still reacted to it. Back when it had been younger, he would often approach it and had given it a blanket made from a shirt he had used to wear. This had been an attempt to get it used to his presence so that it would be easier to deal with in the future.
With that said, he had enslaved its mother and had been the indirect cause of its entire herd being wiped out. He wasn't sure how much the Crimson Hoof Deer understood that, or how much it blamed him for it. But this could go either way.
The Crimson Hoof Deer, after smelling it, looked around as if it was searching for someone before continuing to lick away the block of ice. That was good, Fang Yuan thought to himself. That meant that it did not entirely despise him. That could make this next move much easier.
He emerged from where he was hidden, holding up a frozen block of blood high in the air so that it was very easily visible.
The Crimson Hoof Deer noticed him, and then Fang Yuan paused, bringing more attention to the treat he had brought along for it.
It did not make a move, neither attacking nor approving.
Fang Yuan took a single step forward, very slow.
It did not do anything.
He took another step forward.
It did not do anything.
But when he took the third step, it seemed to have finally decided on what it wanted to do and then bolted. Fang Yuan had been prepared for this, and immediately his wings erupted from his back once more as he flew after it.

chapters.title: Chapter 213 213: Taming the Crimsonhoof Deer: Part Three
chapters.content:
"Hey, hey, this is all right. I'm not going to do anything to you," Fang Yuan tried to coax the Crimonhoof Deer in a soothing voice, though he doubted that this would help. The Crimson Hoof Deer paused for a moment, wondering where he was until it saw him in the sky and then began running once more.
A small speck of black light showed, and then it disappeared. This was some form of stealth-type Gu.
However, Fang Yuan had already tracked it through the blood and knew exactly where it was. Next, it attempted to increase its fleeing speed using some other kind of Gu worm, running almost three times as fast afterward.
Fang Yuan, however, was very experienced when it came to flying and had his own flying-type Gu. Naturally, between someone who could move through the sky and someone who was running on the ground, it was clear who would be faster. There were numerous obstacles, such as hills and rocks, that the Crimson Hoof Deer had to avoid, which Fang Yuan did not.
When these two options had failed, the Crimson Hoof Deer finally turned around and decided to counterattack. It was extremely sudden, like an action made in a final act of desperation. Someone less experienced than Fang Yuan might've been unable to react in time.
A gu worm launched a torrent of blood at him.
Blood-Flowing Lance Gu!
The original Water-Flowing Lance Gu was a Water Path Gu, however, this gu worm had branched out as a Blood Path modification of it.
Not only could it do damage, but once the blood stuck to a target, it would reduce its speed even if they used a defensive type gu. It was perfect for someone who was trying to get away from a target.
Fang Yuan's wings suddenly folded and he dropped like a rock through the air, avoiding the attack before his wings opened up at the last second, saving him from crashing into the ground.
The Crimsonhoof Deer seemed to be astonished at that kind of movement before Fang Yuan activated several gu worms at once in his aperture.
Mortal Killer Move- Bloodline Enslavement!
One of the gu worms atop the Crimsonhoof Deer attempted a counterattack, a defensive type Gu worm that made a thin membrane of blood around it. However, the deer's Gu worms could not keep up with Fang Yuan's killer move, and the deer slowly calmed down.
Since Fang Yuan had not used a proper enslavement Gu, its enslavement was not as complete as he would have liked. His control over it would be somewhat limited. It would definitely not fight until its last breath for him. Were it in danger, it would then begin to flee.
But this was acceptable to Fang Yuan.
Fang Yuan's killer move Bloodline Enslavement would have made it treat Fang Yuan as if he were a close blood relative, so it now treated Fang Yuan as if it was its parent.
Given the fact that Fang Yuan had been somewhat familiar with it in the past already, this was far easier to achieve than it otherwise would have been.
None of its gu worms activated again. Fang Yuan used the Spring Autumn Cicada's aura to refine the wild gu worms on its body.
When the Crimsonhoof Deer as a mount, they turned back to the village. When he arrived, he told the elders he had something important to do and was not to be disturbed.
***
The Crimsonhoof Deer was brought out for the refinement process Fang Yuan was undergoing. It cried out as Fang Yuan began draining some of its blood, but it did not bolt.
He took out one of the gu worms that he had refined from its body and then tossed its blood into it. In addition, he tossed in thirty grams of aged honey, forty Moon Orchid Petals, two Blood Moon Gu, and finally, the most important ingredient - a fang from the mouth of the Blood River Python's corpse.
The ball of light in front of him slowly stabilized as he tossed in primeval stones until, finally, it coalesced into a new gu worm entirely.
It took the form of a small insect barely the size of his finger before Fang Yuan began feeding it with drops of his blood.
This gu worm used blood infused with primeval essence from Gu Masters as both its food and to activate itself - it was the Blood Guillotine Gu! When infused with blood, the insects would begin to multiply until they formed a cloud that could potentially envelop the entire Gu Yue village. If used against Gu Masters, the insects could continue expanding even with enemy blood. It was less effective against animals like the wolves - but had been used by the Gu Yue clan in the past by sacrificing several elders to fuel it.
The original Blood Guillotine Gu left behind by first gen Gu Yue had been destroyed during the fight with Lord Sky Crane. Fang Yuan had wanted to recreate it for some time but had lacked the necessary materials until now.
Now though, Fang Yuan could bring out its full power. Not only that, but there might be a pathway open to him to refine this into the Rank 6 Blood Deity much as he wanted to do in his past life.
With that said, although this was a big victory for him, to obtain a real combat-worthy Rank 5 gu worm, he could not openly use it like he could his other gu. It was a trademark Blood Path demonic gu which could not be flaunted around lest he wanted the Tie clan to send another investigator his way.
He had wanted to advance the Vermillion Blood Moon Gu to Rank 5, but no recipe for it existed in the clan. He could attempt deducing another one himself, but even with his Grandmaster Blood Path attainment level, it would take several attempts.
He turned his gaze to the Crimsonhoof Deer. If he could advance it to a Mutant Beast King, it could naturally draw Rank 5 gu worms to itself. However, this was not the right environment for its nourishment - it would need a Blood Path aperture to best fully develop.
Fang Yuan could do little about that right now. He took the Crimsonhoof Deer and tied it up near the pavilion where it would not encounter any loud noises that might scare it. Domesticated deer were rare but not unheard of.
It would be the best for its development if he could find it a flock, and potentially make more Crimsonhoof Deer, but although he had managed to find two Rank 3 Deer Enslavement Gu from it, the Gu Yue village did not have the resources to support an Enslavement Path Gu Master.

chapters.title: Chapter 214: Benevolence Gu: Part One
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan was lounging in the Dollhouse, expecting someone. "Ah, Lady Qing Ding Bing! It's good to see that you could join us today."
"Ling Ding Ching, get it right this time," she walked in, corrected him.
"Oh, I'm sorry, I just have difficulty remembering names when they're completely stupid," Fang Yuan said, sighing. Bai Ning Bing snorted coldly. "Anyway, what did you want to talk about today? It's regarding the Bai Clan's spirit spring, isn't it?" Fang Yuan asked.
Bai Ning Bing's eyebrows rose. 'How did... how did Fang Yuan know about that?' She furrowed her brows before she came upon the realization. "Oh, so the Gu Clan's spirit spring is also having issues, is that it? That's how you assumed that we were as well? I had come to you thinking you might have a solution but this is how it is... ahahaha.... looks like you're in the same boat as we are!"
"Actually, on the contrary, I think that the Gu Yue Clan will be fine for a while," Fang Yuan said nonchalantly.
When Bai Ning Bing had detonated, the ice had gone deep inside the mountain, also affecting the spirit springs. Many people had hoped that they would recover.
However, Fang Yuan could see the signs of definitive decline with the Gu Village's spirit spring already. It had been a bit more equivocal earlier but now the writing was clear on the wall - their spirit spring ws done for. The other elders were a bit more hopeful, but they lacked Fang Yuan's 500 years of experience. He could tell when a spirit spring was beginning to die out.
Moreover, he had concrete evidence that the spirit spring was dying out. He had gone to check on the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus a few times and found that it was losing petals at a rapid rate. Right now, it only had seven when it had eight and a half back when he had initially seen it.
It was clear what was happening. The Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus would normally absorb the energy from a spirit spring and then use it to refine itself. In this case, however, because the spirit spring was dying, it was doing the reverse, unrefining itself and sending its energy into the spirit spring. That meant that Gu Village's spirit spring would actually last for longer than either the Bai Clan or the Zhang Clan. However, it would eventually die out nonetheless. Fang Yuan had hoped to move it before such a thing happened, but now, it was clear that he would just have to give up on the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus.
If the Flower Wine Monk could see this situation - that the gu worm that he had planted hoping someone would wipe out the Gu Yue clan was instead sustaining them, he would no doubt cough up a mouthful of blood in anger.
Bai Ning Bing's expression changed. "Regardless, how can you be so calm hearing about that? Aren't you supposed to be a righteous path sect leader? Shouldn't you be worried about your clan's future?" She sneered, knowing his true nature. "What on Earth are you planning to do about it, or are you just planning to abandon your clan entirely?"
Bai Ning Bing felt very little affection towards her clan, but she couldn't deny that it was her clan. If she had truly felt no attachments to it, she wouldn't have felt so ashamed and changed her name while assuming the role of external elder. Not to mention, with most of the annoying elders gone from the Bai Clan, there was actually hope of them accomplishing something useful under her leadership.
As for Fang Yuan, Bai Ning Bing understood him clearly - he would easily abandon the clan if it suited his interests. Was that what he wanted to do? To suck the clan dry of all of its resources before bouncing?
"Well, I suppose it can't be helped then," Fang Yuan said, stretching lazily. "Why don't you tell the Bai Clan that they should submit towards the Gu Yue Clan and I'll tell you a solution to this problem."
Bai Ning Bing frowned. A solution to this problem? The only solution could possibly be that they would need to find another spirit spring. "I already know the solution. We need to find another spirit spring. What kind of offer is that?"
"Oh, but do you know the location of a spirit spring like I do?"
Bai Ning Bing's eyes widened.
"You're telling me you know the location of a spirit spring?"
"Yes, a new, fresh spirit spring which is juicy and ripe for the taking," Fang Yuan said.
Spirit springs could die out, but they would also form once again. Heaven was balanced in that way. When one was destroyed, another one would be created. Of course, that place where it would be created could be some place hundreds of li away from where they currently were. So this was little reassurance to any clan whose own spirit spring was dying out.
Bai Ning Bing crossed her arms. "And you want the Bai Clan to submit in exchange for this information?"
"I only know the location of one spirit spring," Fang Yuan said, lying. "How on earth can three clans stay at a place where there is only one? It's better that we all combine together and become one giant, big, happy family. Wouldn't that be for the best?"
Bai Ning Bing snorted once again. She was sure that Fang Yuan had his own reasons for wanting such. She just couldn't figure them out.
"But that does remind me," Fang Yuan said. "Whatever your decision is, do tell me quickly because we might need to move soon. After all, an unclaimed spirit spring is like a primeval stone that you find lying on the road. If you don't pick it up soon, someone else is going to take it, aren't they?"
Fang Yuan was speaking about the spirit spring that would soon be found by the Bei Clan some distance away. There was also an inheritance there, which he wanted to take. He had never gotten around to it though and had even considered abandoning it at one point.
While the Hundred Li Earth Wolf Spider was very good for navigating, it was still limited by the terrain, and it was only a Rank 4 Gu, meaning that it could not suit his needs.
"If you agree to this, we can go ahead and take the White Form Immortal Snake to the place where I know there is a spring," Fang Yuan said.
The White Form Immortal Snake, on the other hand, was a true Rank 5 Gu.
"I can't use it though?" Bai Ning Bing said, frowning. She might have been able to use it back when she still had the full force of her Northern Dark Ice Soul physique, but right now was a completely different story.
"Oh, it's no matter, just lend it out to me," Fang Yuan said lazily.
"Why not just take the Dollhouse?" Bai Ning Bing asked. It could fly very well on its own.
"Too conspicuous," Fang Yuan said. "We would be inviting danger upon ourselves."
Bai Ning Bing sighed. Fang Yuan did have a point. If she had been able to deduce that such a structure could only be used by an immortal, it was obvious that other people could as well, and that would attract a lot of unwanted attention.
"So be it then. I'll go see if I can convince them."

chapters.title: Chapter 215: Benevolence Gu: Part Two
chapters.content:
Bai Ning Bing left and Fang Yuan considered what his next move should be.
He had some free time now, which was a rare thing, meaning he needed to make full use of it as possible. Dual cultivating with Bai Ning Bing in order to advance his aptitude? She was already gone, so he couldn't do that.
He could try cultivating on his own, but it was far less efficient than using Equality Gu, so he would put that off for now. As it was, they would probably have many opportunities once they traveled to the location he was thinking of. Thinking of new refinement recipes or killer moves was quite intensive- and he lacked the necessary gu worms for many of them in the first place.
Instead, he decided to use this opportunity to explore the dream realm that the system had given him. He called the House Spirit, and it was instructed to awaken him should anything happen as he removed the dream realm from his inventory.
Fang Yuan found himself in a large tent.
Based on the design of the tent and how it was set up, it looked like he was somewhere in the Northern Plains.
He was one of a number of Gu Masters who were surrounding a table.
They were all wearing slightly different uniforms, which meant that they probably belonged to different tribes. This was some kind of inter-tribe meeting, and he had been invited to the same.
He checked his aperture, finding that he had Rank 3 Middle Stage cultivation. There were several gu in there, most of which were strength path gu that were common within the Northern Plains.
Several of them, though, were quite old-fashioned gu worms and a few were even extinct in current times, meaning this was likely from the Olden Antiquity era.
There was one gu in particular, though, which caught his attention. Earlier, if he only had his Grandmaster path attainment in the human path, he would have only been able to recognize it as a human path gu.
Now, however, after studying from the records kept in the Dollhouse, he recognized this as being Benevolence Gu. It was a gu that allowed one to share the effects of, say for example, someone used a defensive type ability on themselves. Then, by using Benevolence Gu, you could copy that defensive type ability upon yourself.
While it seemed to be somewhat useful at first glance, it was less so when you considered the practical aspects of it. Gu Masters used gu because they tended to complement each other's effects in various ways. If you took the ability of your opponent, then they would still have their ability, which was likely modified by their other gu, but you would have their ability only weaker. Rather than trying to copy your opponent's abilities, it was far better to just use your own.
That wasn't to say that it didn't have its niche uses. When it came to the Immortal realm, since Immortal Gu were unique, it was one way of replicating a certain gu worm's effects, but this was a mortal gu.
A feast had been set out for all of them and a Gu Master with Rank 4 cultivation stood up at the head of the table.
Whoever he was, he was someone important, either the leader of this meeting or of this inter-tribal alliance. "Thank you all for gathering today. As you all know, destruction and chaos have been spreading throughout this region. Other tribes have gathered around us, attempting to undermine what we can do. We may be at war at any moment now. It is important that we keep our eyes and ears alert, and above all, trust no one."
The feast started.
Fang Yuan looked at the delicacies laid out before him, but before he could reach his hand out, the Gu Master who was sitting next to him suddenly slumped over, falling onto the table.
He was motionless.
There was silence all around them.
One of them pointed out said Gu Master in question, "What happened to Do Ka?"
The person who had been speaking at the head of the table earlier, who had warned them not to trust anyone, snorted and said, "Ah, I poisoned his venison. He really should have learned to test his food before he ate it." The man snorted and there was gentle chuckling throughout the room. Whoever this Do Ka was, he was clearly not very well liked, Fang Yuan noted. Though as to why he had been killed off like this, was still a mystery to him.
Right then, as the meal continued, there was suddenly shouting from outside. "Attackers!" a voice came from outside. "We're under attack!"
"Let's go," the person at the head of the table said, getting up.
Fang Yuan exited the tent.
The Northern Plains were a region of constant strife and fighting, so it looked like whatever enemies these people had, they had chosen to come ahead and strike out at them at this very moment. Was it dishonorable to attack someone at this point, when they were at a gathering? Who would care - it was also dishonorable to poison one's guests as well. Yet in the dog-eat-dog world of Gu Masters, particularly in the Northern Plains, treachery was common.
There was chaos everywhere as Fang Yuan pondered what to do.
He wasn't sure about what the requirements were to clear this dream realm were, but he began fighting. His martial arts prowess from his actual life did translate to the dream realm as he began striking out at people, at the enemy, doing massive damage and punching far above his weight.
However, despite his strength and skills, it was clear that he was being whittled down.
Finally, a Gu Master struck him with something with a strange bee-shaped gu worm, and he fell to the ground as a strange itching and warmth sensation spread from where the gu worm had struck his body. He died.
Fang Yuan came back to his senses as he felt his soul take some slight damage. He took out a Guts Gu from his inventory and then he used it to mend his soul.
'So I failed that time around,' he thought instead. Before he tried to go back into the dream realm, he tried thinking about what had happened.
Should he think of a counter to that strange bee-shaped gu worm? Doubtful, as he couldn't recognize it. There was a bigger problem than it.
During the latter part of their fight, he had been completely surrounded to the point where his individual's friends couldn't have possibly changed things. None of his gu were anything spectacular either, other than Benevolence Gu.
There were several questions, of course, that he had in his mind. A new theory began to emerge in his mind. He had to do something; intervene before the battle took place, otherwise, he would end up right in the same situation once again and would be ejected from the dream realm.
He entered it once again with his new idea.
This time, he got up before the Rank 4 Gu Master could begin his speech. This shocked everyone, as it was a massive breach of etiquette, as well as disrespectful to their host. However, he quickly said, "Everyone! We're going to be attacked from the southwest! We need to prepare to engage the attackers!"
There was noise at his suggestion, with tensions easing.
However, at that moment, the attackers suddenly descended, faster than they had before, nullifying his advantage.
Things shouldn't have played out this way, but sometimes dream realms did not make sense like this. There was a decision to be made, and he hadn't made the right one.
It ended in the same way as last time, and Fang Yuan was ejected from the dream realm.

chapters.title: Chapter 216: Benevolence Gu: Part Three
chapters.content:
Given that he failed during his last attempt, Fang Yuan had something else in mind this time around.
"Remember, you can trust no one," the Rank 4 Gu Master at the head of the table said.
Fang Yuan turned around towards the Gu Master at his side and whispered to him, "Don't eat the venison, it's been poisoned."
This other Gu Master, by the name of Do Ka, gave him an odd look. Fang Yuan wasn't sure how close the person he was playing and this person were in real life. However, if he were sitting at a dinner table and someone next to him told him that something was poisoned, he wouldn't eat it regardless of who they were. "Is all of the venison poisoned, or just mine?" he whispered back to Fang Yuan.
"I don't know," Fang Yuan said, "just don't eat it."
The battle then continued, as it had before, with the attackers coming during the middle of the banquet. Fang Yuan had to hand it to them. Whoever had done this before, it was the perfect time to strike.
The scene played out much like before. Fang Yuan couldn't tell what Duo Ka's role was supposed to be during this situation. He seemed to be contributing rather little to the fighting. As a matter of fact, about half an hour in, he was found. Even as Fang Yuan continued fighting, the battle's tide was the same as before.
As Fang Yuan was injured, a healing path Gu Master came near him, offering to help him. "Sure, just make it quick," Fang Yuan was about to say before he suddenly felt a sharp pain.
The healing path Gu Master glared at him. "The reason why Do Ka didn't die was because you helped him, didn't you? You're in cahoots with him traitor!" Fang Yuan felt extreme pain as the dream ended. He was ejected from it once again. Thankfully, the damage to his soul was rather minor from exploring this one. He thought as he took out a Guts Gu from his inventory.
So, the solution wasn't to warn everyone, nor was it to save Do Ka secretly. Then what exactly was he supposed to do?
Fang Yuan tried the dream realm once again. This time when the Rank 4 Gu Master finished his speech that they shouldn't trust anyone, Fang Yuan immediately got up and yelled out, "Everyone, don't touch the food! An enemy has poisoned it!"
Everyone backed away from the buffet as one. Fang Yuan had made the declaration, and no one dared to eat anything. As soon as the enemy approached once more, this time, Fang Yuan was struck from the back. When he turned around to see who had attacked him, it was the Rank 4 Gu Master in question.
"But... why?" Fang Yuan asked.
The Rank 4 Gu Master sneered. "I was the one who poisoned the meals there, for a specific purpose, and yet you interfered with my plans. I can see you're already out of primeval essence and can't do anything in the upcoming fight. No need for you to see the next sunrise, traitor."
Fang Yuan was ejected from the dream realm again, repairing his soul with Guts Gu.
'What else am I missing?' he thought to himself. 'If only I had something like Unravel Dream to use here.' The dream started again, and he noted the gu in his aperture. There was something there which could have contradicted poison should he offer it to Do Ka. No, the others thought that he was a traitor, so that would mean that he would be implicated as well if he tried to make that kind of swap in the middle of the banquet.
In such a case, what if...?
An idea occurred to him, one that was kind of tricky, but he thought could work anyway. When Do Ka began digging into his venison, Fang Yuan used Benevolence Gu, transferring some of the poison to himself. He wasn't sure if it could be used in this way. It was certainly an unorthodox way of using it. Fang Yuan felt his body shiver under the effects of the poison.
However, his healing type gu activated. It seemed to have the intended effect as Do Ka certainly stopped eating, feeling that there was something off with the venison. "I think that there's something off with the venison," he said to himself, pushing it away and not taking another bite. He hadn't consumed enough to kill him yet, it seemed, and activated a healing-type gu worm of his own.
Fang Yuan for his part felt like he couldn't stand, having taken some of the burden of the poison away from Do Ka. The enemy attacked again, and Fang Yuan couldn't see how he could possibly go ahead and strike out at them, but then the dream realm ended. And this time, his attainment on the human path increased.
"Quasi-Great Grandmaster in the Human Path," he thought to himself. "So that was the solution to it."
By now, this meant that his greatest path, in terms of attainment level, was the human path, even superseding the blood path that he had taken centuries to master back during his previous life. That was the power of dream realms.
'No wonder everyone is after developing the Dream Path during this timeline,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. He had missed the train, so to speak, back during his old life, not being able to explore them back when development was still going on. However, now he could take full advantage of it, raising his attainment level extraordinarily rapidly.
Following this, Fang Yuan got up, noting that quite some time had passed. He returned to his bedroom, glancing at the paintings that Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable had left for him.
The strange blank painting had developed another image after the Awakening Ceremony, depicting the youngsters and mortals going for their awakening. He had taken this away to see that there was another blank painting beneath it.
That blank one was still blank today, but there was something different about another one of them.
One of them that had been said to work when his understanding of the Human Path had increased...
The painting in question had changed and showed a basin with a young man sitting in the middle. There was lush greenery surrounding him. At the corner of the frame, a shadow seemed to be descending upon the scene, as if there were someone who was going to strike at the person in question from the sky.
'What is the secret to this?' he thought to himself.
Suddenly, the painting changed. It was like before when Genesis Lotus had placed a river of time into a painting, with it moving. Now, Fang Yuan watched as the shadow descending upon the man was more clearly visible.
The shadow, however, did not descend upon the man as Fang Yuan had been expecting. Instead, it revealed itself to be a man, and the man in question turned to stare directly at Fang Yuan before his hand emerged from the painting and latched onto Fang Yuan.
Fang Yuan found himself sucked into the painting!

chapters.title: Chapter 217 217: Rizz Taoist Master: Part One
chapters.content:
This was the first time Fang Yuan had found himself within a painting, it was a very odd feeling. He felt himself become part of the art, his body turning into a strange collection of brushstrokes. He looked down at his hands, where he could see the individual lines making up his fingers. Everything about him- his clothes, his gu worms, and his aperture- had all become part of the painting.
Despite still having access to his aperture, Fang Yuan found that he could not use any of his Gu worms. He was unable to move, suspended above the scene the painting depicted, as if he were stuck in the sky and looking down. It didn't seem as if the two people in the painting had noticed him, even though he was sure the person swooping down on the figure in the valley had seen him right before he was dragged in.
The person on the ground was still sitting there, oblivious to the fact that someone was watching him. Now that Fang Yuan got a better look at the Gu Master who was swooping down, he realized that he did, in fact, recognize the face.
It was a face that was not widely known, mainly because the person tended to use a different face when wandering around. That wasn't to say that no one knew his face - once he had reached the pinnacle of the world, he could openly show it and do as he pleased. After all, once he reached the peak of the world, who would care if someone saw his face or not?
"Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable," Fang Yuan mouthed to himself. Confusion began to cloud his mind. It was one thing for Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable to capture someone like him, a mortal, and put him in a painting. How had he been able to capture another Venerable and place him into a painting as well?
From his very limited understanding of the painting path, it had a way of remaining hidden without conflicting with most dao marks. However, the amount of dao marks on a Venerable should have been more than what the path could truly handle.
The Gu Master on the ground suddenly looked up as the shadow approached him and then moved away two paces. As Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable descended, Fang Yuan felt that the other Gu Master in question was likely just a mortal given that they made no attempt to hide, it was clear. As for Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable, although he could hide his traces, by this point, there was actually no need to.
"Who are you?" the Gu Master on the ground asked.
"First, I want you to answer my question," Thieving Heaven answered. "Are you named Guo Lian by any chance?"
"Yes, that's me," he answered. "But who are you?"
"You may know me as Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable."
"Wow, you're Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable! I'll be honest, when I heard about your name, I thought your skin would be a bit darker."
THDV: ...
Thieving Heaven stared at the Gu Master blankly. "Now, what exactly is that supposed to mean?"
"Oh, no, I didn't mean anything like that," Guo Lian answered. "I just meant that, you know, you're from the Western Desert and all, right? Isn't the sun, like, really hot there? Wouldn't your skin have become a bit darker? But it looks like you've kept up with a pretty good skincare routine, my man."
"Despite hearing my name, you don't seem to be quite scared," Thieving Heaven observed.
"Oh, that's because I don't have anything worth stealing," Guo Lian answered.
"Well, I'm not here to steal anything from you," Thieving Heaven said, "or at least I would prefer not to. Although the world may know me as Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable, the truth is my name is Ben Jie Sun, and I am merely a wanderer looking for a way back home. As much as I believe you are as well, are you not, Guo Lian? Is it not true that you are also not originally from this world?"
'So, Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable was also an otherworldly demon?' Fang Yuan thought to himself. 'And this other Gu Master is one as well. There are three of us all being otherworldly demons being brought here -this can't be a coincidence. This must be part of Genesis Lotus's plot, but what is it?' Otherworldly Demons were rare, but not unique. One of the disciples of the Blood Wing Demon Sect happened to be one - Fang Yuan, though, felt no kinship with other Otherworldly Demons.
"Oh, so you mean, like, you're from another world too? Amazing!" Guo Lian said. "I've been looking for someone else who also came from my world for a long time. I was hoping I could find someone I could finally talk to. This is so cool! It's great that we managed to meet, right?" Guo Lian then said: "Aight, listen up. The name's Guo Lian. Main character energy, no cap. I'm here for a glow up and a good time. Bet, if we ain't vibin' here, we can go ahead and meet up in Ohio so long as no one's acting sus, fr, fr."
Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable frowned. "We might come from other worlds, but I don't think we come from the same one. I didn't understand what you just said."
"Oh, so there are other worlds other than the one I came from and this one?" Guo Lian said. "Okay, that's interesting."
"Did you just refine a gu worm?" Thieving Heaven asked.
"Yeah, I did. For some reason, whenever I speak words like that, I end up refining this kind of gu worm. I don't know what it is, though." Guo Lian took something out of his aperture, and Fang Yuan immediately recognized it as being Stupidity Gu.
"Right, right," Thieving Heaven said. "The reason why I came here was not really to chit-chat, but rather because I had heard that you had stumbled upon an interesting development."
"I mean, if you're talking about the weird gu worms, I can show you, but most people don't think that they're very good. But I have a question first: you're Rank 9, right?"
"Indeed, I am. That's what it means to be a Venerable," Thieving Heaven answered.
"So, how did you manage to get your special ability?" Guo Lian asked.
"What special ability?" Thieving Heaven asked.
"Well, you know. I've always been wondering about that ever since I came to this world. Like, it has all these weird insects that you can use for fighting, and it's completely filled up with people who look like they're from Chinese culture. Don't get me wrong, I love Chinese culture! I just love talking the lingo. Knee-how and ari-gay-toe, you know. That's all cool and good, but when people like us go to a different world, we're supposed to get special abilities, right, which make us really strong or something?" Guo Lian said. "For whatever reason, when I came to this world, I just had, like, trash-grade talent. I've been stuck at Rank 2 forever. So, how did you manage to get your cheat skill and then get to Rank 9?"
"I don't know how to tell you this," Thieving Heaven answered, "but there was no special ability."
"Then how did you get to Rank 9?" Guo Lian asked.
"You just have to work hard at Gu Master cultivation or get lucky, like everyone else," Thieving Heaven said.
"Wait- I don't get any advantages for being from another world?"
"No, not really... unless you have some knowledge that you can apply in this world, but even that effect is kind of limited in how much change you can really bring about."

chapters.title: Chapter 218 218: Rizz Taoist Master: Part Two
chapters.content:
Guo Lian was sweating bullets like he was having a heart attack. "Wait, what do you mean I have to work hard just like everybody else in this world? I'm from another world! Aren't I supposed to get like super powers or cheat skills or something? Where's my instant Nascent Soul cultivation base? Where's my heavenly treasure that can instantly kill enemies three major realms above me? Where's my golden finger which rewards me by 100,000% for whatever I happen to do compared to other people? Where's my Primordial Chaos Dragon bloodline? Where's my pocket realm filled with tomboy Jade Beauties where I'm the only male there, and for every child I have, my power increases by 10^n where n is the number of children I have? How am I supposed to survive in this world if it's just me without any cheats? My clan's been telling me I have trash talent anyway - and you're telling me I won't get any kind of powerup eventually?" By this point, he was yelling and screaming, almost rolling on the ground like a toddler throwing a tantrum. "This isn't fair! It's not fair! Not fair! Not fair!"
Fang Yuan had no idea what he was looking at, but even he started to feel like he was taking mental damage listening to this person. He also started feeling secondhand, thirdhand, and even fourthhand embarrassment for Thieving Heaven.
"Well, what can I say? You just have to work hard. Wait - what are you doing-" Thieving Heaven asked as Guo Lian got up and took out a Rope Gu from his aperture, tying it into a knot using his primeval essence.
"Trust me, I'm not living here any longer if that's how things are supposed to be," Guo Lian said.
"Wait, wait, wait," Thieving Heaven said. "You don't have to do that, you know. I mean, as long as you're alive, there's still hope, isn't there?"
Guo Lian considered things and put the Rope Gu back into his aperture. "Maybe, you know... so, what you're telling me is, though, that if I work as hard as you do, then I can also become Rank 9 and become invincible in this world?"
"That's not exactly it... but um... you can certainly get ahead..." Thieving Heaven said, still seemingly unsure of what to say. On the one hand, he didn't want to tell Guo Lian the truth. Otherwise, he might very well try to give up on this path and finish rage quitting. On the other hand, he couldn't lie either and give him false hope. It just rubbed him the wrong way. Perhaps if this person was a normal Gu Master, it'd be different, but he was also an Otherworldly Demon like him, someone who was also lost in this strange foreign world.
"Well, that's great then," Guo Lian said. "You know what? You may start calling me the Rizz Taoist Master! No wait, once I become a venerable, I'll call myself the Great Rizz Venerable! I'll become unparalleled in this world! I'll go around slapping young masters, and I'll collect a massive harem of jade beauties. Yes, that's what I'll do!"
"Sure, you can go around doing that," Thieving Heaven said. "But about this new invention that you had managed to make... I was just curious about it."
"Oh, sure, that's fine. I have no problem with you seeing that," Guo Lian said. "But I am going to have to ask for something in return: 80,000 primeval stones."
Thieving Heaven had a wry grin on his face. "Are you seriously trying to ask the Thieving Heaven Demonic Venerable for paym-wait... did you just say 80,000 primeval stones?"
"Yes," Guo Lian said, not understanding what the issue was. Fang Yuan, meanwhile, was shaking his head. It was clear that whoever this Guo Lian was, they knew nothing about being an immortal. Forget 80,000 - even 80 million primeval stones would have been chump change for Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable. Granted, he also could have just stolen it, but with a price that low, there was clearly no need for it.
"I wanted to save 80,000 primeval stones for my retirement during this life," Guo Lian said. "But with what you said just inspired me, and I think I'm going to use it to improve my cultivation instead."
"Rather than giving you the stones," Thieving Heaven said, "I do have a talent-raising Gu worm, and perhaps you would prefer that instead?"
"Oh, stuff like that actually exists?! Yeah, sure," Guo Lian said.
"Right, so just show me what it is. However, before we start, there's someone else who will be joining us."
Up until this point, Fang Yuan had noted that things within the painting were becoming more realistic with time.
Although initially it looked like he was part of the painting, it now looked like he had actual skin, fingers, and nails. Granted, he still had a bit of a drawn or cartoonish quality to him, but it looked far more realistic than it had before. The same went for the people beneath him. They had initially appeared as slightly blurry images made in watercolor, but now they had solidified into looking like they were almost real people. As Thieving Heaven said that there would be someone else joining them, he looked up at Fang Yuan, and Fang Yuan suddenly felt himself descend.
The ground was rushing up at him, but he wanted to activate his wings - but found that he couldn't. As he was about to crash, his velocity suddenly decreased to the point where he landed on his feet without any issue.
"Oh, so there's someone else here. Hello," Guo Lian said.
"Hello," Fang Yuan said. He wasn't sure how they were all interacting. These people had died a long time ago. It looked like either their memories or parts of their personalities had been preserved within this painting by Genesis Lotus. And yet he was able to interact with them. It was almost like being in a dream realm, but with the people within the dream recognizing they were in a dream and also being able to recognize that the person there was from outside.
"This is Gu Yue Fang Yuan," Thieving Heaven said, introducing Fang Yuan for him. "He is also an Otherworldly Demon like the two of us." Fang Yuan would've liked to keep that information hidden, but Thieving Heaven already let the cat out of the bag.
"Ayo fam," Guo Lian said, pointing at Thieving Heaven using his thumb. "This unc is kinda sus, fr, fr."
"I don't understand your strange wordplay either," Fang Yuan said. He looked at Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable. "So you partnered up with Genesis Lotus Immortal Venerable, I presume?" There was no other way that this sort of interaction could have happened without that being the case.
"Indeed, we did. I think that you would want to learn what this secret is as well." Thieving Heaven turned towards Guo Lian. "Look, kid. You've been annoying me for quite a bit. However, I don't want to harm you or do anything, given the fact that you're an Otherworldly Demon too, out of professional courtesy. However, if you continue wasting my time, I am going to use more drastic measures. You know what, here are your 80,000 primeval stones." He said, tossing a storage gu worm to Guo Lian. Thieving Heaven's expression had changed quite a bit now, appearing far more serious than before. "Tell you what - you can have the aptitude-raising gu as well after you show us what you've managed to discover."

chapters.title: Chapter 219: Refining Rank 0 Gu Worms: Part One
chapters.content:
"Sure thing," Guo Lian said, seemingly oblivious to Thieving Heaven's threats. He turned towards Fang Yuan. "Hey, I'm Guo Lian. My hobbies include... well, I don't really have any. I just like lounging around doing nothing most of the time, but my clan members aren't really receptive to that. Who are you?"
"You already know my name," Fang Yuan said.
"Yeah, but I don't know anything about you."
"You don't need to know anything about me," Fang Yuan said.
"He comes from a different time period anyway, and you'll never meet him again," Thieving Heaven said.
"Oh, are you like from the future then?" Guo Lian said. "Hey, tell me, do I manage to finally become the great Venerable in the future? Is my name famous throughout all the five regions?"
"I have never heard of your name before," Fang Yuan admitted. He had a high suspicion that this person likely died without accomplishing anything of significance. He had never even heard of this person's clan, meaning they were also very insignificant.
"Ah, bummer," Guo Lian said. However, he didn't think about rage quitting again. Instead, he said, "But you know what? Maybe with that aptitude-raising Gu, I might actually accomplish something. Whatever. If you guys want to see this little thing I figured out, we should all sit down." He pulled out a table and three chairs from a storage-type gu worm in his aperture. Fang Yuan took a seat.
All the while, Guo Lian kept blabbering about random things, even while he was showing them this new technique that he had discovered. Fang Yuan thought inwardly that he was far too trusting especially for an Otherworldly Demon. This world was far more dangerous than whatever world he had come from, clearly.
"Oh, hey, do you like poetry?" Guo Lian asked Fang Yuan. "Because I happened to make my own poem. You want to hear it?"
Neither of them wanted to, but that didn't stop Guo Lian:
"In the meme-filled depths of the Internet's haze,
Where emojis dance and trends ablaze,
There's a tale of a vibe that's so on fleek,
With swag and chill, it's the language we speak.
On Insta feeds where selfies pop,
And Tiktoks tick like a Ticktock clock,
We flex our fits, no cap, no lie
With skibidi toilets and that drip so fly.
But deep in the DMs, hearts can yearn,
For a friend to stan and lessons to learn,
We spill the tea and spill it fast,
With squad goals tight, we'll always last.
So slide into my DMs, fam, let's chat,
From memes to dreams, we'll laugh like that,
In this digital world where we all vibe,
We'll slay the day, our spirits thrive."
Fang Yuan: ...
THDV: ...
"So what do you guys think? I was going to call my poem 'Sigma Rizz' - wait, you guys don't know what either of those things mean, do you, well, the word 'sigma' is derived from the ordinary hierarchy seen in wolves with the 'alpha' being..." Guo Lian kept yapping while Fang Yuan felt like he had a headache. Thieving Heaven felt like he had suddenly taken damage from some kind of wisdom path attack, even though once again that should have been impossible given the difference in rank.
'Perhaps I was too harsh when I was telling Fang Zheng he had no talent for poems,' Fang Yuan thought.
"Oh hey look at that - I refined that gu worm again!" Guo Lian said, removing another Stupidity Gu from his aperture.
"Okay, for the last time, enough nonsense," Thieving Heaven said through gritted teeth. "Show us what it is that you managed to discover."
"Right, so. We all come from a different world, right?" Guo Lian said. "So there's something different about us compared to the rest of the people around the world."
"Yes, it's called having Otherworldly Dao marks," Thieving Heaven said.
"What are Dao marks?" Guo Lian asked.
"Just forget I said anything," Thieving Heaven said, waving his hand, not wanting this meeting to become any more sidetracked than it already was.
Fang Yuan had never heard of Otherworldly Dao marks before. He also didn't want to disturb whatever sort of lesson was going on here just to ask some random question so he kept quiet for now.
"So you can take some of that stuff that we have, which is unique, and put them in gu worms like this." He took out a gu that Fang Yuan was familiar with: an Equality Gu, but this was only Rank 2. Guo Lian then took one primordial stone and placed it on the other end of the scale, where normally another Gu Master would place their hand.
"The thing is, even though our bodies have this sort of weird thing because we're from a different world, gu worms don't have that, because they're all born in this world. I don't think either of your worlds had gu worms, did they?"
Both Fang Yuan and Thieving Heaven shook their heads.
"However, there is one place where this difference between us and gu worms actually meet together," Guo Lian said. "That's in our Vital Gu. Because our Vital Gu are parts of ourselves in a way, we can try to combine them with this part of us from another world."
Both Fang Yuan and Thieving Heaven didn't really seem to get what was going on, so Guo Lian decided to demonstrate.
"So, what you need to do is you keep one primordial stone on the other end of Equality Gu and you put your hand on the other side. Then you focus on your own Vital Gu and you try to see if you can transfer this sort of otherworldly... I guess what you were saying, dao marks, between you and that gu. If you do it right, the primordial stone will then start to develop a new kind of gu worm. Here, let me show you."
Guo Lian began pouring his primordial essence into Equality Gu, with the primordial stone seemingly remaining unchanged. After 10 minutes, nothing had happened. "Yeah, this thing takes a bit of time," Guo Lian said. "I've been trying to see if I can do it faster, but I really can't."
After half an hour, both Fang Yuan and Thieving Heaven felt that nothing was going to happen, but then the primordial stone did start to change. It started dissolving, but not in the way that a primordial stone normally would.
Instead, it was shedding its outer layers until it revealed a strange shape, as if a sculptor was carving something out of it. A few hours later, Guo Lian was done, and the primordial stone had turned into the shape of his vital Gu. A while later, and it had completely come to life, fluttering its wings.
"So, this is how I can make what I call 'Rank 0 Gu'," Guo Lian said.
'Rank 0 Gu?' Fang Yuan wondered. He had never seen anything like that. He went over and reached for this Rank 0 Gu and picked it up. On closer inspection, it looked like it was slightly deformed. One of its eyes was bigger than the other. Its wings were not symmetrical, and it had an odd number of legs: four legs on one side and three on the other.
It was as if someone had tried to make the Gu worm from memory, but they were not very good at replicating it. It also had a faded-out appearance, as if the color had been bleached out from it. As for its aura, Fang Yuan could not sense any aura from it. It was as if it lacked it completely. However, simultaneously, it did seem to have the properties of a gu and was not an ordinary insect.

chapters.title: Chapter 220 220: Refining Rank 0 Gu Worms: Part Two
chapters.content:
"Why do you call them Rank 0?" Fang Yuan asked.
"Because they don't seem to be of any rank," Guo Lian said, "but they still seem to be gu worms."
"And what can they do?" Fang Yuan asked.
"Oh, you can't actually do anything with them," Guo Lian answered.
Both Fang Yuan and Thieving Heaven stared at Guo Lian.
"Well, I mean, you can't do anything with them yet. Even if you put your primordial essence into one of them, it's not going to do anything, but... I've been trying to see if there are ways that I can make one which actually works, you know. So, now that I'm done, why don't you all try?" Guo Lian asked Fang Yuan and Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable.
Fang Yuan, however, as much as he was interested in this, was not about to reveal his vital gu to these people.
"Why are you hesitating, Fang Yuan? You really should go ahead and try," Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable said. "Are you afraid of leaking the Spring Autumn Cicada?"
Well, there went his plan of keeping it hidden.
"As a matter of fact, I don't really think we need you anymore," Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable said, turning to Guo Lian even as the other was asking, "What's the Spring Autumn Cic-" before Thieving Heaven waved his hand and Guo Lian disappeared into the rest of the painting.
"Couldn't you have done that earlier?" Fang Yuan asked. "Why did I have to sit through all of his nonsense?"
"If I suffered through it," Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable said, "you, too, have to do it. Now, like I said, why don't you try making a Rank 0 Gu yourself?"
Fang Yuan put one of his own hands on his Equality Gu and a primordial stone on the other end, much like Guo Lian had said. "What else can you give me? Any insight into the Theft Path?"
Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable sighed. "I'm afraid that the theft path does not really suit you, Fang Yuan."
"What do you mean it doesn't suit me?" Fang Yuan asked. "Who else in the entire Five Regions could it possibly suit?"
"That's exactly my point," Thieving Heaven said. "It suits you far too well. Who knows what kind of destruction you would get up to if you happened to master it?"
'Perhaps this was another way of heaven's will balancing things,' Fang Yuan thought. Much like it had given him Charity Gu, which he was not very likely to use, the person who had become Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable was not a perpetual thief.
Towards the end of his career, as he became more notorious, many people would just hand over whatever they had so that he would stop bothering them. In a way, it was perfect for Fang Yuan. Extortion was far easier than going around actually stealing things. However, judging from his expression, it did not look like theft was something that he reveled in.
The process of creating a Rank 0 Gu was very slow. It took Fang Yuan almost as much time as it did Guo Lian. During that time, there was much to speak about.
"Did you manage to find a way home?" Fang Yuan asked. He, himself, had no desires to return back to Earth. What would he do there anyway? His dream of achieving eternal life was only possible in this world.
"That remains to be seen," Thieving Heaven said. "This painting was made far before then. I had come to this place because I had heard that there was some strange invention and that it probably involved an Otherworldly Demon. I came to investigate and found this little invention. But coming to another matter entirely, I have a request for you. If you can help me out, there might be something in it for you..."
"Like what?" Fang Yuan asked. "What kind of job do you need to get done?"
"Back when I was still not a venerable and cultivating," Thieving Heaven said, "I wandered the world, including the Southern Border, looking for a way to get back home. While I was here in the Southern Border, there was something that I needed- a certain gu refinement material- that I had to take from someone's grave. It had been urgent at the time, and I had always thought that I would replace it when I came back. In my long life of searching for a way back home, it seems to have slipped my mind to do so. Although I used it up, I have a replacement for that gu refinement material here. I just need you to return it to that person's proper gravesite."
Thieving Heaven took out a bottle that was filled with what looked like an insignificant amount of clear liquid. Anyone who was an immortal would have been able to detect the numerous dao marks on it, but to Fang Yuan it looked like water.
"What is this exactly?" Fang Yuan asked.
"These are Abyssal Earth Dragon Emperor's Tears," Thieving Heaven said. "Obtained from an Immemorial Desolate Beast. This is a Rank 8 refinement material - very hard to get your hands on. I had a great need for it at the time. By the time I managed to get a replacement, which I said I would give back to the person I had taken it from, it was a bit too late. Do you see? Still, I had promised myself that I would give it back later on, and now that you're here, why don't you go ahead and do that for me?"
"Absolutely," Fang Yuan said with a gentle smile. "It would be my pleasure to help you with this deed."
"You're thinking of taking it for yourself, aren't you?" Thieving Heaven asked.
"What? I would never!" Fang Yuan said. "How could you possibly accuse me of doing such a shameless thing?"
"Oh, don't worry," Thieving Heaven said. "I'd anticipated that. Let's just say that you won't exactly succeed at it, even if you were to try. But there is a reward waiting for you there, Fang Yuan- something that will be worth your while."
"Oh, and what is this?" Fang Yuan asked.
"A gu worm that will be greatly helpful to you," Thieving Heaven said, "and the location to one of my true inheritances. Not a minor one, a true inheritance. You'll need to be an immortal to get to this one, though once you are I think you'll easily manage. "
Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable had set up various inheritances throughout the entire world, but there were only 10 true inheritances. It was rumored that each one was located as a pair, and finding one of them would give you a clue to where the other one was. If that were the case, Fang Yuan could get his hands on potentially two venerable true inheritances; not the kind of fake inheritances Paradise Earth and Genesis Lotus were trying to throw at him.
"Where is this place located?" Fang Yuan asked. If it wasn't an immortal's burial ground, it might be hard for him to reach.
"Oh, you don't need to worry about that," Thieving Heaven said after handing him a gu worm, and the information instantly took root in Fang Yuan's mind. "Trust me, the reward would be worth it," Thieving Heaven said.
Strangely enough, despite using the Rank 5 Equality Gu rather than Rank 2, Fang Yuan took the exact amount of time that Guo Lian had taken in order to create his Rank 0 Gu worm. Fang Yuan suspected this was because his Spring Autumn Cicada was a Rank 6 immortal Gu or that the process of creation was independent when it came to time. Eventually though, the primeval stone in questions began peeling away, turning into the shape of a cicada before it burst out into life.
Fang Yuan picked up a new gu that somewhat resembled the Spring Autumn Cicada, but much like Guo Lian's creation, it was deformed and looked like its colors were bleached away. One of its wings was missing. However, it still somehow looked more lively than the Spring Autumn Cicada within his own aperture as that was still barely clinging on to life.

chapters.title: Chapter 221 221: Bei Gu Mountain: Part One
chapters.content:
Only a single Immortal Gu could exist in the world at a time. How could this Rank 0 Spring Autumn Cicada exist then? There was only one explanation - because this was not an immortal gu! They did not seem to count as immortal, but rather mortal. Fang Yuan had prepared it from a single primeval stone, after all, so it would be incredulous to think that this could have the power equivalent to an Immortal Gu.
"What can this new gu do?" Fang Yuan asked. It didn't seem like it could take him back in time like the actual Spring Autumn Cicada.
"By itself - nothing," Thieving Heaven said. "And let me tell you something more about what I discovered regarding Rank 0 Gu worms. They are true otherworldly gu worms. In other words, they carry Otherworldly Dao Marks and are covered by them completely. Meaning only Otherwordly Demons can refine them. However, they cannot be advanced further beyond Rank 0, nor do they have effects, and they cannot be used in refinement either - at least as far as I have found."
"So, then this really is useless," Fang Yuan said, holding on to the Rank 0 Spring Autumn Cicada.
"Not necessarily," Thieving Heaven said with a wry smile. "There are no useless gu worms, Fang Yuan - only useless Gu Masters. In time, I'm sure that you'll understand the importance of them. For now though, this is all that I have to say to you. Good luck."
Thieving Heaven waved his hand, and Fang Yuan suddenly found himself back in his room, staring at the painting in question.
Only now it depicted a small vial of clear liquid.
Fang Yuan tried to put his hand inside to try to grasp this vial, but all he felt was the surface of the painting. Try as he might, he could see no difference between this and a normal painting. Perhaps an Immortal could, or maybe - it could fool even an Immortal's eyes. Thieving Heaven likely wanted him to take this painting to the area in question.
'So this is Thieving Heaven's anti-theft precaution,' Fang Yuan thought to himself. Even if he could take out the vial in questions, selling it was another issue. Not that he didn't have his methods, but they were all risky and could easily backfire in many ways in addition to requiring a lot of time to set up.
It was not impossible to go to the area that Thieving Heaven had pointed out. If he could use the White Form Immortal Snake he could reach there within four day's of arriving at Bei Gu Mountain.
The issue was that he did not have free control over the White Form Immortal Snake Gu.
At least, not yet...
A plan began forming in his mind, though it might need to wait a while as he got the pieces ready. There were more pressing matters to take care of.
He looked into his aperture and found that the Rank 0 Spring Autumn Cicada was still there.
With a thought, he willed it to self-detonate. It was one thing to carry the actual Spring Autumn Cicada around because that was a Rank 6 immortal gu and could not be easily detected by anyone other than an Immortal. Why would an Immortal find cause to look closely at Fang Yuan?
The Rank 0 Gu worm, on the other hand, didn't seem to have any such properties. It was unlikely that anyone would ever check inside his aperture. Its design was similar to the Spring Autumn Cicada, and although he wasn't sure how many people knew what it looked like, given the fact that it did not give out an immortal aura, he did not wish to take chances. Did any illustrations of the Spring Autumn Cicada exist out there in the world? He couldn't be sure, but it was his ultimate trump card.
Why take the risk? As it was, this Rank 0 Gu worm had no use, as per Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable, or at least no use that its original creator, Guo Lian, had managed to find out.
Fang Yuan thought about it and considered the fact that there must have been something that it could do. Otherwise, Thieving Heaven Demon Venerable wouldn't have wanted to show it to him.
The next morning, Bai Ning Bing approached him and told him that the Bai clan would be somewhat amenable to joining up with the Gu clan.
"It won't be easy to convince them," she said, "especially coming from me, an external elder. However, as their primeval spring continues to dry up, I think they'll end up seeing reason with joining with you."
"Good work, good work," Fang Yuan said. "We can leave this afternoon, then."
The process of moving the entire Gu Yue village to where Fang Yuan intended it to be would be a long and arduous one. Many things had to be settled. However, above all, he needed to establish his presence upon the mountain. Not to mention, this was a perfect excuse to look for the inheritance that was buried there.
That day, he called Qing Shu and Fang Zheng to him in the clan head's pavilion in private.
"What's going on, elder brother?" Fang Zheng asked.
"It is a matter of great importance," Fang Yuan said. "And I need the two of you to keep silent about this. In other words, it's a secret, which could be quite damaging for the clan if it were to ever get out."
Qing Shu and Fang Zheng both nodded.
"What's the matter?"
"The matter is that, and I hate to say this, but our primeval spring is dying out," Fang Yuan said.
Both Qing Shu and Fang Zheng froze.
"Brother, are you absolutely sure?" Fang Zheng asked.
"I am," Fang Yuan said. "The other clans' primal springs have been dying for sure. We had been hoping that ours would last and recover. However, it's now showing signs that it's clearly dying. The old clan head had left behind records on how to identify a dying primal spring, and without a doubt, ours would be following the other clans soon."
There was no such record, of course, not that the two of them would know it. There was a hidden room in the underground cavern where only the clan head could go. With that said, the rest of Fang Yuan's speech was true. Once the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus ran out, their spirit spring would start showing signs of decline that would grow more overt and obvious, but he needed to act before then.
"What do we do then?" Fang Zheng wondered.
Without a primeval spring, a clan was just a sitting duck. Without one, new Gu Masters would not be able to open up their apertures as they would not have a steady supply of Hope Gu. Without one, where would they get primeval stones in order to trade from? Without one, they would no doubt be attacked by other clans. That Blood Path Gu Master who had tried to extort them earlier would just be the first among many if the news got out that their primeval spring was dying. It was a tragedy that was more catastrophic than their losses from Lord Sky Crane and Bai Ning Bing's detonation from a certain perspective - they could always rebuild, but finding another primeval spring was another story entirely.

chapters.title: Chapter 222 222: Bei Gu Mountain: Part Two
chapters.content:
"Isn't it obvious what we need to do?" Fang Yuan said. "We need to relocate the clan to where there is another primeval spring."
"Another primeval spring?" Qing Shu said. "Where would we find one? And we need to find one fast, don't we?"
"Well, thankfully, there is something that can help us," Fang Yuan said with a gentle smile. "I think I know the location of a fresh primeval spring."
"You do? How?"
Fang Yuan waved his hand. "I'm sorry, but it's a bit of a secret, which I can't divulge to the two of you right now. However, we need to move fast if we want to claim this primeval spring before someone else gets to it. Because of that, I am going to the location in question myself to establish our presence there. Once that is done, we can start with the process of relocating our clan."
By his own estimation, the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus would still take about two months to completely dissipate, so they had at least that much time left. And even after that, it would still take time for the primeval spring to completely die out.
There were numerous concerns that they would have to address if they tried to move their clan. It wasn't just the fact that traveling with people was dangerous. There was also the matter of moving the clan's resources, the most obvious of which were the Moon Orchids. They would have to be transplanted in such a way that they could be grown at their new location. Otherwise, how would they feed their gu worms?
"When will you be leaving?" Fang Zheng asked.
"This afternoon," Fang Yuan said.
The clan Elders had noticed that Fang Yuan often took time off way more than the former clan leaders had. They would have liked to reprimand him to some extent, but they just couldn't because of his strength. However, if he took off for even more days, they would no doubt start making noise.
"That's why I need the two of you to stall for time while I go there."
"Can't you send someone else?" Qing Shu asked. "Fang Zheng and I can go in your stead..."
"The place where I'm going is near another clan," Fang Yuan said. "Although a Rank 3 Gu Master can survive in the wilderness and make the trip alone, you would lack the sufficient strength to stake a claim there. You need someone at Rank 5 in order to do so," Fang Yuan said. There's a reason why most clans were founded by Rank 5 ancestors in the past, after all.
Once you found a primeval spring, there would be other people coming in to try to take advantage of it or snatch it away from someone. Only a Rank 5 Gu Master could chase away such people for some time, and afterwards, a Rank 4 Gu master could still oversee it once the clan had been established.
While being transplanted, though, the clan would be in its weakest state and would definitely need Fang Yuan's close care and attention.
"To think that all of that stuff happened, and then this happened on top of it," Qing Shu said.
"All of this happened because of that," Fang Yuan said. "The attack on Qing Mountain is what led to such destruction of the spirit springs. But there's no need for the two of you to get despondent. Hasn't our clan lasted for a thousand years? Who's to say that it won't last for ten thousand more? All we need to do is establish ourselves in this new location. This is not the end of the Gu Yue clan, but a new beginning. So long as we still live, we can continue. And where there's life, there's hope, after all. Our ancestor initially come from the Central Continent. Moving the clan is not as big a deal as the two of you might think," Fang Yuan said. He was, of course, downplaying the difficulties that they would encounter to a great extent, but he needed the two of them to be firmly on his side and also for them to not fall into despair before they'd even started.
"Alright, we understand," Fang Zheng said.
"Alright, we can't announce this news to the other elders for now, I don't want panic spreading. However, Elder Qing Shu, I would like a sort of preliminary report depicting what you think would need to happen should we try to move the clan to that location." The logistics of all of it had to be worked out much in advance.
"And if anything happens, you can communicate with me through this," Fang Yuan said, handing Fang Zheng a special gu which would allow them to maintain contact.
"Alright, brother," Fang Zheng said. "Don't worry, I won't let you down."
"Neither will I," Qing Shu said.
"Good. I believe I can rely on the two of you. If anything happens, or there's some political issue, you can also speak to Elder Han Lin. I didn't because the more people who know about something, the more likely it will be to be leaked out. But I think that we can trust him," Fang Yuan said.
"I also think so," Qing Shu said. "Elder Han Lin is trustworthy. However, I don't know how much he will help us. He's almost gone completely into retirement at this point."
Fang Yuan nodded, "Well, it's good that the two of you understand."
Fang Yuan took several things from the clan into his storage-type Gu worm. The official story was that he was in closed-door cultivation, and if that did not fly, they would say that he had gone to deal with some kind of demonic Gu Master. News of him leaving would cause great panic to the clan as he was one of the few people who could deal with certain threats. It might even, in ordinary times, induce an attack from the Bai Clan - though given Bai Ning Bing would be going with him, they would not dare.
It wasn't as if the village was completely undefended, however.
He spent part of the day teaching Fang Zheng how to handle the Crimsonhoof Deer. The two of them were closely related by blood, and though Fang Zheng was only Rank 3, he could use this to his advantage by directing it using Fang Yuan's method of enslavement.
"It has the strength of a Rank 4 Gu Master, it should be more than enough to dissuade anyone who happens to drop by," Fang Yuan said. "I wouldn't put too much trust in it though, if push comes to shove it would prefer to flee rather than fight. But just threatening to unleash it should be more than enough for anything that pops up."
Later that evening, he snuck out of the village by going to the underground cavern, past the Dollhouse and into the Blood River Graveyard, where he met Bai Ning Bing.
"Are you ready?" Fang Yuan asked.
Bai Ning Bing nodded. "Are you sure about leaving, though? It almost seems like you're abandoning your own clan."
"Nonsense," Fang Yuan said. "How could I possibly abandon my clan?"
Bai Ning Bing snorted.
She removed the White Form Immortal Snake from her aperture. She had refined it, but this was a bit of a double-edged sword when compared to before when it had just joined with her because it had been attracted to the Northern Dark Ice Soul physique.
Back then, although she had not been able to command it fully, it no longer needed her own primeval essence in order to work. Now that she had refined it, it would do whatever she asked for, but she needed to provide it with primeval essence, something which, as a Rank 3 Peak Stage Gu Master, she could not do.
She lent it to Fang Yuan, who began pouring his Rank 5 essence into it, allowing it to show its true strength and speed as it began soaring up into the air.
"Come on," Fang Yuan said, beckoning her to join him, "unless you would rather stay here."
Bai Ning Bing was more of a liability than anything to Fang Yuan at her cultivation level, but she was the one who had the White Form Immortal Snake, after all. It was only being lent to him for some time.
"No, I'm coming," Bai Ning Bing said, snorting.
If Fang Yuan had a method to steal this gu worm, he would have, but the Spring Autumn Cicada could provide him with no help here.
The two of them left through a tunnel and then flew off into the night sky.

chapters.title: Chapter 223 223: Bei Gu Mountain: Part Three
chapters.content:
The cold night air whipped past Fang Yuan's ears. He had a gu worm that could protect him from the cold as he glanced back towards Bai Ning Bing, wondering if she had the same. She seemed to be shivering.
"Feeling cold?" he asked her.
Bai Ning Bing shook her head, either because she felt too proud or because the Northern Dark Ice Soul physique provided some kind of protection from the cold. Fang Yuan doubted it was the latter and more likely that it was the former. However, he felt there was little that he could do if she refused all of his offers of help.
One could not downplay the White Form Immortal Snake's speed compared to the Hundred Li Earthwolf Spider, which may as well have been crawling by comparison. Not only that, but soaring above the skies meant that they encountered very few things that might otherwise obstruct them along their journey. They made amazing time in terms of distance covered.
