chapters.title: Chapter 234: Flesh Bone Lord: Part Four
chapters.content:
They walked through the passageway and happened upon a chamber where there was the skull of some kind of animal with a massive bone pyramid in the middle, along with some text written in front of it in a book similar to what they had found before.
"Oh, this has so many refinement recipes in it," Fang Yuan said, flitting through it smiling. With these recipes, the Gu Yue clan, if they moved here, could indeed become masters of the Bone Path and start manufacturing limitless amounts of those Rank 3 and Rank 2 Gu worms. It made such a thing to be a truly viable concept. "It says here that he tried to refine the Bone Flesh Unity Gu in his earlier life, but had failed," Fang Yuan said, frowning.
He had thought that the Bone Flesh Unity Gu would have already been refined by the time they got here, but it looked like there was still some work to be done.
"It says we should record our efforts whether we succeed or fail," Bai Ning Bing said. Fang Yuan knew that they absolutely could succeed. After all, the Bei twins had. However, what was he supposed to do from beyond here?
"It says here, 'Gemini with one mind, three spirits unite. Fated or not, do not be forceful...'," Bai Ning Bing said, not understanding what it meant.
"Gemini means two people together. Three spirits means the palm, eye, and mind. It means that we need to keep our palms on here," Fang Yuan said. Both Bai Ning Bing and Fang Yuan kept their palms on the pupils of the sculpture but found that it did nothing.
Bai Ning Bing chuckled. "It looks like you were wrong this time, Fang Yuan."
"No, we missed part of that," Fang Yuan said. "It says that the two who put their hands here have to be of one mind." The two of them couldn't be further from that, being diametrically opposed to each other most of the time. Were it not for mutual need, they might have even torn each other's throats out on the spot. The two of them had even tried to kill each other in the past as well.
"Since the two of us are not of two minds of one mind, what can we do?" Bai Ning Bing asked. It was only the two of them there. They had not run into anyone else nor brought anyone else along with them. Fang Yuan had not anticipated this being an issue. 'Should I have kidnapped the Bei twins and brought them here?' It might have been possible with his strength, but it would ruin the rest of his plans. He would have to completely eradicate the Bei clan afterwards.
As he began plotting for this scenario in his head, he was struck by inspiration.
He suddenly realized that he did not need to resort to kidnapping because he had something better. The Integration Gu!
'What were minds, but the manifestation of the wills of individuals?' He had the wills of thousands of Gu Yue clansmen kept within Integration Gu. Although he had used up some of them while fighting the Xuan Yuan Divine Pheasant, there were still many left he had not used up. He just needed to find two of them which were of the same mind.
After searching through them, he found wills belonging to Li Mei and Yu Sai. He took out both of the wills.
"Put this inside your head," Fang Yuan said. "It'll trick this little mechanism."
Bai Ning Bing examined it suspiciously. It looked like a miniature version of a person, but it was also translucent, as if it was some kind of hologram. Fang Yuan took out one for himself and put it in his head, and only after that, did Bai Ning Bing repeat the same.
She had been given Li Mei's thoughts and will, and suddenly her mind was flooded with Li Mei's thoughts.
"Why did you give me the woman's thoughts?!" Bai Ning Bing demanded from Fang Yuan.
"Because you're a woman," Fang Yuan said through gritted teeth.
Fang Yuan was also having difficulties. Why was that?
Because these two were horny beyond belief for each other!
Indeed, their horniness was beyond even Fang Yuan's estimations!
Fang Yuan felt his mind being flood with thoughts about Yu Sai's fantasies of Li Mei's body. His 'little brother' suddenly filled up and became active despite his own inward protests. He had not expected that Yu Sai would be this down bad to the point where it was even affecting him.
It was even worse for Bai Ning Bing - who was seeing Li Mei's fantasies about a man! She most definitely did not want such thoughts flooding her head!
'...Li Mei has such a tight waist, and I bet she can do a lot of things with those hips of hers...' Fang Yuan's mind was being invaded by these kinds of thoughts.
'...and then Yu Sai would take off his pants and force me down and then... - AHHHH! Make it stop!' Bai Ning Bing's thoughts were like this.
"Endure and put your palms back there," Fang Yuan said and Bai Ning Bing complied.
However, as something rose from the ground, "Success," Fang Yuan thought to himself, chasing the unwanted thoughts away from his head.
The wills were rather miniscule, and so after a few minutes they flowed away and both Bai Ning Bing and Fang Yuan returned to normal.
They had been successful in what they intended to do, however, as the skull cracked and revealed some pottery with a scroll lying in the middle with the recipe to refine the Bone Flesh Unity Gu.
New Main Mission Unlocked!
Fulfilling A Dying Wish
Description: Refine the Bone-Flesh Unity Gu successfully.
Reward: ???
They began reading through the requirements needed to refine the gu worm, where they happened upon another problem. "Fang Yuan, it says that the people who need to refine this need to be of one blood," Bai Ning Bing said. "The two of us are not related. How are we possibly going to do this?"
Fang Yuan once again turned his mind towards the Bei twins. No wonder they had been able to do this. They both were of one mind and were related, but these details were omitted from the story he had heard.
Once again, he had not foreseen this. However, that didn't mean that there wasn't a solution to it. He used his communication Gu, reaching out towards Fang Zheng in Gu Yue village.
Meanwhile, in Gu Yue Village...
Fang Zheng and Qing Shu were trying their best to hold down the fort while Fang Yuan was gone.
"Where is clan head now?" one of the elders not directly associated with Fang Yuan complained. "He has taken more days off during his short tenure than the prior clan head did within a decade!"
Many of the elders felt the same way. Although Fang Yuan was clan head he oftentimes ran off to do other things, or took long periods off for his own cultivation. During a time like this, when the clan was at its weakest, they felt it was necessary for Fang Yuan to take a more hands-on approach rather than what he was currently doing.
Now, they couldn't really do anything about it as Fang Yuan was Rank 5, but they had become more vocal as of late. It was almost as if - in their own words - they did not really have a clan head at all!
"Elder brother is not taking time off," Fang Zheng reassured them. "He is simply dealing with an issue related to the clan."
"Indeed," Qing Shu said. "And he will be returning soon."
Naturally this did not stop the questions thrown their way.
"What kind of mission?"
"Why didn't he let us know?"
"He's probably just working on his own cultivation..."
Fang Zheng and Qing Shu continued trying to deflect the questions with minimal success.

chapters.title: Chapter 235: Meanwhile, In Gu Yue Village: Part One
chapters.content:
Fang Zheng practically stormed out of the meeting room. Once it was over, Qing Shu quickly caught him and took him aside.
"It isn't good for you to act like that. You're an elder now, Fang Zheng," Qing Shu said. "Which means that other people will look closely at how you behave and react. Since you're also Fang Yuan's younger brother, it also reflects badly on him if you can't seem to control your temper."
"But the way they were talking inside..." Fang Zheng said, shaking his head. "They're calling my older brother an 'old man' behind his back as if he's shirking his duties, when in reality, he's just trying to keep the clan safe."
"I know," Qing Shu said. "But there must be a good reason why Fang Yuan kept the news of the spirit spring potentially dying a secret. It is to prevent panic, and so we can't let them know that."
"I don't get why they're behaving like this," Fang Zheng said. "As if my brother needs to be here constantly..."
Qing Shu smiled and shrugged. "Tell me, when you were young and felt like things were overwhelming, who did you want to go to?"
Fang Zheng's honest answer was, "No one because there was no one there."
"Both of us are orphans, so I think you can understand this," Qing Shu said. "When you're scared, the one thing that you want is the reassuring hand of a parent. I'm sure you must have sought that many times over when you were younger, to no avail."
"The elders right now are much like scared children. Don't look at their ages. Our clan has stood for a thousand years, and never has it been in such a state of disaster. Despite their vast life experience, they have no precedent for what is going on now. At any moment, it seems as if the flame that is the life of our village could go out. What do they wish for during this situation? Stability. Naturally, they want something to lean on, someone who would tell them that everything is alright, someone like Fang Yuan.
"But brother is not even a quarter of the age of some of those elders..."
"It isn't about age; it's about power," Qing Shu said. "He is Rank 5. When the chips are down and push comes to shove in this world, only strength matters." He gazed far into the distance. "I've realized that now. Although clan ties and family bonds are important, without power, they cannot assert their full force. Fang Yuan is Rank 5. Even though he has just stepped into the realm of Rank 5 and is among the weakest of them, he is still far stronger than any Rank 4 Gu Master. Why do you think no more demonic Gu Masters have come to try and attack our village? Is it just because the Tie Clan was here recently? No, it's also because they fear Fang Yuan."
"I just thought," Fang Zheng said, sighing, "that things might be different once I got to Rank 3." Rank 3 Gu Masters were the backbone of the village, the ones who were in charge of everything, and everyone looked up to them. Fang Zheng had felt ecstatic when he reached that realm.
However, now that he was there, it felt that he had climbed to the top of a mountain, only to note that there was an even bigger peak right next to him, which he had only noticed now that he had climbed to the top.
Unfortunately, he knew that Rank 3 was likely going to be his limit. It had taken a monumental effort to get him to this point, and even advancing to another minor realm might be difficult unless he advanced his Vital Gu. For that, he would need to find, according to his brother, two more Liquor Worms. Even one was difficult to find; how would he find two? Alternatively, they could try to reverse-refine his Four Flavors Liquor Worm back into two Liquor Worms, because the clan had its own sequence of advancement for the Liquor Worm to Rank 3. All of that, however, had to wait.
"Oh, as Rank 3 Gu Masters we are quite powerful," Qing Shu said. "But that doesn't mean that we can shoulder the burden of the entire clan on our shoulders. Not even Fang Yuan, who's rank five, can do that. That's why we have to work hard, don't we? He may be the main pillar, but we are his support."
Fang Zheng had initially felt bitter towards Qing Shu, simply because he thought that Qing Shu was undermining his role as Fang Yuan's main helper. He had thought things would change when he got rank three, but even now, Qing Shu was still ahead of him whether it came to experience or cultivation. However, there was no room for his personal discontent, he knew. Not right now. For now, they had to put up a united front against the others.
"I'm heading off towards the academy now," Qing Shu said. "If you want, you can also come by and just see how things are going."
"You're going to the academy? Why?" Fang Zheng asked.
"Oh, I'm just giving them a lesson or two," Qing Shu said. "Gu Yue Ye is the academy head, but he's not an elder, and I think if I were to drop by to teach them, they would appreciate it." There was another reason, of course. Qing Shu wanted to make sure that things were going smoothly at the academy. It was Fang Yuan's pet project, after all.
"Alright then," Fang Zheng said, also personally interested in how the academy was going now with the fewer number of students.
As he walked into the gate which had been recently repaired, he thought about giving the academy elder a visit for old time's sake - before remembering that the academy elder was dead.
'It looks so... empty...' he thought to himself.
It was almost like walking into a ghost town. It didn't help that most of the buildings were still damaged adding to the uncanny feeling one got while walking in.
The students were assembled in a courtyard. Given how few of them there were, there was no need to clean up most of the mess in the courtyard in a certain corner - Gu Yue Ye might have felt that way but Fang Zheng felt that it would be better for morale to have it tidy.
The students were practicing the basic moonblade techniques against grass puppets, much like he had done. He recalled how he had accidentally managed to hit the grass puppet right where it was important, only for the contest to be won by Fang Yuan.
'Mo Bei... Chi Chen...' They had been his rivals during that time, and were now dead. So were most of his classmates. He had known, from what others had told him, that such things would happen over time. Just not so soon.
"Hello everyone, we have a special guest with us today," the instructor said. "Oh wait, I'm sorry, two special guests here. Elder Qing Shu and Elder Fang Zheng, thank you for joining us!"
The students were divided into two groups not based on size - but based on whether or not they were Gu Yue clansmen or not. The mortals were off to one side and the youngsters off to another. It wasn't a significant separation, mind you, barely imperceptible, but to Fang Zheng who had only recently been in their shoes it was more than obvious.

chapters.title: Chapter 236 236: Meanwhile, In Gu Yue Village: Part Two
chapters.content:
"Good afternoon, everyone," Qing Shu said, smiling. A chorus of replies answered him. "I hope you all enjoyed the exciting art of throwing moonblades - I was here to give you another kind of lesson. Namely, in martial arts."
Understandably, many of them seemed less enthusiastic when they heard that.
"Now, don't get your moods too dampened down," Qing Shu said. "After all, when your primeval essence runs out, it is sometimes only your fists that you can rely upon. Our current clan head, Fang Yuan, was quite good at this when he was at the academy. Now, as a demonstration..." He beckoned to Fang Zheng. "Mind volunteering?"
Fang Zheng stood opposite to Qing Shu. "Alright, Fang Zheng will come at me, just watch closely for now."
Qing Shu knew that they really weren't ready for this kind of lesson, but they needed something flashy or else they'd stop paying attention.
"Are you sure?"
"Sure."
Fang Zheng launched himself at Qing Shu, who was a bit taken aback. Fang Zheng had been training with Fang Yuan for some time, and even if that were not the case, he was not just sitting on the sidelines. He often fought himself now.
That said, Qing Shu was still more experienced, and managed to lock Fang Zheng in.
"Alright, good work from Elder Fang Zheng," Qing Shu said.
The others watching were nearly dumbfounded as the speed with which the two of them moved was amazing.
"Alright, now I'll show you a few basic moves, please pair up and start practicing," Qing Shu said.
They had a bit of an issue here as the youngsters were not as many as the mortals, leading to a lopsided total. Fang Zheng was keeping a particularly close eye on them simply because he wanted to know how they were getting along. Ultimately, Qing Shu paired off against someone while Fang Zheng watched.
One of the mortal woman with long eyelashes was giving him sideways glances, though he didn't care for such. If he remembered correctly, she was the one with the highest aptitude among her class - though it was still only C-grade.
Afterwards, Fang Zheng had to go deal with his own issues.
Being an elder was not just lounging around and giving orders as many people thought, because there were threats that only they could deal with. And because times were uncertain, even the elders were feeling like they were being worked to the bone. One of them had even audibly complained that he had not been so busy even when he had been a rank two Gu Master scrambling for resources.
***
Bai Ning Bing's detonation had killed off most of the life on Qing Mao Mountain, including plant life. Without plants, the herbivores couldn't graze. When the herbivores couldn't graze, the prey animals, such as the wolves, also starved. That left humans as one of their few food sources. However, even the humans were low in number and rarely ventured outside their villages. With the Myriad Beast Kings of the wolves killed, most of those had simply perished.
They were not increasing in number to cause another similar wolf tide for another thirty years, assuming they managed to survive complete extinction. However, it was the nature of heaven to deplete surpluses and replenish deficits. Whenever there was a vacuum, a loss of a predator in an area, there was only one thing to come in and fill its place.
Earlier, when the ice had still covered the mountain, particularly at the base, no animals wandered near. However, now that summer was in full swing and the mountain was beginning to recover, so too were other animals being attracted towards this new ecological vacuum.
Yao Le had actually been the first one to see them. She had gone on a small mission to hunt for some medicinal herbs, which were very limited in supply given the events that occurred on the mountain.
"What happened?" the Gu Master leading the group said, as she suddenly stood up to him, pointing.
"Bears! Yes, there's a lot of them over there." One of their investigative Gu Masters took a look and shuddered at what he saw. "It's not just a bear group about eighty strong, but… there's a Lunar Bear among them."
"A Lunar Bear? Are you sure? There are only eighty of them, that shouldn't be possible."
"I'm definitely sure," the investigative Gu Master said.
Lunar Bears were Thousand Beast Kings and were called such because of the particular markings on their bellies, which resembled the moon, as well as their silvery fur. In the moonlight, their bodies would often emit a soft glow and they had excellent nocturnal vision. It was said that their first-generation ancestor had gotten the inspiration for creating the Moonlight Gu after seeing a lunar bear.
Although it was called a 'Thousand Beast King' it was possible that most of its companions had died out.
The Gu Master in charge said, "Alright, let's head back to the village."
***
"How many are there?" Fang Zheng asked as the group came back to report.
"About eighty. There was definitely a Thousand Beast King among them. I also saw two Hundred Beast Kings in a group that small."
Normally, these things usually ruled over the appropriate number of lower animals. However, there were times when that was not possible. Sometimes they would be the only surviving members of their species, and then go somewhere else. It looked like this flock had encountered some trouble near the base of Qing Mao Mountain, or while traveling, and many of them had died out.
"Alright then, don't worry, we'll deal with it," Fang Zheng said, smiling.
The Gu Master team left. "Where's Fang Yuan? I thought that he would be here," the Gu Master in charge said, clicking his teeth. "With him here, we could have dealt with it easily enough."
If the Lunar Bear was not killed, then it would grow into a true Thousand Beast King as the number of bears would reach that number over time. Soon, there might even be a Myriad Beast King among the bears. Instead of a wolf tide, the village might end up dealing with a bear tide if this problem was not nipped in the bud.
"Don't worry - I'm sure Fang Zheng can take care of it," Yao Le answered. "He's Rank 3 now, isn't he?"
Additionally, Feng Zheng had his own reasons for trying to deal with this.
After all, those bears could pose an obstacle for when they tried to relocate the village in the future. He reached out to Qing Shu and the other elders, though naturally, they were not very happy. "Fang Yuan should go ahead and deal with it, shouldn't he?"
"Where is he now?"
"You said he was dealing with something around the mountain? Isn't this more important"
This was the biggest threat they had faced up until now other than the Blood Path Gu Master who had come to extort them. Although technically they were all Rank 3 Gu Masters a large number of bears; over eighty, would not be easy for a single person to deal with. And naturally, they wished to minimize casualties given just how few Gu Masters the village already had.
"It is no matter," Feng Zheng said. "We will deal with this ourselves."
The elders were not very happy with it but complied nonetheless, as a team was made to deal with this bear problem that they had.
"Ready?" Qing Shu asked, noting the Gu on Fang Zheng's arm, a Chainsaw Golden Centipede. "Where did you happen to find that?"

chapters.title: Chapter 237: Meanwhile, in Gu Yue Village: Part Three
chapters.content:
"My brother gave it to me," Fang Zheng replied. He also had a defensive rank three Gu worm, but other than that, his other Gus were rank two. His vital Gu, the Four Flavors Liquor Worm, was useless to him in a fight.
With just him, Qing Shu, and a few other elders and Gu Masters there, it might seem that they were outmatched in terms of might. However, Fang Zheng had one trick up his sleeve, but he was waiting for the right time to use it.
"Let's go," Qing Shu said, hands digging into the dirt as vines began erupting. The bears scattered about and not in a single group, which was to their advantage. Two of the smaller groups were towards the left and right of the main formation, so to speak, and were being attacked by two teams of Gu Masters led by an elder. Qing Shu and Fang Zheng, along with some other Gu Masters, were dealing with the group in the middle.
Hopefully, the two 'wings' of the formation could be dealt with before the lunar bear had time to retaliate.
As the cries of bears erupted all over, those at the front were being torn apart and were being split in half by numerous Moonblades that were flying.
There was the hundred beast king, and Fang Zheng went to go intercept it. It was three times the size of the other bears, with massive fangs and claws that could easily swipe the roof of a house away in a single blow. As it lunged at Fang Zheng, vines suddenly erupted, stopping it as Fang Zheng took off one of its paws. The Chainsaw Golden Centipede cut through its thick flesh as if it was nothing.
Even if it had had a Rank Two defensive gu worm, it wouldn't have been able to do anything against the might of the Chainsaw Golden Centipede.
The Lunar Bear had not joined the fight directly but was instead rallying the other bears to its side. Unfortunately for it, about a third of them had already been killed before they could rally to it. A vine snapped the Hundred Beast King's neck. However, there was still another Hundred Beast King lurking around.
The bears died in large numbers. The Gu Masters had the benefit of organization, as well as the element of surprise. The bears also looked mostly malnourished, which could have possibly helped with their fighting strength. However, as the battle was going smoothly, or so it seemed, one of the bears suddenly screamed and then grew three times in size.
"Another Hundred Beast King!" someone yelled out. The Lunar Bear seemed to have been waiting for this as it now began entering the fray, which meant that the elders would have to come in and deal with it.
Or... did they?
"I think the time's right," Qing Shu said, nodding towards Fang Zheng, who whistled from the rear of the formation. Something leaped out and tackled the Lunar Bear. It was the Crimsonhoof Deer which Fang Yuan had left behind. Although Fang Yuan had removed several of its gu worms, more of them had been attracted to its body, and some had even advanced to rank four on their own.
One strike from its antlers made a massive gash in the Lunar Bear's body. It roared, the bears coming to reinforce it, but as they retreated, they were slaughtered from behind by the Gu Masters. Whatever gu worms it had on it could not save it from its demise. The difference in strength between the Crimson Hoof Deer and the lunar bear was just too great, even if Fang Zheng could not control it completely, it would not run away when it had such a territorial advantage.
The only thing which surprised them slightly was that the lunar bear had a gu worm which acted much like a Moonblade. However, it was green in color, a color none of them had seen before. They would have liked to have obtained that gu simply for the study and future development of this clan. However, it ended up fleeing into the wilderness before they could catch it.
With the battle over however, they returned back to Gu Yue village.
Yao Le personally came out and asked Fang Zheng if he was injured. "I'm not, but there are some other people in the rear that you might want to look at," Fang Zheng said. "Thankfully, casualties have been low." This was mainly thanks to the Crimsonhoof Deer's existence, otherwise at least one elder would've been injured.
"Oh, it's good to know that you're all right," Yao Le said before heading out to take care of the others. Yao Le had advanced to Rank 2 by now, and everyone said that she would soon become the new medicine hall elder. Fang Zheng himself did not doubt that, as it was clear that her skills were first class.
As things seemed to be going smoothly, however, early the next morning, Fang Zheng felt Fang Yuan contact him.
"What? He wants me to be there?" he wondered. This was an odd thing, but he sent a message to Qing Shu, letting him know that he would be gone and that this was a request from Fang Yuan.
Fang Zheng still had Traveling Son Gu while Fang Yuan had Doting Mother Gu - although they were Rank 4, Fang Zheng's Rank 3 essence was barely enough to activate it, taking him to where Fang Yuan was.
His primeval essence was completely gone as he found himself in the chamber alongside Fang Yuan and Bai Ning Bing.
"Brother, you called?"
"Yes, I happened to need your help," Fang Yuan said.
He handed Fang Zheng the book in question and explained how the refinement of Bone-Flesh Unity Gu went.
"Wait... it wants our flesh?" Fang Zheng wondered, quite concerned.
"I know that it might be painful," Fang Yuan said. "But think about it this way - what was more painful to you? Losing your aptitude, or being injured? Your injuries can be healed, but don't you want to advance to Rank 4?"
Fang Yuan could've forcibly taken some flesh from Fang Zheng, but the recipe also wanted a good relationship between the two Gu Masters who were refining it. Without a doubt, if it was just him and Bai Ning Bing, the result would not be good.
But it was possible that Fang Zheng still had some warm feelings towards him - meaning the result would be much better in that regard.
Fang Zheng thought about it. He had assumed he was one of the lucky few with an A-grade talent who would be able to soar through the skies easily, but these dreams had been dashed by Lord of the Mysteries. Even now, it was unclear if he could even get to Rank 3 Middle Stage if he didn't continue to have Equality Gu's help.
"Alright, let's do it!" Fang Yuan said.
"Take these primeval stones and recover your essence - Bai Ning Bing, it's best you step aside," Fang Yuan said. If she was added to the refinement mix, it was almost certain that they would get a bad result.
Once Fang Zheng was done recovering his primeval essence, Fang Yuan, in one swift motion, cut Fang Zheng's right arm off before tossing it in as gu refinement material.

chapters.title: Chapter 238: Bone-Flesh Unity Gu: Part One
chapters.content:
Fang Zheng screamed as pain erupted throughout his shoulder, only for it to immediately go away as his arm grew back completely. However, the memory of the pain still lingered in his body. A cold sweat coated his brow and his heart raced. He found that he was breathing heavily, even as Fang Yuan brother cut off his own right arm.
Doing something like that, even for Fang Yuan, was quite painful. He gritted his teeth before his arm ended up growing back.
Bai Ning Bing was a bit shocked, not by the fact that Fang Yuan had cut off his own and his brother's arms (she had expected that), but by the fact that he had such a good healing gu worm that it restored his arm completely.
She had thought that she might have to let him borrow the Bone Flesh Unity Gu, which by itself was a first-class healing gu. However, whatever Fang Yuan had clearly superseded it by several magnitudes. Fang Yuan tossed both severed arms into the flame. "Hopefully, that's all it needs," Fang Yuan said, as Fang Zheng felt dizzy, realizing that they might have to give up more flesh in order to get this gu.
Fang Yuan and Fang Zheng placed their hands on the pupil and began injecting their primeval essence. The flames began changing color. Fang Yuan quickly realized there was a problem midway through because of his vast experience when it came to refining.
"It needs more flesh," he said.
Fang Zheng's arm was torn off once again. The fact that it grew back near-instantly did not make the moment any less morbid. It seemed that these two additional arms were enough. As the fire started to die down, two Gu worms were born from the refinement: Bone Flesh Unity Gu! Fang Yuan picked them up. They were in the form of two bracelets - green and blue, one to be worn by each Gu Master.
Main Mission Complete!
Refined the Bone Flesh Unity Gu successfully.
Reward: A detailed map of Bei Gu Mountain!
Fang Yuan did not even have to claim the reward. There wasn't even an option to reject it. Immediately, his head was assaulted with a detailed 3-dimensional construction of the entirety of Bei Gu Mountain, all of its corridors, tunnels, important locations, etc.
It did not show any living things, but he had a clear view of its geography. Most importantly, it showed its primeval springs. There were two primeval springs located on Bei Gu Mountain. One of them was rather close to where they were, but they would have to deal with a large group of beasts before getting there. The other was closer to the foot of the mountain, where Bai Ning Bing would have liked to search initially.
Fang Yuan took the Flesh Bone Lord's book as another mission appeared from the system.
New main mission!
"Sharing is Caring."
Description: Allow the Bei Clan to settle on Bei Gu Mountain as well by giving them the location of the other spirit spring.
Reward: ???
Fang Yuan snorted inwardly. There was no way that he was about to give out that kind of location to another clan. What possible benefit would that give him?
Whether one saw it from a demonic or a righteous perspective, such a thing went completely against common sense. From the righteous perspective, he should look after his own clan, not the needs of another. If he told them where the other spring was, they would surely come to cause trouble for his clan in the future. And from the demonic perspective, why should he give benefits to anyone else? The system seemed to have realized that he was going to reject it and began elucidating what rewards it was going to give him:
Rewards:
The recipe for Rank 5 Testicular Torsion Gu.
The recipe for Rank 4 Bone Javelin Gu.
The recipe for Rank 5 Bone Lance Gu.
Rank 5 Earth Eating Eel Gu (x 1)
Rank 5 Man Triumphing over Heaven Gu (x1).
Rank 5 training weights Gu (x1).
Rank 5 Ink Dragon Gu (x1) [A powerful offensive gu worm].
500,000 primeval stones.
Fang Yuan was slightly taken aback by just how generous these rewards were.
The system had remained mostly quiet until now, but it looked like it was raining everything down upon him at once.
A Rank 5 Training Weights Gu could be useful, as he could combine it with the Bone Flesh Unity Gu to try and improve Fang Zheng's cultivation level.
Although he had gone through much pain in order to refine the Bone Flesh Unity Gu, he was disappointed to learn upon refining it that it was only Rank 4. Since the Bei twins had risen to Rank 5 he has assumed that it would be useful even to Rank 5, but it looked like such was not the case. That meant that it could not carry Rank 5 primeval essence.
It would have been quite useful to him before, but right now, he couldn't even use it to advance someone else's cultivation without diluting his own primeval essence to Rank 4 using something like Training Weights Gu first.
As for the recipes for the Rank 4 and Rank 5 gu worms, they both seemed to be advancements of Bone Spear Gu. If Fang Yuan wanted to settle his clan here, rank four and rank five bone path recipes were quite useful.
As for Man Triumphing Over Heaven Gu, it was a consumable gu worm that could be used to forcibly open one's aperture if one had no talent to cultivate. He had no use for it right now.
Rank 5 Ink Dragon Gu... the system said it was an offensive gu worm, but that could have several connotations. It seemed to be from the Painting Path based on its name.
Rank 5 Earth Eating Eel would be useful for transplanting Moon Orchid seeds from one location to another.
'If such is the case,' he thought to himself, 'and I only need to tell them the location of this primeval spring, perhaps something can be worked out.'
From the righteous path perspective, it was still the wrong thing to reveal to the Bai Clan where the second primeval spring was. From the demonic path perspective, though, it was completely fine for Fang Yuan to prioritize his own benefits over those of others.
The reason why it was wrong from the righteous path perspective was that a good clan leader would recognize that they would not live forever and would not willingly give over such a resource to a potential enemy. However, Fang Yuan had no consideration for the future of his clan beyond what they could give him, and as such, these benefits, which greatly benefited himself, were more than enough reason for him to want to do so.
"Alright. I think we should go down here," he said. They walked further down into the cavern and exited onto the mountain.

chapters.title: Chapter 239: Bone-Flesh Unity Gu: Part Two
chapters.content:
The sun had come up two hours earlier and was shining brightly against the bones of Bei Gu Mountain.
"Fang Yuan, we found an inheritance - but not what we were looking for," Bai Ning Bing said. "We came here to find a primeval spring... and we still don't have one." The resultant inheritance wasn't even that remarkable, particularly for a Rank 5 Gu Master.
"Judging by the amount of bone-path beasts that there are, I think it should be over there," Fang Yuan said, pointing seemingly randomly towards the direction where he knew the primeval spring would be.
"How are you going to get past that?" Feng Shang wondered, seeing the massive amount of bone beasts that stood in their path.
"This is why I got this gu, didn't I?" Fang Yuan said, activating Rainbow Cannon Gu.
A rainbow shot out from his palm. However, it was not simply a mixture of bright lights; wherever it landed it dealt damage, placing massive holes in the bone path beasts as it went from one beast to another like a seamstress's needle. As they walked along the path, Bai Ning Bing still felt that they should look somewhere deeper in the mountain towards the base.
But given all that Fang Yuan had showed her, she was willing to just follow him and see what was going on for now.
Fang Yuan seemingly wandered into a cave at random and said, "Oh, look, we found it."
The two others stumbled into it. It was not a full primeval spring, but rather one of the tiny streams that would unite to form a larger primeval spring. The water was clear and untainted, but carried the faint aura of a spirit spring.
If they followed this deeper, they would happen upon the actual primeval spring.
"Great job, brother," Fang Zheng said, eyes practically sparkling. "With this, we can save our clan."
Bai Ning Bing, meanwhile, was wondering how Fang Yuan knew about all of this.
The inheritance could have actually been something left behind by someone on Qing Mao Mountain, and perhaps the inheritance also mentioned the location of the primeval spring.
But for Fang Yuan to know this with such precise detail... even if he had just been given a vague hint, it would have taken him at least a few more days to find all of this stuff. Moreover, Bai Ning Bing did not know of any such inheritance clues left on Qing Mao Mountain. It could be a Gu Yue Clan specialty, though it looked like Fang Zheng was also surprised. "There's too much randomness for me to make any kind of conclusion," Bai Ning Bing thought to herself.
Following the stream was easier said than done, as it would oftentimes tunnel into passageways too narrow for them to follow. In such a situation they could only use guesswork and alternate paths, but this was far, far, easier than wandering through the mountain blindly.
By noon, they managed to finally follow the small stream into the spirit spring proper.
Clean water flowed from up above into a massive pond, and surrounding it, tens of thousands of bright lights flickered - Hope Gu! Next to the spirit spring, there was another spring filled with whitish liquid: milk, which could be used to nourish many of the Bone Path gu worms that they had. Fang Yuan told Fang Zheng to reach into the milk spring, and he found several hundred more gu worms.
"There's a tiny fortune right here," Fang Zheng said. "We still have one problem, though - the fact that there's no soil." Because of this, growing crops would be difficult. Although the milk could provide a large amount of nutrition and could be modified into various products like cheese and curd, they would need to import a large amount of their food, mainly rice, from elsewhere. Also, they couldn't grow their signature Moon Orchids here.
Fang Yuan shrugged and responded to Fang Zheng, "This is the closest primeval spring that is free, which is near our village. We can't possibly expect for everything to be there in our new home. Perhaps we can think of some way to preserve the Moon Orchid petals, otherwise we may need to switch to cultivating the Bone Path. What's important is that we found this fresh primeval spring full of vitality. It can last for quite a while."
Having marked the location, they now had to deal with preventing the Bei clan from also stumbling upon this resource while they left. To do so, Fang Yuan had them create false trails all the rest of the afternoon around the mountain so it would be hard for them to be followed. Not only that, he had purposefully not exterminated many of the bone beasts so that they would be an obstacle to the Bei clansmen if they chose to follow them.
"Now, if you'll excuse me," Fang Yuan said before they left, "there's something that I wanted to speak to the Bei clan head about."
By this point the Bei clan was in the middle of organizing a large hunting party to see where Fang Yuan had gone. That is, until Fang Yuan happened to show himself right outside their doorstep, asking if the Bei Clan leader was still there and available for a meeting.
"Let him in," the Bei Clan leader said.
She had hoped that he had left, but instead he had returned to the mountain in the middle of the night and was now here to speak with her. What was going on? Fang Yuan walked into her tent and said that he would like to speak with her one-on-one. She dismissed the other elders. Fang Yuan didn't say anything further, but simply handed her an old book.
The Bei Clan head began reading it, and her expression froze. "This is…" The book was written by someone by the name of Flesh Bone Lord. According to it, he had been the eldest child of a Gu Master from the Gu Yue Clan and the Bai Clan who had eloped and found their way to Bei Gu Mountain. After that, it detailed an inheritance that he had left behind in case there were any Gu Yue or Bai Clan Gu Masters who happened to pass by.
"This book… where did you get this?" the Bei clan head asked.
"Oh, I happened to find the inheritance in question. That book is from said inheritance. It looks like the Gu Yue Clan always had a stake on Bei Gu Mountain."
"This can't be real," the Bei clan head finally said. Her first instinct was to tear the book apart. However, if Fang Yuan had handed her a copy, he most certainly had one himself or other evidence. And was it really wise to try to tear up the book before a Rank 5 Gu Master?
Fang Yuan smiled. The truth was that she was right; it was fake. Fang Yuan was quite good at forging documents and the like, and had oftentimes sold fake goods back during his time as a demonic Gu Master.
So it had been child's play for him to alter a few pages to fit his own narrative. The Flesh Bone Lord had not left his name, so he had simply made one up for him - Gu Yue Bai Bo! There was a very emotional section of the book in which he entailed how he had chosen to take both the 'Gu Yue' and 'Bai' clan names as a way of honoring his parents - Fang Yuan had nearly shed a tear while forging it.
He had also either taken or destroyed everything of worth in the inheritance after obtaining Bone-Flesh Unity Gu. Now that there were no further benefits to be achieved, he had no qualms about ransacking the place.
It would not hold up to intense scrutiny, but Fang Yuan did not need it to. So long as he had his strength and this flimsiest of excuses, there was nothing that the Bei Clan could do to stop his plan from taking the mountain. The Bei clan had made many enemies and grudges with the surrounding clans, while the Gu Yue clan was a blank slate to them. A fight with the Gu Yue clan would not go well for them.

chapters.title: Chapter 240: Bone-Flesh Unity Gu: Part Three
chapters.content:
"It will not be wise to provoke me," Fang Yuan said, taking the book back. "Especially given that your clan's spirit spring is dying." The Bei clan leader's expression froze.
'What? Is this man bluffing? How could he possibly know that?'
"It's rather obvious seeing how eager you are to explore this mountain. You intend to make Bei Gu Mountain your own, don't you? To make it your new home? And you're looking for a spirit spring there, it's not a bad idea. It's what I was here to do myself, actually," Fang Yuan said, no longer hiding his intention.
"So you do intend to bring the Gu Yue Clan to Bei Gu?" the Bei clan head asked, her worst fears all but confirmed.
"Indeed, I do," Fang Yuan said. "We need a new home for ourselves, and this seems close enough. I've actually grown quite fond of the place after just seeing it once - its natural beauty has truly captivated my heart."
The Bei clan head's knuckles whitened as she squeezed them against the nearby table. She gritted her teeth. "So then, why are you here? Do you just want to lord your victory over us?"
"No, actually," Fang Yuan said. "I think that just because we happen to move here does not mean that we need to be enemies. Since the Gu Yue and the Bei clans will now be neighbors, shouldn't we try to get along?"
The Bei clan head snorted. "Is this what 'getting along' means? By taking away our only source of salvation?"
"Who said it was your only source of salvation?" Fang Yuan said. "As a matter of fact, I was here to make a deal with you."
The Bei clan head paused. "What kind of deal?"
"As you can imagine, our justifications for moving to Bei Gu Mountain are rather flimsy. However, if the Bei Clan were to come out and say that we had always lived here, then it would make it far easier for us to establish ourselves. In addition, I would like for the Bei Clan to assist us in moving our clan to our new home on Bei Gu Mountain. We would need resources and the like, as well as a secure path to travel, which would be much easier if we had a friendly welcoming force on the other side."
"And why would I do that?" the Bei clan head asked.
"Well, two reasons," Fang Yuan said. "One is my sheer strength as a Rank 5 Gu Master." The Bai Clan head's eyebrows twitched. This man was just coming out and saying that he was going to use violence if they did not give him what he needed! This was not a righteous, but rather demonic way of diplomacy! "But this can also be beneficial towards you," Fang Yuan added. "There's not just one primeval spring on Bei Gu Mountain, after all."
The Bei clan head's eyes widened.
"Are you trying to say that…?"
"Of course, a mountain as large and as ancient as this would have more than one spirit spring," Fang Yuan said. "I happen to know the location of two spirit springs on it. One of them is, of course, going to belong to my clan. However, if you cooperate, I will give you the location of the second spirit spring in question."
The Bei clan head paused, thinking about Fang Yuan's offer.
"It will save you quite a large deal in terms of time and manpower," Fang Yuan said. It was true, it could take them several years to try to find the primeval spring if they were searching blindly. On the other hand, if they knew exactly where they were searching, they could cut down their efforts to only a few months. It would not only save time but the lives of many Bei clansmen as well.
"How do I know that you'll hold up your end of the bargain once this is all over?" she asked.
Fang Yuan pretended to act shocked. "I will have you know that I've always been the pillar of the righteous path on Qing Mao Mountain. My reputation spread far and wide as someone who cares deeply not only for my own clansmen, but for everyone. Do I look like someone so shameless as to renege on my word?"
The Bei clan head was a bit taken aback by Fang Yuan's show of sincerity, but she also wasn't born yesterday. No matter how trustworthy Fang Yuan looked, she was not going on his word alone. "I would still need something better than your word..."
"I am willing to use Poison Vow Gu to bind the two of us," Fang Yuan said. "If that will set your heart at ease."
"I do not have a Poison Vow Gu," the Bei clan head said.
"You are being far too suspicious when I am so sincere. It will take time for me to move my clan to where I want to," Fang Yuan said, shaking his head. "A lot of time. The continued cooperation of the Bei clan would help us greatly in settling down in our new home. If I want to keep that, of course, I will continue to cooperate with you. How about this? If you wish, I'm willing to give you 200,000 primeval stones as a deposit, which you can return to us once you've verified that the primeval spring is there." The Bei clan head considered it. It was not an insignificant amount of primeval stones, even to a Rank 5 Gu Master.
"Alright then, Fang Yuan," she said. "I will need to discuss this with the rest of my clan elders before I can give you a response. Please take a seat in the meanwhile."
The elders' meeting was rather short, as the very next morning, Fang Yuan got their answer, saying that they agreed. Although they demanded a deposit of 300,000 primeval stones, Fang Yuan said, "I do not like such bickering over such a small amount of primeval stones." He agreed to their condition.
He pointed to a place on the map. "This is where the spirit spring that your clan might be allowed to use is." The Bei clan head noted the location. There were a large number of bone beasts there, and it would be hard to get through, even if they knew where it was. It would take them eight to ten months at the very least to get a foothold there, and longer to fully establish themselves.
Fang Yuan and the Bei clan head both used an Information Path Gu Worm to record the transaction and each kept a copy of the same.
Fang Yuan returned to where Fang Zheng and Bai Ning Bing were camped.
"How was the Bone-Flesh Unity Gu?" Fang Yuan asked.
It had five series as per what the Flesh Bone Scholar had written down. The worst quality was Fratricidal and the best was Blood Kin Relation. They had ended up refining an intermediate quality Bone-Flesh Unity Gu of 'Friendly Relation Gu.' Although Fang Zheng thought highly of Fang Yuan, these feelings were not reciprocated, hence the lower quality of the gu worm that was produced. It was still better than the alternative worst case scenario, however.
It had not been as easy to trick the gu refinement as it had been to trick the skull with Bai Ning Bing.
Bai Ning Bing was testing it out for him - injecting her Rank 3 Peak Stage primeval essence into Fang Zheng's aperture. There was a loss of about 60% from this, however, that still meant that Bai Ning Bing could give about 36% of her primeval essence to Fang Zheng.
Each drop was eight times as potent as Fang Zheng's own essence, so this was like him having 288% additional primeval essence!
If Fang Yuan used Rank 5 Training Weights Gu, this amount could be doubled! Given how cultivation was not linear and instead could increase by several multiples depending on how high one's aptitude was, it was an incredible advancement!

chapters.title: Chapter 241: Return Home: Part One
chapters.content:
"Good progress," Fang Zheng noted. "If I could keep this up, I could probably get to rank three middle stage by the end of the week."
Such speed was unheard of. If he had said this to anyone else, he would likely be accused of lying. However, aside from using Relic Gu, there was nothing in the gu world that could match Bone-Flesh Unity Gu's speed and value. Relic Gu, unfortunately, was consumable and hard, and impossible to refine with current methods. Bone-Flesh Unity Gu, though, could be used over and over. Without a doubt many clans would kill to have a method like this.
"Alright then. I think we've seen enough for a new outset. Let's go back to the village."
"Aren't you afraid about the Bei clan taking the spirit spring?" Bai Ning Bing asked.
"We have a bit of an understanding with them."
Fang Yuan was not worried about them reneging on their deal. At the slightest sign of disloyalty, he could destroy them by simply mentioning the fact that their spiritual spring was dying to their surrounding clans. That said, he had other ways of keeping them out. "Let's go, then," Fang Yuan said, and they mounted the White Form Immortal Snake.
While flying, however, Fang Yuan made a quick stop. "Why are we stopping here?" Bai Ning Bing asked. She recognized this place - the place where they had killed the divine pheasant. Its corpse was still there, as it had only been killed recently. Though signs of decay were beginning to set in, soon enough the surrounding animals would have stripped it bare. However, several of its body parts were still intact.
Fang Yuan returned after having removed its testicles, to both Bai Ning Bing's and Fang Yuan's surprise. Why did he need them? For some kind of refinement material? Or perhaps they could be sold for a very good amount? Fang Yuan did not answer as they all went to the White Form Immortal Snake once more. By that evening, they had returned to Gu Yue village and Bai Ning Bing returned to hers.
Naturally, the elders had several questions for Fang Yuan regarding what he had been doing and where he had been all this time. However, he waved them away for now, telling them that he would tell them later on.
Later the next morning, Fang Yuan went to go check on the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus. More of its leaves have been lost, indicating that the spirit spring was dying faster. Once it completely died out, the spirit spring would show signs of dying.
Fang Yuan immediately detonated it. If he couldn't have it, no one could, and it was for the best that the clan know their spirit spring was indeed, truly dying as soon as possible.
Fang Yuan was in the Dollhouse after he had used Equality Gu with Bai Ning Bing to obtain as many of the Northern Dark Ice Soul Physique's dao marks as he could. This was his first time attempting to refine the Righteous Virtue Physique.
The House Spirit was on guard right next to him, and he had already taken out Doctor Gu. While refining Gu worms was one thing, attempting to refine one's body was another. Aside from a low rate of success, there was a far greater risk of bodily injury. With that said, however, the upside truly was amazing if Paradise Earth could be believed.
He began pouring primeval essence into Charity Gu, though he didn't activate it, instead taking it out of his aperture and placing it near his chest. The next ingredient involved a large amount of Hope Gu which he had collected from the clan's primeval spring. The Rank 1 Hope Gu began hopping towards Charity Gu much as if they were trying to open up an aperture as it began glowing.
Fang Yuan felt a strange sensation travel through his chest and into his arms. Charity Gu began glowing brighter as the House Spirit began tossing in primeval stones. The Northern Dark Ice Soul Physique's dao marks on him began flickering though there was no way for Fang Yuan to currently know this.
All of a sudden, the sensation went from a mild current to a heavy shock and Charity Gu was sent flying out towards the wall of the Dollhouse.
Fang Yuan coughed out a mouthful of blood. Healing from Doctor Gu fixed him up, and while the injury was not as bad as he had initially expected, it would've still been disabling had it not been for the Human Path's excellent healing methods.
Charity Gu was damaged as well, so he would need to wait for it to recover before he could attempt to do this again. For a source of large amounts of Hope Gu, it would also be better to do this near the new primeval spring on Bei Gu Mountain rather than here. There had been enough Hope Gu for a singular attempt, but if he took any more the clan would no doubt begin complaining.
'Perhaps obtaining the Ancient Moon Desolate Yin Physique could have been better,' he thought to himself. However, despite attempting to investigate the first gen Gu Yue's methods even further, he still had not happened upon how exactly he had attempted to "concentrate his bloodline" in order to obtain the Ancient Moon Desolate Yin Physique in one of his descendants.
And without the Blood Skull Gu, Fang Yuan would need a different method in order to transfer that physique into himself. Still, it would not carry the risk of bodily injury that refining his body directly did.
For now, though, he would have to deal with other things.
Meanwhile, Fang Zheng was also busy in his own process of refinement.
He had taken out the Four Flavors Liquor worm, his vital Gu, and had added a batch of monkey wine that Fang Yuan had given to him.
This was needed for reverse refinement.
Reverse refinement was said to have a higher success rate than normal refinement and was also easier, but this was the first time that Fang Zheng was attempting to do so and was naturally nervous.
He imitated what his brother had taught him.
Rather than trying to fuse two gu worms together, he now needed to recognize the fact that this gu worm was made of two, and after putting his focus into it, attempt to separate his concentration into two halves.
A glowing ball of white light emerged in his room as he tossed in primeval stones, as well as some more of the monkey wine, until finally, it exploded and two Liquor Worms popped out. One of them was his vital gu, while the other landed on the floor. Both of them were alive, however, they also showed signs of mild injury.
But, Fang Zheng was overjoyed as he had succeeded in his first attempt.
This was only the first step, however. He now needed to advance it to Rank Two Moon Harbinger Gu once it had healed up, and then could advance it to Rank Three Seven Fragrances Liquor Worm which would actually work on his Rank 3 primeval essence. At each step there would be a chance of failure and sustaining backlash from the refinement, but the upside was that so long as it was Fang Zheng's vital gu it would never completely die out.

chapters.title: Chapter 242 242: Return Home: Part Two
chapters.content:
At the next clan elder meeting, a message had come from the Bai Clan that they had accepted the Gu Yue's proposal, and there were smiles all around.
"It truly does seem that the Gu Yue Clan is the number one clan on Qing Mao Mountain!"
"We will be the only clan on Qing Mao now."
There was a round of laughter at this.
Fang Yuan, however, was unmoved. "I'm afraid that there is bad news. Before I say what I mean, I need to tell everyone that this is a highly confidential secret of the clan and anyone who leaks it to an outsider will be killed."
The laughter died down at that as the mood turned grim. A secret like that meant that the clan's future had to be at stake, otherwise there would not be such an extreme punishment.
"Some of you may be wondering why I left for some time," Fang Yuan said. They did not openly say anything to him when he came back, but he knew that the other elders had greatly annoyed Qing Shu and Fang Zheng, although they had done a reasonable enough job of holding down the fort while he was gone. "There is a reason for my absence. I had left Qing Mao Mountain and had gone to a neighboring region, namely Bei Gu Mountain."
Many of them frowned at this. "Why would our clan leader leave to some random location for no reason? Did he think that this was the appropriate time to go on a picnic or vacation?" This was their thought process.
"It was necessary for me to do so because our clan's spirit spring is dying." There were gasps at this declaration.
"Clan leader, surely you must be mistaken. The spirit spring has not shown-"
Fang Yuan held up his hand. "It has not shown any signs yet, but it will soon enough. We thought that we had gotten lucky and had been spared the fate of the Bai and the Xiong clans when it came to our spirit springs. However, it just looks like our fate was delayed compared to theirs." He did not mention the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus, which was the actual reason why their spirit spring wasn't dying out faster.
"Without our spirit spring, our clan will be like a rootless weed, scattering in the wind."
"Even with our clan's strength, it will be difficult for us to survive."
"We won't be able to collect enough Hope Gu for new Gu Masters."
Fang Yuan raised up his hand to indicate that they should remain silent. "Our spirit spring will still survive for a while. We do not need to panic. And that's why I'm getting to why I had gone to Bei Gu Mountain, because although we have one home, it doesn't mean that we cannot find another."
Fang Yuan took out the book made by the Flesh Bone Lord and had it passed around the room. After glancing at it, many of the elders frowned.
"I've never heard of such a tale before..."
"A Gu Yue clan elder running away with a Bai clan elder's daughter? That would have been quite scandalous and the talk of the town, even if it happened several centuries ago."
"All of you are correct," Fang Yuan said. "That never happened. This is a forgery. However, the rest of the book is genuine. There was an inheritance on Bei Gu Mountain." Fang Yuan removed several Bone Spear Gu and Spiral Bone Gu. "I was able to retrieve them from there." He passed these new gu worms around, and the elders examined them with curiosity. "They feed upon milk, and we found a large milk spring on Bei Gu Mountain as well, which can feed these gu worms in perpetuity as well as ourselves."
"Are these offensive gu worms?"
"Short-range at that, but they are powerful."
"I think our Moonlight Gu are still superior..."
"Not only that," Fang Yuan added, "I have found the location of a fresh spirit spring there." At these words, many of the elders' eyes lit up. A fresh primeval spring!
If that was true, then that meant that their clan was saved.
"Elder Qing Shu has been running calculations on how we can possibly move ourselves to Bei Gu Mountain," Fang Yuan said. "It would invite too much suspicion if we were to all leave at once. As such, we are going to send a first wave of Gu Masters as a hunting party, and we will follow this course."
Qing Shu took out a map and traced a path which skirted the river at several points. "The river will mean fresh water will be easy to obtain. However, there are several beasts we may have to deal with, including crocodiles. After that, we need to pass through this forest and mountain here until finally, we get to Bei Gu Mountain. The journey on foot will take between three weeks and a month, depending on how lucky we are." That was the difference in between flying with a Rank 5 gu worm and trying to travel alongside the road. The speed of both just could not be compared.
"It will be an extremely dangerous journey," one of the elders said. Surviving in the wilderness was not easy. Tales from the merchant caravan, which came to Gu Yue village every year, was more than enough evidence for the same.
Although mortals were the ones who died the most, even Gu Masters and elders also perished along the journey.
"It will be risky," Qing Shu said.
"Indeed," Fang Yuan said. "However, I will be going alongside this first batch of travelers." The discussion then moved on to further logistical planning. There were things that Qing Shu hadn't considered, such as rope and oil.
"I have two questions," one of the elders said. "One, isn't there a clan which lives nearby Bei Gu Mountain? Aren't we basically setting up our tent in someone's backyard? Wouldn't they start to oppose us and wouldn't this lead to a fight?"
Fang Yuan laughed coldly. "So what if they do? Before the strength of a Rank 5 Gu Master, what can they do?" He then waved the book around. "And as I said, as far as anyone knows, we always had a claim to Bei Gu Mountain. But you don't need to worry. I've already spoken with the Bei clan head. We have an agreement, and they've even agreed to help us settle in when we get there."
Many of the Gu Yue villagers were astonished. What kind of courtesy was that? Not only were the Bei Clan allowing the Gu Yue Clan to basically squat in their backyard, but they had even built a hotel for them and prepared refreshments!
"You don't need to concern yourselves with the details," Fang Yuan said. "However, this is a combined effort of the Gu Yue and the Bei clans in order to seize the mountain."
The elders fell into silence, wondering what it was that Fang Yuan had promised them to get them to cooperate. The mere threat of him attacking them would be one thing, but the Bei Clan certainly had to have a trump card, otherwise it would not have survived for so long. The price would be high if the Bei Clan had agreed like this.
However, if Fang Yuan said it would be all right, then it would likely be all right, many of them felt.

chapters.title: Chapter 243: Return Home: Part Three
chapters.content:
"Moving on to my second question," the same elder said. "We've been talking about moving there, but what about our Moon Orchids and our signature gu worms that need them? They are a staple of our clan. Even if we try to switch over to using the Bone Path, it could possibly take 30 to 40 years for it to fully flourish with a set of complete gu worms." Although Bone Spear Gu and Spiral Bone Spear Gu were alright for the lower ranks to use, the true strength of the clan was with its elders. Fang Yuan was able to show them several other refinement recipes, but the Rank 3 version of the gu worm, Bone Spike Gu, damaged the user as well. Who would want to use that kind of gu worm?
30 to 40 years was a long time. However, it was actually a very low estimation.
The current proliferation of the Moonlight Gu and its variants in the Gu Yue Clan was a result of over a thousand years of painstaking experimentation with various refinement materials, fusion, and reverse refinement of new gu worms and alternative ingredients. Even now, if one went ahead and saw the recipes in the clan's storage, one would find notes from Gu Masters from centuries ago describing things they had discovered which seemed to increase the refinement rate of gu worms.
So, even if they had a batch of Gu worms already prepared and several bone path recipes as described by the Flesh Bone Lord in his book, it still could not hold a candle to the Gu Yue clan's developments when it came to the Moonlight Gu.
"Speaking of such, there is a potential compromise we can come to," Fang Yuan said. "I've managed to obtain a Rank 5 Earth Eating Eel."
"Earth Eating Eel?" Several of them asked, unfamiliar with this gu worm.
Fang Yuan took it out of his aperture, with it being nearly as large as the room. It was a gu worm that was so flat it looked almost two-dimensional, like it was a rug rather than a living creature. It was covered in green scales. They had been given to him by the Goody Two-Shoes system after giving the location of the second spirit spring to the Bei Clan.
"The effect of the eel is simple," Fang Yuan said. "It can swallow a large amount of earth, and when it does so, its body begins to expand. Don't look at how big it is right now. It can easily swell up to over a hundred times this size. Once that happens, the soil is absorbed onto its scales, and the soil can then be used for planting crops, such as the Moon Orchids. It only needs fresh soil to feed it, so long as we can provide it with that, we can continue growing our Moon Orchids."
Even if it was expanded to 100 times, it would still not be as large as the Gu Yue Clan's current Moon Orchid garden. However, it would be sufficient to grow enough petals to sustain them for some time.
Transplanting the moon orchids would be a bit of an issue, and they may have to take the help of the Moon and Stars Support Vine Gu once more once they got there, but this was better than nothing.
With most of this matter settled in this way, Qing Shu announced to the village the next morning that there would be a large hunting competition in order to train the Gu Yue Clan's Gu Masters to be better prepared to deal with future events.
Many people didn't understand why this was going on, given how very few Gu Masters there were. However, as Elder Qing Shu began listing out some of the prizes, including Moon Orchid Petals and primeval stones, interest began to increase.
To the surprise of many people, the hunt would not be taking place in Gu Yue Village, but rather near a distant peak called Bei Gu Mountain.
***
Fang Zheng took out his vital gu, the Liquor Worm, and then began adding wine to it, as well as two Moonlight Gu.
This was an alternate evolution path of the Moonlight Gu, which had been developed by the Gu Yue Clan to turn it into the Moon Harbinger Gu.
After doing so, he then began tossing in Moon Orchid Petals and then primeval stones. Luckily enough, he succeeded on his first try. Then again, being a rank two Gu, the success of refinement was relatively high. It would not be so easy to make the Seven Fragrances Liquor Worm.
The Moon Harbinger Gu was not very useful - it was a signaling type gu worm that would emit a bright light somewhat like a lighthouse on Earth, but it was so bright that it would alert one's enemies as well. But Fang Zheng didn't really care if it was a dud stage, so was the Four Flavors Liquor Worm, at least with this he had a chance of getting it to Rank 3.
In the evenings, Fang Yuan would use Rank 5 Training Weights Gu in order to dilute his Rank 5 essence to Rank 4 essence, allowing him to use Bone-Flesh Unity Gu to help Fang Zheng in his cultivation. Bright yellow golden essence began to fill Fang Zheng's aperture.
Since Rank 5 Training Weights Gu diluted the primeval essence, the rate at which he recovered it was also far faster. And so this wasn't simply a doubling of what Bai Ning Bing efficiency, but rather multiplying it several times!
Fang Zheng found himself at rank three middle stage within a few days.
And by the time the first caravan was being arranged to leave for Bei Gu Mountain, he had just reached rank three upper stage.
Fang Yuan, for his own part, was not slouching, attempting to use Equality Gu to advance his own cultivation. However, breaking through from Rank 5 Initial to Rank 5 Middle Stage was not easy, even with the amplification of Equality Gu's effect. However, he did feel that he was close to that point.
"If I could somehow reverse-refine Rank 4 Training Weights Gu to rank 3, then I could just give it to Fang Zheng, and this might not be necessary," he thought to himself. Even then though, the recovery to Fang Zheng's aperture would be extremely slow. Nothing could truly rival Bone-Flesh Unity Gu's effectiveness.
***
In the coming days, with the Heavenly Essence Treasure Lotus gone, the signs of the spirit spring drying up became apparent to the clan elders, who quickly put any grievances they had aside and started working to arrange for things to go as smoothly as possible.
The first batch of caravans was going to be led by him and Fang Zheng would be coming along for the ride.
He could have sent Qing Shu instead, however, he needed someone back in the village to look after things, and that was also why Bai Nin Bing was left behind.
It was a Fang Yuan's other contingency against something happening in the village.
Fang Yuan was strong, but he could only be in one place at once: either with the caravan or at the village, not both.
And it was clear that the situation was more dangerous with the caravan. Casualties would be high, and it might even be completely derailed from its path if they were not careful. His presence would greatly affect the success of their relocation.
At least, this is all what Fang Yuan had planned out in his head for their journey. Something happened which caused this plan to change.
"Everyone look! Down there, near the foot of the mountain!"
"I don't believe it!"

chapters.title: Chapter 244 244: Mercantile Expedition: Part One
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan, while this was going on, had been busy trying to cultivate. But he had no doubt noticed the commotion outside the clan head's pavilion. He terminated his session earlier than he normally would have and walked outside, frowning. "What on earth is going on?"
Out in the distance, he could finally see what all the hullabaloo was about. There were a number of Gu worms, carriages, mortals, and Gu Masters near the base of the mountain. The way they were walking and the way that they were carrying goods on their backs, this was not an invasion.
"The merchant caravan came now!" a Gu Master exclaimed in a loud voice.
"But why are they here?"
"This is way beyond the time they would normally come. We thought that they wouldn't come at all," another one intoned.
"Just be happy that they're here."
"They don't seem to be as numerous as they were before," someone else noted. The caravan did not even seem to be one-fifth the size of what it would normally be when it reached Gu Yue Village.
Regardless of the reason for why the caravan was here, since everyone had given up hope that they would visit Gu Yue Mountain, the villagers were all in a cheerful mood now. The absence of the caravan had meant that many things had gone unsold and many products that the villagers needed were unobtainable. Whether they were Bai, Xiong, or Gu Yue clansmen, all of them were in high spirits.
Fang Yuan descended from the clan head's pavilion and went out to greet the merchant caravan. The snow had completely melted away by this point, and the mud had dried up under the sun. Most areas were safe enough for travel up the mountain, although there were one or two mortals who succumbed to accidents along the mountain trail. The merchant caravan stopped before the walls of Gu Yue Village.
Jiang He dismounted from the head of the merchant caravan line. The number 'four' was still inscribed on his plate. He looked far more haggard compared to how he had in the prior times he had come to the village.
He looked like he had lost some weight, and he had signs of injuries which had only been partially healed. He looked like a man who had emerged from a war zone, Fang Yuan noted, as he walked towards the head of the caravan.
"Clan head of the Gu Yue clan Gu Yue Fang Yuan greets you," Fang Yuan said with a gentle smile.
Jiang He was a bit taken aback to see Fang Yuan there.
Fang Yuan had not been the clan head the last time he had dropped by.
While the changing of clan heads was something that happened every now and then, what was even more jarring was the fact that Fang Yuan was now rank five.
That technically put him on higher footing than Jiang He and almost equal footing with his father, the head of the Jiang Clan. Jiang He was almost approaching 30, and yet Fang Yuan was already at rank five while he was still only a rank four.
He was, of course, distracted from his cultivation because it's not easy to cultivate while running a merchant caravan and traveling across half the world. But even if he had been free all the time, he felt he may not have been able to do what Fang Yuan had just done. Was there some secret behind Fang Yuan's meteoric rise? He moved these thoughts to the back of his mind, recognizing that he needed to address Fang Yuan.
He cupped his hands and said, "Jiang He, greets you, Brother Fang Yuan." He did not add 'junior' or 'senior' before the brother title - he was used to calling Fang Yuan 'junior brother' but could no longer. But should he really be talking to him like an equal? When the words left his mouth, he felt that calling Fang Yuan "senior brother" might have been the right option.
Fang Yuan did not care, however. "I have been well enough." He then looked over at the merchant caravan with concern. "However, Brother Jiang He, you seem to have encountered some trouble along the way. This is not the normal time that you would drop by us. Did something happen along the way?"
Jiang He's face paled at the memory of what had just happened. "To say that we ran into misfortune is an understatement, Brother Fang Yuan," Jiang He said. "First of all, we ran into a Wailing Fog, which completely disoriented our sense of direction blinding us and also interfering with out sense of sound. Then there was an attack from a Lightning Panther, which would have killed all of us if I had not managed to fight it back and force it to retreat at the last moment. When the fog had cleared and this beast had been taken care of, we found that we were 20 li off course, and stuck in a swamp. Moving through that took us over ten days with all of the cargo we had, and we were constantly assailed by various kinds of venomous beasts and insects. Once we left, it turned out that two demonic Gu Masters had disguised themselves and joined our caravan. They wreaked havoc before stealing a large amount of our goods and leaving. Then, as if things could not have gotten worse for us, we were attacked by a large cloud of mites. The mites by themselves did not do much damage. However, they carried with them a plague which rapidly slew most of the mortals and many Gu Masters as well. Then there was a dust storm which damaged most of our wheels and other implements." He shook his head. "I do not exaggerate when I say I think we ran into more difficulties during this one trip than I have in my entire career combined."
"My heart pains to hear it," Fang Yuan said. In reality, the merchant caravan's misfortune was Gu Yue Village's great fortune, because now they actually had a chance to sell their wares and buy several things. In addition to that, Fang Yuan was already cooking up a scheme in his mind, adjusting for the changing situation.
Most merchant caravans were not headed by a rank four Gu Master, but a rank three one. If Jiang He had not been rank four, however, it was clear that their merchant caravan would have been completely wiped out, instead of barely managing to limp on towards Gu Yue Village.
"Coming to my attention, allow me to toast to you," Fang Yuan said. Jiang He graciously followed behind him.
"I had heard that there was an attack by a demonic Gu Master on Qing Mao Mountain," Jiang He said.
"Indeed," Fang Yuan said. "It's a very long tale. I can tell you about it once we sit down there."
The thing that the merchant caravan was most starved for was food. When even Jian He looked like he had lost weight, how worse off were the others? The mortals had sunken cheeks and stared greedily at anything they could devour even if it were a lone blade of grass. The Gu Master's gu worms had hardly fared better, many of them only had one or two as the rest had starved out and died.
Although the clan's food supplies had somewhat recovered, it wasn't like they were swimming in grain either. However, many in the merchant caravan were willing to pay three times the normal price for food. And Fang Yuan even ordered some portion of the clan's own storage to be sold. After all, milk could sustain them for quite a while if all went according to plan.

chapters.title: Chapter 245: Mercantile Expedition: Part Two
chapters.content:
Fang Yuan had participated in the rock gambling den the last two times the merchant caravan had been around, the first time directly and the second time indirectly via Fang Zheng as proxy.
This time, however, the person who ran it was dead along with Jia Fu's younger brother Jia Jin Sheng.
Fang Yuan had intended to use the younger brother in the future in case he wanted to sell demonic inheritances or artifacts using him as an intermediary. However, that plan had been derailed by the Goody Two-Shoes System, and it looked like he would ascend to being an Immortal long before he would be able to go back to his demonic ways. Given the case, such a connection was superfluous.
To the Gu Yue Clan's disappointment, there weren't many things being sold at the merchant caravan. Most of the goods had been damaged, and what was being sold was not of great interest to them. To the Bai and the Xiong Clan, who had hoped to unload some of their surplus gu worms to ease their own resources, they found very few buyers.
It felt far more like this was a line of beggars and homeless people who had just happened to stumble into the village! The villagers felt like they had been visited by refugees, not merchants.
The merchant caravan was also greatly disappointed. They had not initially intended to come to Qing Mao Mountain.
However, after being besieged by so many calamities and tragedies, they had no choice but to seek refuge wherever they could find it. Qing Mao Mountain, however, was still mostly barren and not exactly overflowing with resources.
While the merchant caravan had a low-to-moderate supply of primeval stones, that seemed to be all that they really had. The three villages already had primeval stones to suit their own needs. What the villages really needed were refinement materials and alternative feed for their gu worms, as well as to offload some of their own excesses.
They could not really do either.
And so it seemed that the merchant caravan would just have to leave Qing Mao Mountain soon, still about as defeated and exhausted as before. That was, until one evening, Fang Yuan handed Jian Fu something during one of the dinners they were having together.
"This is..." He took it in his hands.
"It's called Bone Spear Gu," Fang Yuan said. "Very easy gu to raise and can be fed with milk." He then handed him a Spiral Bone Spear Gu, Rank 2. "Also very easy to feed with milk. The best part is, of course, that milk can also be used to feed oneself. I've no doubt that they would go for a good price."
